  and its header records the scoping decision explicitly: the cache is per-entity-method, not
  per-Tx. The hoist belongs in the nested method only. This is the easiest way to implement the
  fix wrong.

- `SkipTenancy` must keep short-circuiting ahead of the resolve — unchanged, the gate above is the
  same one `create.go.tmpl` already applies.

**Tests.**

- **§29.6 pin:** a counting `TenantResolver` over a two-edge nested create asserts **one**
  invocation. `docs/tracker/phase-27.md` already books a tenancy test on 27.9 ("nested children
  inherit the ctx-cached tenant; `SkipTenancy` propagates") — **as written that test fails today**,
  which is why this is blocking rather than tracked: 27.9 would otherwise land a known-failing
  requirement, and the fix belongs in the template 27.9 extends.
- **Divergence pin:** a `required:false` table's resolve followed by a `required:true` table's, on
  one ctx, must still raise `tenancy.ErrMissing` from the second — the fail-open the raw-value cache
  exists to prevent. Needs a fixture edge the `tenancy` example does not currently have
  (`legacy_widgets` has `required:false` but no relationships).
- **Explicit-tenant pin:** `Get` with `o.Tenant` set, no tenant on ctx, and a relationship selected
  must succeed and return the children — it errors today.
- Existing `tx_resolver_test.go` counts must be unchanged.

**References.** PRD §29.6 (single-resolve), §29.10 (relationship propagation — the sentence this
violates), §29.4.2a (nested mutations), §29.4.4 (explicit tenant), §29.11 (one tenant per
transaction), §9.9.10. Related: FIX-199 and the `attachTenancyToTables` wiring rule, and FIX-055
which landed the ctx cache this entry reshapes — all the same class: a tenancy fact that is correct
on the direct path and unwired on a composed one.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-18. Landed as the approach above specifies, in four layers.

**Runtime (`tenancy/tenancy.go`).** `cachedTenant[T]` no longer carries `apply`.
`WithResolvedTenant` takes only the value; `CachedTenant` returns `(value, ok)`. A cached zero is a
real answer, so presence stays separate from the value. New unit tests cover the round trip, the
zero case, per-type keying and the derive-don't-mutate property.

**Generated `resolveTenant` (table + view).** Split in two. `tenantValue` answers the
table-independent half — what the resolver said, cached — and `resolveTenant` applies this table's
own `required` branch to it. The view client gets the same split inline. `TestCachedZeroTenant_
DoesNotSuppressAFailClosedTable` is the pin: `legacy_widgets` (required:false) and `products`
(required:true) over one cached zero, and the fail-closed table still raises `tenancy.ErrMissing`.
Before the split it returned the other table's `apply=false` and fell through to a DB constraint
error instead.

**The hoist.** `CreateWithRelated` resolves once before `database.WithTransaction`, gated on
`!SkipTenancy && Tenant == nil`. The 15 chaining stash sites now stash the resolver's answer only,
and skip the stash entirely under an explicit tenant — that value rides on CallOptions, which every
internal call inherits, and the slot cannot distinguish a set zero (honoured verbatim, §29.4.4) from
a resolved zero (takes the required branch). Measured after: **1** resolve for every nested shape
that measured 3, 7 or 10 before; **0** under `SkipTenancy` and under an explicit tenant.

**The gate.** `TableContext.NeedsTenantResolver()` and `HasTenantedNestedEdge()` are **methods**, not
pre-computed fields, deliberately against guidelines/TEMPLATES.md §6. The union is read from three
places that must agree or the package does not compile, and a field would need every hand-built test
fixture to set it — the wiring-rule shape behind FIX-059, FIX-068, FIX-069 and FIX-199. That was not
theoretical here: the field version broke four `BuildClientContext` unit tests on the first run.
`finalizeTenancyWiring` still runs as a post-`wireNestedMutations` pass for the one fact a single
table cannot answer, `ExplicitTenantGoType`, and is wired into all three context-building entry
points (generate, `graphql gen`, `validate`).

**Folded-in half.** `loadRelationships` now takes and forwards `tenant *T` beside `skipTenancy`.
`TestRelationshipLoad_HonoursAnExplicitTenant` pins it on §29.4.4's bootstrap path — ctx carrying no
tenant, explicit tenant set, relationship selected — which failed with `tenancy.ErrMissing` before.

**A second, unrelated blocking bug was found while verifying this one, and fixed here.**
`CreateWithRelated` passed `"create <entity> with related"` to `database.WithTransaction`. That
string doubles as the **SAVEPOINT identifier** when ctx already carries a transaction, and
`database.Tx.Begin` requires `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` — so every call inside a consumer's `Begin` /
`WithTx` block hard-errored before any statement ran:

```
database: savepoint name "create workspaceNote with related" must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
```

This contradicted the method's own doc comment and PRD §18.3. It was invisible to every existing
test because the top-level path — which all of them take — never renders the name into SQL. The name
is now `create_<snake>_with_related`, and `TestCreateWithRelated_ComposesWithACallerTransaction`
covers all four shapes: commit with the caller's tx, roll back with it, a failed nested write rolling
back to the savepoint while the outer tx stays usable, and two nested writes nesting sequentially.
**27.9 inherits the corrected spelling** — its two methods take the same name expression.

**Coverage gap closed in the same pass.** The shared-parent-with-tenanted-child shape — the one the
design question turned on — exists in no example schema: the only tenanted table with nested edges,
`workspace_notes`, is self-referential, so its parent *is* its target, and the gate widening moved
zero goldens. `cmd/sqlgen/gen/nested_test.go` gains a fixture that puts the tenant column on `orders`
alone, making `users` a shared parent writing into a tenanted child, plus both halves of the pin:
the parent hoists (and would not if the hoist were gated on its own tenancy), and a parent whose
edges reach no tenanted client does not.

**The auto-review found four residual gaps; all four were fixed inside this entry.**

1. **The hoist gate was narrower than the rule.** It read `HasTenantedNestedEdge`, so a *tenanted*
   parent whose every edge target opts out of tenancy got no hoist — and `CreateWithRelated`'s
   terminal re-read of the parent, which fires whenever the caller selected a relationship, resolved
   a second time. The gate is now `NeedsTenantResolver`: "some client this method reaches resolves",
   which is what §29.6 actually bounds. Pinned by
   `TestNestedTenancy_TenantedParentWithSharedChildrenStillHoists`.
2. **`TargetTenanted` read the target's tenant *column*, not its resolver need.** A shared target
   that appends a tenanted O2O child's filter, or compiles a relationship filter against a tenanted
   table, resolves inside this write too — the `connect` visibility read goes through
   `filterOptions`. Renamed `TargetResolvesTenant` and populated from a new
   `TableContext.resolvesTenantDirectly()`. That predicate is deliberately the union *minus* the
   nested term: reading the full union would make an edge's answer depend on the order
   `wireNestedMutations` visits tables in, and one level is all that is correct anyway, since v1
   nests one level deep.
3. **The counting pin never exercised the terminal re-read** — every case passed nil `FieldOptions`,
   so the shape that measured **10** was the one shape not counted. A relationship-selected case was
   added; it comes back as 1.
4. **`BuildEntityContextsFromSchema` never attached view tenancy**, so `finalizeTenancyWiring`
   resolved a different `ExplicitTenantGoType` on the `graphql gen` path than under `generate` in a
   package whose only tenanted entity is a view. The attach was added and the comment asserting the
   omission was deliberate corrected. No emitted difference today; latent skew closed.

**One review note was a documentation conflict, adjudicated 2026-09-18 by the user: the
per-operation rule stands and the PRD was amended to match.** §29.11 read "a single transaction runs
with a single tenant resolved from ctx at transaction open. Operations inside the tx inherit the
tenant", which is licence to widen the cache to a caller-opened `WithTx`; `tx_resolver_test.go` pins
the opposite (N mutations → N resolves) and records that scoping as deliberate. The two diverge on
exactly one shape — two or more operations inside a caller-opened transaction.

The test wins. The resolver's whole job is to read ctx (§29.3.1), so a value cached at `Begin` would
ignore a ctx the caller legitimately changed between two operations they chose to group. §29.11 now
states the per-operation rule outright, plus the consequence it previously obscured: **a
mid-transaction tenant switch is undefined, not prevented** — there is no detection, and a caller who
changes tenant between two writes in one transaction gets rows in two tenants, silently. The old
wording read like a safety guarantee the implementation never provided. Building the actual guarantee
is a feature (detect and reject a mid-tx change), not a cache-scope change, and is not in scope here.

Three sibling documents were corrected in the same pass. `docs/tracker/IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md:2494` still
carried the per-Tx wording attributed to §29.6 — phase 14.8 reconciled the identical sentence in
`phase-14.md` and in `tx_resolver_test.go`'s header but never reached that file, **which `/phase`
reads**. `tx_resolver_test.go`'s header now records the settled rule rather than an open discrepancy.
And `TestTx_TenantResolvedAtTxOpenPropagatesToOps` was renamed
`TestTx_TenantIsConsistentAcrossOpsInATx`: its name asserted the per-Tx reading while its own body
disproved it, which is how the wrong reading kept propagating. `docs/tracker/phase-13.md` carries the
rename note so the old name stays findable.

**Verification.** `make check` clean; `make check-examples` clean across postgres, mysql and sqlite.
Goldens regenerated for both `make update-golden` and `make update-golden-e2e`. The existing
`tx_resolver_test.go` counts are unchanged — the hoist lives in the nested method, not in
`database.WithTransaction`, so N mutations inside one user transaction still resolve N times.


### FIX-219

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 27, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_event.go:269-299` (`passThroughOps`)
- **Owner:** **27.6**, whose task list and acceptance criteria now carry both points verbatim. Kept
  open rather than fixed inside 27.5 because the only correct fix is 27.6's own per-row arm: adding
  `OpUpsertMany` to `passThroughOps` would publish the whole deduped slice instead of nil, trading
  one wrong §28.6 shape for another.
- **Surfaced by:** `/verify 27.5` (2026-09-17) — found independently by the parent and the
  reviewer; it is a **fourth** `OpUpsertMany` consumer site that 27.5's interim-state table and
  27.6's task list both omit.

**`UpsertMany` publishes `Event.Input: nil` on every fail-closed table.** `passThroughOps`
enumerates `OpCreate` and `OpUpsert` when `!emitCreate` (`context_event.go:276-283`) but never
`OpUpsertMany`, so `OpUpsertMany` falls out of the §32.3 switch to the fail-closed `default`
and publishes no payload at all. §28.6's shape table mandates a per-row `*Create<T>Input`. This
is the exact shape the function's own doc comment says it exists to prevent: "Letting those ops
reach the default would publish nil where §28.6's shape table says `*<T>Filter` — the very
shape this fix rejected."

_Scope corrected 2026-09-17 by verification._ This entry first scoped the nil payload to a table
that redacts *something* while leaving its create input un-redacted. That is one sub-case, not
the condition. A table that **does** redact a create field gets `case hook.OpCreate,
hook.OpUpsert:` instead of a pass-through entry, and that arm does not name `OpUpsertMany`
either — so it reaches the same `default`. Measured on the `events` example: `accounts` redacts
create (`password_hash: internal`), update **and** increment inputs, and all three fanned-out
`UpsertMany` events carry `Input: nil`.

It is live in a committed golden today, not hypothetical:
`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/models/event_hooks_gen.go:328` lists `hook.OpCreate,
hook.OpUpsert, hook.OpUpdate, hook.OpUpdateWhere, hook.OpIncrement` as pass-through for
`categoryClient` and omits `hook.OpUpsertMany`, which that client generates.

**Root cause.** 27.5 correctly folded `UpsertMany` into `buildEventTableContext`'s `emitCreate`
list (`context_event.go:211`) to close the FIX-207-class leak — a table redacting a create
field now fails closed instead of publishing the whole slice un-redacted. But `emitCreate` and
`passThroughOps` are two different gates on the same switch, and only the first was updated. On
a **non**-fail-closed table the mirror-image gap applies: the `default` arm is
`inputVal = mc.Input`, so every fanned-out per-row event carries the **entire deduped batch
slice** instead of its own row's input — the un-per-row shape PRD §28.6 names explicitly.
Neither is a data leak; both are §28.6 shape violations that ship today, because
`operations.upsert_many` defaults to `true`.

27.6's task list names three consumer arms (`mapOpToAction`, cache `dispatchMutation`, the
§32.3 redaction arm) and this is a fourth site. 27.6 *does* close it — but only if its
`case hook.OpUpsertMany:` arm is emitted **unconditionally**, with redaction nested inside, the
way `case hook.OpCreateMany:` is (`event_hooks.go.tmpl:129-137`). If it mirrors
`case hook.OpCreate, hook.OpUpsert:` instead (`event_hooks.go.tmpl:150-158`), which is wrapped
in `{{- if .EmitRedactCreate }}`, the non-redacting table keeps the wrong payload.

**Suggested fix.** _Verified correct 2026-09-17 — see "Verification" below._
- Emit the `OpUpsertMany` arm in `event_hooks.go.tmpl` unconditionally, indexing
  `mc.Input.([]*Create<T>Input)` by `i` like the `OpCreateMany` arm, with the
  `redact<T>CreateInput` call nested under `{{- if .EmitRedactCreate }}` inside it.
- Plumb `HasUpsertMany` onto `EventTableContext` and widen two gates with it: the fanout block
  (`{{- if or .HasCreateMany .HasUpdateMany }}`) and the `batchCreateInputs` declaration
  (`{{- if .HasCreateMany }}`). No preset produces `create_many: false, upsert_many: true`, but
  a per-table override can and nothing validates against it — without the widened gates that
  config emits a package referencing an undeclared variable.
- With that arm present, `passThroughOps` needs no `OpUpsertMany` entry — but add a comment
  there recording why, so the next reader does not re-open the question.
- Add the `UpsertMany` row to **PRD §28.6's shape table**, which currently has none: the table
  lists `Create`, `CreateMany`, `Update`, `UpdateMany`, `Upsert`, `Increment`, the delete family
  and the `*Where` family, and stops. §28.9's prose (PRD:14015) states the per-row rule but the
  normative table does not carry it.
- Fold both points into 27.6's task list and acceptance criteria so they are not rediscovered.
- Test: assert event *i* carries input *i* on a table with **no** redacted column, and on a
  fail-closed table that redacts only an *update* field — the two shapes the current gates miss.

**References.**
- PRD §28.6 "Event Input" (shape table) and §28.9 (`OpUpsertMany` per-row rule, PRD:14015).
- PRD §32.3 "Per-surface behavior" — the fail-closed default.
- PRD §21.2 — "every consumer switch keyed on `MutationOp` must name it explicitly ... None of
  those fails to compile when an arm is missing, so each needs its own behavioral check."
- `FIX-207` — the un-redacted-payload class 27.5's `emitCreate` change closed; this is its
  shape-side remainder.
- `docs/tracker/phase-27.md` §27.6 tasks; §27.5's "interim state between 27.5 and 27.6" table,
  which counts two live violations and calls this third one safe.

**Verification (2026-09-17).** Both failure modes reproduced on the `events` example (SQLite,
real bus) rather than inferred:

| Table | Shape today | Expected (§28.6 / §28.9) |
|---|---|---|
| `products` (non-fail-closed) | 3 inputs → 3 events, **each carrying the whole 3-element slice** | the i-th `*CreateProductInput` |
| `accounts` (fail-closed, redacts create + update + increment) | 3 inputs → 3 events, **all `Input: nil`** | the i-th redacted `*CreateAccountInput` |

**The `OpCreateMany`-shaped index arm is the correct fix, and `phase-27.md`'s **EQ5** bullet
arguing otherwise is obsolete.** EQ5 held that `DO NOTHING` + `RETURNING` returns only the
inserted rows, so `AffectedPKs` would be shorter than the input slice and an index-aligned
fanout would misalign. 27.5 resolved EQ5 the other way: `AffectedPKs` comes from the inputs, or
from `resolveUpsertManyRows` — which returns exactly one key per deduped value row and errors
otherwise — never from `RETURNING` (**A19**), and the terminal republishes `m.Input = rowInputs`,
the deduped slice. Commit `ad575c5` wrote that guarantee into PRD §28.9. Measured:

- 3 inputs deduping to 2 rows → 2 events, published slice length 2, `slice[0]` the
  last-occurrence-wins input for PK 1 and `slice[1]` the input for PK 2.
- Mixed batch, 2 conflicting existing rows + 1 new → 3 events, `slice[i]` aligned with
  `AffectedPKs[i]` across both branches.
- A junction (`DO NOTHING`, empty `updateColumns`) builds `rowPKs` one-per-input with no
  read-back at all, so alignment there is structural.

The `phase-27.md` bullet has been corrected so the implementer does not build a correlation
mechanism for a problem 27.5 already closed. Line references in this entry drifted with 27.5's
edits and have been refreshed (`context_event.go:203`→211, `:270-281`→269-299, `:275-280`→276-283;
`event_hooks.go.tmpl:128-136`→129-137, `:149-157`→150-158); the golden reference
`event_hooks_gen.go:328` is exact.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-17 **inside 27.6**, as this entry's Owner field
intended — the fix is 27.6's own per-row arm, exactly as the Suggested fix (verified correct
above) described.

`EventTableContext.HasCreateMany` (bool) became `BatchCreateOps` (`[]string`), resolved by the
new `batchCreateOps` in `context_event.go`: it names the enabled ops whose §28.6 payload is a
`[]*Create<T>Input` indexed per row — `OpCreateMany` and `OpUpsertMany`. `event_hooks.go.tmpl`
keys the batch-locals gate, the pre-loop type assertion and the per-row fanout arm off that
list, so the `OpUpsertMany` arm is emitted **unconditionally** with `redact<T>CreateInput`
nested inside, the `case hook.OpCreateMany:` shape rather than the
`{{- if .EmitRedactCreate }}`-wrapped `case hook.OpCreate, hook.OpUpsert:` shape. Both
generated forms are now `case hook.OpCreateMany, hook.OpUpsertMany:`. `passThroughOps` gained
the comment this entry asked for, recording that neither op belongs in the pass-through list and
why re-adding one would be a bug rather than a fix.

**Beyond what this entry listed:** `batchCreateInputs` and its type assertion were gated on
`HasCreateMany` alone, so `create_many: false, upsert_many: true` — reachable by a per-table
override, forbidden by no validation rule and produced by no preset — would have emitted a
package referencing an undeclared variable once the arm existed. Gated on the union instead.

PRD §28.6 gained the `UpsertMany` row, worded off §28.9's existing prose and recording that the
indexed slice is the **deduped** one; the section's `CreateMany` / `UpdateMany` sentence
("the i-th element of the caller's input slice") is not true of `UpsertMany` and now says so.

**Pins, all verified failing-first** by swapping the fixed generated files for their HEAD
versions and re-running — `TestEventUpsertMany_ActionIsUpsert` (`only 0 events delivered`),
`TestEventUpsertMany_PerRowInput` and `_PerRowInputAfterDedupe`
(`Input type = []*models.CreateProductInput`), `TestEventUpsertMany_RedactedPerRowInput`
(`Input type = <nil>`), plus the two template pins
`TestEventHooks_upsertMany_sharesBatchCreateArm` and
`TestEventHooks_upsertManyWithoutCreateMany_stillDeclaresBatchLocals`.


### FIX-218

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 27, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/upsert_many.go.tmpl:11`
- **Surfaced by:** `/verify 27.5` (2026-09-17) — independent reviewer pass; confirmed by the
  parent against the repo's own passing E2E test one branch over.

**`UpsertMany` trusts the caller's primary key on a conflict target that is not the primary
key, so it names rows that do not exist.** `$pkFromInput := or .CompositePK (ne .PKStrategy
"db")` decides key sourcing from the table's **PK strategy** alone, but the conflict target is a
**runtime argument**. On a composite-PK or `app` / `caller`-strategy table, a caller passing a
conflict target whose columns do not cover every PK column gets `rowIDs` / `rowPKs` built from
the *inputs* while the conflicting row in the database keeps its **own** primary key — the PK
column is excluded from the update half of the clause (`upsert_many.go.tmpl:105`,
`append(conflictColumns, <pk cols>)`), exactly as intended. Three consequences, all silent:
`m.AffectedPKs` names rows that do not exist (wrong cache-eviction key for 27.6's arm, wrong
`Event.PK` under §28.6); the terminal `GetMany` filters on those ids and comes back **short**,
violating §9.5 decision 2's "one entity per deduped input on every dialect"; and on a tenanted
table `captureAffectedTenants` looks up the same wrong keys, so `m.AffectedTenants` carries
`nil` for every conflicting row (§29.5). Under the `app` strategy a fresh UUID is minted per
input (`upsert_many.go.tmpl:144-151`), so **every** conflicting row is lost, not just some.

**Root cause.** The single-row `Upsert` does not make this mistake: `upsert.go.tmpl:6-11` sets
`$needsInsertResolve = true` for **any** non-composite-PK table on a RETURNING dialect
regardless of strategy, precisely so the PK comes from `RETURNING` / `resolveUpsertConflictRow`
rather than from the input. `upsert_many.go.tmpl:11` dropped the `supportsReturning` half of
that condition and kept only `ne .PKStrategy "db"`, which is a strictly weaker test. The
correct predicate is "the conflict target covers every PK column", which cannot be evaluated at
generation time — `conflictColumns` is only known at call time.

The defect is unreachable in all 12 example trees, which is why `make check-examples` is green:
every table on the `$pkFromInput` arm (`counters`, `user_credentials`, `workspaces`,
`documents`, `articles`, `binary_keys`, plus the composite-PK junctions and `rate_limits`)
declares **only** a PK-covering conflict target. The gen fixture for the shape already exists —
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/upsert_test.go:125-161` (`tenants`, `PKStrategyCaller`, `TenantConflictPK:
{"id"}` **and** `TenantConflictSlug: {"slug"}`) — and
`TestUpsertManyTemplate_pkFromInput` currently pins the broken behavior, including the
assertion that a caller-known key "must not cost a read-back statement".

The SQL semantics are not in question: `TestUpsertMany_DBGeneratedPK_ResolvesExistingIDs`
(`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/postgres/tests/upsert_many_test.go:262-305`) already measures on
a live PostgreSQL that upserting on `CategoryConflictName` — a non-PK unique target — leaves the
conflicting row's original `id` in place, and asserts `existing.ID == seeded.ID`. That test
passes because `categories` is `db`-strategy and takes the read-back path. The identical shape
one branch over takes the input-sourced path and gets a different answer.

**Suggested fix.**
- Make the choice at **runtime**, not at generation time: emit both paths and select on whether
  `conflictColumns` covers the PK columns. A `slices.Contains` loop over the PK column names in
  the emitted method is enough, and the result is already available where `conflictPositions` is
  computed (`upsert_many.go.tmpl:106`).
- Where it does not cover the PK, fall through to `resolveUpsertManyRows`, which is already
  correct, already dialect-uniform, and already reads the tenant column in the same statement.
  It must then be emitted on `$pkFromInput` tables too, not only under `$needsPKLookup`
  (`upsert_many.go.tmpl:384`), along with `<entity>ColumnValue`.
- Keep the one-statement-per-sub-batch fast path for the PK-covering case, so a pure link table
  is unaffected and §25.1's junction figures stay true.
- Re-check the `$captureTenant` arms (`upsert_many.go.tmpl:286-317`): the `rowPKs[start:end]` /
  `rowIDs[start:end]` slicing assumes the caller-known path, so it must move with the branch.
- Correct **PRD §9.5 decision 3** and **§9.7**'s "Batched, the same lookup is the only
  mechanism" paragraph, both of which currently assert the strategy-only rule ("Where the key is
  known before the write — a composite key, or the `app` / `caller` strategies — it is taken
  from the inputs"). The qualification "and the conflict target covers the primary key" is
  missing from both.
- Tests: extend `TestUpsertManyTemplate_pkFromInput` so the `tenants` fixture asserts the
  read-back path is emitted for `TenantConflictSlug` while the fast path survives for
  `TenantConflictPK`. Add an E2E pin on a caller-strategy table with a non-PK unique target
  asserting that a conflicting row resolves to the **existing** row's key and that the returned
  slice is one entity per deduped input.
- Add, in the same round, the **tenanted runtime pin** 27.5 never got: `make check-examples`
  asserts the widened non-MySQL `captureAffectedTenants` path only as emitted template text
  (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/tenant_capture_template_test.go:323-341`). Nothing exercises
  `m.AffectedTenants` for a tenanted `UpsertMany` at runtime, and it is the same alignment this
  fix moves.

**References.**
- PRD §9.5 "Batch upsert — dedupe, return shape, and key resolution", decision 3.
- PRD §9.7 "Upsert invariant: a conflict that changes nothing still resolves a PK" and
  "Batched, the same lookup is the only mechanism".
- PRD §28.6 (`Event.PK`), §29.5 (tenant stamped from the row), §27.7 (cache invalidation keys).
- `FIX-196` — the single-row `resolveUpsertConflictRow` this is the batched form of; the same
  class of spurious-key bug.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/upsert.go.tmpl:6-11` — the correct predicate to mirror.

**Resolution notes.** Fixed inline inside 27.5 rather than carried, since the defect was in
code 27.5 itself wrote and `/verify 27.5` is what found it. The decision moved from the table's PK
*strategy* to the runtime conflict target: `ConflictTargetContext.CoversPK`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context.go`, computed in `buildConflictTargets`) records per target whether it
includes every primary-key column, and the template emits a generated `<entity>ConflictCoversPK`
table the method reads at call time. A target that does not cover the key reads its written rows
back through `resolveUpsertManyRows`, which was generalized to return composite keys and to select
every PK column rather than only the first.

**The branch is emitted only where it can be taken.** The *set* of conflict targets is fixed at
generation time even though the choice among them is not, so a table whose targets all cover the
key keeps the one-statement fast path with no runtime check — every junction table, and every
`$keyKnownBeforeWrite` table in all 12 example trees. Golden movement across the examples is
consequently confined to a rename (`resolvedRow.id` → `.pk`, `ids` → `pks`) and comment rewording;
`git diff` over the example trees shows no added `pkFromInput` or `ConflictCoversPK` line anywhere,
which is the mechanical confirmation that no shipped example was ever reaching the bug.

**Measured failing-first, and the symptom is the one predicted.** `counters` in the postgres
example gained `slot TEXT UNIQUE` — nullable, so existing rows and tests are untouched, and NULL
never matches under a unique index — which makes it the first example table with a caller-known key
*and* a non-covering target. `TestUpsertMany_CallerKnownKey_NonCoveringTargetResolvesExistingKey`
seeds a row owning a slot under one key, upserts that slot under a *different* key, and asserts the
result resolves to the seeded key. Against the pre-fix template (reinstated in place, everything
else held constant) it reports `UpsertMany returned 1 entities, want 2` — the conflicting row
silently dropped from the result, exactly the §9.5 decision-2 violation this entry describes. The
companion pin `…_CoveringTargetIssuesNoReadBack` asserts the PK target still issues one INSERT and
one SELECT, and passes on both sides, being an inert-case regression pin.

**Two coverage notes.** `TestUpsertManyTemplate_compositePKReadBack` was added *after* the fix, closing a gap the fix itself opened: `resolveUpsertManyRows` was generalized to resolve a **composite** key from a read-back and nothing reached that path, since every composite fixture and every composite example table declares only `ConflictPK`. It is verified non-vacuous — reverting the lookup list to the first PK column alone fails it. **That gap is now closed on MySQL, and closing it also moved the composite read-back from template-only to runtime.** `user_categories` in the mysql example gained a nullable `slot INT` with `UNIQUE (user_id, slot)` — a display position, and a unique that does **not** cover the composite key. One table therefore reaches three things nothing else did: a caller-known **composite** key resolved from a read-back, MySQL's own tuple-`IN` degenerating through `buildExpandedOR` where PostgreSQL and SQLite emit a row constructor, and a **two-column** conflict target (the postgres pin is a single-column key on a single-column target, so it reaches none of them). `TestUpsertMany_CallerKnownCompositeKey_NonCoveringTargetResolvesExistingKey` reports `returned 1 entities, want 2` against the pre-fix template, matching the postgres symptom exactly.

A second MySQL pin came with it: `TestUpsertMany_NonCoveringTarget_IndefiniteConflictValueRefused`. `slot` is nullable, which makes the per-row indefinite-value refusal reachable on a caller-known key for the first time — pre-fix that call wrote the row instead of refusing, so the pin fails with `UpsertMany with an indefinite conflict value succeeded, want a refusal before any write`.

The remaining untested combination is **sqlite** on this shape. Its read-back is byte-identical to PostgreSQL's (both emit a row constructor through the same builder), so it is the lowest-value of the three; left open deliberately rather than by oversight.

**PRD amended at four sites**, all of which carried the strategy-only rule: §9.2's `UpsertMany` row,
§9.5 decision 3 (now two conditions, with the non-covering case stated separately), §9.7's "Batched,
the same lookup is the only mechanism", and §25.1's write-side bound.
`TestUpsertManyTemplate_pkFromInput` pinned the broken behavior and was rewritten to assert both
directions; `TestUpsertManyTemplate_conflictCoversPKTable` pins the generated coverage table.


### FIX-217

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 6, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/{create,update,delete}.go.tmpl` — the
  trailing entity re-fetch every `*Many` mutation issues.
- **Surfaced by:** 27.5 (2026-09-17). `UpsertMany` has the same shape, so the guard had to be
  written for it; probing the siblings showed four of them already carried the bug.

**An empty batch read the whole table and reported it as the rows it had just written.**

The write half was always correct: an empty id set compiles to `WHERE 1 = 0`, so the UPDATE or
DELETE matched nothing. The fault was in the return path. Each `*Many` method re-fetches through
`GetMany` filtered on the keys it touched, every generated key filter guards with `len(...) > 0`
(`comparator/id.go:29`, `_filter.tmpl:50` for composite PKs), and these calls pass `Limit: new(0)`.
With an empty key set the filter contributed **no condition at all**, leaving an unfiltered,
unlimited SELECT whose rows were handed back as the operation's result.

Measured on the `postgres` example before the fix, against a `tags` table holding one row:

| Call | Returned | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateMany(ctx, nil)` | 1 entity | `SELECT "id", "is_deleted", "name" FROM "public"."tags" WHERE is_deleted = $1` |
| `UpdateMany(ctx, nil)` | 1 entity | the same SELECT |
| `RestoreMany(ctx, nil)` | 1 entity | `UPDATE … WHERE 1 = 0`, then the same SELECT |
| `SoftDeleteMany(ctx, nil)` | 0 entities | the same SELECT — 0 only because no row was soft-deleted; latent, not safe |
| `HardDeleteMany(ctx, nil)` | — | `DELETE … WHERE 1 = 0`; returns only an error and has no re-fetch, so it was never affected |

The severity is `tracked` rather than `blocking` because reaching it needs a zero-length batch,
which is a degenerate call. What makes it worth fixing rather than documenting is that the failure
is **silent and scales with the table**: the caller gets a plausible-looking non-empty result, and
on a tenanted or soft-deleted table those rows are still filtered normally, so nothing looks wrong.

**Fix.** A `len(...) == 0` short circuit at the top of the terminal function in all four, returning
an empty slice before any statement runs — the same guard 27.5's `UpsertMany` already carried. It
is keyed on `len`, not on `nil`: a non-nil empty slice reaches the identical path. `HardDeleteMany`
is deliberately left alone.

**Regression pin:** `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/postgres/tests/empty_batch_test.go` — seven
subtests (all five affected methods plus both nil and non-nil-empty spellings) asserting zero
entities *and* zero statements, plus a subtest pinning `HardDeleteMany`'s deliberate asymmetry. The
seeded sentinel row is what makes the test meaningful: the bug returned whatever the table held, so
an empty table would have passed either way.

### FIX-212

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 17, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap.go` (`funcRelationshipStaticFilterExpr`)
- **Surfaced by:** 27.2's `assets` migration (2026-09-17), which moved three edges off `filter:`
  and made the surviving `filter:` edges' generated SQL sit next to the discriminator form in a
  golden diff

**Issue.** **On SQLite, a relationship filter over an edge that declares `filter:` emits SQL naming
a table alias the subquery never defines.** The predicate is qualified at codegen against the
placeholder alias `sqlgenrel` (`RelationshipFilterAliasToken`), and
`funcRelationshipStaticFilterExpr` then splits the qualified string on the literal `"sqlgenrel."`
to splice in the runtime `tgt` variable, whose real value is `tgt0` / `tgt1` depending on nesting
depth.

Each dialect's qualifier spells a rewritten identifier its own way. pg_query and vitess emit
`sqlgenrel.entity_type`, which the split matches. **rqlite/sql emits `"sqlgenrel"."entity_type"` —
quoted** — so the split finds nothing, `len(parts) == 1`, and the function returns the whole string
as a Go literal with the placeholder still in it.

Shipped output, `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/models/asset_gen.go:2171`:

```go
subSQL := "SELECT 1 FROM " + dialect.FormatTable(...) + " " + jn +
    " JOIN " + dialect.FormatTable(...) + " " + tgt + ...
subSQL += " AND (" + "\"sqlgenrel\".\"entity_type\" = 'asset.attachment' AND \"sqlgenrel\".\"name\" LIKE 'link_%'" + ")"
```

The subquery aliases `documents` as `tgt`; nothing is named `sqlgenrel`. SQLite rejects the
statement at execution.

**Confirmed at runtime**, not inferred from the source. Against the shipped `sqlite` example,
filtering on the still-`filter:` edge `PhotoAttachments`:

```go
client.Assets().GetMany(ctx, &models.GetAssetsInput{
    Filter: &models.AssetFilter{
        PhotoAttachments: &models.DocumentFilter{Name: &comparator.String{Eq: new("photo1.jpg")}},
    },
})
// => get assets: query: SQL logic error: no such column: sqlgenrel.entity_type (1)
```

**Reachable shape.** SQLite, plus a relationship filter (`AssetFilter{PhotoAttachments: &DocumentFilter{...}}`
— filtering a parent by a predicate on a child) on any edge carrying `filter:`. Three edges in
the sqlite example are in this state at HEAD — `PhotoAttachments`, `LinkedAttachments` and
`PrimaryOrInvoiceDocuments` (`asset_gen.go:2246`, `:2289`, `:2332`). The loader path is unaffected —
it applies the filter verbatim to a single-table query and never qualifies — so only the `EXISTS`
path is broken, which is why the examples compile and their existing tests pass.

**Why it was not caught.** The example tests exercise relationship *loading* on every dialect but
only exercise relationship *filters* on postgres, where the split matches. The golden tests compare
generated text against a recorded copy of the same generated text, so a wrong alias is recorded as
faithfully as a right one.

**Root cause.** Token substitution by string split assumes the qualifier's output spelling, which is
per-dialect and not a contract. `funcRelationshipStaticFilterExpr`'s own doc comment describes
splitting "on the token" as if there were one spelling of it.

**Second defect, same function, same root cause** (found while adjudicating, 2026-09-17; folded in
rather than logged separately because it is what rules candidate 2 out). **The split also matches
inside string literals, on the two dialects that "work".** A `filter:` whose literal contains the
token has that literal rewritten:

```
in : sqlgenrel.status = 'a' AND sqlgenrel.note = 'sqlgenrel.x'
out: tgt + ".status = 'a' AND " + tgt + ".note = '" + tgt + ".x'"
                                        ↑ the literal value becomes 'tgt0.x'
```

Confirmed by calling `funcRelationshipStaticFilterExpr` directly. Unlike the SQLite defect this
fails *silently* — a valid statement carrying a wrong value — and it contradicts PRD §13.7.1's
"string-literal contents pass through the parser intact".

**Not caused by 27.2, and not fixed by it.** 27.2's `discriminator:` path builds the predicate from
the runtime `tgt` variable directly and never substitutes a token, so it cannot regress this way;
`TestDiscriminator_RelationshipFilterAliasIsRuntimeToken` pins that on sqlite specifically. The
three migrated `assets` edges therefore stopped exhibiting the bug as a side effect, which is what
made it visible in the diff. The `filter:` form still has it.

**Adjudicated** (2026-09-17). Of the three candidates originally listed:

- **Candidate 3 is not achievable.** It assumed some alias spelling escapes quoting. `rqlite/sql`'s
  `Ident.String()` (`ast.go:1506`) double-quotes **unconditionally** — there is no flag and no
  alias name avoids it. Only its assert-the-round-trip half survives, as a guard.
- **Candidate 2 is insufficient.** A tolerant split fixes the SQLite defect and leaves the
  literal-collision defect above untouched, on both dialects where it bites.
- **Candidate 1 is adopted**, in a form that needs no change to the three parser backends.

**Resolution.** `funcRelationshipStaticFilterExpr` cannot be fixed in place: deriving the alias
spelling needs the dialect, which a funcmap function does not receive, and it needs a parse that can
fail — while `guidelines/TEMPLATES.md` §5 requires funcmap functions to be pure, I/O-free and
error-free. The work therefore moves into `relationshipStaticFilter`, which already carries both
(the `PKAutoGenExpr` precedent: a value a funcmap's minimal input cannot compute becomes a context
field). Four parts:

1. **Input guard** — reject a `filter:` whose text contains the token, mirroring the `$` rejection
   three lines above it in the same function. Every `sqlgenrel` in the deparsed output is then
   provably the qualifier's own, which is what makes the substitution total rather than tolerant.
2. **Dialect-derived prefix** — discover the qualifier's spelling of the alias by round-tripping a
   one-column probe through the *same* `QualifyFilterIdentifiers` (`sqlgenrel.c` → `sqlgenrel.`;
   `"sqlgenrel"."c"` → `"sqlgenrel".`), so the splice cannot drift from what the qualifier emits.
3. **Assert** the token is absent from the built expression, failing generation loudly. This is the
   guard that would have caught the original defect instead of shipping it.
4. The template func becomes a joiner over the precomputed expression.

PostgreSQL and MySQL goldens are **byte-unchanged** — their derived prefix equals today's hardcoded
one — so only the three SQLite sites re-golden. PRD §13.7.1 already states the alias "is an internal
codegen detail and is not contractually stable across regenerations", so the emitted
`tgt0."entity_type"` spelling needs no PRD amendment. Verified against SQLite that the alias resolves
when the FROM alias is bare and the column is quoted.

**Related, and already resolved separately: FIX-216.** Probing the three qualifiers to establish
their per-dialect spelling turned up a second dialect disagreement — a `"`-quoted identifier is a
string literal on MySQL, so such a `filter:` silently matches nothing. Different root cause (dialect
semantics, not string splitting) and a different fix (a config-validation guard), so it was logged
and landed on its own; the cross-dialect quoting table it added to PRD §13.7.1 is the reference for
what a `filter:` may safely contain.

**Regression pin.** Render a relationship filter on a `filter:` edge on **all three** dialects and
assert the emitted SQL contains no `sqlgenrel`; add a literal-collision case; and exercise a
`filter:` edge relationship filter at runtime against the shipped sqlite example — the example tests
cover relationship *loading* on every dialect but relationship *filters* only on postgres, which is
the gap that let this ship.

**Resolution notes.** Landed as adjudicated. `relationshipStaticFilter`
(`context_relfilter.go`) now derives the alias spelling from the dialect's own
qualifier instead of assuming it: `qualifiedAliasPrefix` (`filter_qualifier.go`)
round-trips a one-column probe through the same `QualifyFilterIdentifiers` that
produced the predicate and reads the prefix back — `sqlgenrel.` on PostgreSQL and
MySQL, `"sqlgenrel".` on SQLite. `spliceRelationshipFilterAlias` splits on that,
so the splice moves with the parser rather than breaking when it changes.

Three guards close the failure mode rather than narrowing it. A `filter:`
carrying the token is rejected at codegen, mirroring the `$` rejection beside it;
that kills the literal-collision defect (`'sqlgenrel.x'` → `'tgt0.x'`) the
tolerant-split candidate would have left live. It is a substring match, so it
also turns away harmless text — a column named for the token would in fact
survive the splice — which is the trade the `$` guard already makes.

A raw-text check is not sufficient on its own, which the auto-review caught and a
probe confirmed: a predicate can synthesize the token in its *deparsed* form
without spelling it in the config. MySQL folds adjacent string literals
(`note = 'sqlgen' 'rel.x'`) and PostgreSQL decodes escapes
(`note = E'sqlgen\162el.x'`); both deparse to `'sqlgenrel.x'` inside a literal,
and the splice would rewrite the compared value. The post-splice assertion cannot
see it either, because the substitution *consumes* the token and leaves nothing
to find. So the predicate is also qualified against a second, unrelated alias:
real references move to that alias, and anything still spelling the prefix is the
filter's own content. That is the check that makes "every token in the deparsed
output is the qualifier's own" actually true.

The third guard is the post-splice assertion — a surviving token fails generation
outright. That is what would have caught the original defect instead of shipping
it, and it still covers the case the other two cannot anticipate: a qualifier
whose spelling moves out from under the derived prefix.

`funcRelationshipStaticFilterExpr` is gone from the funcmap — deriving the
spelling needs the dialect and an error channel, and `guidelines/TEMPLATES.md` §5
allows a funcmap function neither. Following `PKAutoGenExpr`'s precedent the
value is now the `StaticFilterExpr` context field, and the template emits it
directly.

Goldens moved on SQLite only, exactly as predicted — three lines in
`examples/sqlite/**/asset_gen.go`, PostgreSQL and MySQL byte-unchanged, since
their derived prefix equals the old hardcoded one.

Regression pins, all three parts of the entry's ask: `TestQualifiedAliasPrefix`
and `TestSpliceRelationshipFilterAlias` (gen, internal) pin each dialect's
spelling and the splice against both; `TestRelationshipStaticFilter_NoAliasTokenSurvives`
renders a `filter:` edge on **all three** dialects and asserts no token survives,
with `TestRelationshipStaticFilter_ColumnKeepsDialectSpelling` pinning that the
column keeps its own dialect's quoting; each guard has matching and
non-matching cases, so its reach is pinned in both directions, and
`TestRelationshipStaticFilter_RejectsSynthesizedAliasToken` covers the folded
and escaped shapes on the dialects that produce them. The runtime gap is closed by
`TestRelationshipFilter_StaticFilterEdge{,M2M}` in the sqlite example — verified
non-vacuous by running them against the pre-fix generated code, where both
reproduce the entry's error verbatim: `no such column: sqlgenrel.entity_type (1)`.

`make check` (fmt, lint 0 issues, vet, tests) and `make check-examples` both pass.


### FIX-216

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 13, `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go` (`validateRelationships`), PRD §13.7.1
- **Surfaced by:** adjudicating FIX-212 (2026-09-17) — probing the three `QualifyFilterIdentifiers`
  implementations across quoting shapes to establish how each dialect spells a qualified reference

**Issue.** **A `filter:` that quotes an identifier with `"` silently matches no rows on MySQL.**
Under MySQL's default `sql_mode` a double-quoted token is a *string literal*, not a quoted
identifier, and vitess reproduces that faithfully — which is correct MySQL, and exactly the problem:

```
filter: "\"entity_type\" = 'asset.primary'"
  → vitess → 'entity_type' = 'asset.primary'     two constants, false for every row
```

Confirmed against MySQL 8: `0` rows for the double-quoted form, `1` for the backtick form. It is
**silent** — a string-vs-string comparison raises no error and no warning; only the string-vs-number
shape (`"order" = 1`) raises warning 1292 (`Truncated incorrect DOUBLE value`), which nothing reads.

**What makes it a codegen concern and not just a MySQL footnote.** `ANSI_QUOTES` does not repair it,
and makes the damage *inconsistent across read paths of the same edge* — measured, with the session
mode set:

| read path | how the `filter:` is handled | rows |
|-----------|------------------------------|------|
| o2m / m2m loader | text reaches MySQL verbatim; MySQL resolves the identifier | **1** |
| o2o JOIN `ON`, relationship-filter `EXISTS` | vitess qualified it at *generation* time | **0** |

The qualified paths ship the baked literal in the generated source, so no session setting can reach
them. One `filter:` string would mean two different things on two read paths of one relationship.

**The mirror mistake, for completeness.** A MySQL-style double-quoted *value* on the other two
dialects parses as a column reference and is alias-qualified — `col = "v"` → `<alias>."v"` — failing
at query time as an unknown column. On SQLite it diverges by read path the same way: unqualified,
the double-quoted-string fallback treats `"v"` as a literal and the loader appears to work, while
the qualified paths do not. Loud rather than silent, so documented but not guarded.

**Why it was not caught.** Every `filter:` in the PRD, the fixtures and the examples uses bare
identifiers and single-quoted values — the spelling that means the same thing on all three dialects
— so nothing ever exercised the disagreement. The qualifier tests covered operators, literals and
nesting, but only ever in that one quoting style.

**Resolution.** A double-quoted token in a `filter:` is now a hard validation error **on MySQL
only**, raised in `validateRelationships` where the dialect is known, so it covers every read path
including the loader rather than only the qualified ones. The message names the relationship and
both repairs (backticks for an identifier, single quotes for a value).

`filterHasBareDoubleQuote` tracks single-quoted literals (including `''` doubling and backslash
escapes) and backtick-quoted identifiers, so ordinary MySQL like `note = 'say "hi"'` and
`` `we"ird` = 1 `` is accepted. The guard stays off PostgreSQL and SQLite, where `"x"` is the
standard quoted identifier and the only spelling PostgreSQL accepts for a reserved-word column.

PRD §13.7.1 gains the cross-dialect quoting table, the worked MySQL example, the `ANSI_QUOTES`
asymmetry and the guidance to write bare identifiers with single-quoted values; §13.7.3 gains the
validation row. Each dialect's `filter_qualifier_test.go` pins what its parser actually does with
all four quoting shapes, so a future parser-behaviour change is caught rather than absorbed.


### FIX-215

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 5, `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go` (`ConvertConfig`), `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go`
  (`FromOverride`), `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go` (the `"intermediate"` scan shape)
- **Surfaced by:** chasing FIX-214's nullable-`convert:` note (2026-09-17)

**Issue.** **`overrides.types.<t>.convert` — PRD §4.7's `ConvertConfig`, the scan "Shape 3" — never
worked. It emitted `$value` literally and aborted generation.**

`PostScanExpr` is assigned straight from `Convert.GoExpr` (`context_table.go:2207`, and the two O2O
equivalents) and **nothing anywhere substituted `$value`** — no `strings.Replace`, no funcmap helper.
Confirmed by running the real generator over a minimal schema with a `convert:` override:

```
Generation error: formatting models/models_gen.go: goimports failed for models/models_gen.go:
  models/models_gen.go:181:28: illegal character U+0024 '$' (and 10 more errors)
exit=1
```

Three more ways it was unfinished, each found while confirming the first:

- `ToDBExpr` was carried into the context (`context_table.go:909`) and read by **no template**, so
  the Go→DB half was never wired at all.
- View columns carried no `Convert` field — `context_tenancy.go` documented this as "a pre-existing
  property of the view path" — so `convert:` silently did not apply to views.
- `hasConvert` was registered in the funcmap with **zero** template consumers.

**Why it was not caught.** No example tree uses `convert:`. The ksuid override in the postgres,
mysql and sqlite examples maps `text` → `ksuid.KSUID` with no `convert:` block, relying on KSUID's
own `Scanner`/`Valuer`. Every built-in integration says the same thing in its own comment — "no
ConvertConfig is needed" — so nothing internal ever reached the code path.

**Root cause.** A config surface was specified and wired end-to-end except for the one step that
makes it produce compilable Go, and no test or example exercised it.

**Resolution notes.** Removed, at the user's direction, rather than completed. `ConvertConfig` and
`TypeOverride.Convert` are gone from the config, its JSON schema and `validateConvertConfigs`;
`ConvertMeta` / `GoType.Convert` from `gotype`; `ConvertContext` / `ColumnContext.Convert` and the
`"intermediate"` arm of all three scan-case builders from `gen`; the intermediate declarations and
post-scan blocks from `get`, `stream`, `view/get` and `relationships` templates; and the dead
`hasConvert` helper.

The contract is now stated where the override is declared (PRD §4.7, `docs/configuration.md`, the
`TypeOverride` doc comment and the JSON schema): **an overridden type must cross the driver boundary
on its own** — it implements `sql.Scanner` and `driver.Valuer`, or the driver special-cases it
(`uuid.UUID`, which `database/sql` handles in both directions and pgx routes through `UUIDCodec`).
A type that does neither is wrapped in one of the consumer's own that does, and the override names
the wrapper. PRD's "three scan shapes" is now two, direct and wrapped, throughout.

A config still carrying the block fails closed at parse time rather than being ignored — verified
end-to-end: `Error: parsing config: yaml: unmarshal errors: line 15: field convert not found in type
config.TypeOverride`, exit 2, nothing emitted. Pinned by
`TestSchemaV1_rejectsKnownMistakes/removed_convert_block_on_a_type_override`.

Golden churn is one comment line per generated scan function ("all three scan target shapes" → "both
scan target shapes"), 258 replacements across 78 files and no structural change — the expected
result of a feature no example could reach.

### FIX-213

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 17 / earlier, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/relationships.go.tmpl` +
  `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** a question during 27.2 about how a *complex* `filter:` behaves (2026-09-17)

**Issue.** **A relationship `filter:` containing a top-level `OR` is spliced without parentheses, so
the parent correlation drops out of the predicate and the loader returns other parents' rows.**

The filter is appended with `AND`, and SQL binds `AND` tighter than `OR`:

```sql
-- filter: "kind = 'x' OR name = 'leak'"

-- o2m / m2m loader (buildWhere joins conditions with strings.Join(parts, " AND "))
WHERE entity_id IN ($1) AND kind = 'x' OR name = 'leak'
--    └───────── binds as one AND group ─────────┘   OR   (uncorrelated)

-- o2o JOIN ON (relationships.go.tmpl: On: fmt.Sprintf(...) + " AND " + filter)
ON p.entity_id = a.id AND p.entity_type = 'a' OR p.name = 'b'
```

**Confirmed at runtime**, against SQLite, loading parent 1's children:

```
returned child id=10 owned by parent pid=1
returned child id=11 owned by parent pid=2   <- leaked
```

Severity is **blocking** rather than tracked because the failure is silent cross-parent row
disclosure on a read path — the loader hands a caller rows belonging to an entity they did not ask
for, with no error. On a tenanted schema that is a tenant-boundary crossing whenever the filter's
`OR` arm matches a row in another tenant.

**Which paths are affected.**

| Path | Wraps the filter? | Status |
|---|---|---|
| o2m / m2m loader (`get.go.tmpl`) | No — `strings.Join(parts, " AND ")` in `sql/builder.go:488` | **Affected** |
| o2o JOIN `ON` (`relationships.go.tmpl:7`) | No — `+ " AND " + filter` | **Affected** |
| `comparator.X.Custom` (public runtime API) | No — same `buildWhere` AND-join | **Affected** — see finding 2 |
| Relationship-filter `EXISTS` (`shared/_filter.tmpl:174`) | Yes — `" AND (" + ... + ")"` | Safe |

That the `EXISTS` path already parenthesises is decent evidence the other three are an oversight
rather than a decision.

**Why it was not caught.** Every `filter:` in the PRD, in every fixture, and in every example is an
`AND` of predicates, which is associative and needs no parentheses. Nothing in the repo exercises a
top-level `OR`. The o2o codegen qualifier parses the filter but only rewrites identifiers; it does
not reassociate, and it reports no diagnostic.

**Not reachable through `discriminator:`.** The structured form's predicate shape is fixed at
`column = literal`: `column` is a validated identifier and `value` is either bound as a parameter or
rendered through `sqlStringLiteral`, which doubles embedded quotes. Probed — `asset.primary' OR 1=1 --`
renders as the single literal `'asset.primary'' OR 1=1 --'`. Only `filter:`, which is raw SQL by
§4.8's contract, can express a top-level boolean operator.

**Age.** Present since 2026-05-13 (`d8f3b74` for the o2o splice, `88e45b9` for the loader), so it
predates phase 27 by four months.

**Verification (2026-09-17).** Reproduced against real SQLite, and the originally proposed
resolution — "wrap the filter at both emission sites" — was found **incorrect**. Three findings:

1. **Wrapping the loader's `sql.Raw` clause emits invalid SQL.** On the o2o-join branch of the
   target's own `GetMany` (`get.go.tmpl:260`, `:298`) every condition passes through
   `sql.PrefixConditions`, and `prefixCondition` takes its `Column == ""` branch for a `Raw`
   condition — `c.Clause = alias + "." + c.Clause` (`sql/condition.go:216-219`). Measured:
   `... AND a.(entity_type = 'asset.attachment' AND name LIKE 'photo_%')`. Reachable whenever a
   `filter:` edge's target table carries an o2o relationship the caller requests; not reachable in
   the shipped examples, since `documents` declares no o2o edge. The same branch also aliases only
   the *first* identifier of a multi-column raw clause, which is a latent ambiguity of its own.
2. **The defect is not confined to `filter:`.** `comparator.X.Custom []sql.Condition` takes
   arbitrary `sql.Raw` from callers and lands in the same flat AND-join. Measured:
   `comparator.String{Eq: "widget", Custom: []sql.Condition{sql.Raw("price > $ OR title LIKE $", …)}}`
   renders `WHERE title = ? AND price > ? OR title LIKE ? AND deleted_at IS NULL` — the caller's own
   `Eq` **and** the soft-delete default both drop out. No config needed; the shipped example tests
   already exercise `Custom` this way (`sqlite/tests/filter_test.go:338`).
3. **Authors cannot parenthesise their way out on o2o.** pg_query and vitess strip the author's own
   outer parens during qualification (`(a = 'x' OR b = 'y')` → `d.a = 'x' OR d.b = 'y'`); only
   rqlite/sql preserves them. So there is no config-level workaround and none can be documented.

The blast radius also runs wider than the correlation predicate: because the soft-delete and tenancy
predicates sit in the same AND chain, the `OR` arm defeats those too. On the o2o path the `ON`
splice fans the LEFT JOIN out to several target rows per parent, duplicating the parent row in a
result set the o2o scan assumes is one-row-per-parent.

**Resolution (adjudicated 2026-09-17).** Two layers, because there are two mechanisms:

1. **`sql/` (runtime).** A `Raw` condition must render as a single AND-able term. `sql.Raw` sets an
   unexported marker; `expandCondition` adds the parentheses **at render time, after**
   `PrefixConditions` has done its alias surgery — that ordering is what avoids finding 1, since the
   prefixer still sees the unwrapped clause and behaves exactly as it does today. This one change
   covers the o2m loader, the m2m loader and `comparator.X.Custom`. Hand-built
   `sql.Condition{Clause: …}` literals bypass the marker by design; the only one in the templates
   (`shared/_filter.tmpl:54`) is `col = $` and is atomic.
2. **`relationships.go.tmpl:7` (codegen).** The o2o `ON` clause is string concatenation, not a
   `Condition`, so it takes `+ " AND (" + filter + ")"` directly — the spelling
   `shared/_filter.tmpl:174` already uses.

Rejected, each with a measured reason: wrapping inside `Raw()` at construction (breaks
`PrefixConditions`, finding 1); wrapping at the three codegen emission sites only (same breakage,
and leaves `Custom` exposed, finding 2); rejecting a top-level `OR` at config validation (removes
legitimate predicates, does not reach `Custom`, and §13.7.4 says loader filters are not parsed at
codegen).

Golden churn: the three `filter:` edges in each of the four example trees, plus the `Custom`
assertions. Regenerate with `make update-golden` and `make update-golden-e2e`.

**PRD delta.** §13.7.1 documents the current, buggy splice in two places and must be amended with
the fix: the o2o sentence giving the `ON` output as `AND <alias>.entity_type = … AND <alias>.name
LIKE …`, and the o2m/m2m sentence saying the loaders apply the value "**verbatim** as an `AND` … via
`sql.Raw(...)`". The `Condition`-renders-as-one-term invariant belongs alongside `Custom`'s contract.

**Regression pin.** Four, the first three failing-first:

- `sql/`: a `Raw` condition carrying a top-level `OR`, AND-joined with others, renders parenthesised.
- `sql/`: `PrefixConditions` + a `Raw` condition + an o2o join renders valid SQL (no `alias.(`).
- `comparator/`: a `Custom` raw `OR` does not defeat the sibling terms.
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/`: an o2m `filter:` carrying a top-level `OR`, against a
  schema with two parents, returns only the requested parent's children — plus the o2o equivalent.
  SQLite only (in-memory, no Docker); the defect is SQL semantics and dialect-independent, and the
  emitted-text assertions in `cmd/sqlgen/gen` still cover all three dialects.

**Resolution notes.** Landed as adjudicated, in two layers. Runtime: `sql.Raw` now sets the new
`Condition.Raw` marker (`sql/dialect.go`, `sql/condition.go`) and `expandCondition`
(`sql/builder.go`) parenthesises a marked clause *after* `PrefixConditions` has qualified it, so the
o2m / m2m loaders and every caller-supplied `comparator.X.Custom` condition render as one AND-able
term without breaking the O2O-join prefixing. Codegen: `relationships.go.tmpl` wraps the O2O JOIN
`ON` predicate, which is assembled as a string and so cannot inherit the runtime's wrap. PRD §13.7.1
amended — the o2o example, the "verbatim" sentence, and a new paragraph stating the one-conjunct
invariant and why the wrap is applied at render time. `comparator`'s package doc now states the
contract for `Custom`.

Pins: `sql.TestBuildSelect_RawConditionParenthesised` (three dialects, the fk + soft-delete + Raw-OR
shape) and `sql.TestBuildSelectJoin_RawConditionSurvivesPrefixing` (no `alias.(`);
`comparator.TestCustom_CompoundConditionDoesNotEscapeItsTerm`;
`gen.TestRelationships_O2OJoinFilterParenthesised` (three dialects); and end-to-end in the sqlite
example, `TestRelationshipFilterPrecedence_O2OStaysCorrelated`, verified fail-first (2 rows returned
for one PK before the fix).

**Correction to this entry's own claim.** The O2M / M2M loader leak is *not* observable through the
generated client. The loader re-keys every child on its FK (`byFK[fmt.Sprint(parent.ID)]`), so a row
belonging to a parent outside the result set is dropped there, and for a row whose FK *is* in the
set `fk IN P AND (L OR R)` and `(fk IN P AND L) OR R` agree exactly. The difference becomes visible
only once the target also carries a soft-delete or tenant predicate, so that a row satisfying the
right arm can be one the other AND terms excluded; `documents` carries neither, which is why
`TestRelationshipFilterPrecedence_O2MStaysCorrelated` passes both before and after and is documented
as pinning the FK re-keying rather than the predicate. The predicate is pinned at the `sql/` layer
instead. The runtime observation quoted at the top of this entry was raw SQL, not a client read.
The O2O half needs no such qualification: it is a true cross-parent disclosure plus row fan-out.

### FIX-214

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 17 / earlier, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/relationships.go.tmpl`
  (`scan<Table>WithOneToOneJoins`) + `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go` (`buildO2OScanCases`)
- **Surfaced by:** writing FIX-213's O2O regression pin (2026-09-17), whose first fixture was the
  first thing in any example tree to load an O2O edge for a parent with no matching row

**Issue.** **Reading an O2O relationship for a parent that has no matching target row fails the
whole query.** The joined read selects the target's columns alongside the parent's and tells a real
row from a LEFT JOIN miss *after* scanning, by testing the target's PK against its zero value. On a
miss the driver returns NULL for every one of the target's columns, and a `NOT NULL` column resolves
to a Go type that refuses NULL — so the scan errored before the detection could run.

**Confirmed at runtime on both drivers**, against the shipped examples and the untouched
`PrimaryActiveDocument` edge:

```
sqlite / database/sql : scan asset with joins: stdlib scan: sql: Scan error on column index 2,
                        name "p.id": converting NULL to int64 is unsupported
postgres / pgx        : scan asset with joins: pgx scan: can't scan into dest[2] (col: p.id):
                        cannot scan NULL into *[16]byte
```

Every dialect and every O2O edge, not one shape: the target's PK is `NOT NULL` by definition, so the
first column of the miss is always fatal. `filter:` and `discriminator:` edges are affected
identically — the predicate plays no part.

**Why it was not caught.** Every O2O assertion in every example tree seeds a parent that *has* its
target row. `TestRequiredColumns_O2OWithoutChildPK` is the closest existing coverage and is about a
hit whose PK was not selected, not a miss. Nothing exercised the branch the NULL detection exists to
serve, so the detection itself was never reached.

**Root cause.** `buildO2OScanCases` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`) binds each target column
straight at its field — `sc.ScanExpr = fmt.Sprintf("&%s.%s", varName, col.FieldName)` — which is
correct for the parent's columns and wrong for a target's, because only the target's can be NULL
without the schema saying so. The template's own comment describes detecting the miss "via NULL PK
detection", which cannot work when the destination rejects the NULL first.

**Suggested fix.** Wrap the target's non-nullable scan destinations so a NULL reads as the zero
value and the existing detection decides. Nullable columns already resolve to a type that takes
NULL, and `pq.Array` reads a NULL array as a nil slice, so neither needs wrapping.

**References.** PRD §13.4 (O2O JOIN loading), §13.7.1; FIX-185 (`required_columns`, the O2O target
PK is selected whether or not the caller asked for it); FIX-213, which shares the emission site but
not the root cause.

**Resolution notes.** Fixed in the same change as FIX-213 at the user's direction, though the root
cause is unrelated. New `database.NullScan` (`database/nullscan.go`) wraps a scan destination so a
NULL reads as the zero value, delegating a non-NULL value to `database/sql.Null[T]` so a `T` whose
pointer implements `sql.Scanner` — a UUID or decimal type — is still scanned through it.
`buildO2OScanCases` wraps every non-nullable target destination in it (`nullSafeO2OScanExpr`);
nullable columns and `pq.Array` are left alone, since both already take NULL.

**Slices are excluded on every driver, not just the `pq.Array` arm.** The first cut wrapped by
`!col.Nullable` alone, which under pgx caught array columns that the stdlib arm had been skipping.
Wrapping makes the destination a `sql.Scanner`, which drops pgx off its native array codec onto
`DecodeDatabaseSQLValue` and hands the wire bytes to `convertAssign`. Measured against a real
container, on an ordinary non-NULL array — not on a miss:

```
unwrapped         SELECT ARRAY['a','b']::text[]  → [a b]
database.NullScan SELECT ARRAY['a','b']::text[]  → pgx scan: null scan: unsupported Scan,
                                                   storing driver.Value type []uint8 into type *[]string
unwrapped         SELECT NULL::text[]            → []
```

The last line is the premise for skipping them: a slice reads a NULL array as nil unaided. Caught by
this change's auto-review; it was invisible in the examples because every array column there is
nullable.

Pins: `database.TestNullScan` (NULL to zero, value conversion, Scanner delegation, and that a real
conversion error still surfaces); `gen.TestRelationships_O2OTargetScanAbsorbsJoinMiss`, built from a
real table context rather than the hand-assembled `ScanCases` the sibling fixtures carry — those
supply `ScanExpr` themselves and never reach `buildO2OScanCases` — asserting both halves, that NOT
NULL scalars are wrapped and that nullable and slice destinations are not; and end-to-end
`TestO2OJoinMiss_ReadsAsNil` in **both** the sqlite and postgres examples. The postgres arm is the
one that matters most, since the wrap changes how pgx *resolves the scan plan* rather than only how
it handles NULL, so its hit case asserts a jsonb and an `int4[]` still read back intact. Verified
fail-first on both drivers.

**The `convert:` gap this entry once carried is gone with the feature.** The wrap predicate reads
`col.Nullable`, which was wrong for a `convert:` column whose intermediate is `Convert.DBType` —
never nullable-ized by `gotype.FromOverride`. `convert:` has since been removed outright (it never
substituted `$value`, so it aborted generation), taking the intermediate scan shape with it. The
predicate now sees only real field destinations and is exactly right.

### FIX-209

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 23, `cmd/sqlgen/cli/lint.go`
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-199's auto-review (2026-09-16), which found that resolving the tenant
  exclusion widened a pre-existing divergence by one shape

**Issue.** **`sqlgen lint`'s "invalid operation for table" rule re-derives increment eligibility
from the raw parser table, so it misses the `OpIncrement` hooks it exists to catch.** The rule
(PRD §23.7) warns when a hook filters on an operation the table cannot produce. Its increment arm
reads `tableInfo.HasIncrement` (`lint.go:597`), fed by `hasNumericNonPKColumns` (`lint.go:227`):

```go
for _, col := range t.Columns {
    if col.PrimaryKey { continue }
    if isNumericSQLType(strings.ToLower(col.Type)) { return true }
}
```

Primary keys are the only exclusion. The generator's eligibility — `isIncrementEligible`
(`gen/context_table.go`), documented as "the single decision point" — excludes three more things:
**foreign keys**, **columns whose SQL type is classifiable and non-arithmetic** (FIX-160), and, as
of FIX-199, **the tenant column**.

The predicate therefore over-approximates, so the failure is a **missed** warning, never a false
one. A table whose only numeric non-PK columns are FKs and/or the tenant column generates no
`Increment` method and no `<T>IncrementColumn` enum at all — but the linter believes it does and
stays silent on an `OpIncrement` hook that can never fire. That is precisely the case the rule was
written for, so the rule is under-powered exactly where it matters and silent about it.

**Reachable shape.** A junction or join table whose non-PK columns are all integer FKs; a tenanted
table whose only arithmetic column is the tenant column; a `text` column an override retyped to
`decimal.Decimal` (FIX-160's shape — eligible by Go type, excluded by SQL type). None of these is
exotic.

**Root cause.** `buildTypeRegistry` (`lint.go:152`) walks `schema.Tables` and derives each fact
itself, even though it is already deep in the generator's resolution vocabulary — it calls
`gen.ResolveTableConfig`, `gen.StructNameFor`, `gen.StructNamePlural`, `gen.TableConstantName` and
`config.ResolveTableOperations` in the same loop. Increment eligibility is the one fact it
re-derives instead of reading, which makes `isNumericSQLType` a fourth definition of a predicate
the codebase deliberately keeps single (NW-D1 / FIX-153 / FIX-160). The tenant blindness is only
the newest of the three gaps, not the origin of the class.

Note the PRD phrases the rule the same loose way — §23.7 row 2 says "`OpIncrement` for a table with
no **numeric** columns" — so the spec sentence matches the linter rather than the generator. The
wording wants tightening to "no incrementable columns" alongside the code.

**Suggested fix.**
- Read the fact instead of re-deriving it: `len(tc.IncrementColumns) > 0` off a built
  `gen.TableContext` is exact, and picks up FK, SQL-type and tenant exclusions at once with no
  per-rule knowledge.
- **The cost is structural, which is why this is filed rather than folded into FIX-199.** Getting a
  built context means routing the registry through `gen.BuildTableContextsFromSchema`, which does
  materially more work than the current walk **and can return an error** — `buildTypeRegistry`
  today has no failure mode for context-build problems, and `sqlgen lint` should not start failing
  on a schema that `sqlgen generate` would also reject, since the linter's job is to run against
  consumer code that already generated. Decide deliberately whether lint builds contexts, or whether
  `gen` exports a narrower eligibility helper the linter can call on a `parser.Table` + config.
- Delete `hasNumericNonPKColumns` and `isNumericSQLType` from `lint.go` once the fact has one
  source; leaving them is what lets the next divergence happen quietly.
- PRD §23.7 rule-2 wording: "no numeric columns" → "no incrementable columns", cross-referenced
  to §8.2.
- Regression test: a hook registered for `OpIncrement` on a table whose only numeric non-PK column
  is an integer FK (and a second case: the tenant column) must produce the warning. Confirm
  failing-first — today it produces nothing.

**References.**
- PRD §23.7 (the `sqlgen lint` rule set; row 2 is the rule, and carries the loose wording).
- PRD §8.2 — the eligibility rules the linter should be agreeing with.
- `cmd/sqlgen/cli/lint.go:227` (`hasNumericNonPKColumns`), `:240` (`isNumericSQLType`), `:182`
  (registry population), `:597`
  (the `OpIncrement` arm).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go` — `isIncrementEligible`, the single decision point.
- **FIX-160** — established the single-predicate rule and added the arithmetic-SQL-type exclusion
  this linter never learned about.
- **FIX-199** — added the tenant exclusion; its auto-review surfaced this entry. FIX-199 widened
  the divergence by one shape but did not create it.
- **NW-D1** / **FIX-153** — the "one fact, two derivations" class this belongs to.

**Resolution notes.** `buildTypeRegistry` (`cmd/sqlgen/cli/lint.go:151`) now walks
`gen.BuildTableContextsFromSchema` instead of `schema.Tables`, and every fact the rules test is
read off the built `gen.TableContext`: `HasIncrement` from `len(tc.IncrementColumns) > 0`,
`HasSoftDelete` from `tc.SoftDelete != nil`, the names from `tc.StructName` /
`tc.TableNameConstant`, and `Ops` from `tc.Operations` (`gen.ResolvedOperations`, replacing
`config.Operations`). `hasNumericNonPKColumns`, `isNumericSQLType`, `opsFlags`, `opGroupName` and
lint's private `softDeleteColumnNames` are deleted.

**The divergence was wider than filed — four live shapes, not three.** Measured against the
tree's own fixtures, 7 of the 12 examples in `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/` contain at least one
table the old predicate called incrementable and the generator does not:

| Shape | Example | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Integer FK | `tenancy.posts`, `tenancy.articles`, `tenancy.user_profiles`, `postgres.profiles` | `isIncrementEligible` excludes `FKReference != nil` |
| **Numeric array** | `postgres.profiles.scores` (`integer[]`), `graphql.filter_probes.weights` (`double precision[]`) | `strings.Contains(sqlType, "int")` matches `integer[]`; Go type `[]int32` is not incrementable |
| **Config-declared FK** | `mysql.documents.entity_id` | FK minted by `applyConfigDeclaredFKs` from a `relationships:` entry, not by a `REFERENCES` clause |
| Tenant column | (no in-tree fixture; covered by regression test) | FIX-199's exclusion |

The two bolded rows are not in the filed entry. They matter for the choice of fix: the array case
is a plain substring-matching bug independent of the three listed exclusions, and the
config-declared FK case is invisible to anything reading a raw `parser.Table`.

**The entry's second option was rejected on that evidence.** A "narrower eligibility helper `gen`
exports for a `parser.Table` + config" cannot work: `isIncrementEligible` needs the resolved Go
type (dialect + `overrides.types` + `use_pointers` + `column_map`), `BaseSQLType` with domains
followed, the FK set *after* `applyConfigDeclaredFKs` — which mutates the schema during
`BuildTableContexts` — and `ColumnContext.Tenant`, which only exists after
`attachTenancyToTables` re-runs `buildIncrementColumns`. Any such helper would have been a fifth
derivation of the predicate NW-D1 exists to keep single. `gen.BuildTableContextsFromSchema` had
no non-test caller before this and needed no new API surface.

**The cost objection did not survive measurement.** On the largest example (postgres, 18 tables,
M3): `buildTypeRegistry` 152 µs → `BuildTableContextsFromSchema` 857 µs, against the 1.46 ms
`parseSchema` already spends on the same path. +0.7 ms absolute, under half of what lint already
pays to parse the SQL.

**A second divergence in the same registry was folded in — a false positive, and worse than the
missed warning that surfaced this entry.** Rule 3 read the raw `config.Operations` toggles, but
`toResolvedOperations` forces `Get` / `GetMany` / `Count` on whatever the config says (PRD §9.8)
and forces `SoftDelete` / `Restore` off when the table has no soft-delete column. `operations:
{preset: all, get: false}` passes `ValidatePreParse` with no error, and lint then reported a hook
on `OpGet` as dead while the generated client has `Get` and the hook fires normally. Reading
`tc.Operations` fixes it. The rewrite also picks up `OpStream`, which `opGroupName` never mapped —
`stream: false` could not be reported before.

**The larger defect this exposed: `sqlgen lint` gave a false all-clear on schemas that cannot
generate.** A `column_map` collision (PRD §8.5) makes `generate` exit 1 and `validate` exit 2;
`lint` exited **0 with zero bytes of output** — a clean bill of health for a config that produces
no code, and therefore for generated code that is necessarily stale. Building contexts gives lint
the generation-phase error surface it was missing, so it now exits 1 with the same message. This
is the same gap **FIX-158** closed on `sqlgen validate`; `lint` was the last command still on the
pre-FIX-158 footing, and that alignment is the more valuable half of this change.

**Registry membership narrowed deliberately.** `BuildTableContexts` skips tables matching
`exclude_tables` and tables with no resolved PK (PRD §9.4b), so those no longer appear in
`reg.byConstant` and hooks naming them produce no findings. Neither emits a client or a
`Table<Name>` constant, so the old entries described types that do not exist. Decided with the
user rather than assumed.

**Also in this change.** `gen.ResolveTableConfig` → `resolveTableConfig` and `gen.StructNameFor` →
`structNameFor` (both lost their only caller outside `gen`; neither has a `package gen_test`
caller). `TableConstantName` and `StructNamePlural` stay exported — the former has a `gen_test`
caller, the latter is still used by `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go` and by lint. Three doc
comments that claimed "Exported for `sqlgen lint`" were corrected. PRD §23.7 rule 2 now reads "no
**incrementable** columns" cross-referenced to §8.2, and §23.7's "How it works" documents the two
behavioral consequences above.

**Verification.** Preflight clean — `gofumpt 0.12.0`, `golangci-lint 2.13.2`, `go 1.27.1`, all
matching `.tool-versions` with no drift. `make check` exit 0: fmt clean, `0 issues.` lint on all
8 modules, unit tests green under `-race`. `make check-examples` exit 0 against real PostgreSQL,
MySQL and SQLite, with **no golden drift** — the `gen/` edits are pure renames, so
`make update-golden` / `make update-golden-e2e` were not needed and `TestE2EGoldenFiles` passes
unchanged. Failing-first confirmed in a detached worktree at `ca338a0`: all four increment shapes
reported `registry HasIncrement=true, generator emits 0 increment columns`, and the end-to-end
hook case produced **0 issues** — exactly the "today it produces nothing" the entry predicted.
**Auto-review caught one regression this change introduced, now fixed.** Reading
`gen.ResolvedOperations` made rules 2 and 3 overlap: `toResolvedOperations` force-clears
`SoftDelete` / `Restore` when the table has no soft-delete column, which is a table *shape*, not
an `operations` setting. A hook on `OpSoftDelete` for such a table therefore drew rule 2's correct
