warning *and* a rule 3 info blaming a config that excluded nothing. Rule 2 now records the ops it
accounted for and rule 3 skips them, so exactly one issue is reported and it carries the
structural reason. Pinned by `TestLint_shapeReasonWinsOverOperationsReason`. Two documentation
corrections from the same review were applied inline: the `opResolvedFlag` comment wrongly claimed
every `*Many` / `*Where` variant shares its base toggle (true for soft-delete, restore and
hard-delete; `create_many`, `update_many` and `update_where` are each their own), and PRD §8.2's
lead-in sentence still said only "PK columns and non-numeric columns are excluded" — the loose
wording a reader now hits first, since §23.7 cross-references §8.2 for the definition. The review
also confirmed `opResolvedFlag` covers all 16 `MutationOp` and all 7 `QueryOp` constants in
`hook/hook.go`, with `OpRefresh` the sole deliberate fall-through to enabled.

**A second, more severe blindness in the same function was fixed inline.** Auto-review flagged
`tableInfo.SQLName` as the bare table name; confirmed as a live false negative in rule 1 — the
*only* rule at severity `error`, and so the only one the default `--fail-on error` gates CI on.
The SQL name is not an identity: `public.users` and `audit.users` are both `"users"`, so
`ownerInfo.SQLName != tableInfo.SQLName` was false for every cross-schema pair and the rule
reported nothing. Probed directly: `CreatePublicUserInput` and `*PublicUser` handed to
`TableAuditUsers` — the precise defect the rule exists to catch — produced **0 issues**; it now
produces the 2 expected errors, each naming both disambiguated constants. The comparison moved to
`ConstantName`, which is the correct key because it is the Go identifier the entity claims at
package scope and §8.5 rejects two entities claiming the same one — a config that could collide
here fails the context build before the registry exists, which is itself a guarantee this change
created. Pinned by `TestLint_crossSchemaTypeMismatch` (confirmed failing-first: reverting the one
line to `SQLName` returns it to 0 findings) and `TestLint_sameSchemaTypeMatchIsSilent` for the
negative direction. Pre-existing and independent of the increment bug, folded in rather than filed
because it is one line in the function this entry rewrites.

*Not* changed: rules 2 and 3 still print the bare `table %q` in their messages, which stays
ambiguous when two schemas share a table name. That is cosmetic, affects no verdict, and
qualifying it would churn the PRD §23.7 output example and existing assertions.

**One fixture defect found while verifying, unrelated to the reported bug but exposed by it.**
`newTestRegistry` builds a `config.RootConfig` directly rather than through `config.LoadConfig`,
so it carried neither the dialect nor the `soft_delete_columns` default. Under the old raw-schema
walk that was invisible; reading contexts made it matter, and `products` — the one fixture table
carrying both features — silently reported `HasSoftDelete=false` and `HasIncrement=false`. Both
defaults are now spelled out in the fixture with a comment saying why, and
`TestNewTestRegistry_FixtureFacts` pins all three tables' facts so the fixture cannot degenerate
again unnoticed.

Regression tests added to `cmd/sqlgen/cli/lint_test.go`:
`TestBuildTypeRegistry_IncrementMatchesGenerator` (table-driven over all four shapes plus a
positive control, asserting the registry against the generator's own `IncrementColumns` rather
than a second hand-maintained expectation), `TestLint_incrementHookOnFKOnlyTable` (end-to-end
warning), `TestOpEnabledForTable_ReadsResolvedOperations` (the Rule 3 false positive), `TestBuildTypeRegistry_ReportsGenerationErrors` (the false all-clear),
`TestLint_shapeReasonWinsOverOperationsReason` (rule 2 / rule 3 attribution),
`TestNewTestRegistry_FixtureFacts` (fixture-degeneration guard), and
`TestLint_crossSchemaTypeMismatch` / `TestLint_sameSchemaTypeMatchIsSilent` (rule 1 identity).

### FIX-208

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 12, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/cache.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** nested-mutations events-and-cache analysis (2026-09-11) — recorded as **EQ1** /
  **A14** in `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS_EXAMPLES.md` §7.3

**Issue.** **The non-tenanted `*Where` cache-invalidation arm evicts the target table's entire
namespace, while the tenanted arm beside it evicts precisely.** In `dispatchMutation`'s op switch,
the `OpUpdateWhere, OpSoftDeleteWhere, OpHardDeleteWhere, OpRestoreWhere` arm branches on table
(`cache_gen.go:5317-5336`). Tenanted tables call `invalidateAffectedTenanted(ctx, table,
affectedTenants, affected)` — row-by-row, using the PKs and tenants the mutation already captured.
Everything else falls through to `BuildTablePattern` + `invalidatePattern`, which drops **every
cached row of the table**, regardless of how many rows the statement touched.

The wipe is deliberate in origin, not an oversight: `BuildTablePattern` omits `fingerprint:` and
`pk:` precisely so it also collects orphaned prior-generation entries (`cache/key.go:56-62`). The
question is whether that orphan-collection property is worth paying for on every `*Where` call on
every non-tenanted table, now that the tenanted half of the same switch demonstrates the precise
path is available and already has the data it needs.

**Why it is being filed now.** Phase 27 makes it load-bearing rather than merely wasteful: O2M
`connect` and `disconnect` both compile to `UpdateWhere` (`docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` §4.3), so
linking a single child would evict the whole target table's cache. M2M `disconnect` is unaffected —
it routes through `HardDeleteMany`, which invalidates by PK. Filing it separately because **it is
not a nested-mutations special case**: it is true at HEAD for every existing `UpdateWhere` caller,
and every one of them benefits from the repair.

**Root cause.** `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/cache.go.tmpl:979` emits the pattern wipe as the
non-tenanted fallback. The tenanted arms gained their precise path in Phase 13 (T7, PRD §29.5)
when per-row tenants started being captured on the `MutationContext`; the shared arm was left as
it was, so the imprecise branch is now the odd one out rather than the norm.

**Decision — (a), settled against measurement 2026-09-16.** **EQ1** is resolved: make the shared
arm precise. The three candidates were weighed by probing both sides on a real
`redis:7-alpine` testcontainer and the otter memory backend, not by argument.

*What the wipe costs.* `InvalidatePattern` is `SCAN MATCH` over the **whole keyspace**
(`cache/redis/redis.go:162-180`) — cost scales with keys that have nothing to do with sqlgen, and
the memory backend does the same full walk (`cache/memory/memory.go:167-187`). Evicting the one
row an O2M `connect` touched:

| keyspace | precise (1 key) | pattern wipe | collateral evicted |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 k | 369 µs | 3.75 ms | 1,000 |
| 20 k | 260 µs | 30.4 ms | 10,000 |
| 120 k (shared Redis) | 217 µs | 126 ms | 10,000 |
| 300 k (shared Redis) | 256 µs | 407 ms | 50,000 |

The same 10 k matching keys cost 30 ms in a dedicated Redis and 126 ms once 100 k unrelated
application keys share the DB — the penalty is the consumer's keyspace, which sqlgen does not
control and which only grows. Memory backend: 582×–19,832× over the same range. **There is no
crossover.** Even the worst case for precision — a `*Where` touching the entire table — is faster
precise (250 k rows: 178 ms single `DEL` vs 602 ms `SCAN` + batched `DEL`), so the wipe is never
the better shape at any row count.

*What the orphans cost.* Measured ~190 B/entry, so ~1.85 MiB for a 10 k-row table, decaying to
zero over TTL. Orphans carry the same TTL as live entries (verified: 1h default per PRD §27.2, and
they do expire), and are unreachable by any live read at the current fingerprint. **The sweep was
never a property anything could rely on:** it fires only if a `*Where` happens to be called, so it
is already absent for tenanted tables (T7), absent when `update_where` is disabled per-table
(`config.go:419`), and absent for any table that never sees `*Where` traffic. `CACHE.md` §20A
already names the real mechanisms — "cleaned up by backend LRU/TTL, or by a one-shot
`Cache.InvalidateTable(...)`". Giving up the incidental sweep forfeits nothing the design promised.

**Two findings the original entry did not record, both measured.**
1. **The wipe fires where it cannot possibly help.** A `*Where` matching **zero rows** still wipes
   the table, and a `*Where` on a table with `cache.enabled: false` still issues a full-keyspace
   `SCAN` — so PRD §27.7's own junction remedy ("opt out with `tables.<junction>.cache.enabled:
   false`") does not actually stop the scan it is offered to stop.
2. **A naive (a) would regress commits, because the guard is already missing on `*Many`.**
   `InvalidateMany` errors on non-cached tables (generated `default:` arm), and `fireCallbacksSync`
   returns callback errors straight out of `Commit` (`database/transaction.go:333`, `:469-480`).
   Measured on shipped code: `WithTx(UpdateMany on audit_logs, CallbackSync)` returns
   `cache: unknown or non-cached table "audit_logs"` **after the write committed** — a live
   violation of PRD §27.9 ("a committed write is never failed by cache bookkeeping").

**Scope of the fix.**
- **(a1)** `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/cache.go.tmpl:962-980` — the `*Where` arm becomes
  `if len(affected) == 0 { return nil }` → the existing tenanted switch unchanged →
  `return c.InvalidateMany(ctx, table, affected)`, the exact shape the `OpUpdate…`/`*Many` arm
  above it already uses. The tenanted arms' now-redundant per-case `len(affected)` checks collapse
  into the single leading guard.
- **(a2)** A `cacheSchemaFor(table)` guard on **both** the new `*Where` arm and the existing
  `*Many` arm — mandatory on the former (else finding 2 extends to `*Where`), and it retires the
  shipped §27.9 violation on the latter rather than mirroring it. Also removes the pointless
  full-keyspace `SCAN` for cache-disabled tables and makes §27.7's junction opt-out real.
- **(a3)** PRD amendment in the same change, the way 13.10 amended §29.7: §27.7's behavior-table
  row for the four `*Where` ops, the `*Where` clause of §27.5's "Pattern invalidation is
  fingerprint-agnostic" paragraph, and §29.5's `BuildTablePattern` bullet (already stale for
  tenanted tables since T7). Echoes to repoint: `CACHE.md` §9.3 `MutationHook()` table,
  `IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md` §14.3 ("pattern invalidation fires once per `*Where` call regardless of
  row count"), and `NESTED_MUTATIONS_EXAMPLES.md` §7.1/§7.3/§7.6 **EQ1** + §9 **A14**.
  `BuildTablePattern` itself is unchanged — it stays the `InvalidateTable`, view-cascade, and
  `invalidateTenantedFallback` path.

**Accepted knowingly.** On **MySQL only**, `*Where` collects PKs before the statement
(`update.go.tmpl:1040-1060`, `delete.go.tmpl` same shape), so a row inserted concurrently in that
window is mutated but absent from `AffectedPKs`; the wipe covered it by accident. PostgreSQL and
SQLite use `RETURNING` and have no gap. The same window already drops that row's **event** (events
fan out from `AffectedPKs`, `event_hooks.go.tmpl:88`), so precise invalidation makes the cache
exactly as precise as the event stream — the documented contract — and the exposure is bounded by
TTL. Pre-existing and identical on the tenanted `*Where` arm (T7) and on every `*Many` op. No
non-tenanted analogue of `invalidateTenantedFallback` is added: there is no carrier whose absence
could signal a capture gap, so `len(affected) == 0` means "no rows", the same reading the tenanted
arm already takes.

**Rejected.** **(b)** documents a cliff that is paid by every existing `UpdateWhere` caller, not
just the two nested verbs, and that worsens as the consumer's keyspace grows — the wrong way for a
known limitation to age. **(c)** stands rejected as filed: N statements, and it breaks **D12**.

**Regression pins.**
- A `*Where` mutation on a non-tenanted table evicts the rows it touched and leaves an unrelated
  cached row of the same table intact (the pin named in the original entry).
- A `*Where` matching zero rows dispatches no invalidation at all.
- A `*Where` on a table with `cache.enabled: false` dispatches no invalidation and no pattern scan.
- `WithTx` + `CallbackSync` + a mutation on a non-cached table commits and returns `nil` — covering
  both the `*Where` and `*Many` arms (§27.9).
- `where_mutations_test.go` (cache fixture) inverts: its three
  `…_PatternInvalidationFiresOnce` tests and their header comment assert the behavior being
  replaced, including the claim that `*Where` "would need to know the affected PK set ahead of
  time", which is false — every `*Where` template captures it.

**References.**
- PRD §27.7 (cache behavior by operation), §27.9, §29.5 (tenant-scoped invalidation).
- `cache/key.go:56-71` — why `BuildTablePattern` is fingerprint- and PK-agnostic.
- `cache/redis/redis.go:162-180` and `cache/memory/memory.go:167-187` — both `InvalidatePattern`
  implementations walk the entire keyspace, which is where the measured cost comes from.
- `database/transaction.go:333`, `:469-480` — `CallbackSync` returns callback errors from `Commit`.
- `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS_EXAMPLES.md` §7.3 (the analysis), §7.6 **EQ1**, §9 **A14**.
- `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` §11 (blast-radius row) and §9 (listed as a pre-phase prerequisite).
- **FIX-200** — adjacent caching-layer entry, also on junction/relationship cache behavior.
- **Measurement method (2026-09-16).** Throwaway probes, removed after the numbers were taken:
  `cache/redis` (testcontainers `redis:7-alpine`, seeded keyspaces of 2 k–300 k, `used_memory`
  deltas for the orphan footprint, `TTL` reads to confirm orphans expire) and `cache/memory`
  (otter, `MaxSize: 1_000_000`). Findings 1 and 2 were probed inside the cache fixture
  (`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/cache/tests`) against `audit_logs`, the `cache.enabled: false`
  table, with the spy backend counting `invalidate_pattern` / `invalidate_many` dispatches.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-16 as candidate **(a)**, the decision recorded above.

`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/cache.go.tmpl` — the four `*Where` ops were folded into the existing
key-based arm rather than given a precise arm of their own: `OpUpdateWhere`, `OpSoftDeleteWhere`,
`OpHardDeleteWhere` and `OpRestoreWhere` now sit in the same `case` as `OpUpdate…`/`*Many` and
reach `c.InvalidateMany(ctx, table, affected)` through the identical path, with the tenanted
switch in between unchanged. Merging rather than duplicating removed the arm's copy of the
tenanted `range` block and the per-case `len(affected)` checks, so the template lost 22 lines and
gained 18. `prefix := c.prefix` / `schema := m.Schema` went with the pattern wipe — the last
readers of both.

The `cacheSchemaFor(table)` guard (**a2**) landed on the merged arm, covering `*Many` and `*Where`
together, and retires the §27.9 violation finding 2 measured on shipped code: `WithTx` +
`CallbackSync` + a mutation on a `cache.enabled: false` table now commits and returns `nil`
instead of `cache: unknown or non-cached table`. It also drops the full-keyspace `SCAN` those
tables used to trigger, which is what §27.7's junction opt-out was already advertising.

**Docs (a3).** PRD §27.7's behavior-table row rewritten to "Invalidate many"; §27.5's
tenant-segment sentence and its "Pattern invalidation is fingerprint-agnostic" paragraph now scope
`BuildTablePattern` to `InvalidateTable` / view cascade / capture-gap fallback; §27.7's junction
bullet says the opt-out is honored at the arm; §29.5's `BuildTablePattern` bullet no longer claims
the mutation path uses it; §27.3's `Backend` godoc no longer justifies mandatory
`InvalidatePattern` by `*Where`. Echoes repointed in `CACHE.md` §9.3 + §9.3 implementation notes +
§21 rationale 1, `IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md` §14.3, `NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` §11 + §9, and
`NESTED_MUTATIONS_EXAMPLES.md` §7.1/§7.3/§7.6 (**EQ1** marked answered, **EQ6** downgraded)/§9
(**A14** discharged). A closing grep over the live docs caught three more: `CACHE.md`'s Phase 12
example test-plan bullet and its fingerprint-resolution item 3, and the mirrored test-plan bullet
in `IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md`. `CACHE.md` §20A and §12 (no-PK tables) needed no edit — the first
already named TTL/LRU and a one-shot `InvalidateTable` as the orphan-GC mechanisms, the second
already rests on no-PK tables having no generated mutation methods at all.

The closed-phase trackers (`phase-12.md`, `phase-13.md`, `phase-14.md`) were deliberately left
alone. They record what each phase shipped, not current behavior — `phase-13.md:433` was already
stale after Phase 23's T7 took tenanted `*Where` off the pattern path and was not rewritten then
either. The PRD is the document kept current (project rule 1).

**Tests.** `cmd/sqlgen/gen/cache_template_test.go` gained `TestCacheTemplate_whereOpsShareKeyBasedArm`
(the ops share the arm, no separate `*Where` case survives, exactly one `BuildTablePattern` call
is emitted in a non-tenanted package — `InvalidateTable`'s — and the uncached-table guard is
present) and `TestCacheTemplate_tenantedWhereOpsStayPerRow` (the merge did not cost the tenanted
half its per-row path or its fallback), with a `cacheTestTenantedTable` fixture added to
`context_cache_test.go`. The first was confirmed to fail against the pre-fix template.
`where_mutations_test.go` in the cache fixture was rewritten around the new pins: the four
`…_PatternInvalidationFiresOnce` tests became `…_InvalidatesAffectedRows` (one `invalidate_many`
carrying one key per matched PK, zero patterns), `…_ZeroMatch_PatternInvalidationStillFires`
inverted to `…_ZeroMatch_InvalidatesNothing`, and three new tests cover the blast radius (a
warmed bystander row still hits after an unrelated `UpdateWhere`), the uncached table, and the
`CallbackSync` commit. `mutation_test.go` and `restore_test.go` carried the same stale assertions
and were updated alongside; the `HardDeleteWhere`-on-`products` case now asserts the one
remaining pattern is the `product_summary` view cascade, with its `reset()` moved between the
seed `Create` and the mutation so the count isolates.

**Auto-review round (2026-09-16).** The `sqlgen-reviewer` pass confirmed the behavior change —
`AffectedPKs` verified populated on all 16 `*Where` template branches and, mechanically, across all
512 generated `*Where` methods (one assignment, one mutating call, the only intervening return
being the zero-match guard; the MySQL pre-`SELECT` and the mutation share the identical `conds`,
soft-delete and restore scoping included), the collapsed `len(affected)` guard shown equivalent to
the per-case checks it replaced, and `BuildTablePattern` confined to `InvalidateTable` plus the
tenanted fallback. It also found the doc sweep incomplete in six places, all comment/prose
staleness and all fixed in this change: the template's own `invalidatePattern` godoc (which ships
into all ten generated files, so goldens were regenerated), the exported `BuildTablePattern` godoc
in `cache/key.go` (which still carried the pre-T7 claim that `*Where` on a tenanted table must
clear every tenant), the exported `Backend` godoc in `cache/backend.go` (which PRD §27.3 quotes
verbatim, so source and spec had diverged), `CACHE.md` §10.1's copy of that godoc,
`fingerprint_test.go`'s header comment, and three "unlogged FIX" / present-tense claims in
`NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` §9 and `IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md` §27 — both FIX-207 and FIX-208 are now
logged and resolved, so neither gates 27.6 or 27.9. The first sweep had grepped only `docs/` and
`guidelines/` markdown, which is what let the Go-source and template godocs through.

The reviewer's one non-defect note is recorded here so it is not re-raised: `cacheSchemaFor` admits
cached **views** while `InvalidateMany`'s switch rejects them. Unreachable — views generate no
mutation methods, and materialized-view refresh routes through `dispatchRefresh`, not
`dispatchMutation`.

**Verification.** `make check` and `make check-examples` (Docker, all three dialects) green;
`make update-golden` + `make update-golden-e2e` re-run after the sweep produced no further diff.
Golden churn is confined to the `dispatchMutation` arm in ten `cache_gen.go` files.

Not addressed, and deliberately: the MySQL collect-then-mutate window described under **Accepted
knowingly** above, which is pre-existing on every `*Many` op and on the tenanted `*Where` arm.

### FIX-211

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 9, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/{get,stream,create,update,upsert}.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-207's E2E bring-up (2026-09-16) — a `GetMany(ctx, nil)` written while
  seeding a test panicked, which turned out to be one of six sites

**Issue.** **Eight generated methods dereference a caller-supplied pointer with no nil guard.**
Probed against the `graphql` example, every pointer-taking method called with `nil`:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `GetMany(ctx, nil)` (table) | **panic** → `sqlgen: panic in get_many public.users: … nil pointer dereference` |
| `GetMany(ctx, nil)` (view) | **panic** → same shape |
| `Create(ctx, nil)` | **panic** |
| `Update(ctx, id, nil)` | **panic** |
| `Upsert(ctx, nil, target)` | **panic** |
| `Stream(ctx, nil)` | **silently yields zero rows, no error** |
| `UpdateWhere(validFilter, nil)` | **panic** — masked in the first probe, which passed nil for *both* args so the filter guard fired first |
| `CreateMany(ctx, []*Create<T>Input{nil})` | **panic** — a nil batch *element*, distinct from a nil slice |
| `UpdateMany(ctx, []Update<T>Item{{ID: id}})` | **panic** — `Update<T>Item.Input` is a pointer, so a zero item carries a nil one |
| `Count(nil)` / `ExistsWhere(nil)` / `CreateMany(nil)` / `UpdateMany(nil)` | fine |
| `SoftDeleteWhere` / `RestoreWhere` / `HardDeleteWhere` `(nil)` | fine — `ErrEmptyFilter` |
| `Paginate{}` / `Connection{}` | fine — value types, not nil-able |

The last three were found after the first pass: `UpdateWhere` by a signature sweep (its two-pointer
signature has a combination a both-nil probe cannot see), and the two batch-element shapes by the
auto-review. `UpdateMany(ctx, []Update<T>Item{{ID: id}})` is the easiest of all eight to hit — a
zero-valued item is a shape that compiles naturally.

**`Stream` is the worst of the six.** It discards the executor's error (`_, _ = c.executeQuery(…)`),
so the panic-recovery hook catches the nil deref and the error is *thrown away*: the iterator
yields nothing and the caller sees no error. Probed — `Stream(&StreamUsersInput{})` yields 3 rows,
`Stream(nil)` yields 0 rows and 0 errors on the same data. A caller concludes the table is empty.
That is silent wrong data, not a loud failure.

**Root cause.** The templates read `input.Filter`, `input.Sorts` and `input.requiredColumns`
directly. No guard exists, and **the PRD's own reference bodies have the same unguarded
dereference** (§9.8.3's `GetMany` reads `input.requiredColumns` / `input.Filter` with no nil
check), so this is a spec gap the generator faithfully reproduces rather than a codegen slip.

**Fix.**
- **Reads — nil means "no criteria", which invents nothing.** Probed: `GetMany(&GetUsersInput{})`
  already returns all rows, and `Count(nil)`, `ExistsWhere(nil)`, `Paginate{}` and `Connection{}`
  all already mean exactly that. So `GetMany` / `Stream` normalise `nil` to the zero-value input at
  the top of the method, before the hook context is built — hooks then never observe a nil `Input`
  either.
- **Writes — nil must be an error, and must not be the zero value.** Probed:
  `Create(&CreateUserInput{})` **inserts a row**, so normalising `Create(nil)` the same way would
  silently write a garbage row — worse than the panic. `Create` / `Update` / `Upsert` return a new
  **`ErrNilInput`** sentinel (user decision 2026-09-16, of three options), guarding before
  `executeMutation` so no event or cache side effect fires.
- **`ErrNilInput` is new public API**: `database/errors.go`, re-exported through `error.go.tmpl`,
  added to the PRD §10 sentinel list and the §2.6 exported-surface table, with a `mapErrorToGQL`
  arm so it maps to `INVALID_INPUT` rather than falling through to `INTERNAL`.
- **Regression pins, failing-first**: every nil-able method on the `graphql` example, table-driven,
  asserting no panic and the documented outcome — including the `Stream` row-count comparison that
  a swallowed panic would fail.

**References.**
- PRD §9.8.3 (`GetMany`), §9.8.11 (`Paginate`), §9.4a (`Stream`), §10 (sentinels), §2.6 (exported
  surface), §26.12 (`mapErrorToGQL`).
- `database/errors.go:13-16` — `ErrEmptyFilter`, the precedent this sentinel follows.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-16 — all eight sites guarded, split by direction per the
new PRD §9.4c.

- **PRD first** (project rule 1): new **§9.4c "Nil input handling"** states the rule and why it
  splits; §9.1/§9.2 operation-table rows for `GetMany`, `Stream`, `Create`, `Update` and `Upsert`
  now carry it; §22.1 and the §2.6 exported-surface table gained `ErrNilInput`.
- **`database/errors.go`** — the `ErrNilInput` sentinel, re-exported through `error.go.tmpl`.
- **Reads** (`table/get.go.tmpl`, `view/get.go.tmpl`, `table/stream.go.tmpl`) normalise `nil` to
  the zero-value input at the top of the method, *before* the hook context is built — so a hook
  never observes a nil `QueryContext.Input` either.
- **Writes** (`table/{create,update,upsert}.go.tmpl`) return `ErrNilInput` before
  `executeMutation`, so a nil input fires no hook, publishes no event and invalidates no cache
  entry. `UpdateWhere` checks the input **before** its filter — argument validity is a property of
  the call, `ErrEmptyFilter` a safety guard on what the filter compiles to — so
  `UpdateWhere(ctx, nil, nil)` reports `ErrNilInput`; a non-nil input with an empty filter still
  reports `ErrEmptyFilter`. `CreateMany` / `UpdateMany` reject a nil **element** on the same rule,
  while a nil **slice** stays "no rows": skipping a nil element would silently drop a row the
  caller asked to write.
- **No `mapErrorToGQL` arm** — contrary to the estimate given when the option was chosen. §26.5.5's
  table maps only the sentinels GraphQL can actually surface, and a resolver builds its inputs from
  variables, so it can never hand the client a nil pointer. `ErrNilInput` therefore joins the
  fall-through set, exactly as `ErrEmptyFilter` already does. The manifest's `error_sentinels[]`
  carries it with `graphql_code: ""`, and the "seven sentinels" / "five fall through" counts in
  §22.1, §2.6, §30 and `manifest/builder.go` moved to eight and six.
- **`gen/resolved_names.go`** — `ErrNilInput` reserved as a package-scope name. The
  `TestGeneratedPackageNames_MatchTemplates` pin caught the omission on the first regeneration,
  which is the registry doing its job.
- **Tests, verified failing-first** — reverted the six guards, regenerated, and confirmed every
  site fails, then restored. `nil_input_test.go` is table-driven over every nil-able method
  (reads, writes, bulk-write slices, `*Where`, both views) and asserts no row was written by the
  nil writes; `TestNilInput_ReadsMatchZeroValue` pins nil ≡ zero-value as a row-count equivalence,
  which is the only shape that catches `Stream`'s swallowed panic.
- **A tenanted view's `GetMany(nil)` now reaches `tenancy.ErrMissing`** instead of panicking —
  pinned, since the guard removes the nil dereference without touching the §29 scoping behind it.
- **`make check`** clean across all 8 modules, **`make check-examples`** clean across all 12.
- Golden churn is wide but shallow: every `errors_gen.go` gains the sentinel, the manifests gain
  the `error_sentinels[]` entry plus `ErrNilInput` on each write method's `errors[]`, and the eight
  guarded methods gain their guard.
- **Auto-review round (found two more panics).** The batch-element shapes above were missed by the
  probe, which passed a nil *slice* rather than a nil *element*; §9.4c's bulk-variant paragraph had
  the same hole and was corrected alongside the guards. The review also caught the manifest's
  per-method `errors[]` omitting `ErrNilInput` — a §30.4.2 violation, since that field is specified
  to list the sentinels a body can actually reach — and a set of consistency gaps now closed:
  `docs/design/MANIFEST.md`'s conventions example, `guidelines/ERRORS.md` (hierarchy, count, table row,
  "when to use"), the `database/errors_test.go` message and distinctness pins, the
  `gen/error_test.go` re-export pin, three stale "(Create, Update, Upsert)" doc comments, and the
  PRD's remaining "seven entries" count. `TestBuild_MethodErrors_MatchTemplateGuards` and
  `TestBuild_MethodErrors_Tenancy` caught the manifest expectations on regeneration, which is the
  §30.4.2 pin working as designed.

### FIX-207

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 11, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/event_hooks.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** nested-mutations readiness pass (2026-09-16) — recorded as **A18** in
  `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS_EXAMPLES.md` §9, then found to be **reachable on shipped code** rather
  than the latent class it was filed as

**Issue.** **The §32.3 event-redaction switch's `default` arm publishes the raw mutation input,
and three shipped operations reach it carrying a caller-supplied filter.** The generated per-table
event hook redacts access-restricted columns out of the published event input — `users` has
`redactUserCreateInput` / `redactUserUpdateInput`, which clear `password_hash` (`access: internal`)
and `new_password` (`access: write_only`, `testdata/examples/graphql/sqlgen.yml:107-110`). The
switch covers `OpCreate`, `OpUpsert`, `OpCreateMany`, `OpUpdate`, `OpUpdateWhere`, `OpUpdateMany`
and the three `*Many` deletes, then falls through to `default: inputVal = mc.Input`
(`event_hooks_gen.go:1271-1272`, inside `newUserEventHook` at `:1198`).

Seven of the sixteen `MutationOp` values hit that default. Four are harmless — `OpIncrement`
carries a column enum and an amount; single-row `OpSoftDelete` / `OpRestore` / `OpHardDelete` set
`PK:` and leave `Input` unset, so `mc.Input` is nil there and the arm already publishes the nil
§28.6 mandates. **Three are not.** `SoftDeleteWhere`, `HardDeleteWhere` and `RestoreWhere` set `Input: filter`
(`delete.go.tmpl:410`, `:1122`, `:1724`), and `UserFilter` carries both restricted columns as
filterable comparators — `PasswordHash *comparator.String`, `NewPassword
*comparator.NullableString`. So:

```go
client.Users().SoftDeleteWhere(ctx, &UserFilter{PasswordHash: &comparator.String{Eq: &h}})
```

publishes `h` to every event subscriber, un-redacted — while the same hook, eleven lines earlier,
strips the identical field out of a create. One switch, two opposite behaviors on one column.

Not reachable from GraphQL: an `internal` column is absent from the API projection, so this is Go
client code being deliberate — the FIX-199 reasoning, hence `tracked` rather than `blocking`. What
is worth weighing against that precedent is the **destination**: the value does not stay in server
code, it crosses onto the event bus, whose subscribers may sit at a different trust level than the
caller. Raise to `blocking` if that is the reading.

**Root cause.** `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/event_hooks.go.tmpl:171` — the arm is written as a
permissive fallback (`inputVal = mc.Input`) rather than a fail-closed one, so redaction is opt-in
per operation. Every arm above it had to be written deliberately; anything not enumerated leaks by
default. `redactUserUpdateInput`'s own doc comment states the intended contract — nil passes
through "rather than leaking the raw input" — and the default arm does exactly what that sentence
disclaims.

**Verified 2026-09-16 — the original suggested fix was wrong; superseded by the plan below.**

The leak was reproduced in-process against the shipped `newUserEventHook` (no DB): all three
`*Where` ops publish the caller's `*UserFilter` **by the same pointer**, with
`PasswordHash.Eq == "super-secret-hash"` intact. Reachability is confirmed, not inferred.

**Why `default → nil` is not the fix.** Three independent reasons:

1. **It contradicts PRD §28.6's normative shape table**, which lists `HardDeleteWhere` /
   `SoftDeleteWhere` / `RestoreWhere` → `*<Struct>Filter` (shared across N events). Publishing nil
   there is a spec violation, not a fix.
2. **Nil already means something else.** §28.6's subscriber example documents `case nil:` as
   "HardDelete / SoftDelete / Restore (single + `*Many`)". A bulk `*Where` delete arriving as nil
   is then indistinguishable from a single-row delete — while §32.3 goes out of its way to publish
   "the same concrete type" precisely so "subscribers' type-switch is unchanged".
3. **Unconditionally it breaks two stated guarantees** — §32.3's "tables with no redacted column
   are byte-unchanged and pay nothing", and the §28.6 same-pointer guarantee that STATUS 22.3
   records as pinned by goldens *and* a pointer-identity test — for tables with nothing to redact.

**Fix.** The entry's own second option, which is what §32.3 already mandates for create / update /
increment: a redacted clone of the same concrete type.

- **`redact<T>Filter(*<T>Filter) *<T>Filter`**, nil-in/nil-out like the existing helpers. **It
  cannot be a shallow copy.** A create input is flat; a filter is a graph, and two edges carry
  values out:
  - `And []*<T>Filter` / `Or []*<T>Filter` — `&UserFilter{And: []*UserFilter{{PasswordHash: …}}}`
    bypasses any top-level-only redaction in one line, so recursion here is **mandatory, not
    optional**. Rebuild the slices; never mutate the caller's elements.
  - relationship members (`Categories`, `Events`, `Orders` on `UserFilter`) — a redacted column on
    a *target* table rides out through the parent's event. So the emission set is the **transitive
    closure** over the relationship-filter graph (`TableContext.RelationshipFilters`,
    `TargetStructName` / `TargetTable` / `TargetSchema`), not a per-table boolean.
  - **Wrinkle:** the closure can reach a table whose own events are disabled but which has a
    redacted column. `event_hooks_gen.go` emits helpers only for event tables today, so that
    target's helper needs a home — settle it when the closure is computed in
    `BuildEventHooksContext`, which already ranges over every table.
  - A caller-built *value* cycle would recurse forever, but `ToConditions` has the same failure
    mode today (`models_gen.go`, the `And`/`Or` and `*FilterExists` walks). Same behavior, not a
    new hazard.
- **Explicit `case hook.OpSoftDeleteWhere, hook.OpHardDeleteWhere, hook.OpRestoreWhere:` arms**
  calling it, gated on closure membership and on `Operations.SoftDelete` / `HardDelete` /
  `Restore` (there is no separate `*_where` config flag — `delete.go.tmpl` emits each `*Where`
  under its base op's gate).
- **Fail-closed default, scoped to the redaction closure** (user decision 2026-09-16, of three
  options). For a table in the closure, enumerate all sixteen ops and make `default:` publish nil;
  outside it, `default: inputVal = mc.Input` stands, keeping non-redacted hooks byte-unchanged and
  the same-pointer guarantee intact. **`OpIncrement` needs an explicit pass-through arm** in the
  closure case — it currently falls to the default whenever `EmitRedactIncrement` is false (the
  redacted column is not incrementable, or `Increment` is off), and a blanket fail-closed default
  would regress §28.6's `Increment | IncrementInput[…]` row.
  - Known residue: this does **not** cover A13's other half — on a *non-redacted* table a missing
    op arm still publishes the whole batch on every fanned-out event, a §28.6 fanout violation
    rather than a §32.3 leak. Enumerating every op on every table was considered and not taken,
    on golden churn.
- **PRD amendment carries with this FIX** (user decision 2026-09-16, per project rule 1 — write it
  first). §32.3's Events paragraph names only the create / update / increment helpers, so the
  filter leg is a spec gap; add it there, and annotate §28.6's `*Where` delete row that the
  payload is a redacted clone on a redacted table.
- **Regression pins, failing-first**, on the `graphql` example (the fixture with access-restricted
  columns): publish through `SoftDeleteWhere` and assert (a) `Event.Input` is still
  `*models.UserFilter`, (b) the `internal` column's value is absent, (c) **the value is absent from
  an `And`-nested filter too** — the bypass a shallow helper would leave open, and (d) the caller's
  filter is not mutated, mirroring the existing `TestAccess_EventRedaction` check.
- **Severity stays `tracked`** (user decision 2026-09-16): FIX-199's precedent holds — it needs
  deliberate Go client code and is unreachable from GraphQL, since an `internal` column has no API
  filter field. Ordering is already enforced by the 27.6 block, not by severity.
- Note for whoever lands Phase 27 Ticket **Dc**: `OpUpsertMany` is the next op that would have hit
  this arm. Landing this fix first means that ticket cannot reintroduce the class.

**References.**
- PRD §32.3 (access-redacted columns in events), §28.6 (event payload contract).
- `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` **F9** — the finding that first named this arm, and **§9**, which
  lists this FIX as a pre-phase prerequisite.
- `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS_EXAMPLES.md` §7.4 (the analysis), §9 **A18** (the amendment).
- **FIX-199** — the severity precedent: a tenancy hole reachable only from deliberate server code
  was filed `tracked`, not `blocking`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/sqlgen.yml:107-110` — the fixture's access config.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-16 — closed as a **redacted filter clone**, not the
`default → nil` the entry originally proposed (see the verification block above for why nil
violates §28.6's shape table).

- **PRD first** (project rule 1): §32.3's Events paragraph gained the filter leg — the
  `redact<T>Filter` helper, why it cannot be a shallow copy, the transitive closure, and the
  fail-closed default (scoped to *any* table that redacts something, not only filter-closure
  members, with the explicit pass-through arm that keeps it from contradicting the shape table);
  §28.6's prose and its `*Where` shape-table row now say the published `*Filter` is a redacted
  clone on a redacted table.
- **`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_event.go`** — `FilterRedactorContext` / `FilterRedactorMember` plus the
  closure resolver (`buildFilterRedactors`, split across `closureIndex.propagate` /
  `.reachableRedactors` / `.closureMembers` to stay under the cyclop ceiling). Seed: a redacted
  column that is also *filterable*. Propagate: any table whose filter can reach one. Emit: narrowed
  again to helpers something actually calls, so no dead generated code. Per table:
  `FilterRedactOps`, `PassThroughOps`, `FailClosedDefault`.
- **`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/event_hooks.go.tmpl`** — the `*Where` redaction arm, the explicit
  pass-through arm, the fail-closed `default`, and the `redact<T>Filter` helper block.
- **The closure was load-bearing, not theoretical.** On the shipped `graphql` fixture
  `CategoryFilter` carries a `Users *UserFilter` member, so `categories` — which has nothing
  redacted of its own — joined by propagation and the two helpers are **mutually recursive**.
  Without that rule `Categories().HardDeleteWhere(&CategoryFilter{Users: &UserFilter{PasswordHash:
  …}})` leaked exactly what the `users` hook strips.
- **Golden churn is confined to the two fixtures with redacted columns** (`graphql`, `events`).
  Every other example's `event_hooks_gen.go` is byte-identical, which is the §32.3 "tables with no
  redacted column are byte-unchanged" guarantee and the §28.6 same-pointer test still holding.
- **`hidden` still passes through.** §32.2 redacts only `write_only` / `internal`;
  `users.internal_score` is `hidden` and survives filter redaction, pinned in both test layers.
- **Tests, verified failing-first** — reverted the template + context and re-ran to confirm all
  three legs fail without the fix, then restored. `cmd/sqlgen/gen/event_redaction_template_test.go`
  adds four gen-level pins (emission + And/Or recursion, relationship propagation, the two
  not-emitted shapes, fail-closed pass-throughs);
  `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/tests/access_test.go` adds
  `TestAccess_EventRedaction_WhereFilter` (top-level + `And`-nested + `hidden` pass-through +
  caller's filter unmutated) and `TestAccess_EventRedaction_RelationshipFilter` (the two-hop
  `User → Category → User` path across the mutual recursion).
- **`make check`** clean across all 8 modules, **`make check-examples`** clean across all 12.
- **Known residue, deliberately not taken** (user decision, of three options): fail-closed is
  scoped to tables that redact something. On a *non-redacted* table a missing op arm still
  publishes the whole batch on every fanned-out event — A13's other half, a §28.6 fanout violation
  rather than a §32.3 leak. Enumerating every op on every table was rejected on golden churn.
- **Phase 27 Ticket Dc (27.6) is unblocked**, and `OpUpsertMany` now lands on a redacted table's
  fail-closed default instead of its pass-through, so the ticket cannot reintroduce the class.
- **Auto-review round (caught one real defect).** Fail-closed keys on "redacts anything", but the
  filter closure keys on a redacted column that is also *filterable* — and those differ. A table
  with an `access: internal` column that has no comparator (`jsonb[]`, or `json` on SQLite —
  §11.2) failed closed **without** joining the closure, so its `*Where` deletes fell to the
  fail-closed `default` and published `nil` — reintroducing the exact §28.6 shape-table violation
  this fix rejected. `passThroughOps` now claims every enabled `*Where` op `filterRedactOps` did
  not, and `TestEventHooks_failClosed_whereDeletesKeepTheirFilter` pins it (verified failing-first
  against the unfixed predicate). Two nits fixed inline: the batch-fanout doc comment claimed
  "`*Where` ops … keep `mc.Input` unchanged" directly above an arm that redacts them, and
  `reachableRedactors` rooted at closure tables whose per-table events are disabled, which could
  emit a helper no hook calls — roots are now gated on event-enablement.

### FIX-210

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 18, `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/clean.go`
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-200 verification (2026-09-16) — triggered accidentally against this
  repository's own working tree while probing a throwaway config; `manifest/` was restored from git

**Issue.** **`sqlgen generate` deletes `<output.dir>/manifest/` outright, with no ownership check,
on every run where the manifest is disabled — which is the default.** `RunStage`
(`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit.go:41-53`) reads `cfg.Output.Dir` and, when `manifestEnabled(cfg)` is
false — no `manifest:` block at all, or `enabled: false` — calls `CleanStale`, whose disabled
branch resolves `markdownDir := filepath.Join(outputDir, dirOrDefault(markdownDirOf(m),
"manifest"))` (`clean.go:42`) and hands it to `removeManifestDir` → `os.RemoveAll`
(`clean.go:52`, `:102-106`, `:183-188`). Nothing checks that the directory was ever written by
sqlgen. A consumer whose output directory already contains a `manifest/` subdirectory — their own
Go package, their own docs, anything — loses it and its entire subtree on the first
`sqlgen generate`, silently: the run reports success and the deletion is not listed among the
`deletedFiles` the CLI prints.

Observed against this repository: a config whose output directory resolved to the repo root removed
the tracked runtime package `manifest/` (7 `.go` files, `os.RemoveAll` of the whole directory).
Recovered with `git checkout -- manifest/`; an unversioned directory would not have been.

**Root cause.** `removeManifestDir` (`clean.go:102-106`) guards **containment**, not **ownership**.
Its own doc comment scopes the intent to a misconfigured directory *name* — "a target that resolves
to base itself, or escapes base via `..`, is left untouched so a misconfigured dir name can never
wipe the output tree" — and `within` (`:111-119`) implements exactly that and nothing more. A
pre-existing, sqlgen-unknown `manifest/` sitting legitimately inside the output dir passes the guard
and is removed.

The asymmetry is visible inside the same function. Eleven lines below the `RemoveAll`, the
breadcrumb half of the identical cleanup is provenance-gated: `removeBreadcrumbs` →
`removeIfSqlgenOwned` → `BreadcrumbIsSqlgenOwned` (`clean.go:123-156`), and `CleanStale`'s own doc
comment states the rule — "Breadcrumbs lacking the provenance marker (user-authored or
user-adopted) are left untouched (PRD §30.3 ownership rule)." The §30.3 rule is applied to the
files and skipped for the directory.

**A second, compounding factor.** `LoadConfig` calls plain `yaml.Unmarshal`
(`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:1413`) with no `KnownFields(true)`, so an unrecognized key is silently
dropped. A config that writes `output.path` instead of `output.dir` (`config.go:273-281` defines
only `Dir`) leaves `Output.Dir` empty, which resolves to `.` — the working directory. That is how
the observed case reached the repo root: a typo in one key silently retargeted every write **and**
the `RemoveAll`. The two defects are independent and each is worth closing on its own.

**Suggested fix.**
- **Ownership-gate the directory removal**, mirroring the breadcrumb path: only `RemoveAll` a
  manifest directory sqlgen can prove it wrote. The cheapest marker consistent with §30.3 is the
  emitted content itself — refuse to remove a directory containing any entry that is not one
  sqlgen emits (`_index.md`, `_conventions.md`, `<file_prefix>.md`, the entities dir, the JSON).
  A prune-known-files-then-`os.Remove`-if-empty is strictly safer than `RemoveAll` and needs no new
  on-disk marker. Applies to both `removeManifestDir` call sites (`clean.go:52` and `:94`).
- **Make an unknown config key an error**, or at minimum a stderr warning, in `LoadConfig`
  (`config.go:1413`) — `yaml.Decoder` + `KnownFields(true)`. Independently, warn when
  `output.dir` is unset and defaults to `.`, since writing generated code into the working
  directory is nearly always a mistake.
- **Report the deletion.** The disabled path removes a directory without surfacing it; the stale
  `_gen.go` sweep beside it reports every file (`cli/generate.go:80`). Fold manifest-directory
  removals into the same reported set.
- Regression tests, failing-first: (1) a `manifest/` directory inside the output dir containing one
  file sqlgen does not emit survives a disabled-manifest generate; (2) a directory containing only
  sqlgen-emitted files is still removed (the existing behavior this must not regress — see
  `manifest/emit_test.go:316`); (3) a config with an unknown top-level or nested key is rejected.

**References.**
- PRD §30.3 — the ownership rule the breadcrumb half honors and the directory half does not.
- PRD §23.8 — stale-artifact cleanup on every generation.
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/clean.go:24-58` (`CleanStale` doc comment + disabled branch), `:96-119`
  (`removeManifestDir` / `within`), `:123-156` (the provenance-gated breadcrumb path).
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit_test.go:316-320` — `TestCleanStale_GuardsAgainstOutputDirWipe`,
  the existing test for the markdown_dir `"."` case,
  which covers path-escape but not ownership.
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:273-281` (`OutputConfig`, `Dir` only), `:1413` (non-strict
  `yaml.Unmarshal`).
- **FIX-200** — the entry whose verification surfaced this.

**Resolution notes.** Ownership-gated both removal sites, made unknown config keys fatal, and
surfaced the deletions.

- **The directory gate.** `removeManifestDir` → `remover.manifestDir`
  (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/clean.go`) now clears two gates rather than one: the existing containment
  check, then `sqlgenOwnsManifestDir` — proof that a prior `enabled: true` run wrote the directory.
  That is the precondition §30.3 already states ("Setting `manifest.enabled: false` **after a prior
  `true`**") and the one thing a containment check cannot establish. Proof is read off the emitted
  content, so no marker file and no on-disk state between runs was introduced: an `_index.md`
  carrying `**Generator:** sqlgen`, or a `<json_filename>` whose `generator.name` is `sqlgen`
  (§30.4). `validateManifestEnabledFields` requires at least one format, so an enabled run always
  leaves one anchor. It fails closed — a directory that is missing, unreadable, or written under a
  `json_filename` the current config no longer names reports unowned and is left alone.
- **Not the prune-known-files approach this entry suggested.** The disabled path runs with
  `Doc == nil` (`emit.go`), so entity `file_prefix`es are unknowable there and "files sqlgen emits"
  degenerates to a `*.md` / `*.json` glob — which deletes a consumer's docs directory one file at a
  time instead of all at once. The anchor gate needs no prefixes, and it keeps §23.8 whole: a
  per-entity file for a table dropped *before* the flip is still swept.
- **Second removal site** (`clean.go`, the per_entity → single flip) does use the prune shape, where
  it works: `remover.entitiesDir` prunes `*.json` and removes the directory only once empty, so
  anything else a consumer left inside survives.
- **Strict config parsing.** `LoadConfig` decodes via `yaml.Decoder` + `KnownFields(true)`; an
  unrecognized key is now a config error (exit 2, §23.9). Empty documents still load — `Decode`
  reports `io.EOF` where `Unmarshal` reported nothing. Known gap: keys nested inside a type with its
  own `UnmarshalYAML` (`Operations`, `NullableVariant`) still escape, because `yaml.Node.Decode`
  builds a fresh non-strict decoder that the setting cannot reach.
- **`output.dir` warning.** `validateOutputDir` warns when `output.dir` was omitted and defaulted to
  `.`; an explicit `dir: "."` is deliberate and stays silent. Defaulting erases that distinction, so
  it is captured by an unexported `OutputConfig.dirDefaulted` set in `applyOutputDefaults`.
- **Deletions are reported.** `CleanStale` / `RunStage` return the deleted paths (new
  `manifest.StageResult`), and `cli/generate.go` folds them into the same reported set as the stale
  `_gen.go` sweep, directories marked with a trailing `/`.
- **Drift guards.** `generatorName` and `defaultJSONFilename` promoted to shared constants so
  emission and the ownership probe cannot drift apart; `TestManifestIndexAnchorDrift` pins the
  markdown anchor against real emitted output.
- **Tests**, all verified failing against the pre-fix code:
  `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/clean_ownership_test.go` — unowned directories survive across five shapes
  (including the observed Go-package case), owned directories are still swept whole under
  both-formats / markdown-only / json-only / custom `json_filename`, the fail-closed limitation, the
  entities-dir prune, and breadcrumbs unaffected by the directory gate;
  `cmd/sqlgen/config/strict_test.go` — unknown top-level and nested keys rejected, all 12 shipped
  example configs still load, empty document loads, warning fires only when defaulted.
  `make check` and `make check-examples` clean; no golden files changed.

**Post-review hardening.** The auto-review found three defects in the gate itself, all fixed before
close:

- **The gate was not actually failing closed.** The ownership probe returned an error for any read
  failure other than `ENOENT`, which propagated out through `CleanStale` → `RunStage` and aborted
  generation — so an unreadable `manifest/_index.md`, in a directory sqlgen may have no claim to,
  failed the whole run. Probing is now infallible (`probeFile` returns nil on any read error and
  `sqlgenOwnsManifestDir` returns a plain `bool`): the only thing a failed read can justify is
  declining to delete. `TestCleanStale_UnreadableAnchorDoesNotFailGeneration`.
- **The proof could be relocated.** `json_filename` is unvalidated config and was joined onto the
  directory path, so a value carrying separators (`../real/manifest_gen.json`) read the anchor out
  of a *different* directory and re-authorized `RemoveAll` on the target. It is now reduced with
  `filepath.Base` — the proof has to come from inside the directory being removed.
  `TestCleanStale_AnchorCannotBeRelocated`.
- **Partial sweeps went unreported.** `RunStage` discarded the deleted set when cleanup failed
  mid-sweep, reopening the silent-deletion hole on exactly the path where the consumer most needs
  the list. `StageResult` now travels with the error, and `cli/generate.go` prints it before
  bailing.
- Test gap closed: `cmd/sqlgen/cli/manifest_cleanup_test.go` asserts the deletions at the CLI level
  (the unit tests only asserted `StageResult.Deleted`) and reproduces the incident through the
  binary's own entry point. Both hardening tests verified failing against the un-hardened probe.

**Sibling defects closed in the same pass.** The review surfaced three more of the same class —
cleanup acting on a name rather than on proof of authorship. All fixed here rather than deferred,
since splitting them would leave the identical hole open one directory over:

- **`gen.CleanStaleFiles` deleted any orphaned `*_gen.go` on the suffix alone**
  (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go`). With `output.dir` defaulting to `.` and
  `layout: file_per_table`, the sweep runs over a consumer's module root, where `wire_gen.go`,
  `mock_gen.go` and `stringer` output are ordinary residents — every one of them deleted silently.
  `StaleFiles` now also requires sqlgen's own generated header, matched on the new
  `gen.GeneratedHeaderPrefix` that `gen.Header` is built from. It deliberately does **not** match
  Go's generic `// Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.` form: telling sqlgen's output apart from another
  generator's is the entire point. Fails closed, and stripping the header disowns a file exactly as
  it does a breadcrumb. `cmd/sqlgen/gen/stale_provenance_test.go` +
  `TestGenerate_ForeignGenFileSurvivesSweep` / `TestDiff_ForeignGenFileNotReportedDeleted`
  (`sqlgen diff` shares `StaleFiles`, so its preview had to stop promising the deletion too).
  Two existing diff tests seeded a headerless `"// orphaned"` stub as their fixture; they now write
  what a real sqlgen orphan looks like, which is what they meant all along.
- **`checkManifestDirPlacement` rejected `"."` and `_`-prefixes but not `..` or absolute paths**
  (`cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go`). PRD §30.2 types `markdown_dir` / `json_per_entity_dir` as a
  *subdirectory under* their parent, so `markdown_dir: ../docs` was already out of spec — and it
  made the enabled-path `*.md` prune run outside the output tree. Now rejected, along with a
  `json_filename` carrying a path separator (§30.2 types it as a bare "Filename"). The placement
  rules moved into `validateManifestArtifactPaths` — they share one failure mode and the parent had
  outgrown the complexity budget.
- **The enabled-path prunes had no containment guard** while both directory removals did
  (`clean.go`). Both now check `within` as defense in depth: validation is the real fix, but this
  pass also runs against directly-constructed configs that never reach `LoadConfig`.

**Spec and docs synced.** The ownership rules lived only in code comments, where a later reader
could reasonably simplify them away:

- **PRD §30.3** gains a *Directory ownership* block stating that "after a prior `true`" is a
  precondition the generator MUST establish, naming the two anchors, and requiring the check to fail
  closed and to never fail a generation.
- **PRD §23.8** gains "the suffix decides what is *considered*; the header decides what is
  *deleted*", with the reciprocal pointer added to **§8.1.5**, which now records that the header is
  load-bearing for cleanup.
- **PRD §4.13 / §30.2** validation tables and bullets updated for the placement and filename rules.
- **`docs/design/MANIFEST.md` §4.4** updated to match.

### FIX-200

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 12, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_cache.go`
- **Surfaced by:** nested-mutations design review (2026-09-11) — user question
  "do we cache junction tables as well?"

**Issue.** **Junction tables are cached by default, but no generated read path reads them through
the cache.** Every detected M2M junction gets the full treatment — a composite-PK key builder, a
TTL resolver, a schema fingerprint, six arms across the invalidation switches, and a
`readThrough<Junction>` implementation (`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/models/cache_gen.go:3576-3584`,
`:3620`). Nothing generated reads it. The M2M relationship loader issues a raw `conn.Query`
against the junction (`models_gen.go:4328-4331`) instead of going through the junction's client,
so it bypasses the query-hook chain and therefore the cache; the relationship-filter `EXISTS`
subquery (`:5666`) is raw SQL for the same reason; and `GetMany` / `List` / `Connection` are never
cached at all (PRD §27.7). The only cached read is an explicit by-pair `Get(pk)` — reachable in Go
and exposed on GraphQL as `userCategory(userID: UUID!, categoryID: Int!)`
(`expected/graph/user_category_gen.graphqls:50`) — which answers a question the relationship
loader already answers as a side effect of loading the edge. Writes pay in full regardless: every
junction mutation dispatches invalidation, and a `*Where` delete (the shape an M2M "unlink
everything" takes) pattern-invalidates the junction namespace, which is a SCAN + DEL on Redis. The
net effect is write-side cost against a near-zero hit rate.

**Root cause.** `buildCacheContext` opts a table into the cache render context purely from config —
`if !config.ResolveTableCacheEnabled(tc, cfg.Cache) { continue }`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_cache.go:108`) — and `ResolveTableCacheEnabled`
(`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:1925-1933`) inherits the global `cache.enabled` whenever the table
sets no explicit override. Nothing in that path knows the table is a junction. The predicate itself
already exists and is already computed: `parser.detectRelationships` tests
`len(fkCols) == 2 && junctionConstraint(table, fkCols)` (`parser/relationship.go:19`, predicate at
`:52-70`) — but it is used inline to emit the M2M edge and then discarded, exactly the "one fact,
two derivations" shape NW-D1 / FIX-153 exist to prevent. There is no `IsJunction` on `parser.Table`
and none on the gen `TableContext`.

**Suggested fix.**
- Surface the fact rather than re-deriving it: add `IsJunction bool` to `parser.Table`, set it
  where `junctionConstraint` already returns true (`parser/relationship.go:19`), and carry it onto
  the gen `TableContext`. Do **not** re-test the predicate inside `context_cache.go` — that is the
  second derivation this fix exists to avoid.
- Change the default, not the capability: in `ResolveTableCacheEnabled` (`config/config.go:1925`),
  when the table is a junction **and** `table.Cache.Enabled == nil`, return `false` instead of
  inheriting the global. An explicit `tables.<t>.cache.enabled: true` must still win — the
  tri-state pointer already supports this, so only the nil branch changes.
- Scope the default to a *pure link table* (every column participating in the composite key, no
  payload), matching the predicate `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` **E5** already uses to decide M2M
  nestability. A junction carrying payload columns is arguably a first-class entity and should keep
  the global default.
- Regression tests: a pure link table is absent from `CachedTables` under a global
  `cache.enabled: true`; `tables.<junction>.cache.enabled: true` puts it back; a junction with a
  payload column is unaffected.
- Expect golden churn in `cache_gen.go` for every example pairing `cache:` with a junction —
  `graphql`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `postgres_stdlib`, `sqlite`, `tenancy`, and `cache` all qualify.
  No runtime-module change.

**References.**
- PRD §27.6 — the cache invariant, and the rule that relationship-loading calls bypass the cache
  entirely. That rule is *why* the junction cache is unreachable: the M2M loader is a relationship
  load.
- PRD §27.7 — behavior by operation; `GetMany` is uncached, `Get(pk)` is read-through.
- PRD §27.11 / §29.5 — invalidation, including the `*Where` pattern-invalidate path that makes the
  write-side cost worst for the unlink-everything shape.
- `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` **C9** and **F10** — both already document the raw junction query,
  from the read and correctness angles; this entry is the same fact seen from the cache angle.
  **E5** defines the pure-link-table predicate.
- `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS_EXAMPLES.md` §7.3 — the sibling observation that a non-tenanted
  `OpUpdateWhere` pattern-wipes rather than invalidating precisely; **EQ1** tracks that trade.
- **NW-D1** / **FIX-153** — prior art for hoisting a computed fact onto the context instead of
  re-deriving it in a second place.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-16 as **documented behavior, not a code change** — the
diagnosis held up, the suggested fix did not. Every claim was re-checked against HEAD first.

**Confirmed.** Junctions inherit global `cache.enabled` (`gen/context_cache.go:108` →
`ResolveTableCacheEnabled`, which is at `config/config.go:1975-1983`, not `:1925` as the entry
states). The M2M loader issues a raw `conn.Query` on the junction (`models_gen.go:4331`), the
relationship-filter `EXISTS` is raw SQL (`:5662`), and read-through is gated `q.Op != hook.OpGet`
(`cache_gen.go:4902`), so the junction's own by-pair `Get(pk)` is the only generated read that
reaches the cache. Junction-ness is computed at `parser/relationship.go:19` and discarded; there is
no `IsJunction` on `parser.Table` or on the gen `TableContext`.

**Why the suggested fix was not taken.**

1. **It is a PRD amendment, not a bug fix.** PRD §27.2 states the inheritance rule for
   `TableCacheConfig` and carves out exactly one exception — views — with a written rationale. A
   junction carve-out would be a second, undocumented exception.
2. **It default-disables the cache on the shape where it pays best.** The entry dismisses by-pair
   `Get(pk)` as redundant with the relationship loader; that holds only once the whole edge is
   loaded. A point membership read is the archetypal junction query, and the proposed scoping —
   pure link tables — targets exactly the ACL shape (`user_roles(user_id, role_id)`) where it is
   hottest. The “near-zero hit rate” was asserted, never measured.
3. **The capability already exists.** `tables.<junction>.cache.enabled: false` works today.
   Measured on a three-table probe: `cache_gen.go` 1298 → 1024 lines, removing exactly the seven
   junction cache functions (`keyFor`, `ttlFor`, `hasAnyRelationship`, `fullParentFieldOptions`,
   `readThrough`, `set`, `hydrate`) and nothing else. So this was only ever a question about the
   default, which is a workload judgment.

**Two factual errors in the entry, corrected here rather than carried forward.**

- **E5 is mis-cited.** `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` **E5** reads “the junction has no **required**
  column beyond its two FKs” — a nullable or defaulted payload column still passes. The entry
  restates it as “every column participating in the composite key, no payload,” which is a
  different and stricter predicate. The difference is live on a shipped fixture: `tenancy`'s
  `tag_links` carries `workspace_id` (NOT NULL, outside the PK) and its own schema comment calls it
  “a tenanted pure junction,” while the entry's predicate would classify it as payload-carrying.
  **E5 as actually written is the predicate to use** if this is ever revisited — one predicate then
  serves both nestability and any cache decision.
- **The blast-radius estimate is overstated ~3×.** The entry predicts golden churn in `graphql`,
  `mysql`, `postgres`, `postgres_stdlib`, `sqlite`, `tenancy` and `cache`. Only five examples emit
  `cache_gen.go` at all — `cache`, `graphql`, `tenancy`, `tenancy_mysql`, `tenancy_postgres`; the
  other four carry no `cache:` block. Of those five, only **two** contain a junction: `graphql`
  (`user_categories`, `asset_document_links`) and `tenancy` (`post_tags`, `tag_links`). The `cache`
  example has no junction.

**A gap the suggested fix would have shipped with — measured.** `IsJunction` set only at
`parser/relationship.go:19` covers schema-detected junctions and misses config-declared ones. There
are two sources of M2M edges: `parser.DetectRelationships` and `tables.<t>.relationships`, folded in
by `mergeDeclaredRelationships` (`gen/context_table.go:1333`), and nothing validates that a
config-declared `junction:` has a composite PK or UNIQUE. Probed with a `user_roles` table carrying
a surrogate `id` PK and no composite constraint, M2M declared in config: the full M2M edge and its
raw junction query generate, `junctionConstraint` returns false, and the table is cached. The flag
would have been `false` on a table the config explicitly names a junction — making the default
depend on how the edge was declared rather than on what the table is. Covering both sources means
setting the flag in gen as well as parser, so it cannot be a pure `parser.Table` field.

**What landed.** PRD §27.7 gains a subsection after the `SkipCache` paragraph — “M2M junction
tables inherit the cache, and only one read path reaches it” — stating the inheritance, naming
`Get(pk)` as the single cached read, giving `tables.<junction>.cache.enabled: false` as the opt-out
for an edge-only junction, and noting that `Exists(pk)` is **not** a substitute (read-through is
`OpGet`-gated for every table, so `Exists` always hits the database). No code, template, or golden
change; no runtime-module change.

**If this is revisited**, the open questions are, in order: does the default flip earn a second
§27.2 exception; does a tenant column count against the E5 predicate; and how does the flag reach
config-declared junctions. Nothing here forecloses any of them.

### FIX-199

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 13, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`
- **Surfaced by:** docs consolidation (2026-09-11) — carried over from the retired
  PRD §29.4.2, which recorded it as "deferred, and left open"

**Issue.** **The tenant column reaches the Go client's `<T>IncrementColumn` enum, contradicting
PRD §29.4.2.** The spec requires the tenant column to be absent from *every* increment surface.
The API side honors this — `buildUpdateOps` skips `col.Name == tenantCol` (`context_api.go:3377`) —
but the model side does not: `isIncrementEligible` (`context_table.go`) gates on
`!col.PrimaryKey && col.FKReference == nil && isIncrementableGoType(...) && isArithmeticSQLColumn(...)`
and never consults the tenant column.

**Reachable shape.** The FK clause masks this for the common tenant column, which is a declared
foreign key, and the UUID case is not an incrementable Go type. It is reachable when the tenant
column is an **integer with no declared FK constraint** — ordinary in sharded or denormalized
schemas, and in schemas whose tenants table lives in another database. Verified against the
existing `counterTenantSchema()` fixture (`counters`, `tenant_id bigint`, no FK): the model-side
increment set is `[tenant_id hits]` — `tenant_id` is present.

**Impact.** `client.Counters().Increment(ctx, id, CounterIncrementTenantID, 1)` compiles and moves
a row between tenants. `Increment` constrains which rows it matches, not which column it targets,
so the tenant predicate in the `WHERE` clause does not protect the `SET`. This is server code doing
something deliberate rather than a request crossing a trust boundary, which is why it is `tracked`
rather than `blocking` — but it is a tenant-isolation hole and the spec already forbids it.

**Root cause.** The original tenant-column work scoped itself to the API projection and left the Go
model layer untouched, on the reasoning that server code calling `Increment` is deliberate in a way
a GraphQL request is not. The exclusion was therefore implemented once, on the API side, instead of
at the single model-side source both surfaces read from. The fix is to move the tenant check into
`isIncrementEligible` (or its caller, which has the tenancy config), after which the API-side skip
becomes redundant and can be dropped. Expect golden churn only for tables with an integer,
non-FK tenant column.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-16. The tenant column now leaves the increment surface at
the model side, which is the single source both surfaces read.

- **New fact, carried rather than re-derived.** `ColumnContext.Tenant` (`gen/context.go`) is
  stamped by `attachTenancyToTables` / `attachTenancyToViews` via a new `markTenantColumn`
  helper (`context_table.go`). Both `Columns` and `PKColumns` are stamped — they hold
  independent copies of the same column, so writing one leaves the other saying the opposite.
  Nothing re-tests the tenant column against config in a second place (the NW-D1 / FIX-153
  rule).
- **The predicate stays single.** `isIncrementEligible` gains `&& !col.Tenant`, keeping the
  FIX-160 invariant that the client surface, the GraphQL `_inc` / `_dec` operators and the
  `_inc` namespace check cannot drift.
- **Placement differs from the entry's suggestion, for a reason the entry could not see.**
  It proposed `isIncrementEligible` "or its caller, which has the tenancy config." Neither
  held: the predicate sees one column, and its caller `assembleTableContext` runs *before*
  `attachTenancyToTables`, so `TableContext.Tenancy` is nil there. The tenancy map exists by
  then but is never threaded into the exported `BuildTableContexts` (~30 call sites). The
  exclusion therefore lands in the attach pass, which re-runs `buildIncrementColumns` once the
  fact is known — the same shape `promoteTenantFieldToOmittable` already uses.
- **The API skip is gone.** `buildUpdateOps` (`context_api.go`) no longer computes `tenantCol`
  or skips on it; the model-side gate feeds `apiIncrementColumns` ahead of it. The other
  `serverOwnedTenantColumn` call in `buildAPITableContext` stays — that one drives the
  `required:true`-gated update-input *set* field, a different rule.
- **Gate is `Tenanted` alone, not the API's `Tenanted && !InPrimaryKey && Required`.** Decided
  with the user 2026-09-16. PRD's "not exposed on any increment surface" is unqualified, and
  `tenant_id + 1` is arithmetic on an identity whatever `tenancy.required` resolves to — the
  `required:false` cross-tenant path names a target tenant through `Update`, which arithmetic
  cannot do. **Deliberate behavior change beyond the filed defect:** under `required:false` an
  integer tenant column used to get `tenantID_inc` / `tenantID_dec` on GraphQL and now does
  not. The hole was real there too — a non-zero resolver under `required:false` still scopes
  the WHERE.
- **Regression tests** (`gen/tenant_increment_test.go`, alongside the existing
  `counterTenantSchema` fixture): the tenant column is absent from `IncrementColumns` and from
  the rendered `increment.go.tmpl` under both `required` settings; absent from the API's
  `UpdateOps` and from the rendered `UpdateCounterInput`; a table whose only incrementable
  column is the tenant column loses the enum type and the `Increment` method together; an
  untenanted table is unaffected. Confirmed failing-first — reverting the `!col.Tenant` gate
  fails all four.
- **Docs.** PRD §8.2 gained the third eligibility bullet next to the PK and FK ones (the
  eligibility rules live in §8.2, not §9.8 — the §9.8 pointer the entry and
  `TENANT_SCOPED_REFERENCES.md` §5 both used was wrong, and both are corrected). PRD §29.4.2's
  `_inc` / `_dec` sentence was lifted out of the `required:true`-gated update-input subsection,
  where it read as gated on `required`. `guidelines/TEMPLATES.md` §6 gained the
  `ColumnContext.Tenant` wiring rule beside the FK-metadata and UUID ones.
- **Verification.** `make check` clean across 8 modules (0 lint, all `-short -race` green;
  `cmd/sqlgen/gen` ~48s). `TestE2EGoldenFiles` passes **unchanged** — no example has an
  incrementable tenant column (every one is uuid / blob / char), which is exactly why no golden
  ever showed this. `make check-examples` clean across all 12 example modules against real
  databases; working tree carries no regenerated output.
- **A rejection rule silently relaxed, recorded here because nothing else records it.**
  `validateIncDecNamespace` (`context_api.go`) runs inside `buildOneAPITable`, i.e. post-attach,
  so it now reads the same `Tenant` flag. A schema with a tenanted arithmetic column `foo` and a
  sibling column literally named `foo_inc` used to be **rejected** at codegen; it now generates.
  That is the correct direction — no `_inc` operator is emitted for `foo` any more, so there is
  no duplicate input field for gqlgen to choke on, and the error was exactly the "operator pair
  that was never going to be emitted" shape FIX-160 removed elsewhere — but it is a hard error
  that became a non-error, and no test pins either side of it.
- **Scope left open, recorded rather than fixed.** `columnMemberScope` (`reserved_fields.go`)
  and `incrementSQLTypeWarnings` both call into the eligibility predicates during
  `assembleTableContext`, before the flag is stamped, so they stay tenancy-blind: a tenant
  column resolving to Go field `Column` is still rejected as colliding with
  `<T>IncrementColumn`, and a tenant column made arithmetic by a type override on a
  non-arithmetic SQL type still warns. Both need a tenant column that is integer *and* either
  named `Column` or paired with a `<tenant>_inc` sibling. Making them correct means moving
  field validation after tenancy attachment — a larger reorder than this fix warrants.

### FIX-206

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 23, `cmd/sqlgen/cli/diff.go`
- **Surfaced by:** consumer project (2026-09-16) adopting `sqlgen diff` as its Tier-1 CI
  drift gate — "sqlgen diff ... mutates the working tree"

**Issue.** **`sqlgen diff`, specified twice over as writing nothing (PRD §23.1, §23.6), wrote
into the consumer's GraphQL package on every run — and wrote files that did not compile.**
On a GraphQL-enabled project the command reported `no changes detected`, exit 0, while
rewriting thirteen files under `resolver_dir` / `schema_dir`. Five carried a corrupted models
import naming the temp directory the run was about to delete:

```go
// internal/graph/sqlgenresolver/field_options_gen.go:9 — after `sqlgen diff`
database "example.com/proj/var/folders/.../T/sqlgen-diff-4148923310"
```

`go build` then failed with `no required module provides package .../T/sqlgen-diff-...`, and
the tree stayed broken until the next real `generate`. A preview command left the repository
less buildable than it found it.

Two further consequences followed from the same root cause. On a fresh checkout the command
reported `9 files would change (9 created)` — models only — while silently materializing a
half-generated `graph/` tree that had never existed. And because the graph files were written
to their real home rather than to the sandbox, graph drift was structurally invisible to the
comparison: `diff` both under-reported it and destroyed the evidence for it.

Separately, a `file_per_table` project with `manifest.enabled: true` got a standing false
positive — `delete models/manifest_embed_gen.go` — because the manifest stage writes that file
*after* `gen.Generate` returns, so the preview's written set omitted it and the stale sweep
read it as orphaned.

**Root cause.** The command redirected generation by mutating one config field:

```go
cfg.Output.Dir = tmpDir
_, err = gen.Generate(schema, cfg, Version)
```

That moves the models tree and nothing else. `api.graphql.schema_dir` / `resolver_dir` are
**root-relative** (§26.5.8): they are defaulted to `filepath.Join(cfg.Output.Dir, "graph")` at
*config-load time*, before the mutation, and resolved at generate time against
`Options.ProjectRoot` (`"."`), never against `OutputDir`. So the redirect could not reach
them by construction.

The corrupted import is the same mutation seen from the other side. `apiImportDir` derives the
consumer's models import path from `cfg.Output.Dir`, so pointing that field at the temp
directory did not merely move the writes — it changed *what was written*. `Options` already
carried the right separation for this (`OriginalOutputDir` for imports, `ProjectRoot` for
graph writes); the command used neither.

**Fix.** Make the redirect a property of the generator rather than of one config field.

- `Options.WriteRoot` plus `gen.SandboxPath` (`gen/sandbox.go`): every write destination —
  `OutputDir` and the resolved schema / resolver / `sqlgenresolver` dirs alike — is mapped
  under the root before emission sees it. Absolute dirs and `../` climbs are anchored under
  it too, so no path a config can spell escapes.
- `gen.GenerateInto(schema, cfg, version, writeRoot)`; `Generate` is that with the redirect
  off. Import paths and rendered bodies are untouched by it, so a redirected run emits files
  byte-identical to a real one — the property the whole comparison rests on.
- `GenerateResult.WriteDirs` reports where each directory landed. `diff` pairs a preview file
  with its working-tree counterpart from that map instead of re-deriving the generator's path
  resolution, and treats an unmapped directory as an error. Re-deriving it is what let the
  graph dirs escape in the first place.
- `diff` now compares every generated file, not just the top level of `output.dir`, so graph
  drift is reported rather than silently written.
- `gen.StaleFiles` splits the staleness rule out of `CleanStaleFiles` so `diff` previews
  deletions with the same predicate `generate` deletes by, and `gen.ManifestEmbedEnabled` /
  `ManifestEmbedFilename` let `diff` account for the artifact the manifest stage owns.

**Scope note.** The manifest stage is still not previewed: its JSON and markdown carry a
`generated_at` timestamp, so byte-comparing them would report a change on every run. The one
artifact that would otherwise read as stale is handled above.

**Verification.** Failing-first was confirmed per defect rather than in aggregate. Against the
original `diff.go`, `TestDiff_upToDateGraphQLProject_writesNothing`,
`TestDiff_graphPackageUntouched`, `TestDiff_staleSchema_reportsGraphDriftAndWritesNothing`,
`TestDiff_freshProject_createsNothing` and `TestDiff_manifestEmbedNotReportedAsDeleted` all
fail, each naming its own defect. Un-sandboxing the graph dirs alone fails
`TestGenerateInto_redirectsEveryWrite_andKeepsImportsConfigured` on the write-escape
assertion; anchoring `OriginalOutputDir` to the redirect instead fails the same test on the
content assertion, naming the same five files the consumer reported. `SandboxPath` carries a
table plus a never-escapes property test. All twelve E2E golden fixtures are unchanged, which
is the pin that `generate` output did not move.

**Result.** `sqlgen diff` writes nothing — verified byte-for-byte, permissions included, on
both graph topologies (nested `./models/graph` and top-level sibling), on up-to-date, stale,
and never-generated trees. A project that built before a `diff` run builds after it, and
GraphQL drift now appears in the report.

### FIX-205

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 26, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`
