4. Cache invalidation and event publication are **skipped** — the cache
   mutation hook short-circuits on error (`examples/cache/models/cache_gen.go:1648-1650`),
   so the bogus `m.AffectedPKs = []any{0}` set at `upsert.go.tmpl:145` is never
   consumed. Benign in the no-op case (nothing changed), but it means the
   failure is silent to the cache layer rather than corrupting it.
5. Blocks `UpsertWithRelated` (`docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` **E10**, **D11**): a
   nested upsert keys every child write on the parent PK, and a `0` PK — or no
   PK at all — is unusable.

**Root cause — one defect, two dialect-specific triggers.** PRD §9.7 requires
every entity-returning write to resolve a PK and then re-`Get` it. A conflict
that changes nothing breaks that resolution differently per dialect, and both
halves are reachable:

- **MySQL — `LastInsertId()` reports 0.** `upsert.go.tmpl:317-345` resolves the
  PK from `execResult.LastInsertId()`. MySQL's OK packet carries `insert_id = 0`
  for an `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` that modifies no row, so the template then
  calls `c.Get(ctx, 0)`, which finds nothing. `UpsertClause` never emitted the
  `LAST_INSERT_ID(pk)` self-assignment that would preserve the id
  (`sql/mysql.go:57-76`).

  Measured through `go-sql-driver/mysql v1.9.3` against `mysql:8.0`, on a table
  whose `AUTO_INCREMENT` had been advanced past the row under test so a stale id
  would be visible:

  | Statement | `LastInsertId` | `RowsAffected` |
  |---|---|---|
  | insert `a@x` (new; real id 3) | 3 | 1 |
  | upsert `a@x`, **identical** values | **0** | 0 |
  | upsert `a@x`, changed value | 3 | 2 |
  | with `` `id` = LAST_INSERT_ID(`id`) ``, identical | **3** ✅ | 0 (row untouched) |
  | with `` ... ``, changed value | 3 ✅ | 2 |
  | with `` ... ``, brand-new row | 9 ✅ | 1 |

- **PostgreSQL / SQLite — `DO NOTHING` returns no row.** When the conflict
  target covers every inserted column, `updateColumns` is empty and the dialect
  emits `DO NOTHING` (`sql/postgres.go:88-111`, `sql/sqlite.go:61-83`), which
  yields **zero rows**, so the `RETURNING` branch's `QueryRow().Scan()` returned
  the driver's no-rows error. Reachable and already shipped: `tenancy`'s
  `tags(id AUTOINCREMENT PK, workspace_id, name, UNIQUE(workspace_id, name))`
  and its `users` produce an empty `updateColumns`
  (`tenancy/models/models_gen.go:14789`), and the same falls out of any
  surrogate-PK + natural-unique-key lookup table. MySQL hits this trigger too,
  via its `` `k` = `k` `` degenerate form.

  This half was **missed by the original entry**, which claimed a passing
  `postgres` control bounded the defect to the non-`RETURNING` dialect. That
  control only passed because its table leaves a column outside the conflict
  target, so it takes the `DO UPDATE SET` branch.

**References.**

- PRD §9.2 (`Upsert` row), §9.5 "Upsert Conflict Keys", §9.7 "PK Resolution and
  Entity Return Path" — the invariant this breaks. `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md`
  **P17** proposes pinning the mechanism so it is not refactored away.
- `docs/design/archive/NESTED_MUTATIONS.md` **F5** (finding), **D11** (fix as a standalone
  `/fix` rather than folded into the nested-mutation work), **E10**
  (`UpsertWithRelated` eligibility gate), §2.4 probe E (full transcript).
- FIX-195 — prior art for a live correctness defect surfaced outside `/verify`
  and triaged `blocking`.
- **Method note.** A first pass probed the MySQL half with `SELECT
  LAST_INSERT_ID()` from the `mysql` CLI and appeared to show a broader bug — a
  conflict returning a *different* row's id. That was an artifact: `SELECT
  LAST_INSERT_ID()` reads per-session state, while the driver's `LastInsertId()`
  reads the OK packet of the statement itself. Only the driver path is reachable
  from generated code. Re-probe through the driver, not the CLI.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-10.

**Scope widened during implementation.** The entry was filed MySQL-only and
recommended an additive `UpsertPreservePKExpr(pk)` sibling on the interface,
prepended by `sql/builder.go` into the clause. Verification found the
`DO NOTHING` half above, which that shape cannot express: on the `RETURNING`
dialects the repair is not a prepended set-list entry but a change of clause
form, and a builder cannot splice an entry into `DO NOTHING`. `UpsertClause`
was widened instead.

**Fix — `sql/`: one options struct, one dialect that acts on it.**
`UpsertClause(conflictKeys, updateColumns []string)` became
`UpsertClause(opts UpsertClauseOptions)`, carrying `ConflictKeys`,
`UpdateColumns`, and the new `ResolvePKColumn` — the PK the caller must read
back, `""` when it already knows it. `InsertOptions.UpsertResolvePKColumn`
threads it through `BuildInsert`; `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/sql.go:284` passes a bare
probe for its dialect-family sniff.

`MySQLDialect.UpsertClause` opens its set list with
`` `pk` = LAST_INSERT_ID(`pk`) `` when the field is set, republishing the id into
the OK packet without touching the row. It leads the list so no later
`VALUES(...)` assignment can overwrite it, and it subsumes the degenerate
`` `k` = `k` `` form rather than stacking on it. PostgreSQL and SQLite ignore the
field — documented at each implementation, since "why is this ignored here" is
the question the next reader will have.

**Fix — the template: a lookup fallback on the `RETURNING` branch.**
`insertUpsertAndResolveID` now reads through `Query`/`Next` rather than
`QueryRow`/`Scan`, so "no row came back" is a control-flow branch rather than an
error identity to match — no dependence on `sql.ErrNoRows` surviving adapter
error mapping, and no stdlib `database/sql` import in generated code (where
`sql` is already bound to the runtime package). When no row comes back it calls
the new per-client `resolveUpsertConflictRow`, which rebuilds the conflict
columns' values from the parallel `columns`/`args` slices and selects the row.

Three properties that had to be right, and are:

- **The lookup is unambiguous.** Unlike MySQL's `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, an
  explicit `ON CONFLICT (target)` can only have fired on those columns, so the
  select identifies the same row the statement did. (This is also why the
  entry's fallback-`SELECT` alternative was wrong *for MySQL* — probed: a
  statement conflicting on a key other than the named target still returns the
  real row's id via `LAST_INSERT_ID`, where a select on the named target would
  not.)
- **Soft-deleted rows are not excluded.** The unique index matched regardless of
  the soft-delete column, so a soft-deleted row is still the row that conflicted.
- **The result set is closed before the fallback runs.** `conn` may be a
  transaction, where an open result set blocks the next statement on the same
  connection.

The fallback is a second statement, so a concurrent delete between the insert
and the lookup surfaces as `ErrNotFound` — documented on the generated method.
The single-statement alternative (`DO UPDATE SET pk = tbl.pk`) was rejected:
measured on `postgres:16`, three idempotent upserts rewrote the tuple each time
(`ctid (0,1)→(0,4)`, `xmin` bumped) and fired an `AFTER UPDATE` trigger 3 times,
turning a logical no-op into row-lock, bloat and trigger traffic on what is
expected to be a hot path under `UpsertWithRelated`.

**Two further defects found by the post-implementation review, both fixed here.**

- **The fallback bound its scan targets positionally.** `sql.BuildSelect` sorts
  its column list (`writeSelectColumns` → `sortedCopy`); `ReturningClause` does
  not. So for a tenanted table the fallback asked for `(pk, tenant)` and got
  back `(tenant, pk)` whenever the tenant column sorts first — `account_id`,
  `company_id`, `customer_id`. Measured:

  ```
  declared [id account_id]
    SELECT    -> SELECT "account_id", "id" FROM "t" WHERE ...
    RETURNING -> ... RETURNING "id", "account_id"
  ```

  Same Go type on both = a silently wrong PK into `m.AffectedPKs`, the cache key
  and the terminal `Get`. The `tenancy` example escapes only because
  `id < workspace_id`, so the first round of tests could not have caught it. The
  fallback now binds by column name, the rule `scan<Entity>` already follows
  (`get.go.tmpl:21-29`), and `TestUpsertTemplate_conflictRowFallbackBindsByName`
  pins it with a fixture whose tenant column sorts first.

  `captureAffectedTenants` (`client.go.tmpl:351-380`) had the identical latent
  trap on the MySQL mutation paths — same positional scan over a sorted select —
  and was fixed the same way.

- **The composite-PK + tenanted branch still had the original bug.**
  `upsert.go.tmpl:162-182` (tenanted, `RETURNING`, PK caller-known) scanned a
  statement that can be `DO NOTHING` with `QueryRow().Scan(&rowTenant)` — the
  FIX-196 shape on a sibling branch. Latent rather than shipped: the only
  instance, `tenancy_postgres` `line_items`, escapes because `quantity` sits
  outside its conflict target. It now falls back to a single-column tenant
  lookup by the caller-known PK. One column, so no scan-order hazard exists to
  guard, and no cross-template coupling to `$needsInsertResolve`.

  No example covered this shape — which is why it was latent — so the `tenancy`
  example gains `tag_links`, a tenanted pure junction whose columns are exactly
  its composite key plus `workspace_id` (`workspace_id` deliberately outside the
  PK, unlike `order_items`, so the tenant-capture path is the one under test).
  Its `updateColumns` resolves to empty, so the statement is `DO NOTHING`
  + `RETURNING "workspace_id"` — zero rows on conflict, the exact input the old
  `QueryRow().Scan()` failed on.

**`ErrNotFound` is now actually returned.** The first round documented "a
concurrent delete … surfaces as `ErrNotFound`" but returned the driver's raw
no-rows error — neither adapter maps it — which is the un-mapped shape this very
entry called out as worse than a sentinel. The fallback now detects the empty
result set with `!rows.Next()` and returns `ErrNotFound` explicitly.

**Not changed, deliberately.** The manifest renders the set list as the
`<excluded>` token, so the MySQL `LAST_INSERT_ID` entry and the fallback
`SELECT` do not appear in the published SQL body. That is consistent with how
the manifest already treats call-time-assembled clauses and secondary statements
(the pre-existing `captureAffectedTenants` select and the terminal `Get` are
likewise absent), so it under-describes without misdescribing.

**Regression tests.** Five new E2E cases, each confirmed to fail on the pre-fix tree
and pass after (`git stash` round trip), plus one control that passed before and
after so the branch boundary is pinned:

| Example | Test | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `mysql` | `TestUpsertIdempotent` | `LastInsertId() = 0`, non-empty `updateColumns` |
| `mysql` | `TestUpsertIdempotent_EmptyUpdateColumns` | degenerate `` `k` = `k` `` form |
| `postgres` | `TestUpsertIdempotent_EmptyUpdateColumns` | `DO NOTHING` + `RETURNING` |
| `postgres` | `TestUpsertIdempotent_NonEmptyUpdateColumns` | control — passed before the fix |
| `tenancy` (sqlite) | `TestUpsert_IdempotentEmptyUpdateColumns` | `DO NOTHING` on a tenanted table; asserts the captured tenant |
| `tenancy` (sqlite) | `TestUpsert_IdempotentEmptyUpdateColumnsPerTenant` | two tenants, same name — pins that the fallback is bounded by the conflict columns |
| `tenancy` (sqlite) | `TestUpsert_IdempotentCompositePKTenantCapture` | the caller-known-PK branch, on a new `tag_links` table |

The existing `mysql` `TestUpsert` (`crud_test.go:553`) could not have caught
this: it targets `ProductConflictPK` without supplying an `id`, so the
`AUTO_INCREMENT` value is always fresh and neither call takes a conflict branch.

Plus `TestUpsertTemplate_conflictRowFallbackBindsByName`, a generator test with
a tenant column that sorts before the PK — verified to fail when the
name-matched binding is reverted.

Dialect-clause coverage added to `sql/mysql_test.go` (both `ResolvePKColumn`
forms), `sql/postgres_test.go` and `sql/sqlite_test.go` (the field must not
change the SQL). `make check` and `make check-examples` pass; `make
update-golden` and `make update-golden-e2e` regenerated.

**Known limitation, pre-existing and out of scope.** When the conflicting row is
soft-deleted, the fallback resolves its PK correctly but the chained
`c.Get(ctx, id, ...)` applies the read path's soft-delete filter, so `Upsert`
returns `ErrNotFound`. This is unchanged from the `DO UPDATE SET` branch, which
behaves the same way, and there is no `IncludeDeleted` call option to opt out of
it. Worth a `/fix add` if a consumer hits it.

### FIX-195

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 11, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/shared/_filter.tmpl` + PRD §11.1
- **Surfaced by:** consumer app GraphQL report (2026-09-10)

**Issue.** **A top-level `or` compiled to `AND`, so a union filter returned no
rows.** Reported from a consumer app: with tasks `alpha(DONE,HIGH)`,
`bravo(TODO,HIGH)`, `charlie(DONE,LOW)`, the query

```graphql
taskList(filter: { or: [ { status: { eq: TODO } }, { priority: { eq: LOW } } ] })
```

returned `[]` instead of `{bravo, charlie}` — it evaluated `TODO AND LOW`.

**Two facets, one cause.** The generated body appended one `sql.Or(subConds...)`
**per member** straight onto `conds`:

1. **Across members.** `buildWhere` joins `conds` with `AND`
   (`sql/builder.go:479`), so `or: [A, B]` compiled to `A AND B`. `and` worked
   only incidentally — the outer list is AND-ed either way.
2. **Within a member.** For a lone member with two fields,
   `or: [{status, priority}]`, that same wrapper OR-ed the member's **own**
   fields against each other. A filter object's own fields are always
   conjunctive.

**Measured, not assumed.** Against the `sqlite` example through the real client,
before the fix:

| Filter | Emitted SQL |
|---|---|
| `or: [{title=a}, {sku=b}]` | `WHERE (title = ?) AND (sku = ?)` |
| `or: [{title=a, sku=b}]` | `WHERE (sku = ? OR title = ?)` |
| `and: [{or: [{title=a},{sku=b}]}]` | `WHERE ((title = ?) AND (sku = ?))` |

The GraphQL surface and its translator were **not** at fault:
`filter_translate.go.tmpl` maps `or` → `Or` as a straight pass-through with no
semantic transform. The defect was purely in SQL compilation, and the DSL is
unchanged.

**Root cause — normative, not accidental.** PRD §11.1 spells the generated
`ToConditions` body out verbatim as the reference implementation, and that
sample carried the inverted composition. The template implemented the PRD
faithfully. The behavior had therefore been documented as intended in four
places — `phase-14.md`, `phase-25.md`, and two `STATUS.md` notes — each
teaching the "a union is ONE entry carrying both predicates" workaround to
future test authors, and three tests pinned it deliberately
(`TestFilter_AndOrComposition_*` on all three dialects,
`TestRelationshipFilterAPI_RelationshipUnderOr`, and the `sqlite` and `tenancy`
composition tests). §11.1's own prose said the opposite of its code sample
("`Or` — compose conditions with OR"), and `STATUS.md` recorded the conflict as
an **open decision**: "the open decision about whether that reading should
change before the phase closes stands." This fix takes that decision.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-10.

**Fix: one group condition, not N.** Each `Or` member now contributes
`sql.And(...)` of its own conditions, and the members are OR-ed together as a
single group appended to `conds`:

```go
var orGroup []sql.Condition
for _, sub := range f.Or {
	subConds := sub.ToConditions(dialect, opts...)
	if len(subConds) > 0 {
		orGroup = append(orGroup, sql.And(subConds...))
	}
}
if len(orGroup) > 0 {
	conds = append(conds, sql.Or(orGroup...))
}
```

Because `ToConditions` recurses on the same method, `or` nested inside `and`
(and the mirror) is fixed by the same change. `opts` threading is preserved on
the recursive call, so relationship-filter and tenant predicates still compose.

**The empty-group guard is load-bearing.** `sql.Or` of nothing expands to a
literal `"()"` (`expandComposition`), and `buildWhere` keeps any clause that is
not the empty string — so an unguarded group emits a syntax error. `len(orGroup)
> 0` covers both an empty `or` and an `or` whose every member compiled to
nothing.

**`and` is untouched.** The regenerated diff is uniform across all 256 filter
structs in every example: the `Or` block and its comment, and nothing else.
Tables and views share `shared/filter` (`orchestrate.go:458`, `:473`), so views
are covered by the same change.

**PRD §11.1 amended.** The reference body carries the new composition, and the
field-list prose now states the rule explicitly in both directions: each
member's own fields are AND'd; only `Or`-list membership is disjunctive. The
four tracker notes teaching the old workaround are struck through and point
here.

**Regression tests.** Codegen: `TestFilterTemplate_andOrRecursion`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/filter_test.go`) asserts the emitted group shape and carries a
**negative** assertion against the old spelling — the previous version only
checked that `f.Or` and `sql.Or` appeared somewhere, which both readings
satisfy. Compiled form: `filter_composition_test.go` in the `postgres` example's
generated package (the FIX-190 pattern — the test runs the emitted body, in both
`models/` and `expected/`) asserts the built SQL for members-OR, member-fields-
AND, `and` unchanged, `or` under `and` and `and` under `or`, a single member,
an empty `or`, and a member that compiles to nothing. Behavior:
`TestFilter_OrUnion_SQLite` drives the reported alpha/bravo/charlie shape and a
nested `and`-over-`or` case through real SQL. Its predicates deliberately live
on **different columns** — the pre-existing `AndOrComposition` tests put both
`or` branches on `price`, which is why they passed while the union was broken.
The three dialect `AndOrComposition` tests and the `tenancy` / GraphQL
composition tests were rewritten to the natural spelling, with the
member-conjunction half asserted alongside.

**Verified failing-first.** The compiled-form test was run against the
un-regenerated `models/` and reported exactly the pre-fix SQL in its `got`
column, with the `and` and empty-group cases already passing.

### FIX-194

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 11, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/shared/_filter.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-193 implementation (2026-09-10)

**Issue.** **A nil filter dereferenced nil instead of returning `ErrEmptyFilter`,
so the sentinel the PRD documents for exactly that input was unreachable.**
`UpdateWhere`, `SoftDeleteWhere`, `RestoreWhere` and `HardDeleteWhere` each
document "Returns ErrEmptyFilter when the filter is nil or produces no
conditions", and PRD §10 states it for all four by name — "ErrEmptyFilter is
returned when any \*Where operation (UpdateWhere, SoftDeleteWhere, RestoreWhere,
HardDeleteWhere) is called with a nil or empty filter. Prevents accidental bulk
operations." But each method reaches that decision through
`conds := filter.ToConditions(…)`, and `ToConditions` had no nil-receiver
guard, so the dereference happened before the emptiness check could run.

**Measured, not assumed.** Through the real client surface the fault is not a
crash: the hook framework's panic handler recovers it, so the caller gets

```
sqlgen: panic in update_where .articles: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

for all four methods, with `errors.Is(err, ErrEmptyFilter) == false`. The bulk
operation is still prevented — the guard's stated purpose holds — but the error
is a recovered nil dereference rather than the documented sentinel, so a caller
branching on `ErrEmptyFilter` falls through to its unknown-error path.

**Second reachable shape, same cause.** A nil entry inside `And` / `Or`
(`And: []*ArticleFilter{nil}`) hit the same dereference through the composition
loop's `sub.ToConditions(…)`. Outside a client method — a consumer calling
`ToConditions` directly — nothing recovers it. This also left the filter tree
inconsistent with itself: `usesRelationshipFilter` (FIX-193) nil-checks its
receiver and recurses through the same two loops, so the two traversals of one
tree disagreed on whether a nil node was legal.

**Root cause.** PRD §11.1 spells the generated `ToConditions` body out verbatim
as the reference implementation, and that sample opens directly on
`var conds []sql.Condition`. The per-field nil-checks it prescribes are for the
comparator *fields*; nothing covered the receiver. Every read-path call site
(`GetMany`, `Count`, `ExistsWhere`, `Stream`, and both view methods) guards with
`if filter != nil` before calling, which is why the gap never showed there — the
four `*Where` methods are the only call sites that pass the filter through
unguarded, by design, because emptiness is what they are testing for.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-10.

**Fix: one guard, at the single point of dereference.** `ToConditions` returns
`nil` for a nil receiver. The four `*Where` methods then see `len(conds) == 0`
and return `ErrEmptyFilter` through the path they already had — no call-site
change, and no new branch to keep in sync across four templates. The `And` / `Or`
loops skip a nil entry for the same reason, which matches the "an unset (nil)
relationship member contributes no SQL" rule §11.1 already states for members
and aligns the traversal with `usesRelationshipFilter`.

**PRD §11.1 reconciled.** Its reference body now carries the guard, so the
sample no longer contradicts §10's sentinel contract. No behavioral text
changed — this is the documentation catching up to the rule it already stated
elsewhere.

**Regression tests.** Codegen: `TestFilterTemplate_toConditionsNilReceiverGuard`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/filter_test.go`) pins the guard as the *first* statement of the
rendered body, so a future edit cannot move it below a field dereference.
Behavior: `nil_filter_test.go` in the `postgres` example's generated package
(the FIX-190 pattern — the test runs the emitted body, in both `models/` and
`expected/`) covers the nil receiver, a nil entry alone in `And` and in `Or`, a
nil entry beside a real one (the surviving condition is still emitted), a nil
entry nested two levels deep, all four `*Where` methods driven through the real
client returning `ErrEmptyFilter`, and a non-nil-but-empty filter — the last so
the guard is proven additive rather than the only path to the sentinel. All
verified failing-first against the pre-fix golden.

**Verification.** `make update-golden` + `make update-golden-e2e` clean. Golden
churn is wide but uniform — the guard lands in every filter type in every
example, tables and views alike — and is the same four lines everywhere. Full
`cmd/sqlgen` suite green; all 12 example modules build and test; 0 lint.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/shared/_filter.tmpl` — `ToConditions`, the guard.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/{update,delete}.go.tmpl` — the four call sites
  that pass an unguarded filter, deliberately.
- `database/errors.go` — `ErrEmptyFilter`.
- PRD §10 (sentinel list), §11.1 (the reference body, now carrying the guard).
- `FIX-193` — surfaced this while threading the filter into `filterOptions`.

### FIX-193

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 25 (25.11), `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/client.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** consumer E2E in `../sqlgen-test` (2026-09-10)

**Issue.** **`filterOptions` resolved the tenant on every filter-accepting call,
whether or not the filter carried a relationship member — so a fail-closed
resolver vetoed reads that have no tenanted component at all.** In the consumer
app `go test ./...` failed wholesale at setup with
`get users: tenancy: tenant missing from context`, on `users` — a **shared**
table (§29.2.3 rule 3) whose own `WHERE` is never tenant-scoped, read during
register / login / `me`, all of which legitimately run before any workspace is
selected. Every filter-accepting method on such a client was affected:
`GetMany`, `Count`, `ExistsWhere`, `Stream`, `UpdateWhere`, `SoftDeleteWhere`,
`RestoreWhere`, `HardDeleteWhere` (and `Paginate` / `Connection` through the
first two). The only consumer-side workaround was `tenancy.required: false`,
which would have gutted the fail-closed posture the app is built on.

**Root cause.** 25.11 introduced `filterOptions` to carry the target's tenant
predicate into a relationship filter's correlated `EXISTS` (§11.1 invariant 1)
and called it unconditionally at all eight sites, ahead of the conditions being
built. But the `FilterOption` set it returns is read **only** by the emitted
`filterExists*` helpers, which run only for a non-nil relationship member — so
on a filter with no member the resolve was dead work whose failure modes were
still live.

The `required:false` emission did not absorb it. A shared table reaches the
client template through `backfillRelationshipFilterTenancy`
(`context_relfilter.go`), which leaves `Tenancy.Required` false, so
`resolveTenant` maps a **zero** resolver return to `(zero, false, nil)` — but it
propagates a resolver **error** unconditionally, and `tenancy/tenancy.go`
explicitly blesses the other spelling: "Resolvers that want a clearer diagnostic
can return `ErrMissing` explicitly." The consumer's resolver does exactly that,
so the unscoped-rather-than-fail-closed branch was never reached.

**Why no test caught it.** No example schema pairs a shared parent with a
tenanted list target. `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` records the fixture choice that
avoided it under 25.12 — pointing an untenanted parent at `workspace_notes`
"would have flipped that parent to `HasTenantedRelationshipFilter`, and under
this example's `tenancy.required: true` every previously-unscoped read of it
would start returning `ErrMissing`." The hazard was identified and designed
around rather than fixed. The gen fixture that *does* have the shape
(`categories` in `relFilterTables`) is only ever rendered, never run, and
`TestRelationshipFilters_SharedParentRendersTenantedClient` asserted the
signature compiled — not what it did.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-10.

**Measured first, on the real consumer.** A read of `users` with an
email-comparator filter and no Active Workspace, against a client built with the
app's own resolver, returns `get users: tenancy: tenant missing from context`
before any database round-trip. Post-fix the same call clears the tenant path
entirely.

**Fix: gate the resolve on the filter, at the one place that knows.**
`shared/_filter.tmpl` emits `usesRelationshipFilter()` per filter type — the
per-field nil-checks `ToConditions` already uses, plus recursion through `And` /
`Or` so a member nested in a boolean group counts. `filterOptions` short-circuits
on `skipTenancy || !filter.usesRelationshipFilter()`, and the eight call sites
pass the filter they were about to compile (`input.Filter` for `GetMany` /
`Stream`, the `filter` parameter elsewhere).

**The gate cannot loosen §11.1 invariant 1.** Only the `filterExists*` helpers
read the option set, so a filter with no relationship member compiles to
identical conditions with or without a tenant —
`TestToConditionsIgnoresScopeWithoutRelationshipMember` pins that premise with
`cmp.Diff` rather than leaving it asserted in a comment. Whenever a member *is*
set the resolve happens exactly as before, so a member reaching a tenanted
target still fails closed against a resolver that errors.

**Emission is gated on `HasTenantedRelationshipFilter`**, the same fixpoint that
gates `filterOptions` itself, so filters in packages that never reach a tenanted
target — and every filter when tenancy is off — regenerate byte-identically.
`TestRelationshipFilters_UntenantedFilterOmitsGate` pins that.

**Regression tests.** Codegen: `TestRelationshipFilters_SharedParentRendersTenantedClient`
gained the gate assertion, and `TestRelationshipFilters_SharedParentGatesTenantResolve`
renders the filter template for the same shared parent (`categories`, no tenant
column, tenanted target) and pins the predicate, its per-member checks, and the
`And` / `Or` recursion. Behavior: `filter_options_test.go` in the `tenancy`
example's generated package (the FIX-190 pattern — the test runs the *emitted*
helper, in both `models/` and `expected/`), table-driven over nil filter, no
members, a column comparator only, empty `And` / `Or` groups, each direct
member, and members nested one and two levels deep, asserting both the resolver
invocation count and the error. Plus `SkipTenancy` still winning ahead of the
gate, and `CallOptions.Tenant` (§29.4.4) scoping the subquery without consulting
the resolver. All verified failing-first against the pre-fix template and
against the pre-fix golden.

**Open question, deliberately not decided here.** A shared table's `resolveTenant`
is emitted in its `required:false` form, because `backfillRelationshipFilterTenancy`
constructs `TableTenancyContext{Tenanted: false}` and never carries a `required`
setting across. With the gate in place that is only reachable when a relationship
member *is* set and the resolver returns the **zero value** rather than an error:
the subquery then goes unscoped, i.e. a cross-tenant existence probe under
`tenancy.required: true`. A resolver that returns `ErrMissing` — the spelling
`tenancy/tenancy.go` recommends — fails closed instead. The two blessed spellings
of "no tenant" therefore disagree on a shared parent. Closing it means
propagating `Required` across the relationship-filter fixpoint (a table's
effective required = OR over the tenanted targets it reaches); the PRD does not
state the rule, so it is flagged rather than guessed.

**Verification.** `make update-golden` + `make update-golden-e2e` clean;
golden churn confined to the `tenancy` and `graphql` examples (the only ones with
`filterOptions`). All example modules build. The consumer app in `../sqlgen-test`
regenerates and `go test ./...` passes end to end against live containers — the
suite the regression blocked.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/shared/_filter.tmpl` — `usesRelationshipFilter`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/client.go.tmpl` — `filterOptions` and its gate.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_relfilter.go` — `backfillRelationshipFilterTenancy`,
  `resolveTenantedRelationshipFilters` (the fixpoint).
- `tenancy/tenancy.go` — `TenantResolver`, `ErrMissing`, and the "return
  `ErrMissing` explicitly" allowance the required:false branch does not cover.
- PRD §11.1 (relationship filters, `FilterOption`), §29.2.3 rule 3 (shared
  tables), §29.3.1 (fail-closed), §29.4.4 (explicit tenant).
- `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` — 25.11 / 25.12 notes, including the fixture choice
  that kept the shape out of the examples.

### FIX-192

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` (+ `gen/api_walker.go`)
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-187 auto-review (2026-09-08)

**Issue.** **`rowIdentityFields` picks the columns the walker projects without
consulting API readability, so "every column the walker projects is one it also
emits a `case` arm for" holds by coincidence rather than by construction.**
FIX-187 made the walker project an entity's row identity whenever a selection
set asks for the row but names no column. `rowIdentityFields`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go`) resolves that set from `PKColumns`, then a
view's `CursorKeys`, then `Columns[0]` — none of which is filtered by
`§32.2` access. A restricted column reached that way would be projected into
the `SELECT` by a walker whose own switch has no arm for it.

**Root cause.** Two facts outside the function keep it correct today, and
neither is stated where the function lives:

1. §32.4 hard-errors on a restricted **PK** column
   (`cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:1176`), so the first branch is always
   readable.
2. `context_view.go:142-148` gives every view column the `public` role —
   "views have no column_map" — so the second and third branches are readable
   too.

Fact 2 is the fragile one: it is a property of views having no per-column
access surface *yet*, not a rule anyone stated. A verification pass over all
five generated examples (60 walkers) confirms every projected field currently
has a matching readable `case` arm, so there is no reachable defect — this is
the guard, not a bug report.

**Suggested fix.**
- Extend `ValidateAPIWalkerCompleteness` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_walker.go`) with a
  third check: every `APITableContext.RowIdentityFields` entry must name a field
  that is present in `Fields` **and** `Readable`. The function already owns both
  directions of the readable/`case` correspondence (§26.5.2 as amended by
  §32.3), takes the `APIEntity` + `APITableContext` pair the check needs, and is
  already wired into `buildOneAPITable` / `buildOneAPIView` so it hard-errors
  under `sqlgen validate` as well as `sqlgen generate` (25.2). No new call site.
- Message shape should match the existing two: name the entity, the column, and
  why — a restricted column cannot be projected because the walker emits no case
  for it.
- **Regression tests:** a negative test per branch — a table whose PK is marked
  restricted (which §32.4 rejects earlier, so this is defense in depth), and a
  view fixture whose row identity resolves to a column marked non-readable —
  asserting the lint errors and names the column; plus a positive case pinning
  that a public row identity still validates.

**Relationship to `FIX-188`.** Same access surface, opposite direction. FIX-188
covers a restricted `cursor_keys` column reaching the *edge cursor*; this covers
one reaching the *projection*. FIX-187's resolution notes record that its
PK-first choice separates the two wherever a PK exists — on the PK-less-view
path it does not, and this lint is what would close that gap by construction.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `rowIdentityFields`, the unfiltered resolver.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_walker.go` — `ValidateAPIWalkerCompleteness`, the intended
  home for the assertion.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go:142-148` — the "every view column is public"
  fact the second and third branches lean on.
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:1176` — the §32.4 PK rule the first branch
  leans on.
- PRD §26.5.2 (walker completeness, amended by §32.3), §32.2 / §32.4 — the role
  set and the validation half.
- `FIX-187` — added `rowIdentityFields`; `FIX-188` — the sibling access gap.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-10. The premise was re-verified
before any code was written: a sweep over the five generated examples confirmed
all 58 emitted walkers currently satisfy the invariant (every row-identity field
has a matching readable `case` arm), so this landed as the guard it was filed
as, not as a bug fix.

**The defect shape is real once the §32.4 gate is bypassed.** Measured by
driving `BuildTableContexts` → `BuildAPIContext` with
`column_map.id.access: internal` on a two-column table — the gen layer does not
re-run config validation, so the restricted PK reaches `rowIdentityFields`
intact. The pre-fix walker emitted no `case "id"` arm and still wrote
`fo.ID = true` in the identity block, and the existing lint passed it: the
`case` direction was satisfied, so the third direction is genuinely additive
rather than a restatement. That measurement is now
`TestRowIdentity_LintRejectsRestrictedPK`, which drives the real resolver chain
rather than a hand-built context.

**Implementation.** `ValidateAPIWalkerCompleteness` delegates to a new
`validateAPIRowIdentityProjection` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_walker.go`) after its
two existing loops, so a missing- or dead-`case` error still reports first. The
check keys on `GoFieldName` rather than `SQLName` — `RowIdentityFields` carries
Go field names, and both spell `ColumnContext.FieldName`, so the two keyings
name the same column. Three directions: every entry must name a column of the
entity, that column must be API-readable, and the list must be non-empty. No
new call site; `sqlgen validate` picks it up through `ValidateGeneration` →
`BuildAPIContext` exactly as `generate` does.

**The non-emptiness direction was added beyond the filed scope, deliberately.**
It closes the opposite failure — an entity that can project something but names
nothing walks to an all-false `FieldOptions`, which §9.6 reads as "no rows
wanted". Without it, a future change that filtered `rowIdentityFields` by
readability would silently reopen `FIX-187` for one entity rather than failing.

**Scope decision: an entity with zero API-readable columns is exempt.** Its
walker emits no `case` clauses and its schema type no fields, so no selection
can reach the walker and there is no projection/`case` correspondence left to
hold. That state is itself invalid — §32.4 requires a readable PK, and
`schema.graphqls.tmpl:9-20` would emit an empty `type <T> {}` gqlgen rejects —
but it is reachable only by bypassing config validation, which
`TestAPIFilterRelationships_UnreadableTargetDropped` does deliberately to pin
the §26.5.3 target-exposure gate. Diagnosing it belongs to the rule that owns
it, not to a row-identity message; without the exemption that test's branch
becomes unreachable through `BuildAPIContext`. The carve-out is stated on the
function.

**Regression tests.** `TestRowIdentity_LintRejectsRestrictedPK` (config-driven,
end-to-end) plus table-driven `TestRowIdentity_LintDirections` covering the
restricted-PK branch, a restricted view column (a view takes no `column_map`,
so the cursor-key / first-column branches are only reachable hand-built), a
restricted column placed *second* in a multi-entry identity so the loop is
proven not to stop at the first readable one, an identity naming no column of
the entity, the empty-identity case, and both positive controls. All five
negative cases were re-run against the pre-fix function to confirm they fail
first. `TestValidateAPIWalkerCompleteness_Access`'s hand-built fixtures now
carry `RowIdentityFields` + `GoFieldName`, per the TESTING.md §11 rule that
unit fixtures populate what production always wires.

**Auto-review follow-ups, applied inline.** Three low-severity findings, no
blockers. (1) The carve-out's justification said "no selection can reach the
walker", which is wrong — a parent's relationship case descends into a target's
walker regardless of the target's readability (`mapRelationshipToGraphQL` does
not gate on it), so the comment now rests the exemption on the state being
unreachable through a validated config rather than on the walker being
unreachable. (2) `TestWalker_CompletenessLint_NegativeTest`'s two fixtures
carry `RowIdentityFields` for the same TESTING.md §11 reason as the access
ones. (3) `examples/graphql/tests/walker_lint_test.go` pins the lint's
user-visible message strings so reshapes surface in the example matrix; the
three new messages are now pinned there too.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all modules; `make check-examples`
clean against live PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite containers — both re-run after
the review follow-ups. Zero golden churn — the lint emits no output, confirmed
by a clean `git status` after example regeneration.

### FIX-191

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/connection_walker.go.tmpl`
  and `api/field_options.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-187 auto-review (2026-09-08)

**Issue.** **When one selection set names the same field twice under different
aliases, the walker keeps one alias and silently returns zero values for the
others.** Measured against the `graphql` example on a live PostgreSQL 16
container, one seeded user with one order:

| Query | Returns |
|---|---|
| `users(first:1) { a: edges { node { email } } b: edges { node { name } } }` | `a.node.email: ""`, `b.node.name` correct |
| `users(first:1) { a: … b: … c: edges { node { isActive } } }` (3 aliases) | only `c` correct; `a` and `b` zero |
| `userList(limit:1) { a: items { email } b: items { name } }` | `a.email: ""`, `b.name` correct |
| `user(id:) { x: orders { total } y: orders { createdAt } }` | `x[0].total: "0"`, `y[0].createdAt` correct |
| `user(id:) { p: name q: email }` (aliased plain columns) | both correct — the immune case |

No error is raised. `email` is `String!` and `total` is `Decimal!` on the
generated schema, so the response carries a well-formed value that is simply
wrong — the Go zero value of a column the `SELECT` never fetched.

**Root cause.** The walker is not alias-aware, and the aliased entries reach it
intact: gqlgen's `CollectFields` returns one `CollectedField` per alias, all
carrying the same `Name`. Plain columns survive that because their case arm is
an idempotent `fo.<F> = true` — setting the same flag from two aliases is a
no-op. Every other arm **assigns** and therefore overwrites:

- `unwrapConnectionFields` (`api/connection_walker.go.tmpl:46-68`) assigns
  `entityFields` per `edges` / `items` entry, so the last alias with a `node`
  wins.
- each relationship arm (`api/field_options.go.tmpl:73-83`) assigns
  `fo.<Rel> = …FromCollected(...)`, so the last aliased relationship wins.

**FIX-187 flipped which alias survives at the envelope but did not create the
bug.** The pre-fix helper `return`ed inside the loop, so the *first* alias won —
measured on the same fixture with the pre-fix generated walker: `a.node.email`
correct, `b.node.name` empty. Both are under-selection; the fix moved the loss
from the tail to the head. The relationship arm is untouched by FIX-187 and has
always been last-wins.

**Suggested fix.**
- Union rather than assign. `entityFields` is already accumulated across the
  loop, so both envelope sites become `append(entityFields,
  graphql.CollectFields(...)...)`; duplicate `CollectedField` entries are
  harmless to the walker, which reads only `Name` and `Selections` and whose
  column arms are idempotent.
- The relationship arm needs a merge, not an append: two aliases produce two
  `*<Target>FieldOptions` trees that have to be OR-ed field by field, and the
  `RelationshipOptions` wrapper also carries `Filter` / `Sorts`. **Decide the
  semantics before writing it** — two aliases of the same relationship with
  *different* nested arguments are a legitimate request the flat `[Type!]!`
  relationship shape (PRD §26.4, no per-relationship pagination) cannot express
  as two independent loads. Options: union the projections and accept that both
  aliases render from one load (correct for the measured cases, which differ
  only in selected columns); or reject the query at the walker with a
  descriptive error rather than answering it wrongly.
- Whatever is chosen, state it in §26.5.2 next to the fragment/directive
  paragraph — that paragraph already delegates alias resolution to gqlgen and
  says "the walker only sees real field names", which is exactly the sentence
  that hides this.
- **Regression tests:** a `gen` test that both envelope sites append; E2Es for
  each measured row above, verified failing-first; and a pin on the aliased
  plain-column row so the idempotent case is not broken by the merge.

**Reachability is low but the failure is silent.** Nothing in the checked-in
examples or goldens issues an aliased duplicate selection; a consumer writing
one gets a well-typed wrong answer with no error, which is why this is tracked
rather than a nit despite the low reachability.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/connection_walker.go.tmpl:46-68` — the two
  envelope assignment sites.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/field_options.go.tmpl:73-83` — the relationship
  arm, the site FIX-187 did not touch.
- PRD §26.5.2 "Fragment & directive handling" — the paragraph that delegates
  aliasing to gqlgen and needs the carve-out.
- PRD §26.4 — the flat `[Type!]!` relationship shape that makes two aliased
  relationship loads inexpressible.
- `FIX-187` — flipped the envelope half from first-wins to last-wins and made
  the union a two-line change; not the origin of the defect.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-10. The measurement table was
reproduced first on the `graphql` example against a live PostgreSQL 16
container — all four defect rows and the immune row landed exactly as filed —
and every regression test below was re-run against the pre-fix generated walker
to confirm it fails first.

**Semantics: union, not rejection.** The open question in the suggested fix
resolves structurally rather than by preference. A relationship field takes no
GraphQL arguments — `schema.graphqls.tmpl` emits `{{ $r.GraphQLName }}:
{{ $r.GraphQLType }}` with no argument list, because the relationship shape is a
flat `[Type!]!` (PRD §26.4) and relationship filter / sort args are deferred
(PRD §26.12) — so two aliases of one relationship can differ *only* in what
they select, never in what they would load. There is no divergent-argument
request to reject; rejecting would refuse a query that has one unambiguous
correct answer. And gqlgen renders every alias from the single value the
resolver returned, so a projection covering both aliases makes both correct off
one load. Pinned by `TestAliases_RelationshipCostsOneQuery`: two aliases of one
O2M relationship still cost `1 + 1` queries, so §25.1 is unchanged.

**Mechanism: coalesce before the switch, not merge after it.** Rather than
teaching each relationship arm to merge two `*<Target>FieldOptions` trees, the
fields are collapsed *before* the loop by a new shared helper,
`coalesceAliases`, emitted once alongside `unwrapConnectionFields`. It returns
one entry per distinct field name carrying the union of the sub-selections
every alias of that name collected, which restores the invariant every `case`
arm is already written against — a name is handled exactly once — so no arm
needs to know aliasing happened. Three consequences made this preferable to a
per-type merge: it fixes the envelope and the walker with one idea; it adds one
shared helper instead of a recursive merge function per entity; and row
identity (FIX-187) is still evaluated exactly once, against the fully-unioned
result, so an alias naming no column cannot push identity columns onto a
sibling alias that does. A merge-in-place variant (`<T>FieldOptionsInto`) was
considered and rejected for that last reason — it makes the over-fetch
alias-order-dependent.

**One non-obvious constraint.** The union is built at the
`[]graphql.CollectedField` level — collecting each alias's own selections and
appending the results — never by concatenating the underlying
`ast.SelectionSet`s. gqlgen keys its per-request `CollectFields` cache on the
*address and length* of the selection set passed in
(`graphql/collect_fields_cache_store.go:62-79`, a `uintptr` the cache does not
retain), so a slice synthesized by the walker could be collected and its
address recycled by a later same-length allocation, taking a stale cache hit.
For the same reason the merge allocates a fresh slice instead of appending onto
its base: the base is gqlgen's own cached result, and appending into its spare
capacity writes through into memory gqlgen still owns. That is not theoretical
— `TestCoalesceAliases_DoesNotAppendIntoGqlgensCache` catches an in-place
append, and it was observed doing so when mutation-tested.

**Changes.**
- `api/connection_walker.go.tmpl` — new `coalescedField` / `coalesceAliases` /
  `indexCoalesced`; both envelope sites now union (`append(entityFields,
  …Sub...)`) and both loops run over the coalesced view.
- `api/field_options.go.tmpl` — the walker loop runs over
  `coalesceAliases(opCtx, fields)`; every relationship arm consumes `f.Sub`
  instead of re-collecting `f.Selections`. The fragment/directive doc comment
  gains the carve-out.
- `docs/PRD.md` §26.5.2 — two new paragraphs after "Fragment & directive
  handling": the `(Name, Alias)` grouping and why the old sentence hid it, and
  the union rule with its query-count, row-identity and cache-key consequences.
- Goldens regenerated for the five examples that emit a walker (`graphql`,
  `graphql_null_wrappers`, `graphql_top_level`, `mysql`, `sqlite`).

**Coverage.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_walker_test.go` — `TestWalker_ConnectionUnwrap` pins both
  envelope sites appending and adds `mustNotContain` on the old assignment;
  `TestWalker_FragmentAndDirectiveCoverage` pins the coalesced loop, and moves
  the `CollectFields(opCtx, f.Selections, nil)` assertion onto the shared
  emission, which is where that call now lives.
- `graphql/models/graph/sqlgenresolver/coalesce_aliases_test.go` — behavior
  coverage on the *emitted* helper (the FIX-190 pattern), table-driven over
  empty input, pass-through, aliased leaf columns, two- and three-way
  relationship unions, and first-position stability, plus the cache
  non-mutation test. Mutation-tested: last-wins merge, no coalescing, and an
  in-place append each fail a distinct case.
- `graphql/tests/walker_alias_test.go` — one E2E per measurement row plus the
  aliased `node` case and an O2O case, the immune aliased-plain-column pin, the
  query-count pin and a count-only short-circuit pin. All six defect tests
  verified failing first against the pre-fix walker; the three pins correctly
  passed pre-fix.

**One row the report did not measure.** The O2O arm was affected too, and by
the same mechanism: it assigns a bare `*<Target>FieldOptions` rather than a
`RelationshipOptions` wrapper, so it was last-wins like the list arm. It is
worth separating because an O2O target rides the parent's JOIN rather than a
separate fetch, so the losing alias renders zero values off a row that *was*
joined correctly — `m: primaryDocument { name } n: primaryDocument
{ entityType }` returned `m.name: ""` pre-fix. Covered by
`TestAliases_OneToOneRelationship`, verified failing-first.

### FIX-190

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_shared.go`
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-185 auto-review (2026-09-07)

**Issue.** **The generated `unionColumns` helper has no direct unit coverage —
its semantics are only observed through rendered templates and E2E behavior.**
The helper is emitted as a Go source string
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_shared.go:220-243`), so nothing type-checks or
exercises it inside the `gen` module. Three properties it is relied on for go
unasserted: de-duplication when a required column is already selected or is
repeated across the variadic, correct multi-key behavior (a composite cursor
key passes two columns at once), and non-mutation of the caller's slice — the
`columns` argument can be the package-level `<T>AllColumns` var, so an in-place
append would corrupt every later read in the process.

**Root cause.** Shared runtime helpers live in `sharedHelperDefinitions` as
string bodies rendered by `shared_types.go.tmpl`, a shape that predates this
fix. `context_shared_test.go` therefore tests the *definition* (`:35` asserts
the helper set, `:251` asserts one signature) rather than the behavior. The E2E
suites cover the union end-to-end for the shapes the examples happen to
exercise, which is why the gap has no observable symptom today.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add a table-driven behavior test for the helper. Two viable shapes — pick one
  and note the trade-off in the test's doc comment:
  1. a small Go twin of the body in `context_shared_test.go`, kept honest by an
     assertion that the twin's source matches the emitted `Body` string; or
  2. an execution test that renders `shared-types` into a temp package and runs
     the helper (heavier, but tests the emitted code rather than a copy).
- Cases: required already present; the same column twice in `required`; two
  distinct missing columns (composite cursor key); empty `required`; and an
  input-aliasing case asserting the argument slice is unchanged after a union
  that adds a column.
- **Not** a correctness defect today: `sqlgen`'s own suites and all 12 example
  modules pass, and the composite-key path is covered end-to-end by
  `TestRequiredColumns_CompositeCursorKeysWithoutSelectingThem` in the `graphql`
  example.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_shared.go:220-243` — the helper definition.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_shared_test.go:35`, `:251` — the definition-level
  tests this would sit beside.
- `guidelines/TESTING.md` — table-driven, no assertion libraries, `cmp.Diff`.
- `FIX-185` — introduced the helper.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-10. Covered by a package-internal
behavior test on the *emitted* helper rather than a twin of it:
`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/postgres/models/union_columns_test.go`
(`package models`, mirrored to `expected/` like every hand-written test that
lives in a generated package). That is a third shape, not either of the two
suggested above, and it is the one the repo already uses:
`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/mysql/models/mysql_version_test.go` does exactly
this for `newMySQLVersionCache`, another template-emitted helper
(`client.go.tmpl:102`), and `e2e_test.go:541` `collectFiles` skips `*_test.go`
on both sides of the golden diff precisely so the pattern works. It needs no
drift guard, which is why it was preferred over the twin: the golden trees
already pin the helper's text, so a body edit lands in `models/` on the next
`make update-golden-e2e` and the test then runs against the new body.

Cases: the five listed above plus absent `required`, empty `required`, and nil
`columns`, in one table. `TestUnionColumns_doesNotMutateInput` gives the
argument spare capacity (`make([]string, 2, 6)`) so an in-place `append` is
observable at all, then asserts the full backing array is unwritten;
`TestUnionColumns_fastPathAliasesInput` pins that the nothing-missing path
returns the argument itself rather than a copy.

Mutation-tested before landing — each property fails independently when the
generated body is patched. Dropping `slices.Sort(result)` fails four table
cases plus the non-mutation test; `result := append(columns, missing...)` fails
only `doesNotMutateInput`; dropping the `!slices.Contains(missing, r)` guard
fails the two dedupe cases; a `slices.Clone` fast path fails
`fastPathAliasesInput`.

**Two corrections to this entry.** The premise that the `columns` argument "can
be the package-level `<T>AllColumns` var" holds at none of the four call sites.
`table/get.go.tmpl:176`, `:179`, `view/get.go.tmpl:132` and
`table/relationships.go.tmpl:14` all pass a freshly built slice, because the
union calls sit inside the `if selected := fieldOptions.Columns();
len(selected) > 0` block while `columns := <T>AllColumns` is only the fallback
assignment to the same variable. The aliasing case still earns its place as a
contract test — that block is one refactor away from passing the shared var —
but it pins no live path today. Second, the invariant this entry does not name
is the load-bearing one: `sql.BuildSelect` emits the SELECT list through
`sortedCopy` (`sql/builder.go:610`) while `scan<T>(rows, columns)` fills
`targets[idx]` positionally by walking `columns` in the order given. A
regression that appended without re-sorting would therefore not error — it
would scan values into the wrong fields. That is now the lead paragraph of the
test's doc comment.

No production change: PRD §9.6 spells the helper body out verbatim
(`docs/PRD.md:3738`), so the fast path keeps returning the caller's slice
aliased rather than copying it. Two doc fixes rode along —
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_shared.go` gained a source comment above the
`unionColumns` entry pointing at the test, and `guidelines/TESTING.md:513` no
longer claims `models/` is "gitignored except in `expected/`", the line that
would steer the next author away from this pattern.

### FIX-189

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 10 (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl`, added by
  `1c93a29` on 2026-04-15), surfaced in phase 25
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-185 auto-review (2026-09-07)

**Issue.** **The O2M relationship loader force-selects the FK by writing into
the caller's `FieldOptions`, which leaks the flag back to the caller and races
when two relationships to one target share a pointer.**
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl:419-423` emits
`relFieldOptions := fo.<Rel>.FieldOptions; if relFieldOptions != nil {
relFieldOptions.<FK> = true }` inside each `g.Go` closure (`:385`, `:390`), so
the loaders mutate concurrently. Two consequences: (a) the flag persists after
the call, silently widening every later read that reuses the same
`*<Target>FieldOptions`; (b) a caller that assigns one `*FieldOptions` pointer
to two relationships pointing at the same target — a legal thing to do, and the
`assets` fixture in the `graphql` example has exactly that topology across its
`documents` edges — gets concurrent writes to one bool field, which is a data
race under `-race`.

**Root cause.** The force-select predates any other channel for saying "this
column is structurally required": when the loader needed the child's FK in the
projection, the only reachable lever was the `FieldOptions` value itself.
FIX-185 added that channel — the unexported `requiredColumns []string` on
`Get<T>sInput` — and used it for the M2M sibling
(`get.go.tmpl:579-583`), leaving O2M as the last mutating site.

**Suggested fix.**
- Replace the O2M force-select with `requiredColumns: []string{<FK column>}` on
  the child `Get<Target>sInput` literal, matching the M2M shape. The FK's SQL
  column name is already on the relationship context (`FKColumn`); only the Go
  field name (`FKFieldName`) is used today.
- **Sequence this after `FIX-187` — until then it is not a pure refactor.**
  A force-select makes `HasSelectedColumns()` true, so an all-false child
  `FieldOptions` currently *runs* the child fetch and returns FK-only rows;
  `requiredColumns` rides the non-empty guard, so it would short-circuit and
  return nothing. Over GraphQL that is the difference between
  `orders { __typename }` returning the right number of objects today and
  returning `[]` after — measured 2026-09-08, and the reason `orders` behaves
  while its M2M sibling `categories { __typename }` returns `[]`.
  **Decided 2026-09-08:** do not carve out the all-false case here and do not
  fold this entry into `FIX-187`. `FIX-187` makes the GraphQL walker emit the
  row-identity columns for any selection set that asks for a row and names no
  column, so once it lands no all-false child FieldOptions reaches these loaders
  from the API surface and the conversion becomes a pure refactor. A hand-built
  all-false child from a Go-client caller then short-circuits on both the O2M and
  the M2M path, which is what PRD §9.6 says and removes today's accidental
  divergence between the two.
- State the O2M and M2M nested all-false behaviors together in §9.6 rather than
  leaving them to differ by accident, as they do now.
- **Regression tests:** a `gen` test asserting the O2M loader emits no
  assignment into `fo.<Rel>.FieldOptions` (the shape
  `TestRequiredColumns_noFieldOptionsMutation` already pins for M2M); an E2E
  under `-race` with one `*FieldOptions` shared across two relationships to the
  same target; and a Go-client (not GraphQL) test pinning that an all-false child
  `FieldOptions` short-circuits identically on the O2M and M2M paths.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl:419-423` (the mutation), `:385`,
  `:390` (the errgroup fan-out that makes it concurrent), `:579-583` (the M2M
  shape to copy).
- PRD §9.6 — CallOptions / FieldOptions semantics, the all-false short-circuit,
  and "Structurally required columns".
- PRD §13 — relationship loading.
- `FIX-185` — added the `requiredColumns` channel and converted the M2M half;
  `FIX-187` — the walker-layer half, which this entry is sequenced behind.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-09. The O2M loader no longer touches the
caller's `FieldOptions`: the child fetch declares
`requiredColumns: []string{<FKColumn>}` on its `Get<Target>sInput` and forwards
`co.FieldOptions = fo.<Rel>.FieldOptions` untouched, which is the shape FIX-185
gave the M2M sibling. `FKColumn` is the FK's SQL name (`wireRelFKMetadata`
resolves it off the target table's `byName[c.Name]` map), so a `column_map`
rename that separates it from `FKFieldName` stays correct — `FKFieldName` is
still the Go spelling the filter and the bucketing use.

**Measured before filing the change, against a live PostgreSQL 16 container**
using the `assets` fixture — three O2M edges plus one M2M edge all targeting
`documents`, one `*DocumentFieldOptions` shared across all four:

| | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `-race` | `WARNING: DATA RACE`, write/write on the FK bool between the `Attachments` and `Invoices` closures | clean |
| caller's `FieldOptions` after the call | `EntityID == true` (leaked) | `EntityID == false` |
| all-false child, O2M vs M2M | **2 rows vs 0** — the O2M rows carried `ID=00000000-…`, `Name=""`, only the FK set | **0 vs 0** |
| normal narrowed projection | attachments=2 invoices=1 photo=1 linked=1 | unchanged |

The third row is why this was more than a refactor. §9.6 already specified the
post-fix answer — "an all-false `&FieldOptions{}` still short-circuits its own
entity fetch", with O2O named as the only exception — so the force-select was a
**PRD violation**, not merely a divergence from M2M, and what it bought was a
slice of husk structs for a caller who asked for nothing. FIX-187 is what made
the conversion safe from the API surface: the walker now projects a row's
identity for any selection set naming no column, so no all-false child reaches
these loaders over GraphQL. `TestRowIdentity_NestedO2MTypenameOnlyStillReturnsTheChildren`
is the guard and passes unchanged.

Equivalence everywhere else follows from `GetMany`'s shape: `unionColumns` runs
whenever `Columns()` is non-empty; a nil child, or a child selecting only
relationships, falls through to `<T>AllColumns`, which already carries the FK.
The resulting `columns` slice — and therefore the scanned struct — is identical
to what the force-select produced.

PRD §9.6 amended in three places, per the entry: the "Structurally required
columns" table gained the O2M row it never had (the requirement existed, but as
a mutation rather than a union, so the table that describes the union omitted
it); the nested all-false behavior is now stated for both list loaders together
rather than left to differ; and the "every column it adds is kept API-readable
by §32.4" claim is qualified, because the O2M child FK is the one required
column with no §32.4 rule — §32.5 deliberately permits `access` on an FK so a
config can hide the raw id while keeping the nested object exposable. That is
unchanged behavior (the force-select projected a restricted FK too) and safe for
the same reason the rest of the over-fetch is: nothing serializes the value and
the walker emits no `case` for a restricted column. §26.5.2 needed no change —
its "unioned back into the `SELECT` by the client method that needs them, never
by the walker" sentence is about exactly this class of column and stays true.

Tests: `TestRequiredColumns_o2mDeclaresChildFK` pins the new emission shape and
`TestRequiredColumns_noFieldOptionsMutation` now asserts *neither* loader
mutates the caller's value, in any spelling of the alias;
`TestGetTemplate_o2mRelationshipLoading` was updated off the old assertion. Two
E2Es in `graphql/tests/relationship_field_options_test.go` — the shared-pointer
`-race` case and the Go-client all-false O2M/M2M parity case — both verified
failing-first against the pre-fix generated tree, each reproducing the exact
value recorded above.

Golden churn is confined to the O2M loader block: one `gen` golden
(`get_products_relationships_gen.go`) and the `models/` + `expected/` pair in
the nine example modules that have an O2M relationship. Full sweep green:
`cmd/sqlgen` under `-race` (including `cli`, 635s), runtime and parser modules,
all twelve example E2E suites, `golangci-lint` clean across every module.

`FIX-189` was the last generated read path that wrote to caller-owned state.

### FIX-188

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go` (+ PRD §32.4)
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-185 auto-review (2026-09-07)

**Issue.** **`cursor_keys` is not validated against `access`, so a `hidden` /
`internal` non-PK cursor key has its value base64-encoded into every edge
cursor.** PRD §32.4 already hard-errors on a restricted **PK** column and names
cursor encoding as one of the reasons ("the GraphQL `id` argument, cursor
encoding, and relationship targeting all require a readable PK"), but the same
reasoning is never applied to a `cursor_keys` entry that is not a PK — and
`cursor_keys` may name any column that exists, whether inherited from
`generation.cursor_keys` or set per table / per view (PRD §4.13).
`ResolveTableConnection` (`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:1792-1802`) checks
existence only.

**Root cause.** Until FIX-185 the leak was masked by a different bug: under a
narrowed projection the cursor key was never read back, so the encoder
serialized the column's zero value. FIX-185 unions cursor keys into the
projection precisely so the cursor is correct, which means a restricted non-PK
cursor key now reaches an external surface — every edge `cursor`, plus
`pageInfo.startCursor` / `endCursor` — carrying its real value. Nothing stops
it: the §26.5.2 walker cannot *select* a restricted column, so the classifier
never sees this path, and §32.4's rule is PK-shaped.

**Suggested fix.**
- Extend the §32.4 PK rule to resolved cursor keys: every column in a table's or
  view's resolved `cursor_keys` must carry `access ∈ {public, read_only}`, hard
  error otherwise, with the same message shape as the PK rule. The resolved set
  (after §4.13 fallback) is the right input — an inherited default that fell
  back to the PK is already covered by the existing rule.
- Decide and state whether the rule applies when `api.graphql.enabled` is false.
  The Go client's cursor is not an external surface, so the honest scope is
  "when the entity is exposed on a generated API"; the PK rule is unconditional
  today, so matching it is also defensible. Pick one and say why in §32.4.
- Once landed, tighten the PRD §9.6 sentence added by FIX-185 — it currently
  names this gap rather than asserting the guarantee.
- Reachability is low: no checked-in config hits it, and both examples with
  non-PK cursor keys (`category_price_totals.category_id`,
  `workspace_settings.workspace_id` + `key`) are `public`.
- **Regression tests:** a `config` validation test per surface (table
  `cursor_keys`, view `cursor_keys`, inherited `generation.cursor_keys`) with a
  `hidden` and an `internal` column, asserting the hard error; plus a negative
  case pinning that `public` / `read_only` cursor keys still validate.

**References.**
- PRD §32.4 — the PK rule this extends; §32.2 for the role set.
- PRD §9.6 "Structurally required columns" — names this gap explicitly.
- PRD §4.13 — `cursor_keys` resolution and fallback semantics.
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:1792-1802` — `ResolveTableConnection`, the
  existence-only check.
- `FIX-185` — the fix that made the value reach the cursor.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-08. Extended §32.4 to resolved
`cursor_keys` in `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go`: `resolvedCursorKeys` computes
the table's effective key set (empty when the `Connection` operation is off or
§4.13 omits the method — no encoder, no cursor, nothing to contain), and
`validateOneColumnAccess` hard-errors on any member whose role is not
API-readable, naming whether the keys came from `tables.<t>.cursor_keys` or the
inherited `generation.cursor_keys`. Placed directly after the PK rule so a PK
that is also a cursor key reports the PK error alone; `resolvedPKSet` was
refactored onto a new `resolvedPKColumns` so the rule reads the same
override-aware PK the generator does.

**Open decision resolved as unconditional.** The rule does *not* gate on
`api.graphql.enabled`. The required-on-create rule gates because it is a
functional-impossibility rule — with no API there is no create input to be
unsatisfiable. This is a containment rule, and every §32 containment decision
is ungated: event redaction and manifest marking take no API gate, and the PK
rule is unconditional. §14.2 settles it — a cursor is an unsigned, unencrypted
token built to be handed to a consumer and handed back, so it is an external
surface wherever `Connection` exists, generated API or hand-written handler.

**Scope narrowed to tables.** The suggested view arm is unwritable: `ColumnMap`
exists only on `TableConfig` (`config.go:511`) and `buildViewColumns` hardcodes
`resolveAccess("")` (`context_view.go:143-148`), so every view column is
`public` by construction. §32.4 now states the exemption instead.

**Two findings beyond the entry.** The leak is bidirectional — a crafted
`after` / `before` becomes a keyset condition on the cursor keys, giving an
inequality oracle over a column §32.2 grants no filter surface; and the
Connection query's `ORDER BY` is fixed to `cursor_keys`, so a restricted key was
also an implicit sort exposure. Both are closed by the same rule. `write_only`
is rejected alongside `hidden` / `internal`: the allowed set is exactly the
API-readable one.

**Deliberately not done.** `encode<T>Cursor` still emits a `case` arm per
column rather than per API-readable column. The arms are now unreachable, and
dropping them would make a bypassed validation emit a silently *wrong* cursor
(missing key) instead of failing.

**Auto-review follow-ups, both applied inline.** (a) `resolvedCursorKeys` now
resolves against the post-`exclude_columns` column set, matching what the
generator resolves against (`gen.buildTableColumns` drops excluded columns
before `assembleTableContext` calls `ResolveTableConnection`). Reading the raw
set kept an inherited key list alive that the generator discards for the PK,
hard-erroring on a restricted sibling key no cursor carries. (b) When
`generation.cursor_keys` is unset the keys come from the built-in §4.13
default, so the message now says "the built-in cursor_keys default" rather than
naming a setting the user never wrote. Both verified failing-first and pinned
by `_CursorKeyScope` cases. Two further review notes were left as-is: the rule
does not exempt `exclude_tables` / no-PK skipped tables (identical to the
existing required-on-create rule, so not a new inconsistency), and
`resolvedPKColumns` returns the config slice uncopied (read-only today, and the
pre-existing `ResolveTableConnection` explicit branch does the same).

**Docs.** PRD §32.4 (new bullet), §9.6 (the FIX-185 sentence now asserts the
guarantee), §4.13 (validation-table row + summary-list line), §14.2 (ties the
"not a security boundary" note to the guarantee that makes it safe). Corrected
`PRD §32:179-182`, which carried the reasoning error behind the
bug — "the cursor is opaque base64, not a named field."

**Tests.** `cmd/sqlgen/config/access_validate_test.go`:
`TestValidatePostParse_ColumnAccess_CursorKeyRole` (five roles),
`_CursorKeyScope` (source phrasing, `connection: false` exemption, rule holds
with the API off and with the table opted out, PK precedence, required-on-create
precedence, unresolvable keys), `_CursorKeyConnectionOmitted` (§4.13 Emit-false
exemption). Verified failing-first: neutering the check fails 8 assertions and
leaves exactly the exemption cases green. `make check` clean (exit 0),
`make check-examples` clean (exit 0), zero golden churn — no checked-in config
names a restricted cursor key.

### FIX-187

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/field_options.go.tmpl`,
  `api/connection_walker.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** the FIX-185 widening probe (2026-09-06); deferred out of
  FIX-185 by decision because it is a walker-layer fix, not a client-layer one.
  Widened from the cursor-only symptom to the full family on 2026-09-08 after a
  seventeen-shape measurement against a live PostgreSQL 16 container

**Issue.** **A GraphQL selection set that asks for a row but names no column
returns nothing.** The filed symptom — `{ users(first: 1) { edges { cursor } } }`
returns `edges: []` — is one of nine measured shapes, all the same defect.
Measured against the `graphql` example on a live PostgreSQL 16 container with
two seeded users; `q` is DB round-trips through the §25.1 counting querier:

| Query | Today | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `users(first:1) { edges { cursor } }` | 1q, `edges: []` | 2q, one edge with a real cursor |
| `users(first:1) { edges { __typename } }` | 1q, `edges: []` | 2q, one edge |
| `users(first:1) { edges { node { __typename } } }` | 1q, `edges: []` | 2q, one edge |
| `users(first:1) { pageInfo { startCursor endCursor } }` | 1q, both `null` | 2q, real cursors |
| `users(first:1) { pageInfo { hasNextPage } }` | 1q, **`false`** | 2q, `true` |
| `userList(limit:1) { items { __typename } }` | 1q, `items: []` | 2q, one item |
| `user(id:) { __typename }` | **0q**, `user: null` | 1q, the object |
| `user(id:) { id categories { __typename } }` | 2q, `categories: []` | 3q, one category |
| `user(id:) { id orders { __typename } }` | 2q, one order | unchanged — see below |

The `pageInfo { hasNextPage }` row is the sharpest of these: it is a *wrong
boolean*, not an empty list — the same query selecting `edges { node { name } }`
alongside reports `true`. The `orders` row is correct today only by accident: the
O2M loader's force-select of the FK (`FIX-189`) makes the child FieldOptions
non-empty, which is why O2M behaves and its M2M sibling does not. Two behaviors
measured alongside these must survive the fix: `{ users(first:1) { totalCount } }`
and `{ userList(limit:1) { totalCount hasMore } }` each cost exactly **one** DB
query.

**Root cause.** The client is behaving as specified. PRD §9.6 defines an
all-false `&<T>FieldOptions{}` as "caller doesn't need the result — skip entity
fetch entirely, return nil", and `GetMany` honors it at
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl:163-166`. The wrong value is the
FieldOptions the walker hands it. `<t>FieldOptionsFromCollected`
(`api/field_options.go.tmpl:47-71`) emits one `case` arm per *column* and per
*relationship*, so a selection set naming neither — `{ cursor }`, `{ __typename }`,
or an `edges` with no `node` after `unwrapConnectionFields`
(`api/connection_walker.go.tmpl:20-50`) declines to descend — produces an
all-false tree.

The client cannot recover from this: `{ totalCount }` and `{ edges { cursor } }`
reach `Connection` as byte-identical all-false FieldOptions (measured: both 1q),
and the resolver passes nothing else that separates them
(`api/resolvers.go.tmpl:70-86`). Only the walker knows which one it saw. The
distinction it has to draw is between the two ways an all-false tree arises:

1. **The envelope selected no row-bearing field** — `{ totalCount }` on a
   Connection or ListResult. The entity selection set is *absent*. No rows
   needed; §9.6's short-circuit is exactly right.
2. **A row was requested but no column names it** — `edges { cursor }`,
   `node { __typename }`, `items { __typename }`, `user(id:) { __typename }`,
   `categories { __typename }`. Rows needed, zero columns.

Today the walker cannot tell them apart, so case 2 is served as case 1.

**Suggested fix.** Verified by prototype against the container before filing:
the generated `user` / `category` walkers were patched by hand, all nine rows
above came out at the Expected column, both `totalCount` pins stayed at one
query, and the whole pre-existing `graphql` example suite passed unchanged.

- **Split the unwrap helper's answer in two.** `unwrapConnectionFields` returns
  `(entityFields []graphql.CollectedField, wantsRows bool)`:
  - parent type is neither `<T>Connection` nor `<T>ListResult` → `(fields, true)`
    — a direct entity or relationship selection always wants its row;
  - `<T>Connection` → `wantsRows` iff `edges` or `pageInfo` is selected;
    `entityFields` is the `edges { node { … } }` sub-selection when there is one,
    else nil;
  - `<T>ListResult` → `wantsRows` iff `items` is selected; `entityFields` is its
    sub-selection.
  Treat all of `pageInfo` as row-bearing rather than only `startCursor` /
  `endCursor`: `hasNextPage` is derived from the `limit+1` probe row and is the
  wrong-boolean row of the table above. This also closes a latent hole — the
  helper currently hands the *envelope's own* fields to the walker when it finds
  no `node`, so a column literally named `edges` or `totalCount` would be set by
  the FIX-082 gate's blind side.
- **`<t>FieldOptionsFromContext`** returns a bare `&<T>FieldOptions{}` without
  walking when `wantsRows` is false — that is case 1, and it keeps the count-only
  query at one DB query.
- **`<t>FieldOptionsFromCollected`** ends with: if nothing was selected, set the
  entity's **row-identity columns**. This is the recursive step, so it covers
  nested relationship selections as well as the top level. Row identity is the
  **PK columns**, falling back to the resolved `cursor_keys` for a view with no
  `@pk`, falling back to the entity's first column. Needs a new
  `APITableContext.RowIdentityFields` (Go field names on the FieldOptions
  struct), sourced from the `TableContext` / `ViewContext` the API context is
  built from.
  - **Force the PK, not the cursor keys as this entry originally suggested.**
    `Connection` already declares `requiredColumns: c.cursorKeys` (FIX-185), so a
    non-empty projection is all it takes for the cursor to be correct — stating
    the cursor keys again in the walker would say one requirement in two places.
    The PK also generalizes to the ListResult / by-PK / nested paths where cursor
    keys mean nothing, and it keeps a restricted non-PK cursor key out of a
    `__typename`-only projection (`FIX-188`).
  - Guard the emission on `len(fo.Columns()) == 0 && !fo.HasSelectedColumns()` —
    i.e. use `HasSelectedColumns()`, which is already false only in case 2 and
    already true for a relationship-only selection. A relationship-only selection
    keeps its existing `<t>AllColumns` fallback; narrowing that is out of scope.
- **Leave FIX-185's client-layer guard alone.** It deliberately does not
  resurrect an all-false FieldOptions, and it does not need to: after this change
  the walker never hands it one for a requested row.
- **PRD amendments, in the same change:**
  - §26.5.2 currently asserts that structurally required columns are unioned in
    by the client "never by the walker", so "the walker stays a faithful
    translation of the selection set". Reword: the walker translates the *whole*
    selection set, including the fields resolved from a row's existence rather
    than from a column — `__typename`, an edge's `cursor`, the edge itself — and
    a selection set that names no column still selects the row-identity columns.
    The client-side union (§9.6) is unchanged and still the only place cursor /
    mapping / NULL-detection keys are added.
  - §9.6: the all-false short-circuit is a Go-client affordance. A GraphQL
    request cannot express it below the envelope, so the walker never produces
    one for a row it was asked to return; a count-only envelope selection never
    reaches the entity at all.
  - §25.1: state the query counts this settles. `{ totalCount }` on either
    envelope stays 1. Any connection selection naming `edges` or `pageInfo`
    costs 2 (`COUNT` + the data page) — including a cursor-only or
    `hasNextPage`-only one, which is the correct count for a query whose answer
    is read off rows. A by-PK `{ __typename }` costs 1. A nested all-false
    relationship now costs its full `1 + O2M + 2×M2M` term instead of
