    under-counting when the child fetch short-circuited.
- **Regression tests:**
  (a) `gen` template tests: the entry point returns early on a count-only
  envelope; `FromCollected` emits the row-identity assignment; a view with no
  `@pk` emits its cursor keys instead; the helper's two-value shape;
  (b) E2Es in the `graphql` example, one per row of the table above, each
  verified failing-first — the nine wrong rows plus the two `totalCount` pins,
  which `tests/query_count_test.go`'s counting querier already supports;
  (c) a query-count pin on `{ users(first:1) { pageInfo { hasNextPage } } }`
  asserting 2 and `true`, since that row is a wrong value rather than an
  empty list.

**Decisions taken (2026-09-08).** Scope: the whole walker family, not the
connection alone — a connection-only cut leaves `pageInfo { hasNextPage }`
returning `false` when a next page exists. Row identity: PK first. `FIX-189`
stays open and is not folded in; see its entry.

**References.**
- PRD §9.6 — the all-false FieldOptions short-circuit the client is honoring,
  and the "Structurally required columns" carve-out FIX-185 added.
- PRD §25.1 / §26.5.2 — the walker contract and the query-count guarantee this
  changes for several query shapes.
- `FIX-185` — the client-layer family this was split out of; the two are
  complementary (FIX-185 fixes narrowed-but-non-empty projections, this one
  fixes the empty projection).
- `FIX-189` — the O2M FK force-select. It is what makes `orders { __typename }`
  work today while its M2M sibling returns `[]`; once this fix lands the walker
  guarantees a non-empty child FieldOptions, so converting O2M to
  `requiredColumns` becomes a pure refactor rather than a behavior change.
- `FIX-188` — why the forced set is the PK rather than the cursor keys.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/field_options.go.tmpl:26-71`,
  `api/connection_walker.go.tmpl:20-50`, `api/resolvers.go.tmpl:70-86`,
  `table/get.go.tmpl:163-174`, `table/pagination.go.tmpl:116-126`.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-08. The walker now separates the two
ways an all-false FieldOptions arises. `unwrapConnectionFields`
(`api/connection_walker.go.tmpl`) returns `([]graphql.CollectedField, bool)` —
the entity-level selection set plus whether the request needs rows: a parent
type that is neither envelope passes through as `(fields, true)`; a
`<T>Connection` reports rows wanted iff `edges` or `pageInfo` is selected; a
`<T>ListResult` iff `items` is. `pageInfo` counts in full rather than only its
two cursor fields, because `hasNextPage` is read off the `limit+1` probe row —
the wrong-boolean row of the table above, and the case the entry's original
trigger would have missed. Each per-table entry point
(`api/field_options.go.tmpl`) returns the bare `&<T>FieldOptions{}` without
walking when rows are not wanted, which is what keeps a count-only envelope at
one DB query; everything else walks, and `<t>FieldOptionsFromCollected` — the
recursive step, so nested relationship selections get it too — ends by
projecting the entity's row identity when the selection named no column.

Row identity is the **PK**, per the 2026-09-08 decision, not the cursor keys the
entry originally suggested: `Connection` already declares
`requiredColumns: c.cursorKeys` (FIX-185), so a non-empty projection is all it
takes for the cursor to be correct, and restating the cursor keys in the walker
would say one requirement in two places while meaning nothing on the
ListResult / by-PK / nested paths. It also keeps a restricted non-PK cursor key
out of a `__typename`-only projection (`FIX-188`) **wherever a PK exists** —
every table, and both example views. The fallbacks exist for a view, the one
entity kind that may have no `@pk`: its resolved `cursor_keys`, then its first
column. On that one path the projected column *is* a cursor key, so the
`FIX-188` separation does not hold there; it is unreachable today because
`context_view.go` classifies every view column `public`, and it would become
reachable only if per-view access classification ever lands. Hardening
`ValidateAPIWalkerCompleteness` to assert row-identity ⊆ API-readable fields
would close it by construction. `APIEntity` gained `CursorKeys` and a new
`rowIdentityFields` resolver (`context_api.go`); `APITableContext` gained
`RowIdentityFields`, set from both builders. A scan of all five generated
examples confirms every projected field is also an API-readable column with its
own `case` arm — no restricted column reaches a projection.

PRD amended in three places, as the entry called for: §26.5.2 gained "Row
identity — a selection set that names no column" (the previous text asserted
columns are added "never by the walker", which this change makes false) and the
count-only-envelope carve-out; §9.6 now states that the all-false short-circuit
is a Go-client affordance a GraphQL request cannot express below the envelope;
§25.1 gained the per-shape query-count table this settles — count-only stays 1,
every row-bearing envelope selection is 2, a by-PK `{ __typename }` is 1, and a
nested all-false relationship costs its full `1 + O2M + 2 × M2M` term instead of
under-counting when the child fetch short-circuited.

Tests: six `gen` template tests in `cmd/sqlgen/gen/row_identity_test.go` (the
entry-point skip, the recursive projection, a composite PK projecting its whole
tuple, a PK-less view falling back to its cursor keys, the `pageInfo` arm and
the three-`wantsRows` shape of the helper, and a context-level check that every
API entity carries a row identity), plus ten E2Es in
`graphql/tests/walker_row_identity_test.go` — one per measured symptom, the O2M
guard, a view connection, and a query-count table pinning both `totalCount`-only
shapes at 1 and the three row-bearing shapes at 2. All nine symptom tests
verified failing-first against the pre-fix generated walker, each reproducing
the exact value this entry recorded. Three `api_walker_test.go` assertions were
updated for the helper's new signature.

Golden churn is exactly `connection_walker_gen.go` + `field_options_gen.go`
across the five examples with an `api:` block (`graphql`,
`graphql_null_wrappers`, `graphql_top_level`, `mysql`, `sqlite`) — no other
generated file moved, which is the containment the change was designed for.
`FIX-189` stays open and is now unblocked: the walker guarantees a non-empty
child FieldOptions from the API surface, so converting the O2M FK force-select
to `requiredColumns` is a pure refactor, and
`TestRowIdentity_NestedO2MTypenameOnlyStillReturnsTheChildren` is the guard for
that conversion. Two follow-ups from this fix's auto-review are filed:
`FIX-191` (aliased duplicate selections overwrite instead of merging — a
pre-existing defect at both the envelope and the relationship arm, whose
envelope half this fix flipped from first-wins to last-wins; measured in both
directions) and `FIX-192` (assert row-identity ⊆ API-readable fields in
`ValidateAPIWalkerCompleteness`, the hardening named above). One behavior change
outside this entry's scope is noted and untested: a mutation payload selecting
only `__typename` (`createUser { __typename }`) previously returned nil into a
non-null schema field and now returns the row.

### FIX-186

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go`, `context_table.go`, `context_cache.go`
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-183 auto-review (2026-09-04)
- **Re-verified:** 2026-09-08. **Severity raised `nit` → `tracked`, the "why it is a nit"
  reasoning replaced — it was measured to be wrong — and the scope widened to two further
  instances of the same defect: `errgroup` on the table path and `uuid` in the cache file.**

**Issue.** **A generated view file that needs `pq.Array` gets its `github.com/lib/pq` import
only because goimports resolves it, not because the generator asks for it.** The table path is
explicit: `tableImports` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:336-339`) adds `lib/pq` when the
dialect is PostgreSQL, the driver is stdlib, and `hasBareSliceColumn(columns)` holds. The view
path is not — `buildSingleViewContext` (`context_view.go:82`) builds its import set from
`collectColumnImports(columns)` plus `hook`, and a bare `[]string` contributes no import. The
emitted `pq.Array(...)` call is nevertheless resolved by the `imports.Process` pass the
generator runs over its output.

**Root cause.** The generator maintains the import set by hand in Go while the templates
emit the code that uses it, and the two are only loosely coupled — `orchestrate.go:534-540`
documents declared `Imports` as a seed that goimports back-fills. That back-fill is what hides
disagreement: `imports.Process` resolves an undeclared package by scanning `GOMODCACHE`, which
succeeds in any environment that happens to have the module extracted. So a template that
reaches for a third-party package the context never declares looks correct everywhere a
developer or CI runs, and only fails for a consumer whose cache has never held it. Three
instances accumulated behind that mask.

**Why the original "it is a nit" reasoning does not hold.** The entry claimed resolution
succeeds "because the example's `go.mod` already requires `lib/pq`", and concluded there is no
reachable failing configuration. Both halves are wrong, and the second follows from the first.
Measured 2026-09-08 by generating an `ARRAY_AGG` view into a throwaway consumer module:

- **`go.mod` is not the mechanism.** With `lib/pq` absent from the consumer's `go.mod`
  entirely, `imports.Process` still resolved `pq` and wrote the import. goimports finds
  candidates by scanning `GOMODCACHE`, not by reading the requirement list.
- **The reachable failing input is therefore a cold module cache, not a missing requirement.**
  Regenerating the same module with an isolated empty `GOMODCACHE` emits
  `targets[idx] = pq.Array(&c.ProductNameList)` into `views_gen.go` **with no import block
  entry at all**. The package does not compile: `models/views_gen.go:85:20: undefined: pq`.

This is reachable without contriving anything: a PostgreSQL + stdlib consumer who drives
`database/sql` with `pgx/v5/stdlib` has no reason to have ever pulled `lib/pq` into their
cache, and an `ARRAY_AGG` view is exactly the FIX-183 shape that puts `pq.Array` in front of
them. The severity is not that generation breaks — the table path fails the same way in the
same environment — but that the *failure mode* differs. The table path writes the import, so
the go tool reports `missing go.sum entry for module providing package github.com/lib/pq; to
add: go get`, which names the fix. The view path omits it, so the consumer gets `undefined:
pq` in a `DO NOT EDIT` file, which reads as a generator bug.

**Same defect, second instance — `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup` on the table path.** The entry
treats `tableImports` as the correct model to copy. It is not: `errgroup` is emitted by
`table/get.go.tmpl:385` (`g, ctx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx)`, inside the
`{{ if .HasO2MRelationships }}` guard) and is declared in no import seed anywhere. The same
cold-cache run above produced `models/models_gen.go:354:12: undefined: errgroup` alongside the
`pq` failure. It is the **more** reachable of the two: it needs only a foreign key — the repro
schema declared no relationships in `sqlgen.yml` and got there purely through FK
auto-detection — and it is dialect- and driver-independent, where the `pq` gap needs
PostgreSQL + stdlib + a bare slice column.

**Same defect, third instance — `github.com/google/uuid` in `cache_gen.go`.** Found by
probing rather than by reading: instrumenting `formatWithOptions` to report every third-party
import goimports *added* (i.e. one the generator did not declare) and running it across all 12
examples surfaced `github.com/google/uuid` in `models/cache_gen.go` for `graphql`, `tenancy`
and `tenancy_postgres`. `buildCacheImports` (`context_cache.go:367`) returned a fixed list and
never accounted for the consumer-facing Go types `cache.go.tmpl` spells in the signatures it
generates — `TenantGoType` and `PKGoType` — so a `uuid.UUID` tenant key produced 58 `uuid.`
references with no declared import.

**Unlike the other two, this one is masked and I could not make it fail.** A sibling file in
the same package always declares `uuid` (the tenant column's own type override puts it on the
model, and `models_gen.go` is written before `cache_gen.go` in the same run), and goimports
takes that hint even with an empty `GOMODCACHE` and an emptied output directory. It is a
latent inconsistency of the same kind as the O2O case below, fixed for consistency rather than
to repair a reachable failure — stated plainly so the entry is not read as claiming a
reproduction it does not have.

**Not a gap: the O2O join scan.** `buildO2OScanCases` / `buildO2OParentScanCases`
(`context_table.go:2318,2349`) also emit `pq.Array`, for the *target* table's columns, which
the parent's `tableImports(cfg, columns)` never inspects. Verified not to be reachable: the
target table carries the bare slice column itself, so its own `tableImports` declares
`lib/pq`, and both layouts union every table's declared imports before emitting. Checked
under the cold cache — the import is present.

**Fix (verified).** Declare both imports from the exact predicate that governs their emission,
rather than extracting the whole driver-conditional block as originally suggested:

- `arrayScanImports(cfg, columns)` — extracted from `tableImports`, called from both it and
  `buildSingleViewContext`. Only the bare-slice → `lib/pq` arm is shared, because it is driven
  by a column property both paths have. **The `pgx/v5` arm deliberately stays table-only:**
  `pgx.Batch` appears solely in `table/update.go.tmpl`, so sharing it would declare an import
  views never use.
- `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup` appended in `assembleTableContext` under
  `len(o2mRels) > 0 || len(m2mRels) > 0` — the same predicate `TableContext` publishes as
  `HasO2MRelationships` and the template branches on.
- `cachedTableTypeImports(t)` — the tenant-key and single-column-PK imports, collected per
  cached table and passed into `buildCacheImports`. The PK arm mirrors the `PKGoType` guard in
  `buildCachedTable`; a composite PK contributes nothing, since the template spells it as the
  package-local `<T>PK` struct.

**Re-probed after the fix: zero third-party back-fills across all 12 examples** — every
third-party import in generated output is now declared by the generator rather than inferred
by goimports.

**Zero churn, verified.** A `HEAD` binary and a patched binary each generated all 12 example
modules with a pinned `--manifest-timestamp`, restoring the tree between every run: **431
generated files, byte-identical.** Warm-cache output is unchanged because goimports was
already producing these imports; the change only removes the dependence on it doing so.

**Deliberately not done: a generation-time assertion.** The probe used to find the third
instance (diff the declared seed against goimports' resolved set, ignoring stdlib and
`github.com/teandresmith/sqlgen/...`, both of which resolve without a module-cache scan) is a
sound detector for this whole class and costs nothing — `Format` already has both sides. It
was **declined as a hard error at generation time**, since it would fail generation for any
future template that reaches a new third-party package until someone declares it. The
invariant is documented here instead; the probe is reproducible by instrumenting
`formatWithOptions`.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:336-339` (`tableImports`) and `:773-783`
  (`hasBareSliceColumn`) — the explicit form.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go:82` — the implicit form.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl:385` — the `errgroup` emission site.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go:534-540` — the comment documenting that declared `Imports`
  are a seed goimports back-fills, which is why this class of gap is easy to introduce.
- `FIX-183` — the entry whose auto-review surfaced this; its `ARRAY_AGG` work is what makes a
  bare slice column reachable on the view path in the first place.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-08. Every third-party import the generator emits is
now declared from the exact predicate that governs its emission, rather than inferred by
goimports from the module cache:

- `arrayScanImports(cfg, columns)` (`context_table.go`) — the bare-slice → `lib/pq` arm,
  extracted from `tableImports` and called from both it and `buildSingleViewContext`. The
  `pgx/v5` arm stayed table-only by decision: `pgx.Batch` appears solely in
  `table/update.go.tmpl`, so sharing it would declare an import views never use.
- `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup` (`assembleTableContext`) — appended under
  `len(o2mRels) > 0 || len(m2mRels) > 0`, the predicate `TableContext` publishes as
  `HasO2MRelationships` and `table/get.go.tmpl:385` branches on.
- `cachedTableTypeImports(t)` (`context_cache.go`) — the tenant-key and single-column-PK
  imports, collected per cached table and passed into `buildCacheImports`, which was
  previously a fixed list. The PK arm mirrors the `PKGoType` guard in `buildCachedTable`;
  a composite PK contributes nothing (spelled as the package-local `<T>PK` struct).

**Verified.** Cold-cache repro (isolated empty `GOMODCACHE`, `GOPROXY=off`) that previously
emitted `undefined: pq` and `undefined: errgroup` now generates a package that compiles, and
`go mod tidy` discovers both modules because the imports are present to discover. Re-probing
all 12 examples reports **zero** third-party back-fills, down from three. **Zero churn:** a
`HEAD` binary and a patched binary each generated all 12 examples with a pinned
`--manifest-timestamp`, restoring the tree between every run — **431 generated files,
byte-identical.** `go test ./gen/... ./config/...` passes; build, `gofumpt`, `go vet` clean.

**Carried forward, not done.** (1) The generation-time assertion that would keep this class
closed was **declined by decision** — it would fail generation for any future template
reaching a new third-party package until someone declares it. The invariant and the probe
method are documented in this entry instead. (2) No regression test pins the three imports;
warm-cache output is byte-identical, so the existing suite cannot distinguish the fixed and
unfixed states. Both remain open follow-ups for whoever wants the class guarded rather than
documented.

### FIX-185

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/pagination.go.tmpl`,
  `view/pagination.go.tmpl`, `table/get.go.tmpl`, `table/relationships.go.tmpl`
- **Surfaced by:** 25.9 auto-review (2026-09-04); widened from the cursor-only
  symptom to the full family on 2026-09-06 after a five-probe measurement
  against a live PostgreSQL 16 container

**Issue.** **A narrowed projection silently drops the columns a call
structurally requires, so cursor pagination loops forever and relationship
selections come back empty or null.** `<T>FieldOptions.Columns()` emits one
`if fo.<Field>` arm per requested column and has no notion that some columns
are structurally required rather than requested. Four consumers then read a
column the `SELECT` never fetched. **Measured, not inferred** — against the
`graphql` example on a real container; every row is a query a client can write
today:

| Query | Today | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `users(first: 1) { edges { cursor node { body } } }` | cursor `{"id":"00000000-…"}`; feeding `endCursor` back as `after:` returns the same row forever | the row's real key |
| `user(id:) { name orders { id } }` | `orders: []` | the user's orders |
| `asset(id:) { name primaryDocument { name } }` | `primaryDocument: null` | the document |
| `user(id:) { id categories { name } }` | `categories: []` | both linked categories |

Adding the key column back to each selection (`node { id name }`,
`{ id name orders { id } }`, `primaryDocument { id name }`,
`categories { id name }`) makes all four correct — which is exactly why this
was invisible: every existing E2E happens to select `id`. It is not
view-specific (the `users` table and the `workspace_note_summary` view behave
identically), not a tenancy leak (the tenant predicate is applied independently
and correctly), and not a 25.9 regression; 25.9 is only where the first symptom
was noticed. Row 2 reaches `Paginate` / `<T>List` as well, since both share
`GetMany`. `Stream` is unaffected: `Stream<T>FieldOptions` carries no
relationships (PRD §9.4a) and `Stream` encodes no cursors.

Two behaviors measured alongside these must survive the fix:
`{ users(first: 1) { totalCount } }` costs exactly **one** DB query — the PRD
§9.6 all-false-`FieldOptions` short-circuit — and `{ users(first: 1) { edges
{ cursor } } }` returns `edges: []`, a fifth symptom split out as `FIX-187`
because it belongs to the GraphQL walker rather than the client.

**Root cause.** The projection layer is never told which columns are
structurally required, and four consumers require one:

1. **Cursor keys.** `internalOpts` in the generated `Connection`
   (`table/pagination.go.tmpl:71-74`, mirrored in `view/pagination.go.tmpl:70-73`)
   copies the caller's `CallOptions` verbatim — `*o = options; o.SkipHooks = true`
   — and passes them to `GetMany`. `encode<T>Cursor` (`:140` / `:148`) then reads
   the `c.cursorKeys` fields off a row `scan<T>s` never filled.
2. **Parent key for O2M / M2M.** `loadRelationships` (`table/get.go.tmpl:357`)
   collects the parent side from `<row>.<PK>` (`:365-375` for O2M, `:450-460` for
   M2M) and maps children back through the same field. An unselected parent PK
   makes every key the zero value, so the batched `IN (…)` matches nothing.
3. **O2O child PK.** `resolveO2OJoins` passes `fo.<Rel>.Columns()` as the join's
   column list (`table/relationships.go.tmpl:11`), and
   `scan<T>sWithOneToOneJoins` decides a LEFT JOIN miss by testing the child PK
   against its zero value (`:128-135`). An unselected child PK reads as a miss,
   so a present child is assigned `nil`.
4. **M2M child PK.** Step 3 keys `targetByID` on the child PK
   (`table/get.go.tmpl:563-566`) while passing the child's FieldOptions through
   unmodified (`:553`) — unlike the O2M path, which already force-selects the FK
   at `:392-395`. That one line is the only place in the codebase that currently
   states a projection requirement, and it is the precedent for the rest.

**Suggested fix.**
- **Mechanism.** Thread the requirement through the input struct rather than the
  caller's FieldOptions: add an unexported `requiredColumns []string` to
  `Get<T>sInput` next to `conditions` (PRD §9.2 already documents that channel
  for internal callers) and union it into `columns` in `GetMany`
  (`table/get.go.tmpl:168-174`, mirrored in `view/get.go.tmpl`). Preferred over
  the `withCursorKeys` clone this entry originally suggested: no clone of a
  possibly-shared FieldOptions tree, no mutation of the caller's value, hooks
  keep seeing the FieldOptions the caller actually set, and the union lands in
  one place.
- **Guard.** Union only when the narrowed set is already non-empty
  (`len(selected) > 0`). An all-false FieldOptions must still short-circuit
  (PRD §9.6) — measured at one DB query for `{ totalCount }`; unconditional
  forcing would make it two.
- **Re-sort after the union.** `writeSelectColumns` (`sql/builder.go:605-617`)
  sorts, and `scan<T>s` matches positionally against the slice the caller hands
  it, so an unsorted union mis-scans. Verified against a container during the
  prototype pass.
- **Per consumer:**
  1. `Connection` sets `requiredColumns: c.cursorKeys` on its `Get<T>sInput`
     literal (`table/pagination.go.tmpl:116-121`,
     `view/pagination.go.tmpl:124-129`). `Paginate` needs no cursor union — it
     encodes no cursors — but inherits item 2 through `GetMany`.
  2. Union the parent key `loadRelationships` reads (`index .PKColumns 0`) into
     `columns` when any O2M / M2M relationship is selected. Needs a generated
     unexported predicate on the FieldOptions — `HasSelectedColumns()` is too
     coarse, being true for a columns-only selection too. Emit it only under
     `.HasO2MRelationships` so tables without relationships stay byte-identical.
  3. Union the target's PK into each join's column list
     (`table/relationships.go.tmpl:11`) via a new `TargetPKColumn` on
     `O2OJoinDetail`; chained joins each union their own target's PK.
  4. Force-select the target PK on the child's FieldOptions before the M2M
     step-2 fetch (`table/get.go.tmpl:553`), exactly as the O2M path does at
     `:392-395`.
- **PRD amendment.** Nothing in the PRD states this contract today, which is how
  the templates diverged from it. §9.6's FieldOptions table and §26.5.2's
  narrowing contract both need the carve-out spelled out: a narrowed projection
  is always widened by the columns the call structurally requires (cursor keys,
  relationship join / mapping keys, O2O NULL-detection keys), and an all-false
  FieldOptions still short-circuits.
- Apply the cursor half to `table/pagination.go.tmpl` and
  `view/pagination.go.tmpl` together — they are the same code twice and a
  one-sided fix reintroduces the design-§1.3 divergence Phase 25 exists to
  remove. Items 2-4 are table-only (a view has no relationships, PRD §16.4).
- **Regression tests:**
  (a) `gen` unit tests asserting the rendered `Connection` declares its cursor
  keys and the rendered `GetMany` unions them — for both a table and a view;
  (b) `gen` unit tests for the three relationship unions (O2M parent key, O2O
  join column list, M2M child PK);
  (c) one E2E in the `graphql` example per row of the table above, each verified
  failing-first: page 2 differs from page 1 without selecting the cursor key,
  `orders` non-empty without the parent `id`, `primaryDocument` non-null without
  the child `id`, both `categories` present without the child `id`;
  (d) a query-count pin that `{ users(first: 1) { totalCount } }` still costs
  exactly one DB query (`tests/query_count_test.go` already carries the counting
  querier).

**References.**
- PRD §9.6 — CallOptions / FieldOptions semantics, including the all-false
  short-circuit the guard preserves.
- PRD §25.1 / §26.5.2 — the field-options walker and the query-count contract;
  the narrowing contract is what needs the carve-out.
- PRD §12 / §26.4 — `Connection` / keyset pagination semantics.
- PRD §16.4 — views have no relationships, so items 2-4 are table-only.
- PRD §9.4a — `Stream` has no relationship topology, which is why it is exempt.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl:163-174` (narrowing), `:337`,
  `:357` (`loadRelationships`), `:392-395` (the existing force-select
  precedent), `:553`, `:563-566` (M2M child mapping).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/relationships.go.tmpl:11` (join column list),
  `:128-135` (NULL detection).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/pagination.go.tmpl:71-74,116-121,140` and
  `view/pagination.go.tmpl:70-73,124-129,148`.
- `sql/builder.go:605-617` — the builder sorts columns, so the union must
  re-sort.
- `FIX-187` — the `{ edges { cursor } }` walker-layer sibling, deferred out of
  this entry by decision on 2026-09-06.
- `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` §25.9 Completion Record — the auto-review that
  surfaced the cursor symptom.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-07. The requirement now travels through
the input struct rather than the caller's FieldOptions: `Get<T>sInput` gained an
unexported `requiredColumns []string` beside `conditions`
(`shared/_input.tmpl`), and `GetMany` unions it into a narrowed projection via a
new shared `unionColumns` helper (`context_shared.go`) that re-sorts because the
builder emits columns sorted and `scan<T>s` matches positionally. The union sits
inside the `len(selected) > 0` arm, so an all-false FieldOptions still
short-circuits. Per consumer: `Connection` declares `requiredColumns:
c.cursorKeys` (`table/pagination.go.tmpl`, `view/pagination.go.tmpl`); `GetMany`
unions the parent PK behind a generated `loadsRelationships()` predicate, emitted
only under `.HasO2MRelationships`; each O2O join carries its target's PK via a
new `O2OJoinDetail.PKColumn`; and the M2M loader force-selects the target PK the
same channel, declaring the target's PK column on the target fetch. That last one
needed the target's own PK spelling both ways, so `RelationshipContext` gained
`TargetPKFieldName` + `TargetPKColumn`, wired cross-table in
`wireRelationshipFKMetadata` (whose `pkGoTypes` map became a
`pkColumns map[string]ColumnContext` so one map carries every fact) — the M2M
`targetByID` key was previously spelled with the *parent's* PK field name and
only worked because the two coincide, which is now fixed in the same statement.
The M2M half first shipped as a force-select mirroring the O2M FK precedent
(`relFieldOptions.<PK> = true`) and was reworked after auto-review: writing to
the caller's `*FieldOptions` leaks a flag back to the caller and races when two
relationships to one target share a pointer, since the loaders run under
`errgroup` — and it silently overrode the §9.6 short-circuit for a nested
all-false selection. `requiredColumns` has none of those properties;
`TestRequiredColumns_noFieldOptionsMutation` pins it. The pre-existing O2M FK
force-select is deliberately left alone: converting it would change what
`orders { __typename }` returns today. PRD §9.6 gained the "Structurally required columns" carve-out
(with the §26.5.2 walker contract pointing at it), the amendment the entry called
for. `Paginate` needs no cursor union — it encodes no cursors — but inherits the
relationship union through `GetMany`, so `<T>List` is fixed too; `Stream` is
untouched (§9.4a, no relationships, no cursors). Tests: eight `gen` template
tests in `cmd/sqlgen/gen/required_columns_test.go` (both cursor sites, both
GetMany sites, the parent-key union plus its negative complement, the O2O join
and its chained variant, the M2M declaration, and the no-mutation constraint)
and seven E2Es in `graphql/tests/required_columns_test.go` — one per measured
symptom, a composite two-column cursor key on a tenanted entity, and a pin that
a `{ totalCount }`-only connection query still costs exactly one DB query. All
six behavioral E2Es verified failing-first against the pre-fix generated code,
each with the exact symptom this entry recorded. `make check` clean across
all 8 modules; `make check-examples` clean across all 12 example modules; goldens
regenerated via `make update-golden` + `make update-golden-e2e`. `FIX-187` (the
walker-layer `{ edges { cursor } }` case) is deliberately out of scope and stays
open. Three follow-ups from this fix's auto-review are filed: `FIX-188` (the one
gap this fix opens — a restricted **non-PK** `cursor_keys` column now reaches the
edge cursor with its real value, which §32.4's PK rule does not cover; also named
in PRD §9.6), `FIX-189` (the pre-existing O2M FK force-select, the last site that
still mutates a caller-owned `FieldOptions`), and `FIX-190` (behavior-level unit
coverage for the emitted `unionColumns` helper).

### FIX-184

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go` (+ PRD §30.4.2)
- **Surfaced by:** 25.9 auto-review (2026-09-04)

**Issue.** **Every manifest entity's `files[]` hardcodes the `file_per_table`
spelling, so under the default `single_file` layout it names a Go file that does
not exist.** `builder.go:388` sets `Files: tableFiles(tc)` and `:443` sets
`Files: []string{vc.SnakeName + "_gen.go"}`. Neither consults
`cfg.Output.Layout`. Measured across the example tree: the `sqlite` example sets
`output.layout: file_per_table`, and its manifest's `["article_gen.go"]` is
**correct** — the file is there. The `graphql` example takes the default
`single_file` layout, and its manifest claims `["workspace_note_gen.go"]` /
`["workspace_note_summary_gen.go"]` while the emitted files are `models_gen.go`
and `views_gen.go`. `tenancy_postgres`, `postgres` and `mysql` are in the same
wrong state — four affected trees, not seven: `tenancy`, `cache` and `events`
carry no `manifest:` block and emit no manifest at all (nor do
`graphql_null_wrappers`, `graphql_top_level`, `postgres_stdlib` or
`tenancy_mysql` — 7 of the 12 examples emit none), so only the five that do
(the four above plus the correct `sqlite`) are in scope. Every
`files[]` entry across those four resolves to nothing on disk (0/21 postgres,
0/16 mysql, 0/18 graphql, 0/4 tenancy_postgres), against 20/20 correct on
`sqlite`. The manifest is the surface the MCP server and any agent reads to find
generated code, so this sends a reader — human or agent — to a path that does
not resolve. `sqlgen_get_entity` hands it out in both modes: `compactEntity`
(`cmd/sqlgen/mcp/tools_entity.go:118`) does not strip `files`. The markdown
surface is wrong in step, via the `## Files` section of
`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/templates/entity.md.tmpl:37`.

**Root cause.** `tableFiles` (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go:508-510`) returns
`tc.SnakeName + "_gen.go"` unconditionally, and the view arm (`:443`) inlines the
same expression. The builder already receives the whole config (`Build(in
BuildInput)` guards `in.Config == nil` at `:45`) and already derives a
`layout` variable at `:52` — but `layoutString` (`:91-96`) reads
`cfg.Generation.Manifest.JSONLayout`, which is the manifest's **JSON** layout
(`single` / `per_entity`), an unrelated knob from `output.layout`
(`single_file` / `file_per_table`). The name collision is most of why this
survived: a reader of `Build` sees a `layout` in scope and reasonably assumes
the file naming is already layout-aware.

**Suggested fix.**
- Give `tableFiles` / the view arm the layout: under
  `config.LayoutFilePerTable` keep `<snake>_gen.go`; under
  `config.LayoutSingleFile` emit `models_gen.go` for tables and `views_gen.go`
  for views — the names `gen` actually writes
  (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go:545,592` and `:631,678`).
- Rename the `layout` local in `Build` (`builder.go:52`) to `jsonLayout`, or
  rename `layoutString` to `manifestJSONLayout`. The collision is load-bearing
  in how this shipped; leaving both called `layout` invites the same mistake.
- **Do NOT change `file_prefix`.** It is spec-correct as the per-entity markdown
  / JSON prefix (PRD §30 "File naming"), and FIX-163 exists because it was
  derived some other way. Only `files[]` is wrong. Note that §30's file-naming
  paragraph asserts `manifest/<prefix>.md` sits "beside `<prefix>_gen.go`",
  which is itself a `file_per_table` assumption in the spec — the amendment
  should say the equality holds only under that layout.
- **Regression test:** extend `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder_test.go` with a
  table-driven case over both `output.layout` values asserting `files[]` for a
  table and a view. Stronger still, and in the shape FIX-180 / FIX-182
  established: a drift guard that reads the checked-in golden tree and asserts
  every `files[]` entry names a file that exists on disk — that is the assertion
  whose absence let this ship, and it would have caught it in seven example
  trees at once.

**References.**
- PRD §30.4.2 — entity fields, `files`; PRD §30 "File naming" (the
  `<prefix>_gen.go` adjacency claim that needs the layout qualifier).
- PRD §23.x / `config.Layout` — `single_file` (default) vs `file_per_table`
  (`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:62,160`).
- `FIX-180` / `FIX-182` — the "the manifest names things that do not exist"
  family. Both were fixed with an AST/golden drift guard rather than a
  point edit; this is the third member and wants the same treatment.
- `FIX-163` — why `file_prefix` must keep reading `SnakeName` verbatim.
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/sqlgen.yml:20` — the one example whose
  layout makes the current output correct, which is why no golden disagreed.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-05. `files[]` now follows
`output.layout`. The mapping moved into `gen` as its single owner —
`gen.TableFileName` / `gen.ViewFileName` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/filenames.go`) — and
both sides read it: the four emission sites in `orchestrate.go` (`:563`, `:602`,
`:649`, `:688`) and the manifest builder's `tableFiles` / new `viewFiles`
(`builder.go:513-534`). The two goimports resolution anchors (`:555`, `:641`)
deliberately keep the bare `modelsFileName` / `viewsFileName` constants — they
name the path import resolution runs against once over the concatenated bodies,
not a file any one entity is emitted to, and routing them through the helper
would have changed import resolution under `file_per_table`.

The name collision the entry called load-bearing is gone: `layoutString` is now
`manifestJSONLayout`, the `Build` local is `jsonLayout`, and the new `goLayout`
carries `Output.Layout` to `buildTableEntity` / `buildViewEntity`. Anything that
is not `file_per_table` resolves to the single-file name, mirroring
`generateTables`' own dispatch, so an unset `Layout` on a hand-built config
cannot yield a third answer. `file_prefix` was not touched (FIX-163).

**Scope correction to the entry as filed:** four example trees were wrong, not
seven — `tenancy`, `cache` and `events` carry no `manifest:` block and emit no
manifest at all. Measured before the fix: 0/21 postgres, 0/16 mysql, 0/18
graphql, 0/4 tenancy_postgres, against 20/20 correct on `sqlite`.

**Tests.** `TestEntityFilesExistOnDisk`
(`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/files_drift_test.go`) is the drift guard the entry asked
for — it walks all 10 checked-in golden manifests (`models/` and `expected/`
both) and stats every `files[]` entry, covering both `output.layout` values and
both `json_layout` values including the per-entity `entities/*.json`. Verified
failing-first: it failed on 8 of 10 trees before the builder change, with sqlite
passing throughout. `TestBuild_EntityFilesFollowOutputLayout`
(`builder_test.go`) is the unit half — table-driven over `single_file`,
`file_per_table` and unset, asserting `files[]` for a table and a view and
pinning `file_prefix` as layout-independent in the same cases.

**PRD.** §30 "File naming" gained the layout qualifier — the
`<prefix>.md` beside `<prefix>_gen.go` adjacency holds only under
`file_per_table` — and §30.4.2 gained the `files[]` rule plus a corrected
example, including the explicit statement that the field is the entity's *body*
file and not an index of every file mentioning it (`sorter_gen.go`,
`cache_gen.go`, `event_hooks_gen.go`, the `*_gen.graphqls` are found through
`conventions` / `features`).

**Verification.** `make check` clean except two pre-existing `parser` failures
(`TestBuildView_AggregateInference/ARRAY_AGG{,_with_base}`) that belong to
commit `bf64821` and are untouched by this diff — no `parser/` file appears in
it. `make check-examples` clean across all 13 example modules. Golden churn is
83 files in `models/` and 83 in `expected/`, and every changed line is a
`_gen.go` filename in a `files[]` array or a `## Files` markdown bullet;
`sqlite` is byte-identical, which is the check that the `file_per_table` path
did not move.

### FIX-183

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 25, `parser/view.go` (+ PRD §16.3)
- **Surfaced by:** 25.8 (2026-09-04), while diagnosing the `JSON_ARRAYAGG` panic-resolver defect
- **Re-verified:** 2026-09-04 against live PostgreSQL 16 on both drivers. **Severity raised `tracked` → `blocking`, and the original prescription replaced — it was measured not to work.** The prior write-up called this "a capability gap, not a correctness bug ... nothing is silently wrong"; that holds on pgx and is false on stdlib.

**Issue.** **On the stdlib driver every read of a view carrying `ARRAY_AGG` fails at
runtime.** On pgx the same view reads correctly but cannot be exposed on the
GraphQL surface at all. `inferAggregateType` (`parser/view.go:326-341`) returns
`"[]any"` for `ARRAY_AGG` and `"any"` from its `default` arm. Because that value
lands in `GoTypeLiteral`, `viewColumnGoType` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go:191`)
takes the `FromLiteral` arm and the SQL-to-Go resolver never runs — so
`GoType.IsSlice` stays false, and `buildSingleScanShape`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:1966-1971`, shared by views through
`context_view.go:81`) emits a bare `&t.Field` target instead of wrapping in
`pq.Array`. Measured by generating an `ARRAY_AGG` view into the
`postgres_stdlib` example and reading it through the generated client against
PostgreSQL 16:

```
GetMany err=scan tag_rollup: stdlib scan: sql: Scan error on column index 1,
  name "product_names_arr": unsupported Scan, storing driver.Value type []uint8
  into type *[]interface {}
```

pgx scans `[]any` natively, which is why no shipped example caught this: the only
PostgreSQL + stdlib example (`postgres_stdlib`) has no `ARRAY_AGG` view, and every
example that does use aggregates heavily (`graphql`, `postgres`,
`tenancy_postgres`) is on pgx.

**Root cause.** `inferAggregateType` takes `(aggregate, baseType string)` and
already receives the source column's SQL type, but only `SUM` / `MIN` / `MAX`
use it — `parser/view.go:213-243` routes those three through `resolveFromSchema`
+ the `col.Aggregate` field so codegen can apply dialect-aware handling, while
every other aggregate takes the `col.GoTypeLiteral = col.Type` branch and is
frozen at parse time. `ARRAY_AGG` was never given an element type because the
machinery to resolve one existed but was wired to a three-case allow-list; the
`default` arm's `any` is the honest answer for an aggregate the parser does not
recognise and should stay.

**Measured scan matrix** (PostgreSQL 16; `{a,b}` = populated aggregate,
`{NULL}` = the array a `LEFT JOIN` group with no matching rows produces):

| Go type | lib/pq `{a,b}` | lib/pq `{NULL}` | pgx `{a,b}` | pgx `{NULL}` |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| `[]any` (today) | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `[]string` | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| `[]*string` | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `[]sql.NullString` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Two facts constrain the choice. **`ARRAY_AGG` over an outer join returns
`{NULL}` — an array containing NULL, not NULL** — so `[]string` fails on that
shape. But **the shipped table path has the identical limitation**: a plain
`text[]` column holding a NULL element already fails to scan today
(`pq: parsing array element index 1: cannot convert nil to string`), so
`[]string` inherits an existing, already-shipped semantic rather than
introducing a new defect class. The idiomatic SQL remedy
`ARRAY_AGG(x) FILTER (WHERE x IS NOT NULL)` returns whole-`NULL` for an empty
group, which scans cleanly into `[]string` as a nil slice — verified.

**Decision (2026-09-04): resolve to `[]T`, document the `FILTER` idiom.** Element
type stays consistent with the table array path and yields a clean GraphQL
`[String!]`; `[]sql.NullString` was rejected because it diverges from the table
path for a case the project already accepts everywhere else.

**Suggested fix.** The prescription below replaces the original, which proposed
returning the Go literal `[]<elem>` from `inferAggregateType`. **That was measured
not to work:** `FromLiteral` never sets `IsSlice` (`cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go:725`),
so the column would still take the unwrapped `&t.Field` scan target and still fail
with `unsupported Scan`. The type must reach the model through the **resolver**,
which is the only path that sets `IsSlice` and therefore the only one that earns
`pq.Array` wrapping.

- **Bless first — this amends PRD §16.3's documented fallback, so it needs spec
  text before code (project rule 1).** The delta: `ARRAY_AGG` resolves its element
  type from the source column when one is resolvable, PostgreSQL only, with a note
  on the `{NULL}` / `FILTER` interaction. **While in §16.3, fix the live drift
  beside it:** the section still documents `JSON_AGG` / `JSONB_AGG` /
  `JSON_ARRAYAGG` and the `*_OBJECT_AGG` family as `json.RawMessage`, but 25.8
  shipped `types.JSON` and the PRD was never amended.
- `parser/view.go:326-341` — give `ARRAY_AGG` a `baseType`-aware arm returning the
  **SQL array type** (`baseType + "[]"`), not a Go literal, falling back to
  `"[]any"` when `resolveFromSchema` returns `""` (an aggregate over an expression
  rather than a column, where no element type exists to find).
- `parser/view.go:225-237` — add `"ARRAY_AGG"` to the `SUM`/`MIN`/`MAX` case so
  `col.Aggregate` is recorded and `GoTypeLiteral` is left empty, letting the value
  flow to the resolver. The `baseSQL == ""` arm already falls back to the
  fail-closed literal.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go:190-206` — route `col.Aggregate == "ARRAY_AGG"`
  to `resolver.ResolveAggregate`, alongside the existing `SUM` arm.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go:404-416` — **the dialect gate, which the original
  prescription omitted and which is load-bearing.** `ResolveAggregate` must return
  the fail-closed `[]any` for `ARRAY_AGG` on any dialect other than PostgreSQL.
  Without it, `text[]` reaches `builtinResolve`, misses every mapping, and hits the
  **`return r.goTypeFromInfo(goString, nullable)`** unknown-type fallback — binding
  the column to `string`. That is precisely the fail-open class this entry's
  sibling defect (25.8) was about, and the array branch at `gotype.go:544` is
  already PostgreSQL-gated for the same reason.
- Leave the `default` arm returning `any`. An unrecognised aggregate genuinely
  has no inferable type, and `@type` is the documented escape.
- **Regression tests.** Extend `parser/view_test.go:186-199`'s aggregate table with
  the resolvable and unresolvable `ARRAY_AGG` shapes (note the existing
  `{"ARRAY_AGG", ..., "[]any", false}` row covers the unresolvable case and must
  stay green). Add a `gen` unit test pinning that the resolved column carries
  `IsSlice` and renders the `pq.Array` scan target. **The example fixture must go
  in a PostgreSQL example — `postgres_stdlib` is the one that reproduces the bug**;
  the original prescription's "`mysql` or `sqlite`" is impossible, since neither
  dialect has `ARRAY_AGG` and the resolver's array branch is PostgreSQL-gated.
  Keep `TestBuildAPIContext_viewColumnWithNoGraphQLBindingIsRejected` green for the
  `any` arm, which must still be refused.

**Verification already performed (2026-09-04).** A prototype of exactly the above
was applied and measured, then reverted: the column resolves to `[]string`, the
scan target becomes `pq.Array(&t.ProductNamesArr)`, the model-side filter improves
from `*comparator.String` to `*comparator.Slice[string]`, and `GetMany` returns
`[]string{"prod-1","prod-2"}` end-to-end against PostgreSQL 16 on the stdlib
driver. `parser`, `cmd/sqlgen/gotype` and `cmd/sqlgen/gen` tests all passed with
**zero golden churn** — no shipped example uses `ARRAY_AGG` over a resolvable
source column, so the change is additive.

**References.**
- PRD §16.3 — view column type resolution (annotation files); the section this
  fix amends, including the stale `json.RawMessage` rows.
- PRD §26.4.1 — "codegen errors rather than silently producing a non-compiling
  resolver", the rule the current GraphQL-side refusal already satisfies.
- `parser/view.go:213-243` (the `GoTypeLiteral` vs `Aggregate` routing),
  `parser/view.go:283-307` (`resolveFromSchema`), `parser/view.go:326-341`
  (`inferAggregateType`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go:189-207` (`viewColumnGoType`) and
  `context_view.go:81` (views share `buildScanShapes` with tables).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go:544-568` (the PostgreSQL array branch — the only
  producer of `IsSlice`), `:725` (`FromLiteral`, which never sets it).
- **The sibling defect this was found beside, and is deliberately unlike:** 25.8
  corrected `inferAggregateType`'s JSON aggregates from `json.RawMessage` to
  `types.JSON`. That one failed *open* — `registerScalarUse` is
  first-registration-wins keyed on the scalar name, so a project with both
  `types.JSON` tables and a `json.RawMessage` view silently dropped the view's
  binding and gqlgen answered the field with a panicking resolver that compiled.
  Guarded since by `TestE2EGoldenResolvers_NoUnboundFieldStubs`
  (`cmd/sqlgen/e2e_resolver_stub_test.go`). Any fix here must not reintroduce a
  fallback binding for an unbindable type.
- `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` §25.8 Completion Record — the investigation that
  produced this entry, including why the two fallbacks were left unchanged.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-04. Landed as specified above, spec first.

**PRD §16.3** now reads `ARRAY_AGG(...)` → `[]T` from the source column, PostgreSQL only,
with `[]any` for an unresolvable element type and for MySQL / SQLite. Two notes were added
beside the SUM-widening paragraph: one stating that the resolved slice is what carries the
array flag and therefore the driver's array scan handling (a Go slice literal produced any
other way does not, and fails to scan), one covering the `{NULL}` / `FILTER` interaction.
The stale `JSON_AGG` / `JSONB_AGG` / `JSON_ARRAYAGG` and `*_OBJECT_AGG` rows were corrected
from `json.RawMessage` to `types.JSON`, closing the drift 25.8 left behind.

**Code**, three files, one concern each. `parser/view.go` — `inferAggregateType`'s
`ARRAY_AGG` arm returns `baseType + "[]"`, the SQL array type, and `ARRAY_AGG` joins
`SUM`/`MIN`/`MAX` in the routing switch so `col.Aggregate` is recorded and `GoTypeLiteral`
left empty; the `baseSQL == ""` arm already fell back to the fail-closed literal.
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go` — `viewColumnGoType` routes `ARRAY_AGG` to
`ResolveAggregate`. `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go` — `ResolveAggregate` returns
`FromLiteral("[]any")` for `ARRAY_AGG` on any non-PostgreSQL dialect. **That gate is the
part the original prescription omitted and is load-bearing**: without it an array SQL type
misses every builtin mapping and lands on `builtinResolve`'s unknown-type `goString`
fallback, binding the column to `string`. Measured — reverting `gotype.go` alone turns the
MySQL case into `GoType = "string", want "[]any"`.

**Why not the original prescription.** It proposed returning the Go literal `[]<elem>` from
`inferAggregateType`. That lands in `GoTypeLiteral` → `FromLiteral`, which never sets
`IsSlice`, so `buildSingleScanShape` keeps the bare `&v.Field` target and the column still
fails with `unsupported Scan`. Measured against PostgreSQL 16: `pq.Array(&[]string)`
succeeds where both `[]any` and an unwrapped `&[]string` fail.

**Tests**, each verified failing-first. `parser/view_test.go` — an `ARRAY_AGG with base` row
(`text` → `text[]`) plus `TestBuildView_ArrayAggRouting`, which pins the routing itself:
resolvable ⇒ `GoTypeLiteral == ""` and `Aggregate == "ARRAY_AGG"`, unresolvable ⇒ the frozen
`[]any`. Nothing asserted that routing before, which is how the original prescription looked
plausible. `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_test.go` — `TestBuildViewContexts_arrayAgg`, table-driven
over postgres/stdlib (`[]string`, `IsSlice`, `pq.Array(&p.ProductNames)`), postgres/pgx
(native `&p.ProductNames`) and mysql (`[]any`, no slice). `postgres_stdlib`'s `category_stats`
gained `ARRAY_AGG(p.name) FILTER (WHERE p.name IS NOT NULL) AS product_name_list`, asserted
non-empty on a populated category and nil on an empty one. Dropping the `FILTER` from that
fixture reproduces `pq: parsing array element index 0: cannot convert nil to string` in
`TestCategoryStatsEmptyCategory`, so the idiom the PRD documents is pinned by a test rather
than only described.

**Sweep.** `make check` and `make check-examples` clean; goldens regenerated. **Churn is
confined to `postgres_stdlib`** — the `CategoryStat` model gains `ProductNameList []string`,
the scan switch gains `pq.Array(&c.ProductNameList)`, `views_gen.go` gains the `lib/pq`
import, and the filter gains `*comparator.NullableSlice[string]`; the new `warehouse_roles`
view adds itself to `client_gen.go` and `tablenames_gen.go`. No other example moved, because
none uses `ARRAY_AGG` over a resolvable source column.

**Two auto-review findings were fixed in the same change**, both verified failing-first and
both squarely in this fix's blast radius:

1. **`isAggregateNullable` now reports `ARRAY_AGG` as nullable** (`parser/view.go`). It sat in
   the `default: false` arm, which was already questionable — an aggregate over zero rows is
   SQL NULL, the same reason `MIN`/`MAX` are nullable — and became an outright inconsistency
   once §16.3 started recommending `FILTER`, whose emptied group returns NULL, and once the
   new E2E asserted exactly that nil result. The Go type is unchanged (`resolveByType`'s array
   branch ignores `nullable`, and a slice conveys NULL as nil); the flag drives the comparator
   and the manifest, so the filter moves `Slice[string]` → `NullableSlice[string]`, matching
   what a nullable `text[]` **table** column has always produced.
2. **View columns now carry `SliceElemType`** (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go`). The table
   path set it (`context_table.go:842-843`); the view path did not. **This was a pre-existing
   non-compile, reproduced against the pre-fix binary** and therefore not caused by this entry:
   a view selecting a PostgreSQL enum array emitted `*comparator.Slice[UserRoleSlice]` —
   `UserRoleSlice` is a `[]UserRole` and does not satisfy `comparable` — and additionally
   wrapped a named slice with its own `Scan`/`Value` in `pq.Array`. One field fixes both,
   because `buildSingleScanShape` and the filter both key off it. `ARRAY_AGG(<enum column>)`
   would have been a second route into the same defect. Covered by
   `TestBuildViewContexts_enumSliceColumn` and by a `warehouse_roles` view in the example, so
   the shape is now compiled and read end to end.

**Left alone deliberately.** `docs/tracker/phase-6.md` and `docs/tracker/IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md`
still record `ARRAY_AGG → []any` as phase 6's as-built behaviour. Those are historical records
of what that phase shipped; the PRD is the source of truth and is where the amendment belongs.

### FIX-182

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 18, manifest (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go` + `sql.go`) + PRD §30.4.2 / `docs/design/MANIFEST.md` §5.3
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-181 verification (2026-09-03), while confirming what `increment.go.tmpl` names its method

**Issue.** **`methods[]` does not describe the generated Go client. Its entire method
vocabulary — names, param names, param types, return types, notes, and `sql_bodies` — is
back-formed from a doc example rather than read from the real surface.** This is FIX-180's class
(the manifest advertising symbols the generated package does not declare) applied to the block
that *contains* `errors[]`, and at full scale. **FIX-181 (`Increment` missing from `methods[]`) is
one line of it and is superseded by this entry.**

`counters` in the shipped postgres example. Manifest vs. the generated `CounterClient` interface
(`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/postgres/expected/models_gen.go:10035`) and PRD §9:

| Manifest advertises | Actually generated |
|---|---|
| `FindByID(id)` | `Get(ctx, id, opts...)` — no `FindByID` is generated anywhere |
| `List(f, s, p) *CounterList` | `GetMany(ctx, *GetCountersInput, opts...) []*Counter` |
| `Walk(f, fn func(*Counter) error)` | `Stream(ctx, *StreamCountersInput, opts...) iter.Seq2[*Counter, error]` |
| `Exists(f CounterFilter)` | `Exists(ctx, pk)`; the filter form is the separate `ExistsWhere` |
| `Create(in CounterInput)` | `Create(ctx, *CreateCounterInput, opts...)` |
| `Update(id, in CounterUpdate)` | `Update(ctx, id, *UpdateCounterInput, opts...)` |
| `Delete(id)`, `errors: ["ErrNotFound"]` | `HardDelete(ctx, id, opts...)` — and §9.5 makes it *idempotent*, returning `nil` on a missing PK |
| `UpsertConflictKey(in)`, one per conflict target | one `Upsert(ctx, input, target CounterConflictTarget, opts...)` |
| `FindBy<Col>` from every non-partial UNIQUE index | nothing generates these |

The param and return **types** are fictional too: `CounterInput`, `CounterUpdate`, `CounterSort`,
`Page` and `*CounterList` are not declared in the generated package. Only `CounterFilter` is real;
the sorter is `CounterSorter`.

Beyond `Increment`, the block omits `CreateMany`, `UpdateMany`, `UpdateWhere`, `ExistsWhere`,
`SoftDeleteMany` / `SoftDeleteWhere`, `Restore` / `RestoreMany` / `RestoreWhere`, `HardDeleteMany` /
`HardDeleteWhere`, `Paginate` and `Connection`. Views carry the same defect: the real surface is
`Get` / `GetMany` / `Count` / `Paginate` / `Connection`, and `buildViewMethods` advertises
`List` / `Count`. (`Refresh` / `RefreshConcurrently` on matviews are correct.)

`errors[]` is wrong in both directions on the entries that survive renaming. `Get` omits
`ErrNotFound` although PRD §10 ("`Get` is a thin wrapper that adds `ErrNotFound` semantics") and
`get.go.tmpl:132` both return it, and it carries the contradicting note *"Returns (nil, nil) when
not found."*. `Delete` / `SoftDelete` claim `ErrNotFound`, which §9.5's non-existent-PK table
explicitly rules out for all three idempotent deletes and which no delete template returns.
`Update`'s `ErrNotFound` is unconditional though the template gates it on `.StrictUpdates`. The
three `*Where` methods can return `ErrEmptyFilter` and `Paginate` / `Connection`
`ErrInvalidCursor`; none is advertised.

`sql_bodies` diverge on the same three by-PK mutations, all in the direction of claiming clauses
the generated code does not emit:

- `sqlUpdateByPK` (`sql.go:246`), `sqlHardDeleteByPK` (`sql.go:258`) and `sqlSoftDeleteByPK`
  (`sql.go:269`) all append `trailingSoftDelete`. The generated `Update`, `HardDelete` and
  `SoftDelete` pass `Conditions: []sql.Condition{sql.Where("id").Eq(id)}` — no
  `AND "deleted_at" IS NULL`. (Reads *do* apply the guard, so `sqlFindByPK` / `sqlList` /
  `sqlCount` / `sqlWalk` are right to keep it.)
- `sqlUpdateByPK` appends `RETURNING` every column; the generated `Update` has no `RETURNING` and
  re-`Get`s the row.
- `sqlCreate` / `sqlUpsert` claim `RETURNING` every column; `insertAndResolveID` and
  `insertUpsertAndResolveID` both pass `ReturningColumns: []string{"id"}`.

**Why it matters.** MCP §31 is the consumer. `sqlgen_get_entity` hands an agent a method list to
write Go against, and every name in it fails to compile; `sqlgen_show_sql(entity, method)` is keyed
on those same names, so the tool's own documented example (`"What SQL does UpsertByEmail emit?"`,
`docs/design/MCP.md:574`) names a method that does not exist. `sqlgen manifest diff` cannot see a real
signature change because it is not tracking real signatures. The FIX-181 consequence is the
sharpest instance: an agent enumerating `methods[]` concludes there is no atomic-increment path and
writes a read-modify-write, which is the exact race `Increment` exists to close.

**Root cause.** `docs/design/MANIFEST.md:1497-1512` documents a worked example under
"Query (`c.Q.User()`)" / "Mutation (`c.M.User()`)" — a client shape that has never existed
(the real accessor is `client.Counters().Get(...)`, §20). PRD §30.4.2's entity-shape example
inherits its names, and `buildQueryMethods` / `buildMutationMethods` /
`uniqueIndexFindMethods` (`builder.go:1238-1377`) were implemented against that example rather than
against §9's method tables. The same mistake as FIX-180 — a block derived from prose instead of
read from the thing it describes — which is why the same remedy (a set-equality drift test against
checked-in generated code) is what closes it.

**Suggested fix.**

- **State the rule in PRD §30.4.2**: an entity's `methods.query[] + methods.mutation[]` is exactly
  the method set on its generated `<Entity>Client` interface (§9.1–§9.4a), gated by the same
  `Operations.*` flags `toResolvedOperations` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:1094`) resolves —
  `Get` / `GetMany` / `Count` unconditional, the rest per flag, `Increment` additionally on
  `len(IncrementColumns) > 0`, `SoftDelete` / `Restore` additionally on a detected soft-delete
  column.
- **Document the existing signature convention** rather than leaving it implicit: `params` omits
  the leading `ctx context.Context` and the trailing variadic `opts`; `returns` names the non-error
  result (`""` when the method returns only `error`); the error side lives in `errors[]`.
- **Rewrite `buildQueryMethods` / `buildMutationMethods`** to the real names, params and types.
  Query: `Get`, `GetMany`, `Exists`, `ExistsWhere`, `Count`, `Paginate`, `Connection`, `Stream`.
  Mutation: `Create`, `CreateMany`, `Update`, `UpdateMany`, `UpdateWhere`, `Upsert`, `Increment`,
  `SoftDelete{,Many,Where}`, `Restore{,Many,Where}`, `HardDelete{,Many,Where}`.
- **Delete `uniqueIndexFindMethods`** (`builder.go:1287-1312`), its `hardDeleteMethodName` /
  `softDeleteMethodName` / `upsertMethodName` helpers (`builder.go:1445-1467`), and the
  `source: {kind: "unique_index", columns: [...]}` payload — no generator emits `FindBy<Col>`, and
  `Upsert` is one method taking a `target <Entity>ConflictTarget`, not one method per target.
- **Fix `buildViewMethods`** (`builder.go:1470`) to `Get` / `GetMany` / `Count` / `Paginate` /
  `Connection`; leave the matview `Refresh` / `RefreshConcurrently` entries as FIX-180 left them.
- **Correct `errors[]`** at each site: add `ErrNotFound` to `Get` and drop its `(nil, nil)` note;
  drop `ErrNotFound` from `HardDelete` / `SoftDelete` / `Restore` (§9.5 idempotence); gate it on
  `tc.StrictUpdates` for `Update` and `Increment`; add `ErrEmptyFilter` to the three `*Where`
  methods and `ErrInvalidCursor` to `Paginate` / `Connection`.
- **Tenancy sentinels — `Increment` takes `pkMismatch`, not `inputMismatch`.** FIX-181's entry
  says otherwise; `increment.go.tmpl:46` gates `tenancy.ErrMismatch` on
  `{{- if and .Tenancy.InPrimaryKey .CompositePK }}` with **no `else` branch**, identical to
  `delete.go.tmpl:780` and unlike `update.go.tmpl:49`. So `mutationTenancyErrors(ctx.tenancy,
  ctx.tenancy.pkVerify)`. `Get` and `Exists` take the same shape.
- **Drop `trailingSoftDelete` from `sqlUpdateByPK` / `sqlHardDeleteByPK` / `sqlSoftDeleteByPK`**
  and the all-column `returningColumns` from `sqlUpdateByPK`; narrow `sqlCreate` / `sqlUpsert`
  `RETURNING` to the PK column.
- **Extend the `sql_bodies` placeholder-token set** beyond `<filter>` / `<sort>` / `LIMIT $N` for
  the clauses the runtime assembles from caller input, and document the additions in PRD §30.4.2
  and `docs/design/MANIFEST.md` §5.3: `<set>` (Update's SET list, built from whichever omittable fields
  are set), `<columns>` / `<values>` (Create / Upsert), `<conflict_target>` (the target-selected
  conflict columns), and `<column>` (Increment's target column). The all-column forms are wrong
  about both the column list and the placeholder numbering.
- **Add `sqlIncrement`** alongside the `sqlUpdateByPK` / `sqlUpsert` family in `sql.go`, calling
  `sqlpkg.BuildIncrement` (**not** `BuildIncrementReturning` — that variant exists only to capture
  the tenant column internally) with PK conditions and no soft-delete guard. Note the inverted
  placeholder order: `sql/builder.go:275` places the amount at `$1` and starts the `WHERE` at `$2`,
  unlike every other mutation body. Canonical postgres form:
  `UPDATE "public"."counters" SET <column> = <column> + $1 WHERE "key" = $2`.
- **Regression test — `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/method_drift_test.go`** (new), modelled directly on
  `sentinel_drift_test.go`'s AST approach: parse the checked-in
  `testdata/examples/postgres/models/models_gen.go`, collect each `<Entity>Client` interface's
  method names, and assert set equality both directions against
  `methods.query[].name + methods.mutation[].name` for that entity. This is what makes the block
  unable to drift again and the reason to do the whole surface in one pass.
- **Update the two spec sources** so the fabrication has no home left: PRD §30.4.2's worked example
  and `docs/design/MANIFEST.md`'s `c.Q.User()` / `c.M.User()` blocks (lines 971-1027 and 1490-1512).

**Blast radius.** 73 entities across the four manifest-emitting examples (postgres 21, sqlite 20,
mysql 16, graphql 16), duplicated in `expected/` and `models/`: **146 markdown files, 8
`manifest_gen.json`, 10 files under `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/testdata`**. 61 assertions across 10 test
files pin the old names, including the `find_method(FindByID)` target selection in all four
`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/*/tests/mcp_test.go` legs and `cmd/sqlgen/mcp/fixture_test.go`.
**No JSON-schema change** — every entry is `$defs/method` with existing keys, so `schema_version`
stays at `0.1.0` per user direction. `sentinel_drift_test.go`'s
`TestMethodErrorsNameRealSentinels` already walks both method groups and so covers the new and
renamed entries' `errors` the moment they exist.

**References.** PRD §9.1–§9.5 (the authoritative generated-method tables), §9.8, §10 (`Get`'s
`ErrNotFound` wrapper semantics), §20 (unified client accessor shape), §29.4.2 / §29.7 (tenancy on
mutations), §30.4.2 (entity shape — to amend), §30.7; `docs/design/MANIFEST.md` §5.3 + the worked example
at lines 1490-1512 (to amend); `docs/design/MCP.md` §4.1 / §7 (`sqlgen_get_entity`, `sqlgen_show_sql`);
`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/sentinel_drift_test.go` (the drift-guard pattern to copy);
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/{get,exists,create,update,upsert,increment,delete,pagination,stream}.go.tmpl`;
**FIX-181** (superseded by this entry — its `Increment` gap is one bullet above, and its stated
tenancy-error shape is corrected here); **FIX-180** (the same class, same root cause, narrower
scope).

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-03. `buildQueryMethods` / `buildMutationMethods` /
`buildViewMethods` now emit the real `<Entity>Client` surface, gated on the same `Operations.*`
flags `toResolvedOperations` resolves: 8 query + up to 16 mutation entries per table, and up to 5
per view (was 2). Ten of the 24 table methods had a wrongly-named counterpart in the old block;
the other fourteen — `Increment` among them — had none at all. `uniqueIndexFindMethods`, `findByUniqueName`,
`uniqueIndexParams`, `sameAsPK`, `hardDeleteMethodName`, `softDeleteMethodName`, `upsertMethodName`
and `camel` are deleted; `mutationTenancyErrors` is renamed `tenancyErrors` and joined by four
per-shape helpers, because the mismatch guard turned out to have **four** shapes, not two —
input-verify (Create/CreateMany/Update/UpdateMany/Upsert), pk-verify (the by-PK and batch methods,
`Increment` among them), never (the filter-only methods), and `!inPK` (UpdateWhere alone, whose
input-side check `table/update.go.tmpl:719` skips when the tenant lives in the key). `tenancyReach`
gains `inPK` for that last one.

`sql.go` was rewritten around the corrected bodies. `trailingSoftDelete` came off the three by-PK
mutations, `sqlUpdateByPK` lost its all-column `RETURNING`, and `sqlCreate`/`sqlUpsert` narrowed
theirs to the PK — and to nothing at all for a composite-PK entity or a MySQL package, which resolve
the key without `RETURNING`. Nine helpers were added for the previously-unadvertised methods. The
token set gained `<set>`, `<columns>`, `<values>`, `<conflict_target>`, `<excluded>`, `<column>`,
`<ids>` and `<pks>`, and **`LIMIT $N` became `LIMIT <limit>`** — a change beyond the entry's plan,
made because `sql.writeLimitOffset` interpolates the limit as a literal integer, so the old token
claimed a bind parameter that is never emitted. `Paginate` and `Connection` now carry **no**
`sql_bodies` key: they issue no statement of their own, composing `Count` and `GetMany`.

**Two further live fabrications surfaced in the same block and are fixed here.**
`conventions.client_entry_points` advertised `c.Q.<Entity>()` / `c.M.<Entity>()`, a client shape
that has never existed — the real accessor is one per entity (`client.Users()`, §20), carrying
reads and writes alike. And `conventions.find_returns_nil_on_missing` read `true` while §10 and
`get.go.tmpl:132` both make `Get` a thin wrapper that *adds* `ErrNotFound`; it now reads `false`,
which also removes a contradiction against the corrected `methods[].errors`.

**Regression tests.** `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/method_drift_test.go` (new) is the structural guard:
`TestMethodNamesMatchGeneratedClients` AST-parses the checked-in `postgres/models/models_gen.go` +
`views_gen.go`, collects each `<Entity>Client` interface's method set, and asserts set equality both
directions against the checked-in `manifest_gen.json` — the comparison whose absence let the defect
ship. `TestMethodParamTypesResolve` does the same for every type a param or return names. Both fail
loudly against the pre-fix goldens. `TestBuild_MethodErrors_MatchTemplateGuards` and
`TestBuild_MethodErrors_Tenancy` pin the error lists the drift test cannot see, table-driven over
`strict_updates` on/off and all four tenancy shapes. `TestBuild_SQLBodies_CoverEveryMethodType` was
rewritten over the real method names; `TestBuild_SQLBodies_InsertColumnSet` became
`TestBuild_SQLBodies_RuntimeClausesAreTokens`.

**Coverage note.** FIX-120's serial-PK-exclusion and FIX-122's DO-UPDATE-SET-exclusion invariants no
longer have a manifest expression to police — the expansions they corrected are now tokens. The
generator-side behavior is unchanged and covered by `cmd/sqlgen/gen`'s own tests, and the insertable
column set remains derivable from the entity's `columns[]` block (`default_kind` / `auto`). An
explicit per-column `insertable` marker was **not** added — that would be new schema surface, and no
consumer has asked for it.

**Docs.** PRD §30.4.2 gains the normative method-surface rule, the signature convention, the
per-method error rule, and the full token table; §30.7's `sql_bodies` row and §31's two tool examples
follow. `docs/design/MANIFEST.md` §5.1's worked example, §5.3's `sql_bodies` paragraph, §5.4's view note,
and the `c.Q.User()` / `c.M.User()` markdown-summary example are all rewritten against the real
surface, as are `docs/design/MCP.md`'s three `UpsertByEmail` references. `docs/tracker/IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md` and
the phase trackers are left alone — they record what was built at the time.

**Auto-review follow-ups, all fixed inline before close.** The `sqlgen-reviewer` pass found two
instances of FIX-182's own defect class surviving inside the fix, both confirmed against the
templates and the generated code before acting:

1. **`UpdateMany` advertised an `ErrNotFound` it can never return.** `buildUpdateMethods` shared one
   `writeErrs` slice between `Update` and `UpdateMany`, folding in the `strict_updates` sentinel for
   both. `table/update.go.tmpl` guards `ErrNotFound` at lines 177/192, inside `Update` alone;
   `UpdateMany` issues the same statement per item but never inspects `RowsAffected`, so a missing
   key is silent there even under `strict_updates` — confirmed by `grep -c ErrNotFound` over the
   generated `articleClient.UpdateMany` (0) against `Update` (1). It shipped on 46 entities and
   contradicted the rule this same change wrote into PRD §30.4.2.
2. **`UpdateWhere` and `HardDeleteWhere` sql_bodies still claimed a soft-delete guard.** Both called
   `filterConditions`, whose own doc comment scopes it to the read path. The generated bodies pass
   `filter.ToConditions()` alone — unlike `SoftDeleteWhere` and `RestoreWhere`, which append their
   own `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` guard explicitly. A new `filterOnly()` separates the two paths, and
   `sqlSoftDeleteWhere` now spells its guard out rather than borrowing the read helper, so the
   coincidence of predicates cannot be mistaken for a shared reason.

A third, pre-existing, was fixed with them: **MCP's `methodSignature` rendered no return list at all
when `Returns` is empty**, so `HardDelete(ctx, id string)` read as returning nothing. This fix
multiplied the affected set from one method to six per entity, and would have added a *spurious*
second `error` to `Stream`, whose `iter.Seq2[*T, error]` carries its own. All three return shapes are
now pinned by `TestMethodSignature_ReturnShapes`.

The reviewer's coverage gaps are closed: `TestBuild_MethodErrors_MatchTemplateGuards` grew from 14
methods to 23 (every `*Many` and `*Where` form, `UpdateMany` among them), and the sql_bodies test now
pins `HardDeleteWhere` and `SoftDeleteWhere` alongside `UpdateWhere`. Stale fixtures that still
carried the fabrication were updated — `cmd/sqlgen/mcp/testdata/manifest_gen.json`,
`cmd/sqlgen/cli/testdata/manifest/valid_single.json`, and the `manifest/testdata/golden/` trio, whose
`emit_json_test.go` source fixture gained a void-return method so the emitters exercise that shape.
`MethodSource`'s doc comment no longer cites the deleted `FindBy*` construct, `showSQL`'s `-32005`
text names the deliberate-omission case, and `entity.md.tmpl` renders a void return as `` `error` ``
rather than an empty code span.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all 8 modules (`cmd/sqlgen/cli` ~443s, `cmd/sqlgen/gen`
~253s); `make check-examples` clean across all 13 example modules. 189 golden files regenerated via
`make update-golden-e2e` across the four manifest-emitting examples in both `expected/` and
`models/` trees — including the `graphql` example's `manifest/entities/` per-entity JSON, which the
entry's blast-radius estimate missed. `schema_version` held at `0.1.0`; no JSON-schema change (every
entry is `$defs/method` with existing keys, and `source` stays declared-but-unpopulated). **FIX-181
is closed by this entry** — its `Increment` gap is one of the new mutation entries, and its stated
tenancy shape was corrected to `pkTenancy` as this entry predicted.

### FIX-181

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, manifest (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go`) + PRD §30.4.2
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-180 implementation + auto-review (2026-09-03), while mapping every template
  `tenancy.ErrMismatch` site to a manifest method
- **Superseded by:** **FIX-182** — verification on 2026-09-03 found the missing `Increment` entry is
  one symptom of a `methods[]` block whose entire vocabulary is fabricated. Resolve FIX-182 and this
  closes with it; do not implement this entry standalone (it would regenerate 146 goldens twice and
  leave `Increment` as the only real method name in the block). Two claims below are corrected there:
  the tenancy-error shape is `pkMismatch`, not `inputMismatch` (`increment.go.tmpl:46` has no `else`
  branch), and the blast radius is 73 entities across four examples, not two in postgres.

**Issue.** **`Increment` is generated but absent from `methods[]` entirely.** `buildMutationMethods`
(`builder.go:1319`) emits `Create`, `Update`, the hard/soft deletes, and one `Upsert` per conflict
target — and nothing else. `Operations.Increment` generates real client methods from
`table/increment.go.tmpl`; the shipped postgres example has **six** of them (`counters`,
`rate_limits`), and none appears in any manifest entity. `Counter`'s `methods.mutation` reads
`["Create", "Update", "Delete", "UpsertConflictKey"]`.

The builder already knows the method exists: `buildCacheFeature` lists `"Increment"` in
`features.cache.invalidates_on` (`builder.go:944`). So one block of the manifest names a method
that another block says the entity does not have.

**Why it matters.** This is the same advertise-vs-reality class as FIX-180, in the *other*
direction — a **missing** method rather than a fabricated error name. The consequences differ by
consumer: an agent enumerating `methods[]` through MCP §31 (`sqlgen_get_entity`,
`sqlgen_show_sql`) concludes the entity has no atomic-increment path and writes a
read-modify-write instead, which is the exact race `Increment` exists to close. `sqlgen manifest
diff` cannot see an increment signature change. And `sql_bodies` — the one place the canonical
`UPDATE … SET col = col + $n` form is published — omits it.

**It also hides tenancy errors.** `increment.go.tmpl:41` calls `resolveTenant` and `:49` returns
`tenancy.ErrMismatch`, so a tenanted entity's `Increment` can return both tenancy sentinels.
FIX-180 corrected `methods[].errors[]` on every method the builder emits; this one it could not
reach, because there is no entry to attach errors to.

**Root cause.** `buildMutationMethods` was written against the mutation set of PRD §30.4.2's worked
example, which shows `Create` / `Update` / `Delete` / `UpsertBy…` and no increment. §9's generated
method surface is the authority on what exists, and increment is not represented in §30.4.2 at all —
so this is a spec gap as much as a builder gap.

**Suggested fix.** Emit one `Method` per generated increment under `methods.mutation[]`, gated on
`Operations.Increment` the same way the template is. Three things need deciding first, which is why
this is not an inline FIX-180 correction — each is **new manifest content**, not a corrected string:

1. **Name and arity.** One `Increment` entry, or one per increment column? Follow whatever
   `increment.go.tmpl` actually names the methods (`IncrementViews` vs `Increment(column, delta)`) —
   read it, do not infer from the config key.
2. **`params` / `returns`.** Whether the delta is a typed scalar per column and whether the method
   returns the updated row or nothing.
3. **`sql_bodies`.** Needs a `sqlIncrement…` helper alongside the existing `sqlUpdateByPK` /
   `sqlUpsert` family in `sql.go`, rendering the canonical `UPDATE … SET col = col + $n WHERE …`
   per dialect.

`errors` then falls out of the existing FIX-180 machinery: `ErrNotFound` plus
`mutationTenancyErrors(ctx.tenancy, true)` — increment guards `ErrMismatch` on
`.Tenancy.InPrimaryKey` alone, both branches reachable, matching the create/update/upsert shape
rather than the by-PK deletes.

**Blast radius.** PRD §30.4.2 gains the increment method shape. Golden churn is confined to entities
with increment configured — in the current tree `counter.json` / `counter.md` and
`rate_limit.json` / `rate_limit.md` across the postgres `expected/` + `models/` trees, plus
`manifest_gen.json`. No JSON-schema change: `methods.mutation[]` items are `$defs/method` and an
added entry needs no new keys. **`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/sentinel_drift_test.go`'s
`TestMethodErrorsNameRealSentinels` already covers the new entry's `errors` the moment it exists** —
it walks every method in both groups.

**References.** PRD §9 (generated methods), §30.4.2 (entity shape), §29.4.2 (tenancy on mutations);
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/increment.go.tmpl`; FIX-180 (the same class, opposite direction).

**Resolution notes.** Closed by **FIX-182** (2026-09-03); no standalone work. `Increment` is now one
of the mutation entries FIX-182's rewritten `buildMutationMethods` emits, with the `pkTenancy` error
shape and the `<column>` token this entry's superseded-by note predicted.

### FIX-180

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, manifest (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go`) + PRD §30.4.1
- **Surfaced by:** 25.6 auto-review follow-up (2026-09-02), while blessing the view shape of `features.tenancy` (B9)
- **Verified + scope widened + decisions settled 2026-09-03. Resolved 2026-09-03.**

**Issue.** **The manifest advertises Go error sentinels that the generated package does not
declare.** The names are back-formed from GraphQL `extensions.code` values rather than read from
anything real. **Five** hardcoded sites are affected — the original entry named two; verification
on 2026-09-03 found three more:

| # | Manifest field | Advertised | Actually exists? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `features.tenancy.missing_resolver_error` (`builder.go:982`) | `ErrUnauthenticated` | **No.** The real sentinel is `tenancy.ErrMissing`; `UNAUTHENTICATED` is its *GraphQL code* (§26.5.5). |
| 2 | `features.tenancy.mismatch_error` (`builder.go:983`) | `ErrForbidden` | **No.** The real sentinel is `tenancy.ErrMismatch`; `FORBIDDEN` is its GraphQL code. |
