**Residual, acknowledged:** query methods keep `errors: []` even where `get.go.tmpl:95` / `exists.go.tmpl:45`
can return `tenancy.ErrMismatch`. That list was already curated rather than exhaustive — no read method has
ever listed `ErrDeadlock` / `ErrConnectionFailed` / `ErrInvalidCursor` — so adding only the tenancy sentinels
would have made the curation inconsistent rather than more complete.

### FIX-178

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 11, comparator (spec-level: PRD §11.2 vs §26.4)
- **Surfaced by:** 25.5 auto-review (2026-09-02)

**Issue.** **On SQLite a `JSONComparator` filter is accepted and silently does nothing.**
`comparator.JSON.Parse` has `postgres` and `mysql` arms and no `sqlite` arm, so both operators fall
through and the comparator contributes **zero** conditions — the accept-and-ignore class Phase 25
exists to eliminate, reintroduced through the dialect switch rather than through a missing
translator.

**Why the two sides both look correct.** PRD §11.2 says "SQLite JSON support can be added in the
future via the same pattern", so the runtime's silence is the *specified* state. PRD §26.4's
dialect-gating paragraph says "On MySQL / SQLite a `jsonb` column falls back to `JSONComparator`",
so 25.5's projection is also the specified behaviour. Each section is self-consistent; together
they specify a filter field that parses, dispatches into a real translator, and emits no SQL.
25.2's completeness lint will not catch it either — both surfaces are present, which is all the
lint checks.

**Reachability is narrow.** SQLite's built-in type table maps no column to `types.JSON` (measured:
`json` and `jsonb` both resolve to `string` there), so a column reaches this only through
`overrides.types` / `type_map` / `column_map.type` pointing at `types.JSON`. `TestJSONComparator_dialectGating`
currently pins the SQLite row as *emitting* the family, so the behaviour is deliberate and tested —
that assertion moves with whichever resolution is chosen.

**Decision needed.** (a) Add a `sqlite` arm to `comparator.JSON.Parse` (`json_extract(col, $) IS NOT
NULL` covers `HasKey`; `Contains` has no clean SQLite equivalent and needs its own answer); or
(b) gate the JSON family out of the GraphQL projection on SQLite, amending §26.4's fallback
sentence to name MySQL only. (b) is a small change local to 25.5's code; (a) closes the §11.2 gap
properly. Flagged rather than chosen for the same reason as FIX-177.

**Option (b) as first written is too narrow to close it.** The Go-side `<T>Filter` field comes from
`resolveSimpleComparator` (`context_table.go:1794`), the *same* derivation the GraphQL projection
reads. Gating only the projection leaves `UserFilter.Metadata *comparator.JSON` accepting
`Contains` / `HasKey` on SQLite and emitting nothing — the identical defect one layer down. The gate
has to sit at `columnIsFilterable` / `resolveSimpleComparator`, which serves both surfaces.

**Measured (2026-09-02) — SQLite 3.51.3 through `modernc.org/sqlite v1.48.1`, the repo's own driver,
against PostgreSQL 16 and MySQL 8.0 as controls.** Storage first: `types.JSON`'s `Valuer` returns
`[]byte`, so the value lands in a SQLite TEXT column as a **blob** (`typeof(doc)=blob`); SQLite's
JSON functions parse it anyway, so no `CAST` would be needed.

`HasKey` **has** a faithful SQLite form. `json_type(col, $) IS NOT NULL` matches MySQL's
`JSON_CONTAINS_PATH(col,'one',$)` on all six probed paths — including the one the entry's own
suggested `json_extract` form gets wrong:

| path | `json_type … IS NOT NULL` | `json_extract … IS NOT NULL` | MySQL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$.a` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `$.n` (key present, value `null`) | 1 | **0** | 1 |
| `$.zz` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `$.nested.k` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `$.tags[0]` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `$.tags[9]` | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The operand is a JSON path — MySQL's form, not PostgreSQL's bare key, which fails loudly
(`bad JSON path: 'a'`).

`Contains` has **none**. PG `@>` and MySQL `JSON_CONTAINS` agree on all ten probes against
`{"a":1,"tags":["x","y"],"n":null,"nested":{"k":"v"}}`; both SQLite emulations diverge:

| candidate | pg `@>` | mysql | sqlite `json_tree` path-eq | sqlite `json_patch` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{"a":1}` | t | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `{"a":2}` | f | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `{"nested":{"k":"v"}}` | t | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `{"tags":["x"]}` | t | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| `{"tags":["y"]}` | t | 1 | **0** | **0** |
| `{"tags":["y","x"]}` | t | 1 | **0** | **0** |
| `{"n":null}` | t | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| `{"a":1,"nested":{"k":"v"}}` | t | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `{"zz":1}` | f | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `{"nested":{}}` | t | 1 | 1 | 1 |

`@>` and `JSON_CONTAINS` do element-wise, order-independent array containment; every path-based
emulation is position-sensitive. A SQLite `Contains` would return a *plausible but wrong* subset —
F2, silently wrong data, strictly worse than today's over-broad no-op.

**One hazard is SQLite-only.** SQLite has no JSON column type, so nothing validates the stored text.
A single malformed row anywhere in the scanned set fails the entire query — `SQL logic error:
malformed JSON (1)` — including rows the filter would not have matched. PostgreSQL and MySQL cannot
reach this: their column type validates on write. Structurally the same class as FIX-177's
uncastable-`\u0000` limit, but far likelier.

**Decision (settled 2026-09-02, user).** Option **(b), extended to both surfaces**. §11.2's deferral
is the section that wins; §26.4's fallback sentence is amended to name MySQL only. A `types.JSON`
column on SQLite becomes **non-filterable on both sides** — no field in `<T>Filter`, no field in the
GraphQL input, no translator entry — which is the precedent §26.4 already sets for `json[]` /
`jsonb[]`. Nothing is accepted and ignored, on either surface. The door stays open: adding a
`sqlite` arm later re-enables the family with no surface break.

The other two options were rejected on the measurements above. Full (a) needs a `Contains` that does
not exist. A HasKey-only (a) cannot drop `Contains`: `comparator.JSON` is a dialect-agnostic struct,
so the operator would stay a silent no-op on SQLite and the entry's own defect class would survive.
Two further alternatives were considered and dropped: a generation-time error (the §11.2
PostgreSQL-only-comparator precedent) would forbid mapping a column to `types.JSON` on SQLite for
modelling reasons alone, which is legitimate; and `Opaque[types.JSON]` — blob equality, which does
work on SQLite — invents a classification and makes whitespace and key order load-bearing.

**Scope.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go` — `columnIsFilterable` takes the dialect and returns false for a
  `types.JSON` / `map[string]any` column under SQLite; `resolveSimpleComparator`'s JSON arm becomes
  unreachable there. Four call sites: `context_table.go:1592`, `context_api.go:3237`,
  `reserved_fields.go:138,151` — the last two need `dialect` threaded through
  `validateResolvedFieldNames` / `validateResolvedViewFieldNames`.
- `comparator/json.go` — type doc comment states the family is PostgreSQL / MySQL only and that
  `Parse` contributes no conditions on other dialects. The public runtime API keeps its silence;
  only the generated surface is gated.
- PRD §11.2 — the "JSON Comparator (all dialects with JSON support)" heading, the two `types.JSON`
  rows in the selection table, and the "SQLite JSON support can be added in the future" sentence,
  which becomes normative rather than aspirational. §26.4 — the dialect-gating sentence names MySQL
  only, and the "Non-filterable columns" paragraph gains this case. `guidelines/SQL.md` §13 mirrors.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_slice_json_comparator_test.go` — `TestJSONComparator_dialectGating`'s SQLite
  row flips from "emits `JSONComparator`" to "non-filterable on both sides", and the model side
  gains the matching assertion.

**Predicted churn: zero goldens.** None of the four SQLite configs (`cache`, `sqlite`, `tenancy`,
`events`) has a `types.JSON` column, and `JSONComparator` appears only in the `graphql` (postgres)
and `mysql` example trees.

**Accepted cost.** A SQLite user who overrides a column to `types.JSON` loses the filter field
entirely, including its `Custom` escape hatch — the same trade already accepted for `json[]` /
`jsonb[]` columns.

**References.**
- `comparator/json.go:37,45` — `JSON.Parse`, no `sqlite` case in either switch.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go:143` — `sqliteMappings`, no `json` / `jsonb` entry.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:1744,1794` — `columnIsFilterable`, `resolveSimpleComparator`.
- PRD §11.2 line 7202 "SQLite JSON support can be added in the future" vs §26.4 line 10827 "On
  MySQL / SQLite a `jsonb` column falls back to `JSONComparator`".
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_slice_json_comparator_test.go` — `TestJSONComparator_dialectGating`, the SQLite row.

**Resolution (2026-09-02).** Option (b) extended to both surfaces, as decided above.
`columnIsFilterable` now takes the dialect and returns false for a column whose resolved comparator
is `*comparator.JSON` / `*comparator.NullableJSON` under `config.DialectSQLite`. Keying it on
`resolveComparatorType` rather than on the Go type is what keeps the two surfaces in step: the
model side (`buildFilterFields`) and the GraphQL side (`mapColumnToGraphQL`) both read that one
predicate, so the `<T>Filter` field, the schema field, the comparator input and the translator entry
appear and disappear together, and a future `sqlite` arm in `Parse` re-enables all four at once. The
`json[]` / `jsonb[]` rule is untouched and still runs first. `dialect` was threaded through
`validateResolvedFieldNames` / `validateResolvedViewFieldNames` into `columnMemberScope` /
`viewColumnMemberScope` so the reserved-name scope agrees with the filter it is protecting.

`comparator.JSON.Parse` is **unchanged** — no `sqlite` arm, no new operators. Only its type doc
comment gained the reason, which the PRD now states normatively: the family covers PostgreSQL and
MySQL, and a hand-written filter reaching the silence on another dialect is the one path the gate
cannot close.

**Regression coverage, at three levels.**
- `comparator/json_test.go` — `TestJSON_Parse_SQLiteYieldsNoDocumentConditions` pins the runtime
  contract the gate is built on: both document operators drop on SQLite, `Custom` passes through,
  and `Null` still emits `data IS NULL`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_slice_json_comparator_test.go` — `TestJSONComparator_dialectGating`'s SQLite
  row flips from "emits `JSONComparator`" to absent on both surfaces: no input type, no translator,
  no `doc` field inside `input ProbeFilter` (scoped through the new `graphQLBlock` helper, since the
  column keeps its field on the object type and on the create / update inputs).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_slice_json_comparator_test.go` — `TestJSONComparator_sqliteModelSideNonFilterable`
  covers the half the GraphQL assertions cannot see: `FilterFieldContext.Filterable` is false and
  `ComparatorType` empty on SQLite, with MySQL as the control on the identical schema and override,
  and the `id` column asserted still filterable so the gate is not reading as "SQLite loses filters".

**Verified to fail without the fix.** Reverting the one predicate to `return true` fails all eight
assertions across the two generator tests, on exactly the surfaces the entry describes.

**Files.** `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go`,
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_view.go`, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/reserved_fields.go`,
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/reserved_fields_pin_test.go`, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_slice_json_comparator_test.go`,
`comparator/json.go`, `comparator/json_test.go`, `docs/PRD.md` §11.2 + §26.4,
`guidelines/SQL.md` §13.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all 33 modules; `make check-examples` clean across all
13 example modules. `make update-golden` + `make update-golden-e2e` produced **zero** churn,
confirming the prediction: no SQLite example carries a `types.JSON` column, so no generated file
moves.

**Auto-review follow-ups applied inline.** Three comments the gate falsified were corrected in
place: `context_api.go`'s "JSONComparator is emitted on ALL dialects" (now names the two dialects
and the structural SQLite gate), the "two ways a column loses its filter field" note above the
changed call site (now three), and `reserved_fields.go`'s `Filterable` field doc.

**Manifest divergence, surfaced by the review and fixed with it.** `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go`
derived each column's published `comparator` through `comparatorForColumn`, an independent,
dialect-less string-prefix match, while `buildFilter` read `FilterFieldContext.Filterable`. It was
the one surface FIX-178's "one predicate, all surfaces" claim did not reach — a SQLite `types.JSON`
column would have published `"comparator": "comparator.JSON"` while `filter.fields` omitted it.

The divergence long predates FIX-178 and was far wider than its SQLite tail. Measured against the
old classifier: an `interval` column published `comparator.Time` where the generated filter declares
`Number[time.Duration]`; every nullable column published the non-nullable spelling; `[]string`
published a bare `comparator.Slice` with no element type; a postgres `jsonb` column published `JSON`
rather than `JSONB`; and enum, `bytea`, `inet` and `numeric` columns published **nothing at all**
(the field is `omitempty`). FIX-103's `json[]` / `jsonb[]` columns published `comparator.Slice`
despite having no filter field.

`buildColumns` now takes the entity's `FilterFields` and reads the comparator from there —
`strings.TrimPrefix(ff.ComparatorType, "*")`, empty when the column is not filterable — and
`comparatorForColumn` is deleted. The published value is now exactly what `filter.fields[].type`
carries minus the leading `*`, so the two agree by construction. Same class as FIX-163 (`SnakeName`)
and the enum `go_type` fix: a second derivation of a fact the generator already owns.

`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder_test.go` gains `TestBuildColumns_ComparatorMirrorsFilterFields`, a
ten-column probe (uuid PK, text, nullable text, nullable integer, `interval`, `jsonb`, `bytea`,
`inet`, `text[]`, `jsonb[]`) pinning both the values and the column ↔ `filter.fields` agreement;
seven of its ten rows contradict the old classifier's measured output. Churn is **169 golden files**
(JSON + markdown manifests across the examples) — all of it the corrections above, no column losing
a comparator it should have kept. PRD §30.7 gains the field's row, which it never had; §30.4's
example (`"comparator": "comparator.ID"` on a uuid PK) was already correct and is unchanged.

### FIX-179

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 11, sql (`PrefixConditions`) + comparator (`comparator/json.go`)
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-177 auto-review (2026-09-02); **reproduced against a real MySQL 8.0 the same day**

**Issue.** **`sql.PrefixConditions` blind-prepends `alias + "."` to the whole clause, so any comparator
clause that does not *begin* with the column name is corrupted under an O2O join.** The MySQL JSON
arms are the only such clauses in the repo (`grep 'Clause: "' comparator/*.go` returns exactly
`comparator/json.go:41,49`), and they render as `u.JSON_CONTAINS(metadata, ?)`.

**Reachable in the shipped mysql example today — no schema change.** `users.metadata` is `JSON`,
`UserFilter.Metadata` is `*comparator.NullableJSON`, and `userClient.GetMany` emits
`sql.PrefixConditions("u", conds)` (`models_gen.go:20573`) whenever an O2O join is active. A
`GetMany` filtering on `metadata` with `FieldOptions.Profile` set fails at request time:

```
get users: query: Error 1370 (42000): execute command denied to user 'test'@'%'
                  for routine 'u.JSON_CONTAINS'
```

MySQL parses `u.JSON_CONTAINS(...)` as a call to a **stored routine** named `JSON_CONTAINS` in
schema `u`, so the error reads as a privilege problem and points nowhere near the real cause. As
root the same query gives `ERROR 1305: FUNCTION u.JSON_CONTAINS does not exist`.
`profiles.preferences` (`JSON`, `profileClient.GetMany` at `models_gen.go:15433`) is the second
reachable instance.

**Root cause.** `sql/condition.go:154` `prefixCondition` implements a *positional* contract — its own
doc comment states leaf clauses are expected to carry a single column identifier at the start — but
nothing expresses or enforces it, and `comparator.JSON`'s MySQL arms violate it because MySQL has no
infix containment operator to lead with.

**Measured against MySQL 8.0 (2026-09-02).** Four probes settle the design space:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `u.JSON_CONTAINS(metadata, …)` | `FUNCTION u.JSON_CONTAINS does not exist` — today's output |
| unqualified, join partner **lacks** the column | works (1 row) |
| unqualified, join partner **has** the column | `ERROR 1052: Column 'metadata' in where clause is ambiguous` |
| `JSON_CONTAINS(u.metadata, …)` | correct — qualifying the **argument** is the shape a fix must produce |

So "skip what cannot be qualified" is not a fix: it trades a guaranteed error for a schema-dependent
one. And rewriting the arms to lead with the column is impossible — `col->>'$.x' = v` is
extraction-equality rather than containment, and `MEMBER OF` puts the value first, not the column.

**Decision (settled 2026-09-02, user).** Add a `Column string` field to `sql.Condition` naming the
column token that alias-qualification rewrites. `prefixCondition` rewrites that token when `Column`
is set and falls back to today's prepend when it is not, so `sql.Raw` / `Custom` behaviour is
unchanged. Two alternatives were rejected: clause templates with an explicit column slot (larger
runtime refactor, needs a collision-free token — `&` collides with `Slice`'s `&&`, and `@` / `#` /
`~` / `:` all collide with postgres JSON and array operators) and pushing the alias down into
`ToConditions`/`Parse` (changes a public generated API across 90 definitions and regresses user
`Custom` conditions to unqualified). The chosen option is a strict subset of the clause-template
one, so it does not foreclose it.

**Scope.** `sql/dialect.go` (`Condition`), `sql/condition.go` (`ConditionBuilder`, `prefixCondition`),
the 21 clause-constructing lines in `comparator/{comparator,json,jsonb,slice}.go`. No generated-code
churn — generated `ToConditions` only calls `Parse`. PRD §11.3 describes `Condition` as carrying a
`Clause` and a `Value` and needs the third field recorded.

**References.**
- `sql/condition.go` — `PrefixConditions`, `prefixCondition` and its stated contract.
- `comparator/json.go:41,49` — the only non-column-leading clauses in the repo.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl:235,275` — the two `PrefixConditions` call sites.
- PRD §11.3 "Comparator Interface"; §11.5 "Condition Composition".
- Sibling: FIX-177 (the postgres half of the same file, resolved 2026-09-02).

**Resolution (2026-09-02).** `sql.Condition` gained a `Column` field naming the column token inside
`Clause`. `prefixCondition` qualifies that token in place when it is set and keeps the historical
prepend when it is not, so `sql.Raw` / `Custom` behaviour is byte-identical. `qualifyColumn` matches
the first **whole-token** occurrence — bounded on neither side by an identifier byte — so a column
named `one` is matched as the argument in `JSON_CONTAINS_PATH(one, 'one', $)` and never as a
fragment of `one_more`. `ConditionBuilder` populates `Column` for all 13 of its methods, and the 21
clause-constructing lines in `comparator/{comparator,json,jsonb,slice}.go` set it directly. The
MySQL JSON arms now render `JSON_CONTAINS(u.metadata, ?)`.

**Regression coverage, at three levels.**
- `sql/condition_test.go` — `TestPrefixConditions_QualifiesNamedColumn` (column-leading clause,
  function-leading clause, column name repeated inside a quoted literal, no partial-identifier
  match, and the empty-`Column` prepend fallback) plus
  `TestPrefixConditions_QualifiesInsideComposition` for the AND/OR descent.
- `comparator/json_test.go` — `TestJSON_Parse_SurvivesAliasQualification` now covers **both**
  dialects; the MySQL subtest is the one that would have caught this.
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/mysql/tests/filter_join_test.go` —
  `TestFilter_JSONUnderO2OJoin_MySQL`, both arms against a real MySQL 8.0 through the generated
  client. **Verified to fail without the fix**, with the production error verbatim:
  `Error 1370 (42000): execute command denied to user 'test'@'%' for routine 'u.JSON_CONTAINS'`.

**Files.** `sql/dialect.go`, `sql/condition.go`, `sql/condition_test.go`,
`comparator/{comparator,json,jsonb,slice}.go` and the ten `comparator/*_test.go` files whose `want`
literals now pin `Column`, `docs/PRD.md` §11.3, `guidelines/SQL.md` §7,
`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/mysql/tests/filter_join_test.go` (new).

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all 33 modules; `make check-examples` clean across all
13 example modules. **Zero generated-code churn** — no `expected/` tree changed, confirming the
prediction that the fix stays inside the runtime packages.

**Deliberately not done.** The generator's own conditions — soft-delete (`sql.Where(col).IsNull()`),
tenancy, and `cursorKeyset` — were left alone. Soft-delete and tenancy go through
`ConditionBuilder`, so they pick `Column` up for free; `cursorKeyset` hand-builds column-leading
clauses and stays on the prepend fallback, which is correct for them and costs no golden churn.
[Superseded by FIX-237 (note added 2026-10-01): `cursorKeyset` now quotes each key through the
dialect and sets `Column` to the quoted token, so it no longer uses the prepend fallback.]

### FIX-177

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 11, comparator (spec-level: PRD §11.2)
- **Surfaced by:** 25.5 auto-review (2026-09-02); **measured against a real PostgreSQL 16 the same day**

**Issue.** **`comparator.JSON`'s PostgreSQL arm emits operators the PostgreSQL `json` type does not
have, so every `Contains` / `HasKey` filter on a postgres `json` (non-`b`) column fails at request
time.** Measured against the `graphql` example's `profiles.settings JSON` column:

```
SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE settings @> $1
  ERROR: operator does not exist: json @> unknown (SQLSTATE 42883)
SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE settings ? $1
  ERROR: operator does not exist: json ? unknown (SQLSTATE 42883)
```

The containment and existence operators are defined for `jsonb` only. The same two queries against
a `jsonb` column succeed, which is the control.

**Root cause — and it is in the spec, not only the code.** `comparator/json.go:22,30` emits
`col @> $` and `col ? $` under `d.Name() == "postgres"`, faithfully implementing PRD §11.2's
"Dialect-specific SQL generation" table. But §11.2 also says, four lines later, that a postgres
`json` column uses the JSON comparator rather than JSONB *"since PostgreSQL `json` type does not
support all JSONB operators"* — and then specifies JSON's postgres SQL as exactly those operators.
**The two sentences contradict each other**, so this cannot be fixed as an implementation bug: the
normative text has to be settled first (project rule 1).

**Not a 25.5 regression, but 25.5 is what makes it reachable.** Before 25.5 the column advertised
`StringComparator` with no translator, so the filter was accepted and silently dropped — the F2
class, wrong data returned. It is now a GraphQL error instead. Louder, still broken.

**Measured candidate fix (works; not applied).** Casting the column resolves it, and the cast is a
no-op on a `jsonb` column, so one arm serves both:

```
SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE settings::jsonb @> $1   -- 1 row on match, 0 on non-match
SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE settings::jsonb ?  $1   -- 1 row on match, 0 on non-match
```

There is no index regression to weigh: PostgreSQL has no GIN containment opclass for `json` at all,
so nothing could have been using an index on the old form, while `CREATE INDEX … USING GIN
((settings::jsonb))` would match the new one.

**Independent verification (2026-09-02, PostgreSQL 16.15).** Re-measured through the real runtime
path — `comparator.NullableJSON.Parse("settings", pgDialect)` → `sql.BuildCount` → pgx — not by
hand-written SQL. The entry reproduces exactly, and three further facts settle the decision:

- **Option (b) is empty, not merely narrow.** `pg_operator` defines six operators for `json`:
  `->`, `->>` (int and text overloads), `#>`, `#>>`. There is no `@>` and no `?`. `HasKey` could be
  expressed json-natively as `col -> $ IS NOT NULL`, but that diverges from `?` on arrays
  (`'["a"]'::jsonb ? 'a'` is true; `-> 'a'` on a json array is NULL), so it would give one dialect
  two HasKey semantics.
- **The cast is free on `jsonb`** — the fact that makes an unconditional postgres arm safe, since
  the comparator cannot see the column's SQL type. On a 50k-row GIN-indexed `jsonb` column, through
  pgx with a bound parameter, the planner elides it: `meta::jsonb @> $1` plans as
  `Bitmap Index Scan on jb_meta_gin, Index Cond: (meta @> '{"tier": "gold"}'::jsonb)`, and
  `meta::jsonb ? $1` as `Index Cond: (meta ? 'rare'::text)`. A hand-written `comparator.JSON` over a
  `jsonb` column therefore loses no index.
- **Parameter inference is correct with no driver hint.** PostgreSQL resolves `$1` to `jsonb` for
  `@>` and to `text` for `?`; pgx encodes the translator's `string(in.Contains)` into both.

**One limit the original entry did not surface, and it is unavoidable.** `json` accepts `\u0000`
inside a string; `jsonb` cannot represent it. A single such row anywhere in the scanned set fails
the whole query with `unsupported Unicode escape sequence` (`\u0000 cannot be converted to text`).
Not a regression — today the query errors 100% of the time — and not avoidable, since containment
on `json` requires `jsonb`. Every other shape casts cleanly: arrays, scalars, `null`, and
`1e100000`. This belongs in the amended §11.2 text as a stated limit.

**Decision (settled 2026-09-02, user).** Option **(a)**. Cast in `comparator.JSON.Parse`'s postgres
arms and amend §11.2's table to `col::jsonb @> $` / `col::jsonb ? $`, rewriting the contradicting
"JSONB vs JSON" paragraph so it says a postgres `json` column is cast at filter time rather than
implying it uses a narrower operator set. Options (b) and (c) were rejected: (b) has no operators to
route to, and (c) drops the feature.

**Layer: runtime, not generator.** `prefixCondition` prepends `alias + "."` to the whole clause, so
the O2O-join path renders `t."settings"::jsonb @> $1` — correct, because `::` binds tighter than the
operator (PostgreSQL's own EXPLAIN shows `(settings)::jsonb`). `expandCondition` passes clauses
through verbatim with no identifier rewriting, so the cast is textually safe. Putting it in the
generator instead would leave the public runtime API broken for hand-written filters and would leak
SQL into the column-name argument, which also feeds `parseNull`. `NullableJSON`'s `Null` arm stays
**uncast** (`settings IS NULL`). `comparator.JSONB` needs no matching change: `resolveSimpleComparator`
keys it on `SQLType == "jsonb"` under postgres, so it never sees a `json` column.

**Scope.** `comparator/json.go` (two clause literals + the type doc comment) · `comparator/json_test.go`
(exactly three assertions fail under the patch) · PRD §11.2 dialect table + the "JSONB vs JSON"
paragraph · `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:568` comment ·
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/comparator_translate.go.tmpl:86` comment, which regenerates four
goldens · the now-false comments at `graphql/schema.sql:391-393` and
`mysql/tests/graphql_json_test.go:18`.

**Also settled with it (2026-09-02, user).**
- **E2E coverage:** add `contains` / `hasKey` / `isNull` filter cases against the existing nullable
  `profiles.settings` through the graphql example's gqlgen server — the postgres JSON family has no
  request-time coverage today, precisely because it was broken. No schema churn; the NOT NULL form
  keeps its existing MySQL golden.
- **The `hasKey` operand divergence gets written into §11.2.** One `hasKey` input means a bare key on
  PostgreSQL (`region`, measured) but a JSONPath on MySQL (`$.region` — what the mysql example's own
  passing test feeds). Today only MySQL's arm is reachable, so the fork is theoretical; the fix makes
  both live. It is currently recorded only in a MySQL test comment, nowhere normative. Documented as
  a stated limit of the shared operand — no behavior change.

**References.**
- `comparator/json.go` — `JSON.Parse`, the `postgres` arms.
- PRD §11.2 "JSON Comparator" dialect table vs its own "JSONB vs JSON" paragraph.
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/schema.sql` — `profiles.settings JSON`, the reachable column.
- Sibling: FIX-178 (the SQLite half of the same §11.2 gap).

**Resolution (2026-09-02).** Option (a), as decided above. `comparator.JSON.Parse`'s two postgres
arms now emit `col::jsonb @> $` and `col::jsonb ? $`; `NullableJSON`'s `Null` arm is untouched and
still emits `col IS NULL`. MySQL is byte-identical. §11.2's dialect table carries the cast, and its
"JSONB vs JSON" paragraph no longer contradicts it: the JSON/JSONB split is now stated as being
about which operators the *comparator* offers, not about avoiding a cast. The two accepted limits
(`\u0000` uncastable; `HasKey`'s operand is a bare key on PostgreSQL and a JSON path on MySQL) are
written into §11.2 and mirrored in `guidelines/SQL.md` §13.

**Regression coverage.** `TestJSONComparator_NarrowsOverHTTP` in the graphql example — nine cases
over a real `profiles.settings json` column through the live gqlgen server: `contains` (one- and
two-pair documents), `hasKey` (bare key, universal key, no-match), `isNull` both ways, the
two-operator AND, and the `and:` recursion path. **Verified to fail without the fix**: reverting the
two arms fails seven of the nine with `operator does not exist: json @> unknown (SQLSTATE 42883)` /
`json ? unknown`, while the two `isNull` cases keep passing — exactly the split the fix predicts.
`comparator/json_test.go` gains `TestJSON_Parse_SurvivesAliasQualification`, which pins the clause
through `sql.PrefixConditions` (`t.settings::jsonb @> $`), the O2O-join path's qualifier.

**Files.** `comparator/json.go`, `comparator/json_test.go`, `docs/PRD.md` §11.2,
`guidelines/SQL.md` §13, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go`,
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/comparator_translate.go.tmpl` (+ 4 regenerated goldens, comment-only),
`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/{schema.sql,tests/filter_comparator_test.go}`,
`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/mysql/tests/graphql_json_test.go`.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all 33 modules; `make check-examples` clean across all
13 example modules. Goldens regenerated via `make update-golden` + `make update-golden-e2e`; the
only churn is the four `comparator_translate_gen.go` doc comments.

**Not closed by this.** FIX-178 (the SQLite half) is untouched — `JSON.Parse` still has no sqlite
arm, and §11.2's SQLite sentence was left exactly as it was.

### FIX-145

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** nit
- **Origin:** phase 25, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26); half-closed by 25.4 (2026-09-01), closed by 25.5 (2026-09-02)

**Issue.** **The 25.1 fallback now violates Rule 2 as well as the D1 invariant, and its
accept-and-ignore surface grew.** A *nullable* enum / JSON / JSONB / slice column still resolves
to the NOT NULL `StringComparator` (e.g. `metadata: StringComparator` on a nullable `jsonb` in
`user_gen.graphqls`). Before 25.3 that was only the documented F2 missing-translator case; now
that Rule 2 is normative and every other nullable column takes a `Nullable<X>` twin, the goldens
carry a visible Rule 2 violation too. Separately, those same columns now advertise
`gt gte lt lte nlike` on top of the previous eight operators — all silently dropped — so the
accept-and-ignore blast radius widened until 25.2's lint lands.

**Root cause.** `resolveAPIFilterProjection`'s fallback arm sets `InputTypeName =
fallbackComparatorInput` unconditionally, ignoring `col.Nullable`, because the fallback predates
Rule 2 and exists only to preserve pre-25.1 output for families with no projection yet.

**Suggested fix.**
- No action in isolation — 25.4 (enum) and 25.5 (JSON / JSONB / slice) remove the fallback
  entirely and give these columns real inputs with their own nullable twins.
- Recorded so the Rule 2 violation in the current goldens is not rediscovered as a new defect,
  and so 25.2's lint is understood to be gated behind 25.4/25.5 (already noted in 25.1's
  sequencing correction).
- **Deliberately left Open (2026-08-26).** There is no edit that closes this in isolation —
  the fallback exists precisely because Enum / JSON / JSONB / Slice have no projection yet, and
  25.4 / 25.5 delete it. Resolving now would be false bookkeeping; it should be closed by
  whichever of those two lands last.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `resolveAPIFilterProjection` fallback arm,
  `fallbackComparatorInput`.
- PRD §26.4 Rule 2; §26.5.3 D1 invariant + D2 completeness lint.
- Goldens: `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/expected/graph/{user,profile}_gen.graphqls`.

**Resolution (2026-09-02, 25.5).** Closed by the sub-item its own terms named. 25.4 removed the
enum arm; 25.5 removed the other three — a JSON column now resolves to
`JSONComparator` / `NullableJSONComparator`, a JSONB column to the `JSONB` pair on PostgreSQL,
and an array column to `<Elem>SliceComparator` / its `Nullable` twin. Every one of those inputs
has a translator behind it, so the Rule 2 violation the entry describes is gone from the goldens
(`user_gen.graphqls`'s `metadata` reads `NullableJSONBComparator`, `profile_gen.graphqls`'s
`settings` reads `NullableJSONComparator`) and the widened accept-and-ignore surface is gone with
it.

`fallbackComparatorInput` itself still exists, and deliberately: it now covers only the two
shapes that have no sound projection at all — an enum-like Go type that is not a schema enum
(`makeEnumTranslator`'s guard, which keeps a composite- or domain-typed column off operands
naming an undeclared GraphQL enum), and an array whose element binds to a custom scalar whose
list shape sqlgen has not measured (`sliceOperandElemGoType`; recorded in PRD §26.12). Those are
a different class from the four this entry names — not "no projection yet" but "no projection is
correct" — and what to do about them is 25.2's call, since the completeness lint is what forces
the choice between dropping the field and hard-erroring. Flagged there rather than left implicit.

### FIX-175

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** 25.4 auto-review (2026-09-01); measured, scoped and fixed 2026-09-01

**Issue.** **A schema enum whose PascalCase name lands on a name sqlgen already
owns in the GraphQL type namespace was accepted, and the result was either a
silently wrong filter surface or a gqlgen failure that named neither side.**
`enumComparatorInput` appended `"Comparator"` to the enum's GraphQL name with no
guard, and nothing checked the enum's own type name against the scalars and
object types the same document declares.

**Measured before the fix** (postgres, `CREATE TYPE duration AS ENUM
('short','long')`, column `jobs.kind duration`, **no `interval` column**):

```
col kind: input=DurationComparator translator=translateDurationComparator family=Enum
  ops=[eq:Duration neq:Duration gt:Duration gte:Duration lt:Duration lte:Duration
       in:[Duration!] nin:[Duration!] between:DurationRange nbetween:DurationRange]
translator translateDurationComparator -> *comparator.Enum[models.Duration]
```

The schema declared `enum Duration`, `input DurationComparator` with the
**shipped** family's ten operators, and `input DurationRange { from: Duration!,
to: Duration! }` — a range input over an enum. Generation succeeded, the SDL was
valid, and the Go compiled: the `Enum` arm of `comparator_translate.go.tmpl`
copies only `Eq/Neq/In/Nin`, so six advertised operators were accepted and
dropped. **Fully silent.** 25.2's completeness lint cannot see it — the lint is
presence-level (schema field ↔ `FilterFields` entry) and both were present.

Adding an `interval` column produced the second failure: `translatorsByName` is
last-write-wins in table order, so `translateDurationComparator` resolved to
`*comparator.Number[time.Duration]` while its nullable twin stayed
`*comparator.NullableEnum[models.Duration]` — one column then gets a translator
its model filter cannot accept. That schema also declared `scalar Duration`
alongside `enum Duration`; gqlparser v2.5.33 rejects it with `Cannot redeclare
type Duration.`

**Corrections to the original write-up** (all measured):

- `String`, `ID` and `Boolean` were **already hard errors** via the create-input
  scalar-binding check (`api: column "kind" resolves to Go type "ID" but its
  GraphQL type "ID" binds gqlgen to "string" …`). Not part of this defect.
- **`Numeric` was missing from the list** and is the most silent case: `Float` is
  a spec built-in so no scalar is declared, and the translator name does not even
  collide (`translateNumericComparator` vs the shipped per-`T`
  `translateNumericComparatorInt32`).
- **`Bytes` and `MacAddr` are unreachable by that route** — `StructName("bytes")`
  is `Byte`, `StructName("mac_addr")` is `MACAddr`. Measured reachable set for
  the comparator axis: `Time`, `Decimal`, `Duration`, `Numeric`, `IP`, `CIDR`.
  The hand-listed set was unreliable, so the guard derives it.

**Two axes.** The comparator-input name is one; the enum's own type name is the
other. `buildAPIEnumContext` sets `GraphQLName: e.GoTypeName`, so an enum shares
a namespace with every scalar and object type. `enum Duration` vs `scalar
Duration` is a redeclaration independent of comparators and predates 25.4
(`CREATE TYPE uuid AS ENUM` + any `uuid.UUID` column). Renaming the comparator
input cannot rescue that half.

**Fix (landed).** Four parts, per the PRD deltas taken first (§4.1, §4.11, §4.13,
§8.5, §26.4 "Monomorphized names disambiguate…" + "GraphQL type name ownership",
§26.5.3).

- **`gen/api_names.go` (new) — the owned-name registry.** `fixedOwnedGraphQLName`
  is the fixed set (spec built-ins, the four structural types, every shipped
  family + `Nullable` twin + range input); `collectGraphQLTypeNames` reads the
  schema-derived claims (nine names per table, and per enum its type name plus
  both forms of its comparator input); `validateGraphQLTypeNames` runs both rules
  over them and is called at the end of `BuildAPIContext`, where every name is
  known. It **reuses** `resolved_names.go`'s `claimedName` / `entityRef` /
  `duplicateClaims` / `claimReport` rather than duplicating the machinery, with
  GraphQL-specific renderers.
- **`enumComparatorInput` disambiguates** to `<Enum>EnumComparator` when the
  derived name is fixed-owned. Keyed on the **static** set only, so a published
  input name is a function of the enum alone and cannot shift when an unrelated
  table is added. `<Elem>SliceComparator` needs no equivalent — that name always
  carries `Slice` before `Comparator`, so 25.5 inherits the guard untouched.
- **`enums:` config block** (`config.EnumConfig`, `RootConfig.Enums`) with
  `struct_name` and `description`, implementing PRD §4.11 — which existed but was
  unimplemented and left its location and field name open. `gen.EnumGoTypeName`
  is the **single** derivation, consumed by both `BuildEnumContexts` and
  `registerSchemaTypes`: the two previously called `StructName` independently, and
  an override reaching the type but not the COLUMN emits a models package that
  does not compile.
- **Manifest de-duplication.** `buildEnums` re-derived names with `pascal(e.Name)`,
  ignoring singularization, the collision prefix, and now the override. It reads
  `[]gen.EnumContext` instead, threaded through `GenerateResult.Enums` →
  `manifest.StageInput` → `BuildInput`.

**Why suffix-then-error rather than error alone.** Suffixing keeps the common
case generating (an enum named `duration` on a schema with no interval column is
now correct rather than rejected), and hard-erroring covers what suffixing cannot
reach — sqlgen owns the comparator input it derives, but not the enum or table
the consumer's schema declares.

**Two collision classes the fix deliberately catches that the family list could
not.** `collectComparatorFamilies` dedupes an enum-derived family *into* the
shipped one it collides with, and keys `operatorsByName` last-write-wins, so a
check over the finished list sees no duplicate at all. Enums therefore claim
their monomorphized names directly — which also catches `duration` (suffixed to
`DurationEnumComparator`) beside `duration_enum` (deriving it directly).

**Rejected alternative.** Suffix-only, with no namespace check: it leaves `enum
Duration` vs `scalar Duration` failing at gqlgen with a message naming neither
claimant, and a uniquifier loop for the residual enum-vs-enum case would make a
published API name depend on unrelated schema.

**Tests.** `gen/api_name_collision_test.go` —
`TestEnumComparator_disambiguatesAgainstFixedFamilies` (the silent case: input
name, the four-operator set, operand types, translator name and return type, no
`DurationRange`); `TestEnumComparator_disambiguatedFamilyCoexistsWithShipped`
(`numeric` enum beside an integer column — both families and both translators
survive with distinct return types); `TestGraphQLTypeNames_collisionsAreGenerationErrors`
(three shapes: enum vs declared scalar, two enums on one comparator input, table
vs a structural type — each asserting both claimants and the remedy appear in the
message); `TestEnumStructNameOverride_resolvesCollision` (the §4.11 remedy,
including that the override reaches the translator's Go type parameter);
`TestEnumComparator_uncollidedNameIsUnchanged` (the guard on 25.4's goldens);
`TestEnumConfig_descriptionOverridesSQLComment` (bare and schema-qualified keys).
**Verified failing-first:** all five bug tests fail against the pre-fix
`enumComparatorInput` and the absent validation call.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all 33 modules (lint included — the
added branch pushed `BuildAPIContext` past the cyclop limit, resolved by
extracting `collectUsedScalars`, not by a `//nolint`). `TestE2EGoldenFiles` and
`make check-examples` clean across all 13 example modules with **zero regenerated
files**: the suffix applies only on collision, and the manifest's enum names were
already identical under both derivations for the example schemas.

**Auto-review findings, all addressed in-place (2026-09-01).**

- **MySQL SETs were offered a remedy that does nothing.** `enumContextsForSets`
  feeds `usedEnumsByName`, so a SET reached `UsedEnums` and the error pointed at
  `enums.<set>.struct_name` — a key `BuildSetContexts` never reads. It also
  claimed a `<Set>ValueComparator` the SET surface never emits (a SET column
  filters through `comparator.String`). Fixed with `EnumContext.FromSet` →
  `APIEnumContext.FromSet`: a SET now claims only its type name, through
  `setRef` (kind `"SET type"`, no escape), matching what `collectResolvedNames`
  already does on the Go side. Covered by
  `TestGraphQLTypeNames_setIsNotOfferedTheEnumsOverride`.
- **The manifest test factory had gone stale.** `testBuildInput` never set
  `Enums`, so after the `buildEnums` rewrite every manifest test built a document
  with `enums: []` and passed silently — the FIX-068/FIX-059 fixture-drift shape.
  All three example enums are singular, un-prefixed and un-overridden, so the
  goldens could not cover the bug either. Factory now threads
  `gen.BuildEnumContexts`, and `TestBuildEnums_namesFollowTheGeneratedGoType`
  asserts a plural enum (`statuses` → `Status`, not `Statuses`) and an overridden
  one (`shipping_state` → `Fulfilment`). **Verified failing-first** against the
  `pascal(e.Name)` derivation, on all four names plus both slice types.
- **A collision test case proved nothing.** The structural-name case used
  `page_infos` → `PageInfo`, which `generatedPackageTypes` already rejects
  earlier in `validateResolvedNames`. Replaced with `sort_directions` →
  `SortDirection` (declared only in `shared_gen.graphqls`, so this rule is the
  only one that sees it) and a second case, `string_comparators` →
  `StringComparator`, which also pins that the reserved set is read off the built
  context rather than the static family table.
- **Doc drift fixed inline:** `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL_READ_SURFACE.md` §D3, the D3
  comparator table, and the 25.4 line now carry the on-collision spelling.

**Known gap, marked in code.** `collectGraphQLTypeNames` iterates
`ctx.Tables` only. Harmless today — views are not on the API surface at all — but
25.8/25.9 must grow a view arm or a view colliding with a table goes unreported.
A `TODO(25.8/25.9)` sits on the function.

**Follow-up for 25.5.** `<Elem>SliceComparator`, `JSONComparator` and
`JSONBComparator` join `shippedComparatorFamilies`; the slice monomorphization
should claim its input names in `collectGraphQLTypeNames` the way enums now do,
so an enum-vs-slice-element collision is caught by the same rule.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_names.go` (new), `context_api.go` (`enumComparatorInput`,
  `APIEnumContext.SQLName`/`SQLSchema`, `BuildAPIContext`, `collectUsedScalars`),
  `context_enum.go` (`EnumGoTypeName`, `EnumConfigFor`), `orchestrate.go`
  (`registerSchemaTypes`, `GenerateResult.Enums`), `resolved_names.go` (`enumRef`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go` — `EnumConfig`, `RootConfig.Enums`;
  `config/enums_test.go` — YAML round-trip for both key spellings.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context.go` — `EnumContext.FromSet`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/{builder,emit}.go`, `cmd/sqlgen/cli/{generate,graphql}.go`.
- PRD §4.1, §4.11, §4.13, §8.5, §26.4 (Rule 1 + "GraphQL type name ownership"),
  §26.5.3.
- Sibling: FIX-145 (the fallback the same surface carries until 25.5).

### FIX-176

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 11 (`comparator/`), surfaced in phase 25
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-174 verification (2026-09-01)

**Issue.** **`comparator.Slice` builds its PostgreSQL array literal without quoting, so a
caller-supplied element containing a comma silently changes which rows match.** Measured against
a real `text[]` column (`products.tags`, postgres example) before the fix:

| element | result |
|---|---|
| `plain` | matched |
| `with space` | matched |
| `with,comma` | **0 rows, no error** — split into two elements server-side |
| `with"quote` | `ERROR: malformed array literal: "{with"quote}"` |
| `with{brace}` | `ERROR: malformed array literal: "{with{brace}}"` |
| `` (empty) | vanishes from the literal entirely |

The comma case is the one with teeth: a filter that quietly matches a *different* set is worse
than one that errors, and it is the accept-and-ignore class Phase 25 exists to eliminate. **Not
SQL injection** — the literal still travels as a bound parameter — but it is caller-controlled
corruption of the filter's semantics.

**Root cause.** `sliceToArrayLiteral` was `fmt.Sprint` per element joined with `","`. Building the
literal by hand is deliberate and correct — it is what lets an ENUM array travel without pgx
registering the type's OID — but it makes the function the owner of PostgreSQL's array-literal
grammar, and the grammar was never implemented. Enum members are identifiers and never need
quoting, which is precisely why it stayed invisible: the only arrays any test or example filtered
on were enum arrays.

**Fix (landed).** `quoteArrayElement` / `arrayElementNeedsQuote`: quote when the element is empty,
case-insensitively `NULL`, or contains `{`, `}`, `,`, `"`, `\` or whitespace; escape `"` and `\`
inside the quotes. Conditional rather than unconditional quoting, mirroring PostgreSQL's own
`array_out`, so numeric / uuid / enum elements keep their bare spelling and the literal a filter
sends reads the same as one the server would print. No signature change, no `reflect`, no new
dependency.

Rejected alternative: pass typed slices (`[]string`) for non-enum element types and keep the
literal only for enums. It reintroduces the element-type sniffing FIX-173 deliberately removed
and splits one code path into two for no gain.

**Why it was blocking rather than tracked.** Reachable from the Go client today, and **25.5 makes
it caller-reachable over HTTP** — `<Elem>SliceComparator` puts `containsAny: [String!]` on the
GraphQL surface, where the values are whatever a client sends.

**Tests.** `comparator/slice_test.go` `TestSlice_Parse_ArrayLiteralQuoting` (10 cases: bare
identifiers, enum members, comma, braces, quote, backslash, leading/trailing/inner whitespace,
empty string, `NULL` in three casings, mixed safe/unsafe) and
`TestSlice_Parse_QuotingAppliesToEveryOperator` (all three array operators share the literal);
`postgres` example `TestFilter_SliceArrayLiteralQuoting_Postgres` against a real `text[]` column,
including an absent-value case so quoting is shown to preserve the predicate rather than merely
stop it erroring. **Verified failing-first:** 13 unit subtests and 4 of 7 E2E subtests fail
against the pre-fix implementation.

**References.**
- `comparator/slice.go` — `sliceToArrayLiteral`, `quoteArrayElement`, `arrayElementNeedsQuote`.
- `guidelines/SQL.md` §8.1 — the array-literal grammar is now documented alongside the IN/NOT IN
  table.
- PRD §11.2 (`Slice[T]`, PostgreSQL-only), §26.4 (`<Elem>SliceComparator`, 25.5).

### FIX-174

- **Status:** Resolved — **not reproducible; entry retracted**
- **Severity:** tracked (as filed)
- **Origin:** n/a
- **Surfaced by:** /implement 25.4 auto-review (2026-09-01); retracted the same day

**What it claimed.** That `comparator.Slice[T]` carries FIX-173's defect on the array-element
axis — handing pgx a `[]T` for its `@>` / `&&` / `<@` operators, which would fail to encode
against an enum array's OID exactly as `Enum[T].In` did.

**Why it is wrong.** `Slice[T]` never takes the array-parameter path. `sliceToArrayLiteral` renders
the operand as a PostgreSQL array **text literal** string, and `slice.go`'s own doc comment states
the reason: *"This allows pgx to send the value as a string without needing custom type OID
registration for enum arrays."* The entry was written from the FIX-173 analogy without reading
`slice.go`.

**Measured, not argued.** All four operators against `assets.declared_categories`
(`document_entity_type_enum[]`) on pgx, via the Go client:

```
ContainsAny   -> [probe-spv probe-both]                    err=<nil>
ContainsAll   -> [probe-both]                              err=<nil>
ContainedBy   -> [probe-primary probe-spv probe-both]      err=<nil>
IsEmpty=false -> [probe-primary probe-spv probe-both]      err=<nil>
```

**What the verification did find.** A real defect in the same function, on a different axis —
the array literal was built without quoting. Logged and fixed as **FIX-176**.

**Recorded rather than deleted** so the retraction is on the record: the entry asserted
"almost certainly" from an analogy, and the correct response to that phrasing is a probe, not a
filing.

### FIX-173

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 11 (`comparator/`), surfaced in phase 25
- **Surfaced by:** /implement 25.4 E2E (2026-09-01)

**Issue.** **`comparator.Enum[T].In` / `.Nin` fail outright on pgx.** Any filter using an
enum column's set operators errors before returning a row:

```
get users: query: failed to encode args[1]: unable to encode
[]models.UserRole{"admin", "viewer"} into text format for unknown type
(OID 16385): cannot find encode plan
```

Reproduced from the **Go client**, with no GraphQL involved — 25.4 only made it reachable
over HTTP by projecting `in` / `nin` onto `<Enum>Comparator` (PRD §26.4).

**Root cause.** `parseIn` / `parseNin` take the array-parameter path on any dialect with
`SupportsArrayParams()` (pgx), handing the driver the whole `[]T` as one value. A generated
enum is a named string type (`type UserRole string`), and pgx has no encode plan for a slice
of one against the column's enum-array OID. `Eq` / `Neq` were unaffected — a *scalar* named
string goes through the driver's string-kind conversion — which is why every existing enum
filter test passed while `In` and `Nin` were unreachable. Dating from phase 11; no test or
example exercised `Enum.In` against a real PostgreSQL enum column.

**Fix (landed).** `Enum.Parse` now uses the expanded `IN ($, $, …)` / `NOT IN ($, $, …)` form
on **every** dialect, via `parseInExpanded` / `parseNinExpanded` split out of their
dialect-aware wrappers. It asks the driver for nothing beyond what `Eq` already proved it can
do, and needs neither `reflect` nor a narrowing of `Enum[T]`'s `comparable` constraint (an
enum-shaped column retyped to an integer through `overrides.types` still compiles and still
filters — `resolveGenericComparator` routes it through `Enum[T]` too).

Rejected alternatives, both measured against pgx v5 / PostgreSQL 16:
- Rendering the values as `[]string` so `= ANY($1)` encodes. Works (PostgreSQL coerces
  `text[]` to the enum array), but needs `reflect.TypeFor[T]().Kind()` to tell a string-kinded
  enum from an integer one — the first use of `reflect` in a runtime core package.
- Registering enum OIDs on the pgx connection. Needs schema introspection at connect time,
  for a defect local to one comparator.

The placeholder-count cost is the right trade here and nowhere else: an enum column's value
domain is its declared members, so the list is bounded by the type rather than by the caller —
unlike `ID.In`, which is exactly where the array parameter earns its keep.

**Tests.** `comparator/enum_test.go` `TestEnum_Parse_SetOperandsAreDriverEncodable` (all four
dialects plus the non-string type parameter) and the amended
`TestEnum_Parse_In_DialectAware/postgres_pgx_uses_IN`; `postgres` example
`TestFilter_EnumSetOperators_Postgres` (Go client, pgx, real enum column); `graphql` example
`TestEnumComparator_NarrowsOverHTTP/{in,nin}`. All three verified failing-first against the
pre-fix runtime.

**References.**
- `comparator/enum.go` — `Enum.Parse`; `comparator/comparator.go` — `parseIn` /
  `parseInExpanded`, `parseNin` / `parseNinExpanded`.
- PRD §11.2 (`Enum[T]` operator set), §26.4 (the `<Enum>Comparator` projection that made it
  reachable).
- **`Slice[T]` was suspected of the same defect and does not have it** — see FIX-174's retraction. It was found to have a different one, FIX-176.

### FIX-172

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 6, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-171 auto-review (2026-09-01)

**Issue.** **Two relationships on one table resolving to the same Go field are
accepted by every validator, and the models package does not compile.** This is
FIX-171's defect class on the axis FIX-171 does not cover — neither side is
inferred, so the §13.4 replacement rule does not apply. `sqlgen validate` and
`sqlgen generate` report success; `go build` fails in generated code.

Two shapes reach it:

```yaml
tables:
  accounts:
    relationships:
      - {name: ledger_entries, type: o2m, table: entries, fk: account_id, filter: "kind = 'ledger'"}
      - {name: LedgerEntries,  type: o2m, table: entries, fk: account_id, filter: "kind = 'audit'"}
```

Distinct `name:` values, distinct `filter:` values — legal under both existing
config checks — that pascalize onto the single field `LedgerEntries`. The
second shape is two FK-inferred edges to *different* targets whose names
pluralize onto one field.

**Root cause.** Nothing enforced PRD §13.7.3 row 2 ("Each relationship's
`name:` field must be set so the Go field names on `<Table>FieldOptions` are
distinct"). `config.validateRelationships`
(`cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:346-360`) compares `r.Name` **byte-equal** and
the §13.7.3 dedup key `(target, fk, filter)`; two names differing only in case
or separators pass both. `validateDuplicateFieldNames`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`) claims relationship `FieldName`s into
exactly the right map, but is gated on some column carrying a `column_map`
override and then skips any pair where neither side is `overridden` — a
relationship is never `overridden`, so a relationship/relationship pair can
never be reported even with the gate open.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add an ungated `validateDuplicateRelationshipFields`, called from
  `validateResolvedFieldNames` alongside its override-gated sibling. Ungated
  because the pair is unconditionally non-compiling — the override gate exists
  to avoid failing pre-existing column collisions, a judgement that does not
  transfer.
- Check the **merged, post-replacement** set, so it composes with FIX-171
  rather than duplicating it: a declared-vs-inferred pair is already resolved
  by replacement and cannot reach the check, leaving only same-provenance
  pairs. Name both sides symmetrically — neither is privileged.
- Do **not** put it in `config.validateRelationships`: pascalization lives in
  `gen` (`toPascalCase`), and a config-side copy would drift from the function
  that actually derives `FieldName`.
- Regression tests: declared names pascalizing onto one field; two declared
  entries both colliding with one inferred edge (also covers the `!replaced`
  guard); distinct Go fields still coexisting.

**References.**
- PRD §13.7.3 row 2 (the unenforced rule), §4.8 (distinct-name requirement).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go` — `validateResolvedFieldNames`,
  `validateDuplicateFieldNames` and its two gates.
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:346-360` — `validateRelationships`, whose own
  doc comment names this hazard ("a Go field collision would surface as a
  compile error far from the config typo").
- FIX-171 — the config-vs-inferred axis of the same collision, resolved by
  replacement; this entry is its declared-vs-declared sibling.
- FIX-168 — the defect class (generate reports success, models package does not
  compile) and the reason both are severity `blocking`.

**Resolution notes.** Shipped as specified. `validateDuplicateRelationshipFields`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`) walks the merged, sorted relationship set,
claims each `FieldName`, and reports every pair that collides via
`errors.Join`; `validateResolvedFieldNames` calls it ahead of
`validateDuplicateFieldNames` and its doc comment gained the third rule. Both
FIX-171-era comments that described this gap as unenforced were corrected to
point at the new check. Emitted error:

```
tables.public.accounts.relationships: relationships "LedgerEntries" and
"ledger_entries" both resolve to the Go field "LedgerEntries" — two
relationships on one table cannot share a Go field name (PRD §13.7.3);
rename one, or drop an auto-detected edge with `exclude_relationships`
```

Surfaces from `sqlgen validate` (exit 2) and `sqlgen generate` (exit 1), both
verified against a two-table fixture; the FIX-171 happy path re-verified
unchanged on the same fixture (one field, one warning, consumer compiles).
`config.validateRelationships` was deliberately left alone — see the third
bullet above.

**Regression test.** `TestValidateResolvedFieldNames_DuplicateRelationshipField_FIX172`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table_test.go`), three arms: distinct declared names
pascalizing onto one field (error names both sides, the field, and cites
§13.7.3); two declared entries both colliding with the inferred edge — which
also closes the `!replaced` coverage gap FIX-171's auto-review flagged, pinning
exactly one replacement warning *and* the error; and §13.7 sub-categorization
with distinct Go fields still accepted.

`TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean with zero golden churn — no example config trips the
new check, so the ungated rule is non-breaking for every config in the repo.

### FIX-171

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 6, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-169 probe (2026-09-01)

**Issue.** **A config-declared relationship whose name matches the one FK
inference already derived emits the Go struct field twice, and both `sqlgen
validate` and `sqlgen generate` report success.** The failure lands on the
consumer at `go build`. This is the FIX-168 shape — a models package that does
not compile, on any dialect, with or without the API — and it is reachable from
an entirely ordinary config:

```yaml
tables:
  accounts:
    relationships:
      - {name: Entries, type: one_to_many, table: entries, fk: account_id}
```

with `entries.account_id REFERENCES accounts(id)` in the schema. Measured:

```
$ sqlgen validate   -> config and schema are valid
$ sqlgen generate   -> sqlgen: generated 8 files (2 tables, 0 views)
$ go build ./...    -> models_gen.go:27:2: Entries redeclared
                       models_gen.go:116:2: entriesDefaultSort redeclared
                       models_gen.go:1403:2: Entries redeclared
```

The emitted struct carries the field twice, comment and tags included:

```go
type Account struct {
	// Entries - one-to-many relationship with the entries table.
	Entries []*Entry `db:"-" json:"entries"`
	// Entries - one-to-many relationship with the entries table.
	Entries []*Entry `db:"-" json:"entries"`
}
```

**The trigger is narrow but the bait is the obvious choice.** It fires only when
the declared `name:` resolves to the same Go field as the inferred edge — the
pluralized target table, which is exactly what a consumer naming the
relationship after its target would write. Naming it `LedgerEntries` instead
produces two coexisting relationships that compile (verified), so the config is
not wrong in principle; only the name collides.

**There is an intended workflow and it works:** `exclude_relationships:
[entries]` alongside the declaration drops the inferred edge, yielding one field
that builds clean (verified). The defect is that *omitting* the exclude is
silent rather than an error.

**Root cause.** Two independent gates, both in
`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`.

1. `buildRelationshipContexts` (`:1086`) appends schema-derived relationships
   from `schema.Relationships` and config-declared ones from
   `tableCfg.Relationships` into one slice, filtering each only through
   `excludeSet`, then sorts. There is no name dedupe **across** the two sources.

2. The dedupe machinery that would catch it already exists and is gated off for
   this case. `validateDuplicateFieldNames` (`:478`) claims every column and
   every relationship `FieldName` into a `seen` map — precisely the right check
   — but (a) `:479-488` returns `nil` unless some column carries a `column_map`
   field-name override, and (b) `:503` ignores any pair where neither side is
   `overridden`. A relationship is constructed with `owner{sqlName:..., kind:
   "relationship"}` (`:520`) and so is never `overridden`, which means a
   relationship/relationship collision **can never be reported**, even with the
   gate open.

`config.validateRelationships` (`cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:340`) does check
name uniqueness, but only *within* `table.Relationships`; it has no access to
the parsed schema, so it structurally cannot see inferred names. Its own doc
comment names this exact hazard: "a Go field collision would surface as a
compile error far from the config typo."

**Suggested fix.** Prototyped and verified end-to-end before being written here;
all claims below were measured, not reasoned.

- Give `buildRelationshipContexts` an `error` return and do the check there,
  where provenance is known by construction — the schema-derived pass has
  already run, so the inferred `FieldName` set can be captured before the config
  pass and the message can name the **inferred** edge specifically. Doing it in
  `validateDuplicateFieldNames` instead is worse: `RelationshipContext` carries
  no provenance field, so the error can only say "whichever sorted second",
  which names the wrong side half the time.
- One caller to update: `assembleTableContext` (`context_table.go:361`), which
  already returns `error` and already calls `validateResolvedFieldNames` on the
  next line.
- Emit the remedy in the message, including the exact token. Verified output:

  ```
  relationship "Entries" collides with the foreign-key-inferred relationship
  "entries" — both resolve to the Go field "Entries"; add
  `exclude_relationships: [entries]` to replace the inferred edge instead of
  duplicating it
  ```

- **`sqlgen validate` catches it with no further work.** Verified: `validate`
  builds table contexts, so the same error surfaces there. Widening
  `config.SchemaTable` (`validate.go:952`, which today carries no FK or
  relationship data) to run the check in `ValidatePostParse` is therefore
  unnecessary, and would have meant growing the deliberately lightweight
  config-side schema projection for nothing.
- Do **not** ungate `validateDuplicateFieldNames` as the fix. Its
  override-gating governs column/column and column/relationship pairs, whose
  collision semantics are a separate question with its own back-compat surface;
  the relationship/relationship case is unconditionally non-compiling and wants
  its own ungated check.
- Regression tests: a `gen` unit case per arm — collision rejected;
  `exclude_relationships` accepted; distinct names accepted with both edges
  present. An example module is not needed, since the failure reproduces in a
  two-table fixture.

**Verification already performed on the prototype.** `TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean
across all 12 example modules — **no existing config trips the new check**, so
the fix is non-breaking for every config in the repo — plus `./gen/`,
`./config/` and `./cli/` unit suites green. The prototype was reverted; the tree
carries no part of it.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:1086` (`buildRelationshipContexts`), `:361`
  (the caller), `:453` (`validateResolvedFieldNames`), `:478-523`
  (`validateDuplicateFieldNames` and its two gates).
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:340` (`validateRelationships`, config-only
  name check), `:952` (`SchemaTable`), `:987` (`ValidatePostParse`).
- PRD §4.8 (`tables.<table>.relationships`, `exclude_relationships`) — the
  distinct-name rule this extends from config-vs-config to config-vs-inferred.
- FIX-168 — same defect class (generate reports success, models package does not
  compile) and the reason that class is severity `blocking`.
- FIX-169 — surfaced this while probing; every existing example declares
  explicit relationships only for polymorphic columns with no FK constraint
  (e.g. `documents.entity_id`), which is why no example collides and the bug
  went unseen.

**Resolution notes.** Shipped **replace + warn**, not the hard error this entry prescribed. PRD §4.8 (the `relationships` row) and §13.4 both already specify the opposite semantic — "if a manual relationship has the same name as an auto-detected one, the manual definition replaces it" — so erroring would have required deleting a documented rule rather than implementing it. Raised before writing code and confirmed by the user.

`buildRelationshipContexts` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`) now returns `([]RelationshipContext, []string)`: the merged set plus one notice per replacement. The schema-derived pass collects into `inferred`, which is indexed by resolved `FieldName`; the new `mergeDeclaredRelationships` helper folds `tables.<t>.relationships` in, dropping the inferred edge a declared entry claims the same Go field as. Matching is keyed on **FieldName, not Name** — a declared name is PascalCase as written (`Entries`) and an inferred one is the pluralized snake form (`entries`), so nothing matches until `relationshipFieldAndType` has run on both; this is also the identifier that actually collides. The sole caller `assembleTableContext` (`:361`) appends the notices to `input.Warnings`, the same channel `incrementSQLTypeWarnings` uses, so they surface from `generate` **and** `validate` (which reaches this path via `gen.ValidateGeneration`). Emitted text:

```
Warning: tables.public.accounts.relationships: "Entries" replaces the
foreign-key-inferred relationship "entries" — both resolve to the Go
field "Entries" (PRD §13.4). Rename the declared relationship to keep
both edges.
```

The entry's diagnosis was correct on both gates and neither was touched: `validateDuplicateFieldNames`' override-gating is left as-is per the entry's own argument, and `config.SchemaTable` was not widened. Two lint-driven extractions rode along — `tableImports` out of `assembleTableContext` (funlen 101 > 100) and `mergeDeclaredRelationships` out of `buildRelationshipContexts` (cyclop 16 > 15).

**PRD updated** (documenting existing behavior, not adding any): §13.4 gained a paragraph stating the FieldName keying, the warning, and why emitting both is non-compiling; the §4.8 `relationships` row now says "resolves to the same Go field name … — with a non-fatal warning" and links §13.4.

**Regression test.** `TestBuildRelationshipContexts_DeclaredReplacesInferred_FIX171` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table_test.go`), table-driven over four arms on a two-table accounts/entries fixture: inferred-only baseline; the reported collision (one field, surviving `Name` is the config's `Entries`, exactly one warning naming both sides and the field); `exclude_relationships: [entries]` alongside the declaration (one field, no warning — the inferred edge is gone before the merge); and a distinct declared name (`LedgerEntries`, both edges coexist, no warning).

**Verified end-to-end.** A binary built from HEAD in a throwaway worktree reproduces the entry's measurement exactly — `validate` and `generate` both report success, then `go build` fails with `Entries redeclared` (×2) and `entriesDefaultSort redeclared`. The fixed binary warns from both commands, emits `Entries []*Entry` once, and the consumer package compiles. `make check` clean across all 33 modules under `-race`; `make check-examples` clean across all 13 example modules; `TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean with **zero golden churn** — no config in the repo trips the replacement, confirming the entry's non-breaking finding.

**Auto-review reconciliation.** Two findings, both comment-accuracy, corrected inline: the `inferredByField` comment no longer claims a two-inferred-edge collision is "unreachable" (two edges to *different* targets whose names pluralize onto one field still can), and the `!replaced` comment no longer claims `config.validateRelationships` owns declared-vs-declared collisions — it compares `name:` byte-equal, so two declared entries whose names pascalize onto one field (`primary_document` + `PrimaryDocument`, or same-name-different-`filter:` §13.7 sub-categories) pass validation and both reach the struct. **That residual gap is real, pre-existing, and the same non-compiling class as this entry on the declared-vs-declared axis** — §13.7.3 row 2 requires distinct Go field names on `<Table>FieldOptions` and nothing enforces it. Closed immediately after, by user direction, as **FIX-172** — which also covers the `!replaced` coverage gap. Also noted, pre-existing and not introduced: `BuildTableContextsFromSchema` (`orchestrate.go:1908`, the `sqlgen graphql gen` path) discards `input.Warnings` entirely, so this notice — like `incrementSQLTypeWarnings` — is silent there.

### FIX-169

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples
- **Surfaced by:** landing the FIX-151 `scalar_probes` fixture (2026-08-29)

**Issue.** **Every example with a GraphQL surface is PostgreSQL, and none sets
`overrides.use_pointers: false`, so two whole axes of the generated API compile in no module.**
This is the entry FIX-148, FIX-151, FIX-165 and FIX-166 have been citing as "FIX-135" — a
misnumbering, corrected in those entries: FIX-135 is a PRD §11.1 / §11.5 relationship-filter
documentation fix and has nothing to do with example coverage.

What the `scalar_probes` table (2026-08-29) *did* close is the type-coverage half on PostgreSQL:
all twelve FIX-151 Go types now round-trip through a live gqlgen handler and a real database. What
remains:

- ~~**No API-enabled MySQL example.**~~ **Closed 2026-08-31 by FIX-166.** The `mysql` example now
  sets `api.graphql.enabled`, so MySQL `SET`, the `blob` family, `year`, `bit(1)` and the unsigned
  integer widths all compile into a real gqlgen schema, and `tests/graphql_set_test.go` exercises the

  (FIX-166) and `warehouses.external_id` / `ksuid.KSUID` (a consumer `api.graphql.scalars`
  declaration + a `gqlscalars` package); every other column in that schema already bound cleanly.
- **Still no API-enabled SQLite example.** `graphql` and `graphql_top_level` are both PostgreSQL.
  **Correction (2026-09-01):** this bullet originally read "SQLite's `types.DateTime` defaulting
  reaches no GraphQL surface in any module", which is wrong about the TYPE — `types.DateTime` /
  `types.NullDateTime` already compile into a gqlgen schema in the `graphql` example, via the
