  `processedAt: NullDateTime`). What reaches no GraphQL surface is the SQLite **dialect-default
  registration path** — `registerDialectDefaults` (`gotype.go`) claiming datetime/timestamp/date
  for those two types with no override present — and the SQLite dialect on the API surface at all.
- **No module sets `use_pointers: false`.** The `database/sql` wrappers reach `scalar_probes`
  through a table-scoped `overrides.types` block, which produces the identical Go types, but the
  production route is the module-wide flag and it is exercised by no module. FIX-168 — a models
  package that did not compile under that flag, on every dialect — survived from phase 6 for
  exactly this reason, and its regression pin is a unit test rather than a module.
- The examples' own hand-written tests are written against `*T`, so flipping the flag on an
  existing module is not the fix; it needs a module of its own.
- **No module routes a column onto a gqlgen-bundled scalar.** FIX-170 fixed that route — a
  `marshaling: builtin` scalar now pins gqlgen's own marshaler rather than inheriting its
  `Model[0]` — but it is pinned only by unit tests, and the defect was "the generated module does
  not compile", which no unit test can prove. Declaring it in an existing example is not a cheap
  add: `api.graphql.scalars` is keyed by Go TYPE, so `Int64: {go_type: int64}` retypes every
  `int64` column in the module. In both API-enabled examples that means the `categories` BIGSERIAL
  PK and the `category_id` FKs, rippling into PK resolver args, cursors, filter inputs,
  relationship loaders and connection edges. It wants the module of its own this entry calls for.

**Suggested fix.** ~~An API-enabled example on a second dialect is the higher-value half~~ — **done
for MySQL (2026-08-31, FIX-166)**; SQLite remains. What is left is the `use_pointers: false` module,
which can be small: one table, a handful of nullable columns, the generated package compiled and one
round-trip test. The gqlgen-bundled-scalar route (FIX-170) still wants a module of its own for the
reason spelled out above.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/{schema.sql,sqlgen.yml}` — `scalar_probes` and its
  table-scoped overrides; `tests/scalars_test.go::TestBuiltInScalarProbes`.
- FIX-151 (the class this coverage exists for), FIX-166 (MySQL SET — resolved; it landed the
  API-enabled MySQL example this entry called for), FIX-168 (what the missing `use_pointers: false`
  module let through).
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/mysql/{sqlgen.yml,gqlgen.yml,gqlscalars/,tests/graphql_set_test.go}`
  — the shape a second API-enabled example takes, for whoever adds the SQLite one.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-09-01. Both remaining bullets closed, by two changes. Every
claim below was measured on throwaway modules before anything was written into the repo — the
approach was probed on both dialects first, not reasoned about.

**1. `api:` enabled on the existing `sqlite` example.** The entry's own References section named
the mysql example as "the shape a second API-enabled example takes, for whoever adds the SQLite
one", and that is exactly what it cost: **one binding.** `warehouses.external_id` is retyped to
`ksuid.KSUID` by a table-scoped override, so §26.4.1 requires a consumer declaration — the same
`KSUID` / `marshaling: external` / `gqlscalars` trio mysql carries. Every other column across all
18 tables bound through the built-in registry or a spec built-in, including the `binary_keys`
BLOB primary key (`BinaryKey(ctx, id []byte)`), the composite PKs, both views, `decimal.Decimal`
and the `file_per_table` layout. Zero `panic("not implemented")` field resolvers; all 24
pre-existing test files pass unchanged.

*Why the existing 18-table example rather than a small purpose-built one:* the SQLite dialect's
whole mapping table, its BLOB PK, its composite PKs, its views and `file_per_table` now compile
into a real gqlgen schema. A 2-table module would have proven the dialect works on two trivial
tables.

*Golden churn is one line.* Enabling the API is purely additive on the models side: the only diff
to a pre-existing sqlite golden is `"graphql": false` → `true` in the manifest feature block (and
its `_index.md` mirror). Everything else is new files — `api_envelopes_gen.go` plus the
`models/graph/` tree.

*The regression pin* is `tests/graphql_datetime_test.go`, which drives a live gqlgen handler over
the in-memory SQLite (no Docker) and asserts the DIALECT-DEFAULT `types.DateTime` /
`types.NullDateTime` binding — the path the corrected bullet above identifies. It reads values back
through a second query rather than trusting the mutation's echo, so a marshaler that round-trips on
the wire while storing something else in the TEXT column fails.

*Two things the test had to work around, both properties of the example rather than defects.*
`articles.deleted_at` is the soft-delete column, so creating a row with it set makes the
post-insert fetch filter its own row away ("not found") — the test uses `users` instead, whose
`created_at` / `updated_at` pair carries the same two Go types with no soft-delete interaction.
And `users.updated_at` carries a SQLite-side `DEFAULT (datetime('now'))`, so the NULL arm is seeded
through SQL: a gqlgen input cannot ask for NULL anyway — a nullable input field arrives as a nil
pointer whether it was omitted or written as an explicit `null`, so both read as unset and the
database default fills in. What the scalar owns, and what the test asserts, is the read direction.

**2. New `graphql_null_wrappers` module (PostgreSQL, pgx)** closes the other two bullets together.
They are orthogonal — nullable ints take `NullInt64` while non-null ints take `Int64`, verified —
so one module holds both without either masking the other, and the entry already gestured at a
single "module of its own" for both.

*`overrides.use_pointers: false`, module-wide.* PostgreSQL is the deliberate choice: it is the only
dialect that reaches all seven `sql.NullX` wrappers **and** lands soft delete on `sql.NullTime`.
SQLite maps every integer width to `int64` (no `NullInt16` / `NullInt32`) and claims `datetime` for
`types.NullDateTime` (no `NullTime`), so a SQLite module would have covered four of seven. Docker
costs nothing here — `make test-examples` already requires it for the postgres/mysql examples.

The schema is built for the paths `scalar_probes` cannot reach, which is the entry's own argument
for why the module-wide flag needs a module: `scalar_probes` is a standalone table with no FK, no
relationship, no soft delete and no cursor keys. `accounts.parent_id` is a nullable self-FK, so
both relationship loaders key on a `sql.NullInt64`; `accounts.deleted_at` puts the soft-delete
predicate on a `sql.NullTime`; `balance` / `tenant_ref` sit the integration-owned Null variants
(`decimal.NullDecimal`, `uuid.NullUUID`) alongside the stdlib family.

*`Int64: {go_type: int64, marshaling: builtin}`* — the FIX-170 route no module compiled. The defect
was "the generated module does not compile", so the load-bearing evidence is that the package
builds; `TestBundledScalarInt64RoundTrip` adds the runtime half by pushing 2^53+1 through a live
handler, which survives only if every hop is a true 64-bit integer. Because that assertion would
also pass on a 64-bit host without the declaration (`graphql.UnmarshalInt` is
`interfaceToSignedNumber[int]` and only range-checks when `strconv.IntSize == 32`),
`TestBundledScalarInt64IsDeclaredInSchema` introspects the wire types and pins `id` / `externalRef`
to `Int64` — so dropping the config line fails a test rather than silently degrading.

**Verification.** `make check-examples` clean across all 12 example modules (11 pre-existing + the
new one, with sqlite now carrying an API surface); `TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean across every example,
with a second no-update run confirming idempotency. The new module's 9 tests and 11 subtests run
against a real PostgreSQL container; `golangci-lint` reports 0 issues on both changed modules.
gqlgen is pinned to v0.17.90 in the new module and in sqlite, matching the other three API examples
— `go mod tidy` had defaulted sqlite to v0.17.94, which would have put the one module FIX-170's
`injectBuiltins` table does not describe on a different gqlgen.

*`make check`: fmt / lint / vet clean across all 8 modules, and every `cmd/sqlgen` package passes.
The `make test` leg fails on a **pre-existing** 600s timeout in `cmd/sqlgen/cli`, not on an
assertion. Measured rather than assumed: the package takes **434.9s** standalone at HEAD and
**441.0s** with this change (~6s, 1.4% — noise), and only exceeds 600s under `make check`'s
whole-module parallel CPU contention; re-run with `-timeout=25m` the whole module is green
(`cli 567.2s`, exit 0). The 24.11 sweep recorded this package at ~340s and FIX-170's at ~506s, so it
has been drifting toward the default `go test` limit for two phases. Left alone deliberately —
raising the Makefile timeout is a build-config change outside this entry's scope.

**Auto-review follow-ups, all applied inline.** (1) `graphql_null_wrappers` was in no CI matrix —
see **CI** below; a runtime pin CI never runs is not a pin. (2) The verification paragraph said "15
example modules" and "10 tests"; the real numbers are 12 modules and 9 test functions (the tenth
`func Test*` is `TestMain`), corrected above. (3) The sqlite datetime test seeded three `users` rows
with no cleanup. Harmless today — every sibling assertion in that package is id- or name-scoped —
but `email` is UNIQUE, so it broke `go test -count=2`; it now registers a `t.Cleanup` that deletes
its own rows by email. Note the package is still not `-count=2` clean for a **pre-existing** reason
(`views_test.go` seeds fixed-email users without cleanup); this fix removed only its own
contribution rather than widening into that. (4) `TestGraphQLDateTimeFilter`'s positive query was
ANDed with an `email` equality that already narrowed to one row, so an always-true TimeComparator
would have passed; it gained a negative case (`createdAt: {lt: "2000-01-01"}` must NOT match a row
stamped 2030).

**Not fixed here, deliberately.** Declaring an explicit relationship on a column that already
carries a FK constraint collides with the FK-inferred one and fails inside the gqlgen subprocess
(`Field Account.entries can only be defined once`) rather than at `sqlgen validate`. Hit while
building the probe; it is a pre-existing DX wart, not part of this entry, and every existing
example follows the convention it violates (explicit relationships only for polymorphic columns
with no FK). Surfaced to the user rather than logged.

**PRD.** No amendment — this is example coverage of behavior §4.7 and §26.4.1 already specify.

**CI.** `graphql_null_wrappers` is wired into both matrices in
`.github/workflows/examples.yml` — a runtime pin CI never executes is not a pin. That file's matrix

### FIX-167

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-151 analysis (2026-08-28); re-scoped and measured against live
  PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite 2026-08-31

**Issue.** **A column whose Go type has a real GraphQL scalar still filters through
`comparator.String`, so the generated filter compares a binary, network or duration column
against a text parameter.** It compiles — which is why it is not part of FIX-151, that entry
covered the shapes that failed generation — and the translator wires it end to end
(`graphql/expected/graph/filter_translate_gen.go:508-533`), so these filters *execute*. Measured,
they either return silently wrong results or raise a runtime database error:

| Column | Dialect | What a `comparator.String` operand does today |
|---|---|---|
| `bytea` | postgres | `eq` matches only a hand-written `\x0102ff` literal. The `Bytes` scalar's wire form is **base64**, so a client filtering on a value it just read gets **0 rows, no error** |
| `blob` | mysql | matches only a raw-byte string; base64 → **0 rows, no error** |
| `blob` | sqlite | a BLOB never equals a TEXT value, so `eq` / `in` / `like` **always return 0 rows** |
| `interval` | postgres | `-2h45m0s` is read as `-01:15:00` — PostgreSQL applies the sign to the leading field only, so a negative duration filter is **silently wrong**; `like` / `contains` / `startsWith` / `endsWith` / `nlike` → **SQLSTATE 42883** |
| `inet` | postgres | `eq` with the wire form `"10.0.0.1"` → **0 rows** (see the write-path defect below); `like` → **42883** |
| `cidr` / `macaddr` | postgres | `eq` works; `like` → **42883** |

Silent wrong results are the failure mode PRD §26.5.3 names as "the worst available", which is why
this is `blocking` rather than the `tracked` it was first logged as. It is live in shipped goldens
on two axes: `sqlite/expected/user_gen.go:1920` gives `users.avatar` (a BLOB) a
`*comparator.NullableString` that can never match, and `mysql/expected/graph/user_gen.graphqls:84`
advertises `avatar: NullableStringComparator` on an API-enabled schema whose field type is `Bytes`.

**Correction to the original entry (2026-08-31).** It also named "under `use_pointers: false` a
nullable `integer` is `NullInt32` / `StringComparator`". True when written, no longer: FIX-168
(2026-08-29) added `gotype.StdNullUnderlying`, so a `database/sql` wrapper is classified by the
type it wraps and the whole `sql.NullX` family resolves to its real family. The live set is exactly
the five Go types the built-in dialect tables reach that have no comparator arm: `[]byte`,
`time.Duration`, `net.IP`, `net.IPNet`, `net.HardwareAddr`.

**Root cause.** `resolveSimpleComparator`'s `default: return "String"` arm
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`), reached by every Go type its explicit arms do not name.
`resolveAPIFilterProjection` then derives the GraphQL input from the model comparator, so the two
surfaces disagree by construction rather than by accident.

**The defect is model-side first.** `ScalarProbeFilter.Payload` is `*comparator.String` on a
`[]byte` column with no GraphQL involved (`graphql/expected/models_gen.go:20790`). A GraphQL-only
fix cannot reach it: `resolveAPIFilterProjection` faithfully projects whatever
`resolveComparatorType` returns, and that is the "one derivation" D1 invariant working as
designed. The fix therefore starts in `comparator/` and `resolveGenericComparator`.

**Fix — blessed into the PRD 2026-08-31.** §11.2 gains `Opaque[T]` / `NullableOpaque[T]` plus five
selection rows; §26.4 gains five projection rows, the Rule 1 / Sharing carve-out for
`Duration`, and the dialect gating; §26.4.1 gains the IPv4 normalization rule; §26.5.3 gains the
translators. Shape:

| Column | Model comparator | GraphQL input | Operands | Dialects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bytea` / `blob` family | `Opaque[[]byte]` | `BytesComparator` | `Bytes` | all |
| `interval` | `Number[time.Duration]` | `DurationComparator` + `DurationRange` | `Duration` | all |
| `inet` | `Opaque[net.IP]` | `IPComparator` | `IP` | postgres |
| `cidr` | `Opaque[net.IPNet]` | `CIDRComparator` | `CIDR` | postgres |
| `macaddr` | `Opaque[net.HardwareAddr]` | `MacAddrComparator` | `MacAddr` | postgres |

Operators are `eq neq gt gte lt lte in nin` (+ `isNull` on the nullable twin), and `between` /
`nbetween` additionally on `DurationComparator`. The text operators are dropped deliberately —
`LIKE` does not exist on `interval` / `inet` / `macaddr`, and on `bytea` it matches raw bytes.

**Verified before blessing** (probe scripts were scratch, findings recorded here):

- **25/25 native operators pass** against live PostgreSQL 16 / pgx v5.9.1 for all four opaque
  types: `= != > >= < <=` plus `= ANY($1)` / `!= ALL($1)`. `[]byte` additionally verified against
  MySQL 8 and modernc sqlite v1.48.1.
- **`Opaque[T any]` compiles and emits the right SQL.** Prototyped in `comparator/` against the
  real `sql` package: all four instantiations plus `NullableNumber[time.Duration]` produce the
  expected clauses (`payload = ANY($)` on pgx, `payload IN $` on sqlite) and hand the driver the
  **native Go value**, not a rendering of one.
- **`T any` is required, and safe.** `[]byte`, `net.IP` and `net.IPNet` are not `comparable`, so
  the `Enum[T]` constraint cannot be reused. It also buys nothing: no comparator body compares in
  Go — `Enum[T]`'s own `comparable` is already nominal (`comparator/enum.go` never uses `==`).
- **`time.Duration` needs no new family.** It is `~int64`, so it satisfies `comparator.Numeric`,
  and pgx encodes it as an interval — `dur > $1`, `= ANY($1)` and `BETWEEN` all verified correct.

**Two constraints the implementation must respect** (both verified, both silent if missed):

1. **Do not widen `isComparatorNumericGoType` to admit `time.Duration`.**
   `sqlTypeCategory("interval")` is `categoryUnknown`, which `isArithmeticSQLColumn` *trusts*, so
   widening it would also make `interval` increment-eligible and emit `dur_inc: Int` /
   `dur_dec: Int` — the exact operand mismatch this entry exists to remove. The Duration arm
   belongs in `resolveGenericComparator`.
2. **The `default: return "String"` arm stays.** It is correct for the population that reaches it
   — consumer `type_map` / `overrides.types` entries, which must satisfy `driver.Valuer` and
   conventionally return a string. `uuid.UUID`, `decimal.Decimal` and `ksuid.KSUID` all do, and all
   three store into text columns (`mysql/schema.sql:150` — `external_id TEXT`). Only the five
   sqlgen-resolved types move.

**Folded in: the `net.IP` write path.** `UnmarshalIP` uses `net.ParseIP`, which returns the
**16-byte** IPv4-in-IPv6 form for a dotted quad, so pgx writes `::ffff:10.0.0.1/128` instead of
`10.0.0.1/32`. `net.IP.String()` renders both as `"10.0.0.1"`, so the GraphQL round-trip hides it
completely — but the stored `inet` matches neither a text literal nor the subnet operators, and any
non-sqlgen reader of the column sees the mapped form. It is folded here rather than logged
separately because `IPComparator` inherits the identical 4-byte/16-byte ambiguity: fixing one
without the other leaves the filter correct and still returning 0 rows. Verified: `ip.To4()` when
non-nil (the guard is required — `To4()` returns nil for real IPv6) stores every IPv4 as
`x.x.x.x/32`, reads back as a 4-byte `net.IP` whose `.String()` is unchanged (**no wire-format
change, no scalar golden churn**), leaves `2001:db8::1` / `::1` untouched, and flips both text
equality and `<<=` from 0 rows to correct. Values read out of the database need no normalization —
pgx already decodes `inet` to the 4-byte form.

**Sequencing.** This contradicts `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL_READ_SURFACE.md`'s blast-radius table
("`comparator/`: **None.** Every family the GraphQL layer gains already exists"), which is why the
PRD delta landed first. It is independent of 25.4 / 25.5 — those close families whose *model*
comparator is already correct (FIX-145); this one is the class where the model comparator is itself
wrong — but it should land after 25.1's single derivation and be covered by 25.2's completeness
lint.

**Example coverage is already in place.** `graphql`'s `scalar_probes` carries all eleven affected
columns on both nullabilities, and the API-enabled `mysql` example's `users.avatar` gives the
`Bytes` family a second dialect for free. The `scalar_probes` schema comment currently records the
`StringComparator` filters as known-and-tracked; that note comes out with the fix.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go` — `resolveSimpleComparator` default arm,
  `resolveGenericComparator`, `isComparatorNumericGoType`, `isIncrementableGoType`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `resolveAPIFilterProjection`, `comparatorTranslatorVariant`,
  `shippedComparatorFamilies`, `comparatorOperandScalars` / `registerColumnScalars` (§26.4 Rule 3:
  the five operand scalars must be registered on use or the schema names scalars it never
  declares).
- `comparator/` — new `opaque.go`; `enum.go` for the shape to mirror.
- PRD §11.2 (`Opaque[T]` + selection rows), §26.4 (projection rows, Rule 1, Sharing, dialect
  gating, "Opaque columns" / "Duration columns"), §26.4.1 (IPv4 normalization), §26.5.3
  (translators).
- FIX-151 (names this as the adjacent defect), FIX-168 (closed the `sql.NullX` half),
  FIX-145 (the Enum/JSON/JSONB/Slice fallback 25.4/25.5 close — a different class),
  FIX-103 (`columnIsFilterable`, the `T comparable` limit `Opaque[T]` deliberately sidesteps).

**Resolution (2026-08-31).** Landed as blessed. `comparator/opaque.go` adds `Opaque[T any]` /
`NullableOpaque[T any]` — eight operators (`eq neq gt gte lt lte in nin`) plus `Custom`, and `Null`
on the twin. `resolveGenericComparator` gained two arms: `time.Duration` →
`Number[time.Duration]`, and the four opaque Go types → `Opaque[T]` via `isOpaqueComparatorGoType`.
On the API side `comparatorTranslatorVariant` grew an `Opaque` case (monomorphized by type
parameter, per Rule 1) and a `time.Duration` case inside `Number`; `shippedComparatorFamilies` gained
five entries. `UnmarshalIP` now normalizes IPv4 to its 4-byte form.

**The PostgreSQL-only gating needed no dialect switch.** `collectComparatorFamilies` already emits a
family only when a column references it (§26.4 Rule 3), and `inet` / `cidr` / `macaddr` exist on no
other dialect — so `IPComparator` / `CIDRComparator` / `MacAddrComparator` are absent from the mysql
goldens while `NullableBytesComparator` is present, with nothing in the generator saying so.

**Neither did the operand-scalar registration.** For all five families the comparator's operand
scalar IS the column's own field scalar (`Bytes`, `Duration`, `IP`, `CIDR`, `MacAddr`), which
`registerColumnScalars` registers before the operand loop — unlike `Decimal`, whose
`decimal.NullDecimal` column declares `NullDecimal` but filters on `Decimal`. None of the five has a
Null-variant registry entry, so the identity holds on both nullabilities.
`TestOpaqueComparatorBindings_matchRegistryAndPredicate` pins it, since a future Null variant would
silently make the schema name an undeclared scalar.

**Two decisions verified against real systems rather than reasoned.**

- *gqlgen operand shapes.* Measured against v0.17.90 in a scratch module, because the rule is not
  uniform: a nullable operand is pointer-wrapped iff the Go type is not nilable (`[]byte` / `net.IP`
  / `net.HardwareAddr` arrive bare, `*net.IPNet` wrapped), but LIST elements follow a *different*
  rule — struct elements are pointer-wrapped (`[]*net.IPNet`) while basic-kind ones are not
  (`[]time.Duration`, even though `time.Duration` is equally non-nilable). Within Opaque the two
  coincide only because `net.IPNet` is the sole non-nilable member and happens to be a struct, so
  `opaqueComparatorBindings` states both facts instead of deriving one from the other.
- *SQL behaviour.* All 25 native operators verified against live PostgreSQL 16 / pgx v5.9.1 for the
  four opaque types; `[]byte` additionally against MySQL 8 and modernc sqlite v1.48.1.

**The Duration arm is comparator-only, deliberately.** `time.Duration` was NOT added to
`isComparatorNumericGoType`: that predicate feeds `isIncrementableGoType`, and
`sqlTypeCategory("interval")` is `categoryUnknown` — which `isArithmeticSQLColumn` *trusts* — so an
interval column would have silently gained `dur_inc: Int` / `dur_dec: Int`, the same operand
mismatch this entry exists to remove. `TestDurationColumn_isNotIncrementable` was confirmed
fail-first by temporarily making that mistake.

**Import emission was the other silent hazard.** `comparator_translate_gen.go` renders through
`FormatOnly`, which does not run goimports, so `comparatorTranslatorsUseTime` became
`comparatorTranslatorStdImports` — a missing import and an unused one are both compile errors in the
consumer's project, and `[]byte` needs none while the `net` types do.
`TestComparatorTranslatorStdImports_matchEmittedBodies` cross-checks the computed list against what
the rendered bodies actually reference.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all modules; `make check-examples` clean across all 13
example modules against real databases. Behavioural regression pin:
`graphql/tests/scalar_filters_test.go` runs every family through the live gqlgen handler against a
real Postgres — including the headline case (a base64 `Bytes` value read back and fed straight into
`eq`, which matched nothing before), `Duration` `eq` on `"90m"` against a row stored as `1h30m0s`
(same interval, different string), and `TestIPScalarNormalizesIPv4`, which reads `addr::text` to
assert `10.0.0.1/32` and checks `addr <<= '10.0.0.0/8'` matches — both of which the 16-byte form
defeated. Unit pins: 10 new rows in `TestFilterProjection_perGoType`, 5 in
`TestComparatorFamilies_projectEveryGoOperator`, and `comparator/opaque_test.go`.

**One entry-scope claim did not survive contact and the PRD text was corrected.** The draft §11.2
paragraph justified keeping the `String` fallback with "an override type must satisfy
`driver.Valuer` to be storable, and the conventional implementation returns a string". False: the
postgres example's `source_ip` is overridden to `netip.Addr`, which implements neither `Valuer` nor
`Scanner` — pgx has a native codec for it. The fallback is still right there (its text input format
matches the operand), but the paragraph now states the two limits honestly: an override type over a
non-text column still advertises text operators the database may reject at runtime, and one whose
driver encoding does not match its column's text input format compares wrongly rather than loudly.
Both are consequences of sqlgen not modeling the type, and are out of this entry's scope — what is
not accepted is sqlgen doing it to a type it resolved itself.

**Not covered: MySQL `SET` and PostgreSQL enum arrays.** FIX-166 deferred its
`[Enum!]!` field / `StringComparator` filter disagreement here, and this entry does **not** close it
— the two are different defects that look alike. FIX-167 was *the model comparator is wrong*: a
`bytea` column filtering through `comparator.String` sends text to a binary column, which is
incorrect SQL at the model layer with no GraphQL involved. A SET column's model comparator is
`comparator.String` and PRD §7.6 makes that **correct**, because the column really is stored as
comma-separated text; its filter is wired to a real `translateStringComparator` and returns right
answers. What disagrees there is only the GraphQL projection — the field advertises
`[<Set>Value!]!` while the filter advertises `String` — which is the same shape as the enum array
(`comparator.Slice[T]`, no projection, `fallbackComparatorInput`) and therefore belongs to FIX-145
and 25.4 / 25.5, not here. Both were left untouched by this change: the `IsSet` and `IsSlice` arms of
`resolveGenericComparator` precede the new ones, and neither example golden moved.

**Auto-review caught one real regression, fixed before close.** The new
`resolveGenericComparator` arms run BEFORE `resolveSimpleComparator`'s PK/FK arm, so a `[]byte` /
`net.IP` / `net.IPNet` / `net.HardwareAddr` / `time.Duration` PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY moved off
`comparator.ID` — but `funcmap.go`'s `funcPKFilterExpr`, `pkFilterInExpr` and `funcPKIsStringType`
re-derived the family from `isComparatorNumericGoType` alone, which is still false for all five. The
generated client therefore assigned `&comparator.ID{…}` into a `*comparator.Opaque[[]byte]` field
and **the package stopped compiling** — 10+ sites per table (GetByID, GetMany, the
Create/Update/Delete ID collections, every O2M and M2M loader). Reproduced end to end: a
`BLOB PRIMARY KEY` plus a child FK on sqlite yields six `cannot use &comparator.ID{…} … as
*comparator.Opaque[[]byte]` errors against the pre-fix binary and builds clean after.

The example suite missed it by coincidence, which is worth recording: `tenancy/sqlgen.yml` overrides
`blob` → `uuid.UUID`, the only `INET` column in a postgres example is overridden to `netip.Addr`, and
the `mysql` / `sqlite` `avatar BLOB` columns are ordinary nullable columns, never keys.

**The cause was a third independent derivation**, which is the exact defect class §26.5.3's D1
invariant exists to remove — the same shape as the schema/translator split 25.1 collapsed, one layer
down. So the fix is a collapse rather than a patch: `pkComparatorFamily` (`context_table.go`) now
owns the classification, mirrors `resolveGenericComparator`'s arm order, and all three funcmap
helpers read it. `pkIsStringType` returning false for the new families is load-bearing — it is what
makes the templates collect `[]T` natively instead of `[]string` via `fmt.Sprint`. That is also
strictly better than the pre-fix behaviour for `[]byte`, which rendered a binary key as
`fmt.Sprint([]byte{…})` → `"[1 2 255]"` and matched nothing. Pinned by
`TestPKFilterExpr_matchesFilterFieldType` across all nine key-eligible shapes, asserting the emitted
literal's type against the filter field's own type rather than against a routing decision.

Also from review, both doc-only: a comment cited a test name that does not exist
(`TestOpaqueComparatorBindingsMatchRegistry` → `TestOpaqueComparatorBindings_matchRegistryAndPredicate`),
and the `scalar_probes` fixture comment claimed "every column here" filtered through
`StringComparator` — false for the shape-B `sql.NullX` columns, which FIX-168 had already moved, and
the same overclaim this entry's own correction paragraph fixes.

**Files changed.** `comparator/opaque.go` + `opaque_test.go` (new); `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`
(`resolveGenericComparator`, `isOpaqueComparatorGoType`); `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go`
(`shippedComparatorFamilies`, `opaqueComparatorOperators`, `comparatorTranslatorVariant`,
`makeOpaqueTranslator`, `makeDurationTranslator`, `opaqueComparatorBindings`,
`APIComparatorTranslator` fields); `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go` (`comparatorTranslatorStdImports`,
`stdImportForQualifiedType`); `cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap.go` (`funcPKFilterExpr`, `pkFilterInExpr`,
