### FIX-166

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-151 auto-review (2026-08-28)

**Issue.** **A MySQL `SET` column has no GraphQL binding, and now fails generation instead of
emitting a panic resolver.** A SET column resolves to a named slice (`UsersPermissionsSet` =
`[]UsersPermissionsSetValue`) which carries `String()` / `Value()` / `Scan` but **no**
`MarshalGQL` / `UnmarshalGQL` — unlike enums, whose named types do.

Not a regression: pre-FIX-151 the column fell through to `String`, so gqlgen answered the read side
with a `panic("not implemented")` field resolver and typed the input field `string` against a
named-slice model field, which did not compile. FIX-151 turns that into a named error.

**Root cause.** `BuildAPIContext(tables, enums, cfg)` threads only `EnumContext` into
`typeBindings.enums`; SET types live in `SetContext` and nothing in `graphQLTypeForGoType` consults
`col.IsSet`. PRD §26.4's mapping table is also silent on SET.

**Suggested fix.** Bind SET the way enums are bound — emit `MarshalGQL` / `UnmarshalGQL` on the
named slice in `templates/set.go.tmpl`, thread sets into `typeBindings`, and add the PRD row. Decide
the wire form first: a GraphQL enum list (`[UsersPermission!]!`) is the honest projection of SET
semantics, and is a §26.4 decision rather than an implementation detail.

**Coupled hazard.** If SETs are registered, `isNilableGqlgenGoType` must learn about them: a named
slice type is Go-nilable but its NAME reveals nothing, so the current syntactic check returns false
and the translator would emit a deref that does not compile. Any fix must set the `Nilable` flag or
extend the check, and add SET to `TestScalarBinding_everyBuiltInGoTypeResolves`.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `graphQLTypeForGoType`, `typeBindings`, `isNilableGqlgenGoType`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_set.go`, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/set.go.tmpl`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/mysql/schema.sql:11` — `permissions SET(...)`, invisible because
  that example has no API.
- PRD §26.4 (mapping table, no SET row). FIX-151 (the class), FIX-169 — the missing
  API-enabled MySQL example, which is why no module ever compiled a SET column into a schema.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-31. **Wire form (the §26.4 decision the entry asked for
first): a GraphQL enum list, named after the VALUE type** — `permissions: [UsersPermissionsSetValue!]!`,
not the entry's speculative `[UsersPermission!]!`. Naming the enum after the Go value type keeps the
invariant `graphQLTypeForGoType` already holds for every enum (`return e.GoTypeName`) and introduces
no new naming rule; `UsersPermission` would have needed a strip-`_set`-and-singularize rule plus a
`computeNameCollisions` entry, since a `users_permissions` table or enum resolves to the same name.

**The projection is not an analogy to the PostgreSQL enum array — it is the same shape.** An enum
array is a bare enum plus a named slice sibling carrying `MarshalGQL` / `UnmarshalGQL`; a SET is a
value type plus a named slice that IS the column's Go type. So `enumContextsForSets`
(`context_api.go`) projects each `SetContext` onto `EnumContext{GoTypeName: ValueGoTypeName,
SliceGoTypeName: GoTypeName}`, and every downstream consumer — `buildEnumGoTypeLookup`,
`APIContext.UsedEnums`, the shared-schema `enum` block, the wrapper's two-entry `models:` merge —
works unchanged. `BuildAPIContext` gained a `sets []SetContext` parameter (3 production call sites).

**Emitted surface.** `templates/set.go.tmpl` emits `MarshalGQL` / `UnmarshalGQL` on **both** types,
and `generateSets` adds `io` unconditionally, mirroring `generateEnums`. The named slice's
`MarshalGQL` is load-bearing rather than symmetric: gqlgen's generated list marshaler for a
named-slice binding is literally `return v` typed as `graphql.Marshaler`, so without it the emitted
server does not compile. Wire identifiers route through the same `gqlEnumIdent` helper enums use,
so the SQL literal (`"multi_word_value"`) stays in the Go constant and only the wire form is
SCREAMING-cased. `mapColumnToGraphQL` wraps the list via a new `columnIsListShaped` predicate
(extracted rather than inlined as `col.IsSlice || col.IsSet`, which pushed the function over the
cyclop cap); `gqlgenInputGoType` returns `[]<Set>Value`; `inputCoercionFor` folds SET into the
existing named-slice cast arm. `gotype`'s SET branch now sets `SliceElemType` — `IsSlice` stays
false, so pq.Array wrapping and comparator resolution are untouched and the model side has zero
golden churn.

**The "coupled hazard" was a false alarm, and the entry's remedy would have been wrong.**
`isNilableGqlgenGoType` needs no change and no `Nilable` flag: it keys on the GQLGEN type, not the
model type (`context_api.go`, `inputCoercionFor`). Measured against gqlgen v0.17.90, a list field's
generated input Go type is a bare `[]T` for BOTH nullabilities — never `*[]T` — so the existing
`[]`-prefix arm already answers correctly. Adding a `Nilable` flag keyed on the model's named slice
would have been a second, redundant path to the same answer.

**Verification.** Probed against real gqlgen v0.17.90 before implementing (standalone module,
scratch): no field resolver stubs for either `[E!]!` or `[E!]`, and the generated exec accesses
`obj.Permissions` directly. Then proved in-repo: **`api:` is now enabled on the `mysql` example**
(FIX-169's first bullet), the only module compiling a MySQL-specific Go type into a gqlgen schema.
Its generated graph package has zero `panic("not implemented")` field resolvers, and
`tests/graphql_set_test.go` writes and reads SET values through a live handler against a real MySQL
— asserting both the wire identifiers and the lowercase literal actually stored in the column, so a
marshaler that round-trips on the wire while corrupting the column would fail. Unit pins:
`TestScalarBinding_setColumnProjectsEnumList` + `TestInputTranslate_SetColumn`
(`api_scalar_binding_test.go`, the file the entry asked for) and a new `gen/set_test.go`.

**Deliberately out of scope.** The filter stays `StringComparator` — PRD §7.6 fixes the model
comparator as `comparator.String` because the column is stored as comma-separated text, and the
resulting `[Enum!]!` field / `StringComparator` filter disagreement is identical to what the
PostgreSQL enum array already ships (`declaredCategories` in `graphql/expected/graph/asset_gen.graphqls`).
That belongs to FIX-167. **Correction (2026-08-31):** it does not. FIX-167 fixed columns whose MODEL
comparator was wrong; a SET column's `comparator.String` is correct per §7.6, and only its GraphQL
projection disagrees — the same shape as the enum array. It belongs to FIX-145 / 25.4 / 25.5, and
FIX-167's resolution notes record why.

**Auto-review caught one real regression, fixed before close.** Keying the list projection on
`ColumnContext.IsSet` was wrong: `IsSet` is derived from the SQL type NAME (`context_table.go`:
`input.Resolver.IsSet(col.Type)`), but `type_map.<col>` and `overrides.types` win over the SET branch
in the resolution chain — `gotype.Resolve` steps 1-4 all precede the SET branch at step 4.5, and
`FromLiteral` fills no element type. So a SET column retyped to `string` still carried `IsSet=true`
with no element, and the fix advertised it as `[String!]!` in front of a `string` field while emitting
`models.string(in.Permissions)` in the input translator — a NEW defect on a path that generated
correctly before. Reproduced, then closed: every API-side SET decision now keys on `setElemGoType`,
which reads the RESOLVED `SliceElemType` and is therefore override-aware. Pinned fail-first by
`TestScalarBinding_overriddenSetIsNotListShaped`.

Also from review: the SET **value** type name is now claimed in `resolved_names.go` alongside the set
type. It was never claimed, so a MySQL inline ENUM resolving to `<Set>Value` was a redeclaration
`sqlgen validate` did not see — and this fix would additionally have made it a silent last-write-wins
shadow in `binds.enums`, since the SET entries merge after the enums. Doc drift corrected in
`APIEnumContext.SliceGoTypeName`, `buildEnumGoTypeLookup`, and the `cli/graphql.go` models-merge
block, all of which still described enum arrays as the only list-shaped binding. The new example
tests gained `t.Cleanup` + `HardDelete` (matching `set_test.go`'s convention) so they survive
`-count=2` against one container.

**Also landed:** `warehouses.external_id` (`ksuid.KSUID`) was the only other column blocking the
mysql example's API — it now has a `KSUID` entry under `api.graphql.scalars` plus a `gqlscalars`
package, modelled on the graphql example's `IPAddr`. PRD updated: a §26.4 mapping row for SET (and
one for the enum array, which was also undocumented) and a §7.6 paragraph on the GraphQL projection.

### FIX-170

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-165 gqlgen probe (2026-08-31), confirmed by FIX-165 auto-review

**Issue.** **Routing a column onto gqlgen's bundled `Int64` scalar — the escape hatch the code and
PRD both recommend — emits a create/update translator that does not compile.** A consumer declaring

```yaml
api.graphql.scalars:
  Int64: { go_type: int64, marshaling: builtin }
```

gets `out.X = in.X` where `in.X` is Go `int` and `out.X` is `int64`.

**Root cause.** `marshaling: builtin` means sqlgen merges **no** `models:` entry (`scalarModelPath`
returns `""` for it, `cli/graphql.go`), on the premise that gqlgen already binds the scalar. gqlgen
does — but as an *extraBuiltin* whose model list is `[graphql.Int, graphql.Int64]`, and a GENERATED
position takes `Model[0]`, which is `graphql.Int` → Go `int`. Meanwhile `gqlgenGoTypeFor` returns
`modelGoType` for any scalar that is not one of the four spec names, so it answers `int64`, the two
sides look equal, and `inputCoercionFor` takes the identity arm.

This is the same `Model[0]` rule FIX-165 measured, on a different axis: FIX-165 is about the width a
COLUMN resolves to, this is about the scalar a consumer ROUTES it to.

**Not caught by anything.** `ReservedScalarNames` deliberately leaves `Int64` declarable ("the
supported way to route a column onto them"), and no test or example declares it. The read side is
fine — `graphql.Int64` is in the list, so a bound `int64` field binds — which is why only the input
translator breaks.

**Suggested fix.** `gqlgenGoTypeFor` needs to know gqlgen's extraBuiltins, not just the four spec
scalars: `Int64` → `int`, and the same question should be asked of `Map` / `Upload` / `Any` before
assuming they are sound. With that, `isNumericWidthCast("int", "int64")` is already true and the
existing cast arm handles it. Decide first whether `Int64` should keep being recommended at all —
it is a 64-bit value on a wire type gqlgen types as `int`, so the honest options are "cast and
document the truncation risk" or "withdraw the recommendation and tell consumers to declare an
external scalar". That is a §26.4 call, which is why FIX-165 flagged rather than guessed.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `gqlgenGoTypeFor`, `gqlgenNumericWidthCasts`, and the two
  comments corrected under FIX-165 that used to assert this route worked.
- `cmd/sqlgen/cli/graphql.go` — `scalarModelPath`'s `ScalarMarshalingBuiltin` early return.
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go` — `ReservedScalarNames`, whose doc comment recommends the route.
- `docs/PRD.md` §26.4.1 category 2 (corrected under FIX-165 to record the defect).
- gqlgen v0.17.90 `codegen/config/config.go::injectBuiltins` (`extraBuiltins`).
- FIX-165 (the same `Model[0]` rule on the column-width axis).

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-31. **The suggested fix was measured and withdrawn.** The
entry proposed teaching `gqlgenGoTypeFor` gqlgen's extraBuiltins (`Int64` -> `int`) and letting the
existing `isNumericWidthCast` bridge it. A gqlgen v0.17.90 probe showed a better lever: the
extraBuiltin only applies when NO `models:` entry exists (`injectBuiltins` skips any key
`c.Models.Exists`), so naming the marshaler outright collapses the two-entry list rather than
bridging it. Pinning `Int64: [graphql.Int64]` yields `type FooInput struct { V int64 }` and a single
`unmarshalNInt642int64` -- lossless, symmetric with the read side, platform-independent, and it needs
no cast at all. The cast route would have been asymmetric (read marshals via `graphql.Int64`, write
unmarshals via `graphql.Int`), would have needed the marshaling mode threaded into `gqlgenGoTypeFor`
anyway (a scalar named `Int64` declared `external` DOES get a `models:` entry, so its `Model[0]` is
the model type -- a hardcoded `Int64 -> int` would have broken that config), and rests on a
`Model[0]` ordering that upstream carries a FIXME to change. Pinning removes the ordering dependency
entirely.

*Correction to the entry.* It called this a truncation risk and framed the choice as "cast and
document the truncation" vs "withdraw the recommendation". There is no truncation:
`graphql.UnmarshalInt` is `interfaceToSignedNumber[int]`, and `safeCastSignedNumber` range-checks
`int` only when `strconv.IntSize == 32`. On 64-bit it is byte-identical to `UnmarshalInt64`; on
32-bit it *rejects* with `NumberOverflowError`. The real defect was the non-compiling assignment, and
the real cost of the cast route was a platform-dependent wire contract.

*Shipped.* `config.gqlgenBundledScalars` (scalar -> {qualified Go type -> marshaler symbol}) records
`injectBuiltins`' `extraBuiltins`, with `canonicalGoType` folding the `interface{}` spelling onto
`any` so one type has one key, plus `GqlgenBundlesScalar` / `GqlgenBundledMarshalerPath` /
`GqlgenBundledGoTypes` / `GqlgenBundledScalarNames`. Keys are the qualified short form
(`QualifiedGoType`), which is what reconciles the two call sites: `scalarModelPath` sees the COLUMN's
spelling (`time.Time`) while `validateScalarBinding` sees the config's full path -- the same
convention `BuiltInScalarGoTypes` already uses. `cli/graphql.go::scalarModelPath` returns
`GqlgenBundledMarshalerPath(s.Name, s.GoType)` in place of its `""` early return.
`gen/context_api.go` is comment-only apart from `gqlgenGraphQLPkg` becoming an alias of
`config.GqlgenGraphQLPkg`, so the two tables cannot drift onto different packages -- `gqlgenGoTypeFor`,
`inputCoercionFor` and `dictatedInputGoType` are untouched, because the premise they encode ("every
non-spec scalar binds gqlgen to the model's own Go type through the merged `models:` entry") is now
true by construction rather than by luck.

*Scope: two sibling holes closed with it.* Both are the same defect class and both were silent, so
`validateBuiltinScalarBinding` rejects them at `sqlgen validate` rather than at `go build` on
generated code. (1) `marshaling: builtin` on a name gqlgen does not bundle -- probed, and gqlgen
silently binds the scalar to `string`: `type FooInput struct { V string }` plus
`panic("not implemented: V - v")`, the exact FIX-151 shape. (2) `marshaling: builtin` on a bundled
name whose marshaler cannot carry the declared `go_type` (the `Map` / `Upload` / `Any` question the
entry asked). Those three have SINGLE-entry model lists, so `Model[0]` IS their Go type -- they are
sound when `go_type` matches and take `inputCoercionFor`'s loud `default:` arm when it does not,
which is why only `Int64`, the one multi-entry list, failed silently. An entry with no `go_type`
stays legal: it establishes no binding, reaches no column, and the unresolved-declaration warning
already covers it.

*Regression pins, all verified fail-first.*
`TestBuildMergeInput_BuiltinScalarPinsTheBundledMarshaler` replaces
`TestBuildMergeInput_BuiltinScalarGetsNoEntry`, which asserted the rule backwards -- that `builtin`
emits no binding. It covers both a consumer-declared bundled scalar (`Int64`) and a registry-owned
one (`Time`); reverting `scalarModelPath` drops both keys from the merge. `Time` is pinned alongside
`Int64` precisely because it is the case that made the old rule look sound.
`TestScalarBinding_bundledRegistryEntriesPinAGqlgenMarshaler` asserts over the REGISTRY, not a
literal list, so a second `marshaling: builtin` entry cannot be added without the table growing to
match. `TestValidatePreParse_ScalarBinding` gains both rejection arms plus the two `interface{}`
spellings. `TestScalarBinding_int64ScalarSuppressesSelfConversion` keeps its assertions unchanged --
the identity arm was always the right output; what changed is that the other side is now `int64`.

*PRD.* §26.4.1 category 2 rewritten: `builtin` now means "gqlgen ships the marshaler AND sqlgen pins
the `models:` entry to it", with both validation preconditions and the no-`go_type` carve-out stated.
The `Time` registry row and the "Additions, not overrides" sentence recommending the route are
corrected to match. No config surface change -- `ScalarBinding` is untouched.

*Verification.* `make check` clean across all modules under `-race` (6:2x; `cmd/sqlgen/cli` ~506s,
`cmd/sqlgen/gen` ~193s), zero lint. `TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean with **zero golden churn**, which is
the load-bearing evidence for the "emit uniformly" decision: `Time` now gets an explicit
`[graphql.Time]` entry where it previously rode `injectBuiltins`, and the generated output is
byte-identical because the two are the same string. `make check-examples` clean.

*Was left open, deliberately; closed 2026-09-01 by FIX-169.* No module compiled this route -- the
defect was "the generated module does not compile", and unit tests cannot prove that. Declaring it
in an existing example was not a cheap add: `api.graphql.scalars` is keyed by Go TYPE, so
`Int64: {go_type: int64}` retypes every `int64` column in the module, which in both API-enabled
examples meant the `categories` BIGSERIAL PK and the `category_id` FKs -- rippling into PK resolver
args, cursors, filter inputs, relationship loaders and connection edges. The dedicated module
FIX-169 called for is `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql_null_wrappers`, which declares this
scalar over a schema built for that blast radius; `tests/bundled_scalar_test.go` pins both the
losslessness past 2^53 and, via introspection, that the declaration is actually taken.

*Auto-review follow-ups, all applied inline.* (1) `scalarModelPath`'s summary paragraph still said
`builtin` scalars need no merge entry, naming `time.Time` as the example — the exact claim this fix
disproves, and a contradiction with the new Builtin bullet three lines below. (2) The no-`go_type`
carve-out justified itself with "the unresolved-declaration warning covers it", which is false:
`unusedScalarWarnings` skips `declared[name].GoType == ""`, so a typo'd bare `builtin` entry is
INERT, not diagnosed. Corrected in all three places the claim was written (PRD, `validate.go`, the
test comment) to say what actually holds — it binds nothing, which is why it is left alone. (3)
`docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL.md` still carried the pre-fix category-2 bullet ("No sqlgen-side work") and the
unpinned `Time` row; both brought in line with §26.4.1. (4) `Upload` is the only bundled key that is
package-qualified, so it is the only one whose lookup depends on `QualifiedGoType` collapsing the
import path — pinned with a new validation case. The review also found that validation and
generation can spell that key differently: config computes `QualifiedGoType(import, name)` while a
column carries the `overrides.types.<t>.type` literal verbatim (`gotype.FromLiteral`), so
`{type: "gqlgraphql.Upload", import: ".../gqlgen/graphql"}` validates as `graphql.Upload` and
arrives at `scalarModelPath` spelled otherwise. Benign — gqlgen's single-entry `Upload` extraBuiltin
then applies and yields the identical binding — but the comment claiming "empty only for a pair
validation rejects" overstated it and now records the gap.

*Gqlgen version coupling.* The table encodes v0.17.90's `injectBuiltins`. sqlgen pins no minimum
gqlgen version, so a bump means re-checking that `extraBuiltins` has not gained a scalar or changed a
marshaler's Go type. Pinning does remove the `Model[0]` ORDERING dependency FIX-165 has to re-check
-- there is no list order left to depend on -- and a scalar gqlgen drops entirely fails loudly at
generate time via the new name check rather than silently degrading.

### FIX-165

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-151 auto-review (2026-08-28). Scope widened and both suggested fixes
  withdrawn after an empirical gqlgen probe (2026-08-31).

**Issue.** **A column whose model Go type gqlgen has no binding for breaks the API on one of two
axes, and only one of them is loud.** The original entry saw the loud half:

- *Write side.* `smallint[]` / `integer[]` / `bigint[]` / `real[]` with `api.graphql` enabled fail
  generation. gqlgen emits `[]int` for a `[Int!]!` input field, the model resolves to `[]int32`,
  and Go has no conversion between slices of differing element types.
- *Read side (folded in here 2026-08-31).* `int8`, `int16`, `uint`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`,
  `uint64` and `float32` — **scalar columns, not just arrays** — bind to nothing on the row struct,
  so gqlgen silently emits a `panic("not implemented")` field resolver. No error, no log line. A
  PostgreSQL `smallint` or `real` column, or any MySQL unsigned column, already ships a broken read
  surface today with no array in sight.

The two halves are one axis and are fixed by one pair of levers, which is why they are one entry.

FIX-151's class table above tabulates only the Go type gqlgen emits for a **generated input
object**, which is the half FIX-147 / FIX-148 fixed; its first two rows now carry "read side
**BROKEN (C)**" and defer here. Concretely reachable: PostgreSQL `smallint` (`int16`) and `real` /
`float4` (`float32`); MySQL `tinyint` (`int8`), `smallint` (`int16`), `float` (`float32`),
`int unsigned` (`uint32`) and `bigint unsigned` (`uint64`). SQLite is unaffected — it maps
`smallint` to `int64` and `real` to `float64`, both of which gqlgen binds.

**Measured, not inferred.** Against gqlgen v0.17.90 (the pinned version), a bound row struct whose
fields carry each width, schema `Int!` / `[Int!]!` / `Float!` / `[Float!]!`:

| model Go type | read side | model Go type | read side |
|---|---|---|---|
| `int`, `int32`, `int64` | bound | `[]int`, `[]int32`, `[]int64` | bound |
| `int8`, `int16` | **panic stub** | `[]int8`, `[]int16` | **panic stub** |
| `uint`, `uint8/16/32/64` | **panic stub** | `[]uint…` | **panic stub** |
| `float64` | bound | `[]float64` | bound |
| `float32` | **panic stub** | `[]float32` | **panic stub** |

**Root cause.** `codegen/config/config.go::injectBuiltins` binds `Int` to exactly `graphql.Int` /
`Int32` / `Int64` and `Float` to exactly `graphql.FloatContext`, and
`internal/code/compare.go::CompatibleTypes` requires an **exact** basic-kind match. That single
fact has two consequences:

- A *generated* type (the create/update input objects) takes `Model[0]` — `int` / `float64` —
  because `Binder.TypeReference` is called with a nil bind target. Hence `[]int` vs `[]int32`.
- A *bound* type (the row struct) whose field matches no entry in the list falls through
  `TypeReference`'s loop; `codegen/field.go::buildField` swallows the error into
  `f.IsResolver = true`. Hence the panic stub. This path is outside the wrapper's Query/Mutation
  stub rewriter, so nothing downstream catches it.

The prior root-cause claim — that the bridge "would have to be an element-wise loop and
`templates/api/input_translate.go.tmpl` has no shape for one" — is **wrong**. No translator change
is needed at all; the disagreement is removable at its source. Both previously-suggested fixes are
withdrawn: an element-wise loop would leave the read side broken for `smallint[]` / `real[]`
(turning a named codegen error into silently-broken output), and binding narrowed arrays to a
width-specific scalar would change the emitted `.graphqls` for array columns only, leaving the same
SQL type projecting as `Int` when scalar and `Int32` when array.

**Fix — two levers, both verified end-to-end.**

*Lever A — read side. Append sqlgen-owned marshaler anchors to the `Int` / `Float` `models:` lists.*
sqlgen emits `MarshalInt8` / `MarshalInt16` / `MarshalUint…` / `MarshalFloat32` (+ `Unmarshal…`)
into `scalars_gen.go` — the same category-4 external-marshaler anchor shape `scalarModelPath`
already produces — and `buildMergeInput` merges:

```yaml
Int:   {model: [graphql.Int, graphql.Int32, graphql.Int64, <resolver>.Int16, <resolver>.Uint32, …]}
Float: {model: [graphql.FloatContext, <resolver>.Float32]}
```

gqlgen's own entries must be restated first, because `injectBuiltins` skips any key already present
and because `Model[0]` is what generated input objects bind to — putting a narrowed width first
would retype every `Int` input field in the schema. Emit the block **only when a narrowed width is
actually in use**, so the restatement (and its coupling to gqlgen's defaults) reaches only the
schemas that need it. `mergeModels` already yields to a consumer-declared `Int:` key (§26.5.6).

Side benefit: the range check lands in sqlgen's `Unmarshal` function. Today an out-of-range `Int`
wraps silently through the width cast.

*Lever B — write side. Dictate the input field's Go type via `models.<Type>.fields.<f>.type`.*
gqlgen's `TypeMapField.Type` overrides the Go type of a **generated** field, leaving the `.graphqls`
untouched. `APIGoFieldOverrides` already emits a `models.Create<T>Input.fields.<f>` /
`models.Update<T>Input.fields.<f>` node carrying `fieldName` for every input field (FIX-152), so
this writes a second key into a node that already exists — `wrapper.MergeInput.ModelFields` widens
from `map[string]map[string]string` to a two-field struct value, and `mergeModelFields` emits
`type:` alongside `fieldName:`. `gqlgenInputGoType` then returns the model's own `[]T` for a slice
column on a spec numeric built-in, so `inputCoercionFor` takes the **identity** arm. The
`case col.IsSlice:` error arm becomes unreachable for numeric arrays and stays for everything else.

Order matters: Lever B alone is **not** sufficient. Applied to `[]int16` / `[]float32` without
Lever A, gqlgen accepts the override and then falls back to an **input-object field resolver**
(`ProbeInputResolver.A16(ctx, obj, data []int) error`) — another panic stub. Lever B alone closes
only `integer[]` and `bigint[]`, the two widths gqlgen ships a marshaler for.

**Verification performed (2026-08-31).** Five scratch modules, real `gqlgen generate` + `go build`
against v0.17.90. Lever A alone: every panic stub gone, generated input types unchanged
(`int` / `float64` / `[]int`). Lever B alone: `[Int!]!` → `[]int32`, `[Int!]` → `[]int32`
(omitempty), `Int!` → `int32`, schema unchanged — and the `[]int16` / `[]float32` input-resolver
fallback above. Both together: **zero** field-resolver stubs, input arrays typed `[]int16` /
`[]int32` / `[]float32` / `[]uint32` matching the model exactly, scalar input fields still `int` /
`float64` so the FIX-147 / FIX-148 width cast keeps running unchanged, `.graphqls` byte-identical,
build clean.

**Adjacent defect found by the same probe, not yet fixed.** `context_api.go:2643` documents
retyping `int64` onto "the gqlgen-bundled `Int64`" via `api.graphql.scalars`. gqlgen's `Int64`
extraBuiltin is `[graphql.Int, graphql.Int64]`, so a generated input field typed `Int64` comes out
as `int` while `gqlgenGoTypeFor` returns `int64` for any non-spec scalar name — the identity arm
emits `out.X = in.X`, which does not compile. Lever B fixes it incidentally if the `type:` override
is emitted for consumer-declared scalars too; otherwise the doc-comment's advice must be withdrawn.

**Why no example caught either half.** Both API-enabled examples (`graphql`,
`graphql_top_level`) are PostgreSQL. Between them there is no `REAL` column at all, and the sole
`SMALLINT` — `scalar_probes.small_count` — is nullable and retyped onto `sql.NullInt16`, a registry
scalar bound to its own Go type, so it never resolves to `int16` against `Int`. Unsigned widths are
MySQL-only and no MySQL example has an `api:` block. No module anywhere exposes a bare `int16`,
`float32` or unsigned column to the API — see FIX-169.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `inputCoercionFor`'s `case col.IsSlice` arm, `gqlgenGoTypeFor`,
  `gqlgenInputGoType`, `gqlgenNumericWidthCasts`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_field_overrides.go` — `APIGoFieldOverrides`, where Lever B's `type:` hangs.
- `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/merge.go` — `MergeInput.ModelFields`, `mergeModelFields`, `mergeModels`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/cli/graphql.go` — `buildMergeInput`, `scalarModelPath` (Lever A's anchor shape).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_scalar_binding_test.go` —
  `TestScalarBinding_numericArrayIsRejectedWithAnActionableMessage` pins the message that goes away;
  `TestScalarBinding_everyBuiltInGoTypeResolves` asserts the input-side invariant only and needs a
  read-side twin (model Go type ∈ the scalar's gqlgen model list).
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/postgres/schema.sql` — `scores INTEGER[]`, invisible because that
  example has no API.
- gqlgen v0.17.90 `codegen/config/config.go::injectBuiltins`, `codegen/config/binder.go::
  TypeReference`, `internal/code/compare.go::CompatibleTypes`, `codegen/field.go::buildField`.
- PRD §26.4.1. FIX-151 (the class; its table's first two rows are input-side only), FIX-147 /
  FIX-148 (the scalar width casts, unchanged by this), FIX-169 (the missing example coverage).

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-31. Both levers shipped; the GraphQL schema is unchanged
and no existing `.graphqls` moved a byte.

*What the probe changed about the plan.* The entry proposed sqlgen-emitted `Marshal<Width>` pairs
for every unbound width. Probing gqlgen v0.17.90 directly showed that is unnecessary for all but
one: `graphql/int.go` already ships `MarshalInt8` / `MarshalInt16` and `graphql/uint.go` the entire
unsigned family, complete with `NumberOverflowError` / `UintSignError` range checking. They are
simply absent from `injectBuiltins`' `Int` list, so nothing ever reaches them. Naming them in the
list is the whole fix for seven of the eight widths — sqlgen emits no code and inherits gqlgen's own
overflow behaviour rather than reimplementing it. `float32` is the sole width gqlgen has no
marshaler for anywhere, so that one pair is emitted into `scalars_gen.go`.

*Lever A — read side.* `numericWidthAnchor` (`gen/context_api.go`) resolves the anchor a column's
model Go type needs, keyed on the ELEMENT so an array and its scalar sibling ask for the same one;
`collectNumericWidthScalars` dedupes them onto `APIContext.NumericWidthScalars`.
`cli/graphql.go::numericWidthModels` turns that into the `models:` entries, restating gqlgen's own
paths first (`Model[0]` is what every GENERATED position binds to, so a narrowed width in front
would retype every `Int` input field and truncate a bigint). The key is written only when a
narrowed width is actually in use, so a schema that needs none leaves gqlgen's builtins untouched —
pinned by `TestBuildMergeInput_FIX165_NoAnchorsLeavesSpecScalarsAlone`.

*Lever B — write side.* `dictatedInputGoType` decides when sqlgen states the generated input
field's Go type outright; `APIInputField.GqlgenGoType` carries it to `APIGoFieldOverrides`, and
`wrapper.MergeInput.ModelFields` widened from `map[string]map[string]string` to a `ModelField`
struct so `type:` lands on the same node as `fieldName:` (FIX-152's key) rather than a second one.
Precedence is now per KEY: a consumer who named a field keeps their `fieldName` and still receives
sqlgen's `type`, and vice versa. `inputCoercionFor`'s `case col.IsSlice` error arm survives for
non-numeric element disagreements and is simply unreachable for the four types this entry named.

*Ordering is load-bearing and was verified, not assumed.* Lever B alone on `[]int16` / `[]float32`
does not fail — gqlgen accepts the override and then falls back to an input-object field RESOLVER
(`ProbeInputResolver.A16(ctx, obj, data []int) error`), a second panic stub in place of the first.
Lever B alone closes only `integer[]` and `bigint[]`.

*What is deliberately NOT changed.* The SCALAR numeric case keeps gqlgen's `int` / `float64` input
type and the FIX-147 / FIX-148 conversion. It is sound and tested, and dictating it too would churn
every numeric input field in every consumer's schema to buy nothing. The consequence is a real
asymmetry, recorded here: an out-of-range value in an `smallint[]` element is now REJECTED by
`graphql.UnmarshalInt16`, while the same value in a scalar `smallint` column still wraps silently
through the cast. Pinned both ways by `TestNumericWidths_OverflowIsRejected`.

*Example coverage.* `numeric_widths` in the graphql example — bare `int16` / `float32` on both
nullabilities plus `smallint[]` / `integer[]` / `bigint[]` / `real[]` and a nullable `integer[]`,
with no table-scoped overrides so the columns reach the bare Go widths (`scalar_probes` retypes its
nullable columns onto the `database/sql` wrappers, which is exactly what hid the `int16` case
there). `tests/numeric_widths_test.go` round-trips every one through the live gqlgen handler and a
real PostgreSQL, re-reading through a separate query so the MARSHAL side runs on a value loaded
from the database. Values sit at their type boundaries (`math.MaxInt16`, `math.MinInt16`, 2^53+1
through `[Int!]!`) so a wrong binding truncates visibly instead of passing by luck. The generated
`NumericWidth` object type carries **no** field resolvers and there is no `NumericWidthInputResolver`
— that absence is the read-side fix, observed in gqlgen's real output.

*Regression pins.* `TestScalarBinding_everyReadableGoTypeBindsOrAnchors` is the read-side twin the
entry asked for and the assertion whose absence let this survive from phase 16: for every dialect ×
nullability × `use_pointers`, an API-readable column's model Go type must be one gqlgen binds or
carry an anchor. Verified fail-first — stubbing `numericWidthAnchor` reproduces exactly the widths
the gqlgen probe flagged: postgres `int2` / `smallint` (`int16`) and `float4` / `real` (`float32`);
mysql `tinyint` (`int8`), `smallint` and `year` (`int16`), `float` (`float32`), `int unsigned`
(`uint32`) and `bigint unsigned` (`uint64`). SQLite is unaffected — it maps `smallint` → `int64` and
`real` → `float64`, both of which gqlgen binds.
`TestScalarBinding_numericArrayIsRejectedWithAnActionableMessage` is replaced by
`TestScalarBinding_numericArrayDictatesItsInputGoType` (identity arm, no cast) and
`..._numericArrayAnchorsItsElementWidth`.

`TestNumericWidthScalarsFileCompilesWithoutCategory4Scalars` covers the one shape no example can
reach: a module needing the `float32` pair but declaring no category-4 scalar. `scalars_gen.go` was
previously emitted only when `ExternalScalars` was non-empty, so its four-import preamble was always
justified by a UUID or Decimal body; the Float32 pair alone uses three of them, and every example in
the repo carries a uuid PK or a numeric column. The test runs the real emission path (template →
`WrapWithPreamble` → `Format`) and asserts every surviving import is referenced — the invariant, not
"`fmt` is absent", so it does not go stale if the body later grows a `fmt.Errorf`. Verified
fail-first by swapping `Format` for `FormatOnly`, which skips goimports' pruning.

*PRD.* §26.4.1 gains a "Numeric width binding" subsection: the `Int` / `Float` registry row now
distinguishes generated positions (take `Model[0]`, bridged by a conversion) from bound positions
(exact match required, silent panic resolver otherwise), and states the array rule. No config
surface and no schema change, so nothing else in §26.4 or §26.5 moved.

*Still open, deliberately not fixed here.* The escape hatch documented at `context_api.go` —
retyping `int64` onto "the gqlgen-bundled `Int64`" via `api.graphql.scalars` — is broken by the same
`Model[0]` rule: gqlgen's `Int64` extraBuiltin is `[graphql.Int, graphql.Int64]`, so the generated
input field is `int` while `gqlgenGoTypeFor` returns `int64` for any non-spec scalar name, and the
identity arm emits a non-compiling `out.X = in.X`. It is a different axis (consumer-declared scalar
routing, not column width resolution), has no test or example coverage, and the right wire semantics
for a lossy `Int64` are a §26.4 decision rather than an implementation detail — so it is flagged
rather than guessed at, and is now logged as **FIX-170**. MySQL's unsigned and `int8` widths reach a
real `models:` list only in `TestBuildMergeInput_FIX165_UnsignedAnchors`, not in any example — no
MySQL module has an `api:` block, which remains FIX-169. **Correction (2026-09-01):** the MySQL
example gained its `api:` block under FIX-166 (2026-08-31), and FIX-169 closed the rest.

*Auto-review follow-ups, all applied.* The two comments in `context_api.go` that still asserted the
`Int64` route worked are corrected and now point at FIX-170, as is PRD §26.4.1 category 2. The
unspellable-anchor path no longer degrades in silence: `buildMergeInput` returns warnings and
`runGraphQLGen` prints them, pinned by `TestBuildMergeInput_FIX165_UnspellableAnchorWarns` — it is
not the same fail-soft as `scalarModelPath`, because `generateAPIScalarFile` still emits the
`float32` body, leaving a marshaler nothing anchors. `TestNumericWidths_OverflowIsRejected` now
asserts the error text names the out-of-range value and that no row was written, rather than merely
that something failed. The `numericWidthModels` doc comment no longer claims the E2E example catches
any gqlgen default drift: it catches a REMOVED path loudly (`FindObject` errors), but an added entry
or a reordered `Model[0]` would leave anchored schemas frozen on the stale order while everything
still compiles — upstream carries a FIXME to default `Int` to `int32`, and sqlgen pins no minimum
gqlgen version, so a bump means re-checking that map by hand.

### FIX-168

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 6, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** building the FIX-151 shape-B example fixture (2026-08-29)

**Issue.** **`overrides.use_pointers: false` emits a models package that does not compile.** Every
nullable column of a `nullSQL` type resolves to a `database/sql` wrapper, so the generated file
imports `database/sql` — which binds the package name `sql`, the name sqlgen's own runtime package
(`github.com/teandresmith/sqlgen/sql`) already claims. The runtime import never lands and every
reference to it goes undefined.

Probed on the `postgres` example — no API, no GraphQL, 18 tables — by appending four lines to its
`sqlgen.yml` (`overrides: use_pointers: false`), regenerating, and building:

```
models/models_gen.go:3141:21: undefined: sql.Dialect
models/models_gen.go:3142:21: undefined: sql.Table
models/models_gen.go:6427:37: undefined: sql.Sort
models/models_gen.go:11593:24: undefined: sql.Dialect
```

Every other import resolves (`comparator`, `database`, `omittable`, `types`, the example's own
`customtypes`); `github.com/teandresmith/sqlgen/sql` is the only one missing, and `database/sql` is the
only one added. `sqlgen generate` reports success — nothing in the pipeline compiles the models
package unless `api.graphql` is enabled — which is why this has never surfaced.

**Root cause.** `resolvePackageImports` (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/format.go:33`) seeds the import block with
the contexts' declared imports and lets goimports resolve the remainder against the module. The
seed carries `database/sql` (contributed by the column Go types); goimports will not add a second
package named `sql`, so `sql.Dialect` / `sql.Table` / `sql.Sort` / `sql.Condition` / `sql.Build*`
all resolve against `database/sql` and vanish. Seeding both paths does not help: two unaliased
imports named `sql` in one file is itself a compile error. Whichever package is aliased, its
qualifier in the generated body has to change with it.

**Scope.** Any dialect, any driver, any layout, API or not. `file_per_table` does not escape it —
the row struct and the table client that uses `sql.Dialect` land in the same file. It is not
confined to `use_pointers`: `overrides.types.<t>.nullable: {type: sql.NullString, import:
database/sql}`, `column_map.<col>.type`, and a `type_map` literal all reach the same collision.
No existing example imports `database/sql` in its models package, which is exactly why the defect
is invisible to the suite.

**Suggested fix — a decision, not an edit.**
- *Alias `database/sql` in generated output* (`stdsql "database/sql"`, fields spelled
  `stdsql.NullString`). Smallest body-side surface: the `sql.` qualifier from `database/sql`
  appears only in the null-wrapper type names, which come from a handful of `gotype.go` constants
  plus config-supplied `nullable:` values. Ripples into `knownWrapperExtractions` keys,
  `builtInScalarRegistry` keys, `config.BuiltInScalarGoTypes`, the PRD tables, and needs a
  normalization step so a consumer writing `nullable: sql.NullString` still works. Zero golden
  churn — no current golden imports `database/sql`.
- *Alias the sqlgen runtime package everywhere* (`sqlgensql "github.com/teandresmith/sqlgen/sql"`).
  Mechanical and permanent, but touches every template site that says `sql.` and churns every
  golden in the repo.
- *Stop emitting `database/sql`* — give the runtime its own wrappers (`types.NullString`, …) and
  resolve `use_pointers: false` onto those. Removes the collision by construction; changes what
  §4.7 documents the setting to mean.
- Whichever is chosen, the general shape is collision-aware import resolution (an import whose base
  name collides with one sqlgen already claims gets an alias, and the qualifier is rewritten with
  it). `database/sql` is the only collision reachable today; `hook`, `types` and `database` are the
  same hazard waiting on a consumer import path that ends in one of those names.

**Blocks.** The shape-B half of FIX-151's example coverage. The fixture is written — a
`scalar_probes` table in the `graphql` example plus a table-scoped `overrides.types` block landing
all seven wrappers on one table without flipping the module-wide `use_pointers` — and fails
generation with this collision at the gqlgen validation build.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/format.go:33` (`resolvePackageImports`), `:62` (`WrapWithPreamble`),
  `:134` (`imports.Process`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go:523-547`, `:568-584` (import collection per layout),
  `:738` (`deduplicateImports`, which dedupes by path and cannot see a name collision).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go:68-79` (`null:` / `nullImp:` on the `nullSQL` typeInfos),
  `:895-912` (`maybeRegisterWrapper`), `knownWrapperExtractions`.
- PRD §4.7 line 505 (`use_pointers`), §11 lines 1549 / 1612 / 1972 (documented behavior at
  `use_pointers: false`).
- FIX-151 (registers the seven `sql.NullX` scalars this makes unreachable in practice),
  FIX-169 (the missing `use_pointers: false` module that would have caught it).

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-29. Two independent compile failures, both reached only
by a Go type no example produced.

*The import collision.* Generated files now import `database/sql` as `stdsql`
(`generatedImportAliases`, applied by `WrapWithPreamble`), and `aliasStdSQLQualifiers` rewrites
the qualifier of every `sql.Null…` selector to match. The alias falls on `database/sql` rather than
on the runtime package because the runtime qualifier is the one the templates spell, at 211 sites.
`sql.Null…` is unambiguous: the runtime `sql` package exports no identifier beginning with "Null",
and a `sql.Where("x").IsNull()` chain has a call expression rather than the `sql` identifier on the
left of the selector. The rewrite splices the identifier's bytes at AST-reported offsets instead of
reprinting the file, so everything the templates positioned survives byte-for-byte, and it is
skipped entirely for a file that does not import `database/sql` — which is every generated file in
every example today, and why the goldens did not churn.

**The alias is a property of generated files only.** The Go type sqlgen *names* is still
`sql.NullString` in `overrides.types.<type>.nullable`, in `builtInScalarRegistry`, in
`knownWrapperExtractions` and in the manifest's published `go_type` — verified against
`scalar_probe.json`, which reads `"go_type": "sql.NullString"` — because that is what a consumer
importing `database/sql` themselves would write. Keeping identity and rendering separate is what
kept this from rippling into the config surface, the scalar registry keys and the docs.

*The comparator classification.* `resolveComparatorType` reads through the wrapper via the new
`gotype.StdNullUnderlying`, so a nullable `double precision` column takes
`comparator.NullableNumber[float64]` instead of the `[sql.NullFloat64]` that does not satisfy
`comparator.Numeric`. That was the compile error; the same normalization also fixes two silent
mis-classifications the wrapper caused — `sql.NullBool` and `sql.NullTime` were falling through
`resolveSimpleComparator`'s default arm to a **string** comparator. The table maps each wrapper to
its own value-field type, not to the SQL types that resolve to it: `smallint` and `tinyint` both
land on `sql.NullInt16` and `real` on `sql.NullFloat64`, so the inverse of gotype's mapping tables
is ambiguous where the wrapper's field type is not.

**Verified by generating and compiling, which is the check that was missing.** `use_pointers: false`
appended to the `postgres` (18 tables, 3 views, pgx), `mysql` and `sqlite` examples in turn:
before, `go build ./models/` failed with `undefined: sql.Dialect` / `sql.Table` / `sql.Sort` and
then with `sql.NullFloat64 does not satisfy comparator.Numeric`; after, all three compile clean.
The probes were reverted. Their own hand-written tests cannot run under the flag — they are written
against `*T` — which is a fact about the examples, not about the fix.

**Tests.** `cmd/sqlgen/gen/std_null_wrappers_test.go`:
`TestStdNullWrappers_generatedFileImportsBothSQLPackages` (a body referencing both packages by the
same qualifier — the row-struct-plus-client shape — asserting both imports land, the alias applies,
and the runtime qualifier is left alone); `TestStdNullWrappers_fileWithoutDatabaseSQLIsUntouched`
(the no-churn guarantee); `TestStdNullWrappers_comparatorClassifiesByUnderlyingType` (all seven
wrappers, each expecting the comparator its `use_pointers: true` twin resolves to);
`TestStdNullUnderlying`. **Verified failing-first** with the production files reverted: the import
test failed on all three assertions and six of the seven comparator subtests failed with their
pre-fix values (`NullableNumber[sql.NullInt16]`, `NullableString` for bool and time). The
`sql.NullString` subtest passed pre-fix — it already landed on `NullableString` through the default
arm — which is what a parity test should say.

**Example coverage.** The `scalar_probes` fixture that surfaced this landed with it; see FIX-151's
resolution notes. `make check` clean across all 33 modules; `make check-examples` clean across all
13; goldens byte-identical outside the `graphql` example, which gains the fixture.

**PRD amended.** §7.3 gains two paragraphs: generated files alias `database/sql` (and the Go type
sqlgen names does not move), and a Null wrapper is classified by the type it wraps.

### FIX-151

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** exhaustive audit of the FIX-147/FIX-148 bug class (2026-08-26)
- **Rewritten:** 2026-08-28 after an evidence pass corrected the root cause, widened the class,
  and settled the two open design questions. See "Revision note" at the end for what changed and why.

**Issue.** **`sqlgen generate` emits non-compiling create/update input translators, and in one
configuration a silently-wrong read schema, for every column whose resolved Go type has no GraphQL
binding.** FIX-147 (integer widths) and FIX-148 (`float32`) each fixed one member of this class by
adding an entry to a hand-maintained predicate. The class has no fixed membership — the set of
reachable Go types is a function of config (`overrides.use_pointers`, `overrides.types`,
`type_map`), not of `gotype.go`'s tables — so it cannot be closed by enumeration.

Two distinct failure shapes:

*Shape A — hard generation failure.* Any column resolving to `[]byte`, `time.Duration`, `net.IP`,
`net.IPNet` or `net.HardwareAddr` emits a translator that does not compile. `[]byte` is the severe
one: `bytea` on PostgreSQL, `blob` / `binary` / `varbinary` / `tinyblob` / `mediumblob` /
`longblob` on MySQL, `blob` on SQLite. Confirmed end-to-end against the real `graphql` example with
`sqlgen generate` + gqlgen v0.17.90:

```
input_translate_gen.go:231:16: cannot use omittable.Set(in.Payload) (value of struct type
    omittable.Value[string]) as omittable.Value[[]byte] value in assignment
input_translate_gen.go:232:13: cannot use omittable.Set(in.Dur) (omittable.Value[*string])
    as omittable.Value[*"time".Duration] value in assignment
input_translate_gen.go:235:14: cannot use omittable.Set(*in.Addr) (omittable.Value[string])
    as omittable.Value[net.IP] value in assignment
input_translate_gen.go:238:18: cannot use omittable.Set(in.NetBlock) (omittable.Value[*string])
    as omittable.Value[*net.IPNet] value in assignment
Error: gqlgen subprocess failed ... exit status 1
```

*Shape B — silently-wrong schema, at much larger scale.* Under `overrides.use_pointers: false`
(documented, PRD §4.7 line 505; default `true`) every nullable column of every `nullSQL` type
resolves to a `database/sql.NullX` wrapper, none of which is registered. Probed against a plain
fixture (`gen.BuildAPIContext`, postgres, `use_pointers: false`):

```
FIELD description  gql=String     model=sql.NullString
FIELD stock        gql=String     model=sql.NullInt32
FIELD active       gql=String     model=sql.NullBool
FIELD ratio        gql=String     model=sql.NullFloat64
FIELD created_at   gql=String     model=sql.NullTime

out.Description = omittable.Set(*in.Description)   // string -> sql.NullString, does not compile
```

Shape B needs no exotic column — any nullable `text` column does it — and the emitted **schema**
is wrong before the translator ever fails to compile: a nullable `integer` is advertised to clients
as `String`, a nullable `boolean` as `String`. The prior revision of this entry asserted the class
was "a hard generation failure, not silently-wrong output". That is true of Shape A only.

**Root cause.** Not the fallthrough itself. The fallthrough is the *symptom* of four independent
derivations of one fact — *what Go type will gqlgen emit for this field?* — none of which is
reconciled against the others, and one of which is already complete and correct but used in only
one place:

| Site | Answers | State |
|---|---|---|
| `gqlgenPKArgGoType` (`context_api.go:1202`) | GraphQL scalar → gqlgen Go type | **complete and correct** — but reached only from `buildAPIPKArgs`, for PK resolver arguments |
| `isNarrowedNumericGoType` (`context_api.go:2035`) | which model Go types need a cast | hand-list; grew by one entry in FIX-147, one more in FIX-148 |
| `GqlgenIsBareNullable` (`context_api.go:2001`) | which gqlgen Go types are Go-nilable | hand-list (`col.IsSlice`, `json.RawMessage`, `types.JSON`) |
| `graphQLTypeForGoType` fallthrough (`context_api.go:2392`) | everything unrecognised → `String` | silent |

`inputCoercionFor` never consults `gqlgenPKArgGoType`. It re-derives the same fact by guessing from
the *model* type. Had it instead asked "gqlgen emits X, the model wants Y, are they the same?",
FIX-147, FIX-148 and every member of this entry would have been one condition. That is why the class
yields one FIX per member: each member is a missing entry in a list, and the invariant those lists
are approximating is written down nowhere.

**Correction to the prior root-cause claim (`[]byte`).** The prior revision stated that
`graphQLTypeForGoType` "sends `[]byte` to `String` via its explicit case". It does not.
`mapColumnToGraphQL` (`context_api.go:2051`) computes `stripPointerAndSlice(col.GoType)` first,
which reduces `[]byte` to `byte`, so `case "[]byte":` (`context_api.go:2377`) is **dead code** and
`[]byte` reaches the same unknown-type fallthrough as the other four. Verified by instrumenting the
fallthrough: it logs `goType="byte" sqlType="bytea"`. This matters operationally — the prior
revision's own suggested fix (add `"[]byte"` to `builtInScalarRegistry`) **would silently fail to
match**, because the lookup key at that point is `byte`. The `[]` strip is correct only for
PostgreSQL array columns, where `context_api.go:2085` re-applies the `[...]` wrapper under
`col.IsSlice`; nothing re-applies it for `bytea`. The same unconditional strip is present at
`context_api.go:1480` (the PK-arg path), with the same latent defect.

**Complete class, by failure shape.** `inputCoercionFor` keys on the bare Go type and is
dialect-independent, so this is exhaustive over the Go types reachable from `gotype.go`'s tables
**at both settings of `use_pointers`** — which is the axis the prior revision's table omitted.

| Go type | Reached from | GraphQL today | gqlgen Go | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `int8/16/32/64`, `uint/8/16/32/64` | integer columns | `Int` | `int` | input fixed — FIX-147; read side **BROKEN (C)**, see FIX-165 |
| `float32` | `real`, `float4`, MySQL `float` | `Float` | `float64` | input fixed — FIX-148; read side **BROKEN (C)**, see FIX-165 |
| **`[]byte`** | `bytea`, `blob`, `binary`, `varbinary`, `tinyblob`, `mediumblob`, `longblob` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (A)** |
| **`time.Duration`** | `interval` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (A)** |
| **`net.IP`** | `inet` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (A)** |
| **`net.IPNet`** | `cidr` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (A)** |
| **`net.HardwareAddr`** | `macaddr` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (A)** |
| **`sql.NullString`** | any nullable string column, `use_pointers: false` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (B)** |
| **`sql.NullBool`** | any nullable bool column, `use_pointers: false` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (B)** |
| **`sql.NullInt16/32/64`** | any nullable integer column, `use_pointers: false` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (B)** |
| **`sql.NullFloat64`** | any nullable float column, `use_pointers: false` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (B)** |
| **`sql.NullTime`** | any nullable timestamp column, `use_pointers: false` | `String` | `string` | **BROKEN (B)** |
| `string`, `bool`, `int`, `float64` | — | — | same | sound |
| `uuid.UUID`, `decimal.Decimal`, `types.DateTime`, `types.JSON`, … | — | custom scalar | model's own | sound (`models:` binding) |

Shape C was added 2026-08-31 and is the axis this table's `gqlgen Go` column cannot show: it
tabulates the type gqlgen emits for a **generated input object**, which is the only half
FIX-147 / FIX-148 fixed. On the **read** side gqlgen binds `Int` to exactly `int` / `int32` /
`int64` and `Float` to exactly `float64`, so every other width on a bound row struct falls back
to a `panic("not implemented")` field resolver — silently, with no array column involved.
Tracked and measured in FIX-165.

Shape B is additionally a **spec gap**: PRD §26.4.1 "Null-wrapper scalar pairing" names
"the `database/sql.NullX` family" as one of the wrapper families the pairing exists for, while the
built-in registry table below it lists none of them and `builtInScalarRegistry` carries only three
pairs (`NullUUID`, `NullDecimal`, `NullDateTime`).

**Why widening the cast predicate is wrong.** Only `[]byte` has a lossless Go conversion from
`string`. `time.Duration` and `net.IPNet` cannot be converted from `string` at all;
`net.IP` and `net.HardwareAddr` *would* compile (both are `[]byte` underneath) but produce
**garbage**, reinterpreting the text's raw bytes instead of parsing it. The `sql.NullX` family
cannot be converted at all. Those need `time.ParseDuration` / `net.ParseIP` / `net.ParseCIDR` /
`net.ParseMAC` / a `Valid`-aware unmarshal, all of which can fail, and the input translators have
no error return. The correct place for a fallible parse is the scalar's `Unmarshal` function, which
already returns an error.

**Resolution plan.** Three layers. Layer 1 is what closes the class; Layers 2–3 are what keep it
from erroring on schemas that should work.

*Layer 1 — state the invariant once, and enforce it.*
- Generalize `gqlgenPKArgGoType` into `gqlgenGoTypeFor(scalarName, modelGoType)`. It already holds
  the whole rule; `buildAPIPKArgs` keeps using it and `inputCoercionFor` starts using it.
- `inputCoercionFor` becomes a comparison rather than a predicate lookup. Three outcomes:
  gqlgen type == model type → identity, no cast; they differ **and** the pair is in a declared
  value-preserving conversion set (`int` → `int8/16/32/64`/`uint*`, `float64` → `float32`) → cast;
  they differ otherwise → **error at codegen**, naming the column, both Go types, and the two
  escapes (`api.graphql.scalars`, `overrides.types`).
- Delete `isNarrowedNumericGoType`. FIX-147 and FIX-148 become consequences of the rule rather than
  entries in a list.
- Move `GqlgenIsBareNullable` onto the same source: a `Nilable bool` on the registry entry, so
  nilability is declared once next to the binding instead of being a third hand-list. Verified
  against gqlgen v0.17.90 `codegen/config/binder.go:578` (`IsNilable`) and `CopyModifiersFromAst` —
  gqlgen pointer-wraps a nullable field unless the Go type is nilable (slice / map / ptr /
  interface / chan, recursing through named types). That is exactly `gotype.go`'s `nullRef` vs
  `nullPtrOnly` split, so the two line up by construction rather than by coincidence.

*Layer 2 — the fallthrough becomes an error.* Layer 1 only covers writable columns; a read-only
column never reaches `inputCoercionFor` and would still get `String` in front of a non-string Go
field. PRD §26.4.1 (line 10834) already asks for this: "codegen errors otherwise rather than
silently producing a non-compiling resolver". **Verified safe:** an instrumented run over all 11
E2E example goldens (`TestE2EGoldenFiles`) records **zero** fallthrough hits, so no example newly
fails and no golden churns.

*Layer 3 — give the reachable types real bindings.*
- Gate the `[]` strip on `col.IsSlice` at **both** call sites (`context_api.go:2051` and `:1480`).
  Nothing else in Layer 3 can match without this.
- Register five new external-marshaling scalars: `Bytes` (`[]byte`, `Nilable`), `Duration`
  (`time.Duration`), `IP` (`net.IP`, `Nilable`), `CIDR` (`net.IPNet`), `MacAddr`
  (`net.HardwareAddr`, `Nilable`).
- Register seven `sql.NullX` NullVariant pairs: `NullString`, `NullBool`, `NullInt16`, `NullInt32`,
  `NullInt64`, `NullFloat64`, `NullTime`. Two novelties for the pairing machinery, which has only
  ever seen custom↔custom: the non-null partner is a **spec built-in** (`Int` / `Float` / `String` /
  `Boolean`), which still satisfies §26.4.1's wire-format invariant (`Int` ↔ JSON number); and
  `UnmarshalNullInt16` / `UnmarshalNullInt32` must range-check, because gqlgen hands them a Go `int`.

**Wire formats (settled 2026-08-28, user decision).** PRD §26.4's mapping table is silent on all
five Shape-A SQL types, so these are new PRD rows, not restatements.

| Scalar | Go type | Wire form | Round-trip |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bytes` | `[]byte` | base64, std encoding | exact |
| `Duration` | `time.Duration` | Go duration string (`"1h30m0s"`) | exact, `time.ParseDuration` |
| `IP` | `net.IP` | `"10.0.0.1"` / `"2001:db8::1"` | exact, `net.ParseIP` |
| `CIDR` | `net.IPNet` | `"10.0.0.0/8"` | exact, `net.ParseCIDR` |
| `MacAddr` | `net.HardwareAddr` | `"01:23:45:67:89:ab"` | exact, `net.ParseMAC` |

base64 over hex for `Bytes` because it is the JSON convention; the Go duration string over ISO-8601
because it round-trips exactly through `time.ParseDuration` with no hand-written parser, and
PostgreSQL `interval` already lands on `time.Duration`. `MarshalIP` must not emit `net.IP(nil).String()`
(`"<nil>"`) for a NOT NULL zero value — same hazard `MarshalUUID` documents for `uuid.Nil`.

**Registry additions touch five hand-maintained lists, only one pair of which is pinned.**
`gen.builtInScalarRegistry`; `config.BuiltInScalarGoTypes` (pinned to the first by
`TestBuiltInScalarGoTypesMatchRegistry`); `config.ReservedScalarNames`; `gen.scalarImports`
(name → import switch, `orchestrate.go:1817`); `templates/api/scalars.go.tmpl` (name → marshaler
body if-chain). The unpinned three should gain parity tests in the same change — the existing parity
test is the only reason a registry addition cannot go half-done today.

**Prototype evidence (2026-08-28).** Registry entries + the `IsSlice`-gated strip +
`Nilable`-driven `GqlgenIsBareNullable`, built and rendered, then reverted:

```go
out.Payload = in.Payload              omittable.Set(in.Signature)    // []byte, no deref
out.Dur     = in.Dur                  omittable.Set(in.DurN)         // *time.Duration
omittable.Set(in.AddrN)               omittable.Set(in.NetBlockN)    // net.IP / *net.IPNet
omittable.Set(*in.Dur)                omittable.Set(in.Payload)      // update arms
```

All eight arm/nullability combinations correct, including the two the current code gets wrong in
opposite directions (a missing deref on nullable `[]byte`, a spurious deref on required `[]byte`).
Field types resolve to `Bytes!`/`Bytes`, `Duration!`/`Duration`, `IP`, `CIDR`, `MacAddr`.
**Blast radius: one failing test** — `TestBuiltInScalarGoTypesMatchRegistry`, the existing parity
guard doing its job. **Zero golden churn**: `TestE2EGoldenFiles` passes byte-identical across all
11 examples.

**Tests required.** The prior revision asked for a test enumerating every Go type in `gotype.go`'s
tables. That is necessary but not sufficient, and the axis it omits is the one that produces
Shape B:
- Table-driven over (dialect × every SQL type in the three `gotype.go` mapping tables × nullable /
  NOT NULL × `use_pointers` true / false), asserting each column resolves to an **explicit**
  binding and that `gqlgenGoType == modelGoType` or a declared value-preserving conversion applies.
- A failing-first pin per Shape-A type on all four arm/nullability combinations, alongside
  `TestInputTranslate_NullableSizedIntGoesThroughALocal` (FIX-147) and
  `TestInputTranslate_Float32ColumnsAreCast` (FIX-148).
- A pin that Layer 2's error fires for an unregistered Go type (an `overrides.types` entry pointing
  at an arbitrary type with no `api.graphql.scalars` declaration), and that its message names the
  column and both escapes.
- Enumeration is the regression pin, **not** the closure. `overrides.types` and `type_map` literals
  produce Go types no test can enumerate; Layer 2's error is what actually closes the class.

**PRD amendments required.** §26.4's SQL→GraphQL mapping table gains five rows (the Shape-A types);
§26.4.1's built-in scalar registry table gains twelve (five Shape-A + seven `sql.NullX`); §26.4.1's
Null-wrapper pairing section needs the spec-built-in-partner case written down, and its existing
mention of "the `database/sql.NullX` family" reconciled with the registry table that lists none —
that inconsistency is what let Shape B sit unnoticed.

**Adjacent defect, deliberately not folded in.** `resolveSimpleComparator`'s
`default: return "String"` (`context_table.go:1600`) is the same "unmodeled type ⇒ pretend it is a
string" reflex on the comparator axis: a `bytea` / `inet` / `interval` column takes
`*comparator.String` on the model filter and a `StringComparator` in the schema, so the generated
filter compares a `bytea` column against a text parameter. It **compiles**, so it is not part of
this entry's failure, and giving those columns real comparator families is a §26.4 projection
design job rather than a fix. Log separately.
