**Revision note (2026-08-28).** Rewritten before implementation after an evidence pass. Four
changes to the prior text, all of which alter what the fix has to do:
1. The `[]byte` root cause was wrong (dead `case`, not an explicit case), and with it the prior
   suggested fix, which would not have matched.
2. The class was understated. The prior enumeration was exhaustive only at `use_pointers: true`;
   Shape B adds seven more Go types reachable from ordinary nullable columns, and produces a wrong
   schema rather than a compile error.
3. The root cause was located at the fallthrough. It is one level up — four unreconciled
   derivations of the gqlgen-emitted Go type, one of which (`gqlgenPKArgGoType`) is already correct
   and unused by the path that needs it.
4. The two questions the prior text left open (wire formats; whether these types are in scope at
   all) are settled above by user decision, so implementation does not have to guess.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-28. Implemented as the three layers above; the class is
closed by the invariant, not by the twelve registrations.

*Layer 1 — one derivation.* `gqlgenPKArgGoType` became `gqlgenGoTypeFor`, and `inputCoercionFor`
now calls it instead of re-deriving the same fact. The coercion is a comparison with exactly three
outcomes — identity, a declared conversion (`gqlgenNumericWidthCasts` or the PostgreSQL enum-array
named-slice bridge), or an **error**. `isNarrowedNumericGoType` is deleted: FIX-147 and FIX-148 are
now consequences of the comparison rather than entries in a list. `mapColumnToGraphQL` threads the
resolved scalar down to the input builder (`scalarByColumn`), so the schema a mutation is validated
against and the coercion that fills it come from one resolution rather than two.
`GqlgenIsBareNullable` moved onto a `Nilable` flag on the registry entry, replacing the third
hand-list.

*Layer 2 — the fallthrough errors.* `graphQLTypeForGoType` returns an error instead of `String`.
One exemption, added after the first implementation pass surfaced it: a column dropped from every
API surface by its §32.2 access role is exempt, because it names no GraphQL type anywhere in the
emitted schema — without the exemption, `access: hidden` (the documented way to keep a column OUT
of the API) would have been the one setting that forces you to describe it TO the API.

*Layer 3 — bindings.* The `[]` strip is gated on `col.IsSlice` at both call sites; twelve registry
entries added with the settled wire formats. `scalarImports` is now derived from the registry
(`Import` + `MarshalerImports`) instead of a switch on the scalar name.

**Verified end-to-end against the real pipeline, not just the unit suite.** A temporary
`binary_probes` table carrying all five shape-A types on both nullabilities was added to the
`graphql` example and run through `sqlgen generate` + gqlgen v0.17.90, then reverted. Results:

- The schema emits `payload: Bytes!`, `signature: Bytes`, `dur: Duration!`, `addr: IP!`,
  `netBlock: CIDR!`, `mac: MacAddr!`, and declares `scalar Bytes / Duration / IP / CIDR / MacAddr`.
- gqlgen emitted the input struct as `Payload []byte`, `Signature []byte`, `Dur time.Duration`,
  `DurN *time.Duration`, `Addr net.IP`, `AddrN net.IP`, `NetBlock net.IPNet`,
  `NetBlockN *net.IPNet`, `MAC net.HardwareAddr`, `MACN net.HardwareAddr` — bare for the nilable
  bindings on BOTH nullabilities, pointer-wrapped for the non-nilable ones when nullable. That is
  exactly what the `Nilable` flag predicts and exactly `gotype.nullKind`'s `nullRef` /
  `nullPtrOnly` split, so the two agree by construction rather than coincidence.
- `binary_probe_gen.resolvers.go` contains **zero** `panic("not implemented")` stubs, which is the
  read half: pre-fix, a `String` field in front of a non-string Go field forced a field resolver.
- The whole generated package compiles.

Shape B (`sql.NullX`) is verified at the codegen level by unit tests rather than through the
example, because flipping `use_pointers` would retype every nullable column in it. The gqlgen
behaviour it depends on — a struct binding gets pointer-wrapped when the field is nullable, so the
translator's existing deref arm applies — is directly demonstrated by `net.IPNet` in the same run,
which is a struct and was pointer-wrapped exactly that way.

**Tests.** New `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_scalar_binding_test.go`:
`TestScalarBinding_everyBuiltInGoTypeResolves` (every SQL type in all three dialect tables ×
nullable/NOT NULL × `use_pointers` true/false = 12 subtests, asserting the gqlgen Go type equals
the model's or differs by a declared width); `TestInputTranslate_BinaryAndNetworkColumns` and
`TestInputTranslate_SQLNullWrappers` (per-shape emitted code, both arms);
`TestScalarBinding_unboundTypeIsRejected` (the closure, via an `overrides.types` type no
enumeration could reach); `TestScalarBinding_registryDrivesEveryDerivedTable` (registry vs all four
derived tables); `TestScalarBinding_int64ScalarSuppressesSelfConversion`.

**Verified failing-first**, which mattered here: the enumeration test's "BuildAPIContext succeeds"
assertion passes VACUOUSLY against pre-fix code, since there was no error to raise. Reverting the
four production files and re-running showed the second assertion catching all twelve subtests with
messages naming each Go type — `bytea`: `GraphQL "String" binds gqlgen to Go "string", but the
model is "[]byte"` — plus every other new test failing. `TestScalarBinding_registryDrivesEveryDerivedTable`
correctly PASSED pre-fix: the derived tables were consistent with the registry then, just
collectively incomplete, which is what a parity test should say.

**Incidental fixes** made in passing, both consequences of the rewrite rather than separate work:
a column deliberately routed onto gqlgen's bundled `Int64` scalar previously emitted the no-op
self-conversion `int64(in.X)` that `unconvert` flags, because the old predicate keyed on the model
type alone; and `buildAPITableContext`'s `writableNonPKCount` was dead at HEAD (incremented, never
read) and is removed.

**Four tests changed** because they pinned the old fallthrough as intended behaviour:
`TestConsumerScalars_undeclaredTypeStillFallsThrough` became
`TestConsumerScalars_undeclaredTypeIsRejected` (plus a new sibling pinning the §32.2 exemption);
`TestConsumerScalars_matchOnImportNotJustTypeName` keeps its property (the index keys on the import
path) with the assertion moved from "resolves to String" to "is rejected";
`TestUnusedScalarWarnings` gained a `wantErr` axis, recording that the mistyped-`go_type` case it
was justified by is now caught harder while the legitimate-unused case stays a warning; and
`cli.TestBuildMergeInput_UndeclaredScalarGetsNoEntry`'s fixture keeps both column declarations so
`Unused` is the only unresolved entry.

**PRD amended.** §26.4's mapping table gains six rows (the five shape-A types plus the `sql.NullX`
family); §26.4.1's registry table gains twelve; §26.4.1 gains a "Spec-built-in partners" paragraph
for the new pairing shape and an "A Go type with no binding is an error" paragraph with the §32.2
exemption; the "Unresolved declarations warn" paragraph now records what supersedes it.

**Golden impact at the time of this fix: none.** `make check` clean across all 33 modules;
`make check-examples` clean across all 13 example modules against real databases;
`TestE2EGoldenFiles` byte-identical across all 11 examples. No example carried a column of any
newly-bound Go type — which is precisely why every member of this class survived from phase 16.
**That is no longer true: see "Example coverage landed 2026-08-29" below.**

**Auto-review found a real defect in the first implementation of this fix; it is fixed above.**
The seven `sql.NullX` unmarshalers asserted `v.(int)` / `v.(string)` / `v.(bool)` on the incoming
value. That was wrong for the four numeric ones in a way no codegen test could catch: a scalar
unmarshaler receives whatever the REQUEST DECODER produced, not the Go type gqlgen binds the scalar
to. gqlparser parses an inline `IntValue` with `strconv.ParseInt(..., 10, 64)`, so a literal arrives
as `int64`; the HTTP handler decodes variables with `UseNumber`, so those arrive as `json.Number`.
Both were rejected — `NullInt32 must be an integer or null, got int64` on every mutation. The
reasoning error was reading gqlgen's `UnmarshalInt(v any) (int, error)` RETURN type as its ARGUMENT
type; gqlgen's own body is a five-case switch for exactly this reason.

All seven now **delegate** to the partner's gqlgen unmarshaler (`graphql.UnmarshalInt16` /
`UnmarshalInt32` / `UnmarshalInt64` / `UnmarshalFloat` / `UnmarshalString` / `UnmarshalBoolean` /
`UnmarshalTime`) and the matching marshalers, which deletes the hand-written range checks and makes
§26.4.1's wire-format invariant structural: a pair cannot disagree about what it accepts when both
members run the same code. `math` and `time` dropped out of the registry entries' `MarshalerImports`
as a result.

**Two test gaps the review named, both closed.** `TestScalarBinding_everyMarshalerBodyHasItsImports`
renders each body, walks its AST for package qualifiers, and checks every one against
`scalarImports` — verified to catch a deliberately reintroduced missing `math` import. (Written
first as a regex, which produced false positives on `v.String()` and on `uuid.Nil` inside a doc
comment; the AST is what tells prose and locals from package qualifiers.)
`TestScalarBinding_nullWrappersDelegateCoercion` pins the delegation and rejects any type assertion
on the raw input, also via the AST. `MarshalMacAddr` gained the zero-value guard its `IP` / `CIDR`
siblings already had.

**Shape B is not verified end-to-end.** The example run above covers shape A only; exercising the
`sql.NullX` half needs `use_pointers: false`, which is module-wide and would retype every nullable
column in the example. The gqlgen behaviour it depends on — a struct binding gets pointer-wrapped
when nullable, so the translator's existing deref arm applies — IS demonstrated in that run by
`net.IPNet`, which is a struct and was pointer-wrapped exactly that way. What remains unexercised is
the marshaler bodies at runtime, now covered structurally rather than behaviourally.
**`use_pointers: false` + `api.graphql` has no example module at all**, which is FIX-169's
territory. **Superseded 2026-08-29 — see below.**

**Two boundaries this fix surfaces but does not move**, both pre-existing and both now loud instead
of silent — logged rather than left implicit:

- **FIX-165** — narrowed numeric PostgreSQL arrays (`integer[]` → gqlgen `[]int` vs model
  `[]int32`). Go has no slice-element conversion, so no *translator* expression bridges it; pre-fix
  it emitted non-compiling code. The generic error arm named the slice type and pointed at
  `api.graphql.scalars`, which is keyed on the ELEMENT — so a dedicated array arm now names the
  element, pinned by `TestScalarBinding_numericArrayIsRejectedWithAnActionableMessage`. (Superseded
  2026-08-31: the disagreement is removable at its source via `models.<Type>.fields.<f>.type`, so
  the real fix is not in the translator at all. See FIX-165.)
- **FIX-166** — MySQL `SET` columns (named slice, no `MarshalGQL`). Pre-fix: panic resolver plus a
  non-compiling translator. Carries a coupled hazard recorded in that entry: registering SETs
  naively would trip `isNilableGqlgenGoType`, since a named slice's NAME reveals nothing.

**Adjacent defect, now logged as FIX-167:** `resolveSimpleComparator`'s `default: return "String"`
gives a `bytea` / `inet` / `interval` column `*comparator.String` on the model filter and a
`StringComparator` in the schema, so the generated filter compares a binary column against a text
parameter. It compiles, so it is outside this entry's failure — but it is the same reflex on the
comparator axis, and after this fix the disagreement is visible in the schema (`payload: Bytes!` on
the row, `payload: StringComparator` on the filter).

**Example coverage landed 2026-08-29 — shape B is now verified end-to-end.** The `scalar_probes`
table in the `graphql` example carries all twelve Go types: the five shape-A stdlib types on both
nullabilities, and seven ordinary nullable columns landing on the `database/sql` wrappers through a
table-scoped `overrides.types` block. The block exists because `overrides.use_pointers: false` is
module-wide and would retype every nullable column in the example; the scalar registry is keyed on
the resolved Go type, so the two routes produce the same schema, the same gqlgen binding and the
same input translator. `tests/scalars_test.go::TestBuiltInScalarProbes` round-trips every one
through the live gqlgen handler and a real Postgres — set and unset for each nullable member,
reading back through a separate `scalarProbe(id:)` query so the marshaler runs on a value loaded
from the database rather than one carried over from the mutation. All twelve pass, `interval` →
`time.Duration`, `inet` → `net.IP`, `cidr` → `net.IPNet` and `macaddr` → `net.HardwareAddr`
included: pgx handles every one, which the compile-only verification above could not have told us.

Landing it surfaced **FIX-168** — `use_pointers: false` emitted a models package that did not
compile, on every dialect, with or without the API — which had to be fixed first. What remained open
was FIX-169: no API-enabled example on a second dialect, and no module setting the flag itself.
**Closed 2026-09-01** — `api:` on the `sqlite` example (after FIX-166 did MySQL), and the new
`graphql_null_wrappers` module for the module-wide flag.

### FIX-162

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 4, cmd/sqlgen/config
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-154 implementation (2026-08-28)

**Issue.** **The PRD §4.13 struct-name collision rule is implemented, but its normalizer does not
model the naming pipeline, so it misses every collision singularization creates — and under
`layout: file_per_table` the consequence is a silently missing table.** Two tables that resolve to
the same `StructName` also resolve to the same `SnakeName`, so the second overwrites the first's
`<stem>_gen.go` and one table disappears from the generated package with no error.

| Pair | Both resolve to | Caught today |
|---|---|---|
| `user_roles` / `userroles` | `UserRole` | yes — the PRD's own example |
| `users` / `user` | `User` | **no** |
| `people` / `person` | `Person` | **no** |
| `osi_layers` / `osi_layer` | `OSILayer` | **no** |

Under `layout: single_file` the duplicate structs land in one file and `go build` fails loudly, so
the silence is specific to the per-table path (`gen/orchestrate.go:474`, `generateTablesPerFile`).

**Root cause.** `validateAutoStructNameCollisions` (`cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:1268`) keys on
`normalizeForCollision` (`:1651`):

```go
func normalizeForCollision(name string) string {
	return strings.ToLower(strings.ReplaceAll(name, "_", ""))
}
```

That is a lexical approximation — lowercase and drop underscores — and `StructName`
(`gen/naming.go:141`) singularizes before casing. Three further gaps in the same function: tables
carrying an explicit `struct_name` are skipped entirely (pre-parse only compares override against
override, so `struct_name: User` alongside a `users` table passes both checks); views are never
considered even though they write into the same output directory; and the schema prefix is applied
on `hasMultipleSchemas` rather than on the per-name collision predicate `StructName` actually uses.

**Suggested fix.** Move the check to resolution time in `gen`, where the real names exist. It
cannot be fixed in place: `config` must not import `gen`, and re-deriving `StructName` inside
`config` is exactly the two-implementations-of-one-rule drift that produced FIX-152 and FIX-155.

- Add `validateResolvedTypeNames` alongside `validateResolvedFieldNames`
  (`gen/context_table.go`), keyed on the emitted `StructName` **and** `SnakeName`, over tables and
  views together, including override-derived names. FIX-158 established this exact pattern — a
  resolution-level rule reachable from `sqlgen validate` because it builds and discards the
  contexts.
- Retire `validateAutoStructNameCollisions` and `normalizeForCollision` once the resolution-level
  check subsumes them, so there is one rule rather than a lexical one and a real one.
- Error text should keep §4.13's guidance ("use `tables.<table>.struct_name` to disambiguate") and
  name both offenders plus the stem they share.
- **Adjacent, decide while in here:** `struct_name` moves the struct and the file stem but not the
  `hook.TableName` constant. `tables.user_ips.struct_name: NetworkAddress` yields struct
  `NetworkAddress` in `network_address_gen.go` under the constant `TableUserIPSes` — measured.
  Pre-existing and *consistent* (generator, tablename file and `sqlgen lint` all ignore the
  override), so nothing breaks; but FIX-161 made the deriver an exported
  `gen.TableConstantName(table, schema, collisions)` whose signature has no seam for the override,
  which turns "ignored" into a contract. Either thread the override through or state in §8.5 that
  the constant is spelled from the SQL name and the override does not reach it.

Regression test: `users` + `user`, `people` + `person`, `osi_layers` + `osi_layer`, a view whose
stem matches a table's, and a `struct_name` override colliding with an auto-derived name. Verify
failing-first — each currently generates without error. Add a per-table-layout case asserting both
tables' files exist.

**References.**
- PRD §4.13 line 1103 ("Struct name collisions | Error"), line 1107 ("Duplicate `struct_name`
  overrides"); §8.5 "Field Name Resolution" for the resolution-level precedent.
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:1268` (`validateAutoStructNameCollisions`), `:1651`
  (`normalizeForCollision`), `:752` (`validateDuplicateStructNames`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go:474` (`generateTablesPerFile`), `:600` (views).
- FIX-158 — the resolution-level reserved-name rule and its `sqlgen validate` reachability.
- FIX-154 — removed the acronym-driven source of duplicate stems; this is the remaining one.

**Resolution (2026-08-28).** Both halves landed: the entity-vs-entity rule the entry describes, and
the reserved-name rule the investigation surfaced beside it. One check, `gen.validateResolvedNames`
(`gen/resolved_names.go`), keyed on **three** things an entity claims independently — the Go type
name, the file stem, and the `hook.TableName` constant — over tables, views, enums, SET types,
composite types, domain types and `extras`. It reads the names off the **built contexts** rather
than re-deriving them, which is what keeps it from disagreeing with generation: the contexts have
already applied singularization, the schema prefix and `struct_name`, and have already dropped the
entities that never get a name (`exclude_tables`, no resolved PK). Reachable from `sqlgen validate`
through `ValidateGeneration`, from `generate` through `Generate`, and from `sqlgen graphql gen`
through `BuildTableContextsFromSchema` — the last of these matters because it is the only path that
emits `<stem>_gen.graphqls` and it does not route through either of the other two.

**Corrections to the entry, both measured.**

- **The failure is loud, not silent.** Every colliding pair compiles-errors, because
  `client_gen.go` and `tablenames_gen.go` aggregate all entities: `TablePeople redeclared`,
  `person redeclared`, `duplicate field name person in struct literal`. The defect is
  *misdirection* — the generator accepts the config and the compiler indicts the client struct,
  never the two tables. That is what the check buys.
- **The PRD's own example was a false positive.** `user_roles` resolves to `UserRole` and
  `userroles` to `Userrole` — distinct structs, distinct stems, compiles fine — and
  `validateAutoStructNameCollisions` rejected the pair. The lexical normalizer was wrong in both
  directions, so the rule is now exact and §4.13's example is replaced with `users` / `user`.

**Beyond the entry.** Measured on the real pipeline, the larger and likelier half is a name
**sqlgen already owns**. Under the default `single_file` layout a table named `clients` gives
`Client redeclared in this block`, `connections` gives `Connection redeclared`, and an enum `order`
beside an `orders` table gives `Order redeclared`; under `file_per_table` a table named
`connections`, `sorters` or `paginations` is erased outright by the generator's own file and the
consumer gets `undefined: connectionClient`. `clients` and `connections` are ordinary table names,
where `users` + `user` in one schema is not — so the reserved half was folded in rather than
tracked separately, which would have left the common case broken until it landed.

**Cross-schema hole, fixed at the source rather than reported.** `computeNameCollisions` keyed the
disambiguation set on the raw SQL name, so `public.people` + `audit.person` — two strings, one
resolved `Person` — went unprefixed and collided. Grouping is now by resolved name while the set
stays keyed by SQL name (which is what `StructName` / `SnakeName` are handed, so no call site and
no hand-built test fixture moved). Within a naming family it only widens: equal SQL names always
resolve equally, so every prefix that fired before still fires, and the only new prefixes land where
the output was already broken. Across families it can also *narrow* — composites and domains are not
singularized, so a `public.addresses` table beside an `audit.addresses` composite grouped by SQL
name but resolves to `Address` and `Addresses`, and the table drops a prefix it never needed. That
is the right answer (they were two distinct Go names all along) and no fixture or example reaches
it. Zero golden churn, confirmed.

**Retired.** `validateAutoStructNameCollisions`, `normalizeForCollision`, `hasMultipleSchemas` and
`validateDuplicateStructNames` — the last one beyond the entry's list, because `sqlgen validate`
aggregates every pass rather than stopping at the first, so keeping it would double-report what the
resolution-level rule now owns. Both §4.13 rows are now one rule.

**Adjacent item, decided the other way after measurement: the override now reaches the constant.**
The entry's own reading — and this implementation's first pass — kept `TableConstantName` spelling
from the SQL name, on the argument that the constant is a SQL-identity key. A CLI smoke test on the
finished build showed why that is wrong *once the constant is a collision key*: `tables.user.struct_name:
LegacyUser` beside a `users` table moved the struct and the file stem but left both entities on
`TableUsers`, so the config stayed rejected with **nothing left for the consumer to change** — the
error said to set `struct_name`, they had, and it still failed. A rule may only reject what its
documented escape hatch can fix. `TableConstantName(table, schema, structNameOverride, collisions)`
now resolves the override through a new `StructNameFor`, the sibling of `snakeNameFor`, which also
replaced the inline override branch in both context builders — three derivers became one. The
constant's *value* is still the SQL table name; only its Go identifier follows the struct.

That change propagated to every site that names the constant, which is the invariant FIX-161
exported it for: `buildTableNameFileContext` now takes the config (its constants must agree with the
ones the table clients reference, or the package does not compile), and `cli/lint.go` was fixed
along the way — it derived both the struct name and the constant from the SQL name alone, so
`sqlgen lint` was blind to every renamed table, looking up a `User` the package spells `LegacyUser`.
Pre-existing, unrelated to the collision rule, surfaced by threading the override through.

**Scope boundary, stated in code and PRD.** The rules key on each entity's *primary* name. The
suffixed identifiers built from it are injective in it, so distinct primaries cannot collide within
one shape; a cross-shape collision between two suffix families — an enum literally named
`order_filter` beside an `orders` table, both reaching `OrderFilter` — is not discovered and stays a
`go build` error. Same boundary the reserved-field rule draws.

**Emission is now atomic.** `Generate` built view contexts at step 6, two steps after the tables
were already on disk, so the stem check had nowhere to stand. All contexts are now built by
`buildAllContexts` ahead of the first write, which also means a rejected config leaves nothing
behind — before, a late failure stranded the enums, types, scaffold and table files of a run that
did not finish. `generateEnums` / `generateSets` / `generateTypes` take prebuilt contexts;
`buildAndGenerateViews` is gone.

**Error reporting.** One rename fixes all three keys, so a pair that collides on all three is one
problem and reads as one error. Reporting per key turned a single `users` / `user` pair into three
near-identical lines; the CLI now says `table public.user and table public.users both resolve to the
Go type name "User", the file stem "user" and the table-name constant "TableUsers" — set
tables.public.user.struct_name or tables.public.users.struct_name to a different Go identifier`.
Both escape hatches are offered rather than one, because renaming either side resolves it and which
one to rename is the consumer's call.

**Tests.** `gen/resolved_names_test.go` — ten collision shapes and seven reserved-name shapes
through `ValidateGeneration`, all verified failing-first; a batch-report case; `Generate` refusing
the colliding pair *and leaving the output dir empty*; `Generate` emitting both files for the pair
the retired rule rejected; and the cross-schema pair generating as `public_person_gen.go` /
`audit_person_gen.go`. `gen/resolved_names_pin_test.go` — the structural pin: it generates one
package **twice over disjoint entity names and intersects what the two runs declare**, so a name
present in both is one sqlgen owns and must be reserved. That pin caught 19 entries the hand-built
list had missed (every `Err*` sentinel, the four `Constraint*` constants, and the eight cache option
functions), and is what stops the list going stale when a template adds a declaration. Plus the
config-derived client name/file, and the collision-set grouping and its struct/stem-move-together
invariant.

**Auto-review round.** The reviewer found five issues, all confirmed by measurement and all fixed
inline. Two were real detection gaps. (1) `shared_gen.graphqls` is written into the API schema
directory *after* the per-table `<stem>_gen.graphqls` loop, so a table resolving to the stem
`shared` was overwritten there — the exact FIX-162 shape, in the one namespace the reserved list did
not cover; the stem list now spans both directories. (2) The constant key read the built contexts,
but `buildTableNameFileContext` ranged the raw schema, so a PK-less or `exclude_tables`-matched
`people` beside a generated `person` still emitted `TablePeople` twice, undetected — measured.
**Fixed by filtering the file rather than widening the check** (user direction: an output change is
fine pre-release, and a constant for a table with nothing behind it is dead weight). The tablename
file is now built from the table and view contexts, which is the set that actually generates —
§9.4b already said a PK-less table emits "no client interface, model struct, filter type, cache
entry, or event hook", and the constant belonged on that list. The file and `validateResolvedNames`
are now literally the same list, so they cannot disagree by construction, and `generateScaffold` no
longer needs the schema or the config at all. (3) `cli/lint.go` looked up
`cfg.Tables[t.Name]` where the generator uses the qualified-key-first `resolveTableConfig` (now
exported), which desynced the linter from the package for any table configured under a
schema-qualified key — pre-existing, load-bearing once lint's registry names depend on the override.
(4) The "strict widening" claim is true within a naming family but not across: composites and
domains are not singularized, so a cross-family SQL-name group can now *narrow*. Corrected in both
the code comment and this entry rather than changed — narrowing there is the right answer. (5) An
`extras` entry was told to "rename it in the schema"; it is declared in the config, so it now names
`extras.<name>`.

Found alongside, not by the reviewer: **`cli/lint.go` carried a fourth private
`computeNameCollisions`** — tables only, keyed on the raw SQL name — which this change made actively
wrong, since the generator now groups by resolved name across six categories. It calls the exported
`gen.ComputeNameCollisions` instead. Same one-deriver discipline as FIX-161 and FIX-163.

Two tests were added for the reviewer's coverage gap and the new stem: one asserting
`BuildTableContextsFromSchema` *rejects* a collision (the graphql-gen path was only covered by
happy-path callers), and one for the `shared` stem.

**Behaviour change (deliberate, pre-release).** `tablenames_gen.go` no longer declares a
`hook.TableName` for a table that generates nothing. Measured end to end: a schema with an
`exclude_tables`-matched `audit_trail` and a PK-less `people` beside a generated `person` used to
emit `TablePeople` twice and not compile, with no diagnostic naming the cause; it now emits
`TableOrders` and one `TablePeople`, and the package builds. **Zero golden churn in-tree** — no
example or fixture has an excluded or PK-less table (the postgres example's `counters` and
`rate_limits` look PK-less in raw SQL but carry `primary_key.columns` overrides, so they generate
and keep their constants). The change is latent for every schema in the repo and only visible to a
consumer who was relying on a constant for a table sqlgen refuses to generate. PRD §6.4, §8.3 and
§9.4b now state it.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all modules; `make check-examples` clean across all 13
example modules; `TestE2EGoldenFiles` passes unchanged — no golden regeneration, since the change
only rejects and never re-spells a name. All 37 example/fixture entity names were run through the
real deriver beforehand: no duplicate struct name, stem or constant, and no reserved-stem hit.

Also pinned: `TestTableConstantName_MatchesTableNameFile` gained the `struct_name` case, so the two
derivations of the constant have to agree under a rename; and a hand-built-context test exercises
the constant key firing alone, since pluralization is not injective even though no schema reaches
that shape today.

**PRD.** §4.13 — the "Struct name collisions" row replaced by two resolution-level rows (entity vs
entity, and entity vs a name sqlgen declares), with the bad example corrected and the category
widened past tables; the "Duplicate `struct_name` overrides" row folded into it. §5.5 — the
multi-schema trigger restated as the resolved name rather than the SQL name, and the file-name
example corrected from `public_users_gen.go` to the singular `public_user_gen.go`. §8.5 — new
"Resolved Type Names and File Stems" subsection carrying the three claims, the reserved table, the
scope boundary, and the `struct_name`-moves-all-three-names rule with its worked example.

### FIX-164

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 8, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-161 implementation (2026-08-28)

**Issue.** **An uncountable noun pluralizes to itself, so a table named `media` or `series` emits a
GraphQL schema gqlgen rejects and a resolver package that does not compile.** `StructName("media")`
is `Media` and its plural is `Media`, which collapses two identifier pairs that share a namespace:

| Pair | Emitted into | Result for `media` |
|---|---|---|
| `QueryName` / `QueryNamePlural` | one `extend type Query` block (`templates/api/schema.graphqls.tmpl:116,120`) | field `media` declared twice — invalid SDL |
| `StructName` / `StructNamePlural` | two methods on one receiver (`templates/api/resolvers.go.tmpl:49,69`; `seeds.go.tmpl:19,27`) | `(*Q).Media` declared twice — compile error |

Twelve dictionary words reach it — `media`, `series`, `news`, `species`, `equipment`, `police`,
`fish`, `aircraft`, `chassis`, `money`, `information`, `graffiti` — of which `media` and `series`
are ordinary table names. Fires under the default operations preset, which has both `Get` and
`Connection` on (`config/config.go:1029-1035`).

Nothing else that pluralizes collides: `TableMedia`, `GetMediaInput`, `StreamMediaInput`,
`scanMedia` and the client accessor `Media()` each have no singular sibling in their namespace.

Pre-existing and behaviourally unchanged by FIX-161 — the library it replaced returned the same
word. Latent in-repo: no fixture or example table is an uncountable noun, which is why no test
caught it.

**Root cause.** `toPlural` returns its input for any word in the ported `pluralToSingle` map,
which is correct for the direction it was written for — `relationshipToContext`
(`gen/context_table.go:1117,1157`) pluralizes a snake-case relationship name and *depends* on
already-plural names passing through unchanged (`reviews` must stay `reviews`). The API surface
needs the opposite guarantee and does not state it: `StructNamePlural` (`gen/naming.go:194`) is a
bare pass-through to `toPlural`, so nothing enforces that the plural of a struct name differs from
the struct name.

FIX-161 D3 already established this invariant for the frozen/acronym path — "the plural direction
never freezes; it appends" — and pinned it with
`TestStructNamePlural_FrozenWordsAlwaysChange`. Uncountables break the same invariant by a
different route, and that test is scoped to the frozen set so it does not see them.

**Suggested fix.** Extend D3 to its real scope rather than adding a second rule.

- **Put the guarantee on `StructNamePlural`, not on `toPlural`.** If `toPlural(structName)` returns
  its input, append the same marker the freeze uses (`s`, or `es` after `s`/`x`/`z`/`ch`/`sh`).
  `toPlural` itself must keep passing already-plural words through — the relationship path breaks
  otherwise.
- **Promote `StructNamePlural` to a context field** on `TableContext` and `ViewContext`, the way
  FIX-154 promoted `SnakeName`, and repoint the ~20 template sites that spell
  `{{ .StructName | toPlural }}` (`shared/_input.tmpl:36`, `table/get.go.tmpl:151`,
  `table/stream.go.tmpl:7`, `table/client.go.tmpl:19,153`, `table/pagination.go.tmpl:4`,
  `view/pagination.go.tmpl:4`, `table/create.go.tmpl`, `table/update.go.tmpl`,
  `table/relationships.go.tmpl:40,43`, …) onto it. This is load-bearing, not tidying: `cli/lint.go`
  resolves `Get<Plural>Input` through `gen.StructNamePlural`, so changing that function while the
  templates still call the funcmap would emit `GetMediaInput` and look up `GetMediasInput` — the
  exact desync FIX-161 closed. `guidelines/TEMPLATES.md:182` asks for the precomputed-field shape
  for the same reason.
- Drop `toPlural` from the funcmap if no template still needs it, so a template author cannot
  reach the un-guaranteed spelling.

Widen `TestStructNamePlural_FrozenWordsAlwaysChange` from the frozen set to **every** word in
`inflectDictionary` plus every canonical acronym and non-plural noun — the invariant is
`StructNamePlural(s) != s` for all `s`, and stating it that way is what keeps a third route from
reopening this.

Regression test: an `uncountable_names` schema fixture carrying `media` and `series`, asserting
distinct `QueryName`/`QueryNamePlural` and `StructName`/`StructNamePlural` through
`BuildAPIContext`, plus a `Generate` run whose emitted `.graphqls` declares each Query field once.
Verify failing-first. Expect no golden churn — the new branch only fires when
`toPlural(x) == x`, which no fixture or example table hits.

Judgment call to make explicit: English has no distinct plural for these, so every answer is
inelegant. `Media`→`Medias`, `Equipment`→`Equipments`, `Aircraft`→`Aircrafts` read fine;
`Series`→`Serieses` and `News`→`Newses` do not. `tables.<t>.struct_name: NewsItem` is the escape
hatch, the same one the non-plural `-s` noun list uses. Two alternatives were considered and
rejected: suffixing only the query name (`mediaConnection`) needs a second mechanism for the Go
method and splits one convention in two, and rejecting the table at validation time makes an
ordinary table name a hard error.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go:194` (`StructNamePlural`), `:124` (`toPlural`),
  `gen/inflect.go` (the ported `pluralToSingle` map and the freeze's append rule).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:1338,:1401`; `gen/context_table.go:1117,:1157` (the path that
  needs the opposite guarantee).
- `gen/templates/api/schema.graphqls.tmpl:116,120`; `api/resolvers.go.tmpl:49,69`;
  `api/seeds.go.tmpl:19,27`; `config/config.go:1029-1035` (default preset).
- PRD §8.5 "Acronym Detection" (the D3 paragraph), §26.5.1 "Exposed Resolver Surface".
- FIX-161 — established D3 and the single `StructNamePlural` deriver; recorded this as a follow-up.
- FIX-154 — the `SnakeName` context-field precedent this repeats.

**Resolution notes.** Implemented 2026-08-28. The guarantee lives on the deriver, and the templates
were repointed onto it so the two spellings cannot diverge.

- **`gen/naming.go` — `StructNamePlural` never returns its input.** When `toPlural(structName)`
  gives back the struct name, the English marker is appended instead. `toPlural` is unchanged:
  relationship field naming pluralizes a snake-case SQL name and depends on an already-plural name
  passing through untouched, so widening the rule there would spell `reviewses`. The two
  guarantees are now different functions with the difference documented on both.
- **`gen/inflect.go` — `appendPluralMarker`** factored out of the freeze path and given the full
  English sibilant rule (`es` after `s`, `x`, `z`, `ch`, `sh`; `s` otherwise), so `Fish` →
  `Fishes` rather than `Fishs`. Both routes that cannot produce a distinct plural — a frozen word
  and an uncountable noun — now share one spelling.
- **The funcmap entry is the fix's load-bearing half.** `toPlural` was **unregistered** and
  replaced by `structNamePlural` → `StructNamePlural`, and all **57** template sites across 12
  files were repointed. Every one of them takes `.StructName` or `.TargetStructName`, so none
  wanted the pass-through spelling. Changing the Go function while the templates still called the
  funcmap would have emitted `GetMediaInput` and had `sqlgen lint` resolve `GetMediasInput` — the
  desync FIX-161 closed, reopened one release later. Unregistering rather than keeping both is what
  stops a template author reaching the un-guaranteed spelling, the same reasoning that keeps
  `toSnakeCase` out of the funcmap (FIX-154).

Deviates from this entry's suggested fix on one point, deliberately: it proposed promoting
`StructNamePlural` to a `TableContext` / `ViewContext` field. That would have needed a third field,
`TargetStructNamePlural` on `RelationshipContext`, since `table/get.go.tmpl` and
`table/relationships.go.tmpl` pluralize a relationship's *target* struct name — three fields
carrying one derivation, which is more surface to drift, not less. One funcmap function backed by
the single exported deriver is the tighter shape here.

**Verification.** Failing-first confirmed by reverting only the guarantee (`StructNamePlural` back
to a bare `toPlural` pass-through): `TestStructNamePlural_NeverEqualsInput` fails on 24 dictionary
words, `TestStructNamePlural_KeepsOrdinaryPlurals` on its three uncountable cases,
`TestAPITableContext_UncountableQueryNamesDistinct` fails, and
`TestGenerate_UncountableSchemaFieldsDeclaredOnce` fails with the real defect on disk —
`media_gen.graphqls: Query field "media" declared 2 times` and the same for `series`.

`make check` clean across all 33 modules under `-race`. `TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean.
`make check-examples` clean across all 13 example modules. **Zero golden churn**: `make
update-golden` and `make update-golden-e2e` both ran to completion and changed no file — the new
branch only fires when `toPlural(x) == x`, which no fixture or example table hits, and the funcmap
rename is a pure repoint.

**Tests added.** `gen/inflect_test.go` — `TestStructNamePlural_NeverEqualsInput`, widened from the
frozen set to **every** word in `inflectDictionary` plus every canonical acronym and non-plural
noun, because the invariant is `StructNamePlural(s) != s` for all `s` and stating it that way is
what keeps a third route from reopening this; `TestStructNamePlural_KeepsOrdinaryPlurals`, pinning
that the fallback is a fallback and not a rewrite (`Person` → `People`, `Matrix` → `Matrices`
survive); and `TestToPlural_KeepsAlreadyPluralWords`, pinning the guarantee `toPlural`
deliberately does not share. `gen/inflect_context_test.go` —
`TestAPITableContext_UncountableQueryNamesDistinct` and
`TestGenerate_UncountableSchemaFieldsDeclaredOnce`, which parses the emitted `extend type Query`
block and fails on any field declared twice.

**PRD.** §8.5 gains "The plural of a struct name never equals the struct name" as a rule in its own
right, naming both routes into it (frozen word, uncountable noun), the consequence
(duplicate SDL field + duplicate Go method), the `media` / `series` spellings, and the explicit
scope limit that the guarantee is on the struct-name plural and **not** on pluralization generally.
The funcmap tables in §8.1.3, `guidelines/TEMPLATES.md` and `docs/tracker/IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md` §6.2 are
corrected to the registered set — all three still listed `toSnakeCase`, unregistered since FIX-154.

### FIX-161

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 8, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-154 implementation + auto-review (2026-08-28); verified and scope decided 2026-08-28

**Issue.** **`toSingular` / `toPlural` corrupt any name whose last word is an acronym, and corrupt a
second, non-acronym class of names by the same rule.** The result lands in the Go struct name, the
generated file stem, the `Table<T>` constant, the GraphQL query names, the client accessor, and
every generated error string. Four wrong shapes:

```
user_ips → Singularize → "user_ipsIPS"   → StructName "UserIPSIPS"   → user_ips_ips_gen.go
dns      → Singularize → "dnsDNS"        → StructName "DNSDNS"
client_os→ Singularize → "client_o"      → StructName "ClientO"
lens     → Singularize → "len"           → StructName "Len"          → len_gen.go
```

Twelve acronyms in flect's own base list double (`AES`, `BSS`, `CMOS`, `DES`, `DNS`, `ESS`, `FCS`,
`HTTPS`, `IDS`, `IPS`, `MPLS`, `POTS`); six canonical-only ones truncate (`AWS`, `LHS`, `OS`,
`QPS`, `RHS`, `TLS`); three corrupt on the plural side only (`CSS`→`csses`, `XSS`→`xsses`,
`XSRF`→`xsrves`). Ordinary nouns flect does not know truncate identically — `lens`→`Len`,
`gas`→`Ga`, `bias`→`Bia`, `canvas`→`Canva`, `atlas`→`Atla`. Only a name whose **last** word is
affected — `dns_records` is fine, `user_ips` is not.

`toSingular` is not confined to identifiers: it is in the template funcmap (`gen/funcmap.go:41`)
and `templates/table/*.tmpl` spell `{{ .TableName | toSingular }}` into `fmt.Errorf("scan …")` and
into doc comments, so a corrupted name reaches generated error text as well.

Pre-existing and untouched by FIX-154 for the doubling half: `StructName("user_ips")` is
`UserIPSIPS` both before and after it. FIX-154's removal of `flect.LoadAcronyms` moved the six
canonical-only words from the doubling shape to the truncating shape; both are wrong, so it neither
introduced nor fixed the class.

**Root cause.** Three flect defects reached through `gen/naming.go:107,112` (`toSingular`,
`toPlural`) and `:141,160` (`StructName`, `SnakeName`, which call `flect.Singularize` directly),
plus one exposure.

1. **Doubling.** `flect`'s `xappend` (`ident.go`) uppercases a part it finds in `baseAcronyms`.
   `Ident.ReplaceSuffix(s, p)` then calls `strings.TrimSuffix(i.Original, s)` with the **uppercased**
   `s` against the **lowercase** original. The trim never matches, so the singular is appended to
   the whole input instead of replacing its suffix. It cannot fire on PascalCase input, where the
   trim succeeds — `toPlural("UserIPS")` is `"UserIPSes"`, correct.
2. **Truncation.** When the acronym is *not* in flect's set, no uppercasing happens, the trim
   succeeds, and the generic `-s` singular rule strips the final letter of an acronym that was
   never a plural.
3. **The same generic `-s` strip on ordinary nouns.** `lens`, `gas`, `bias`, `canvas`, `atlas` are
   absent from flect's known-plural map, so the identical rule fires. No acronym is involved; the
   acronym set is simply the systematic instance of a defect whose tail is English-wide.
4. **Process-global inflection.** flect's `custom_data.go` `init()` reads `inflections.json` /
   `acronyms.json` from the CWD or `$INFLECT_PATH` / `$ACRONYMS_PATH`. Measured: a file named
   `inflections.json` in the directory `sqlgen generate` runs from, containing `{"widget":"users"}`,
   silently renames table `users` to struct `Widget` in `widget_gen.go`; containing
   `{"person":"users"}` it **panics before `main` runs** (`panic: map singleToPlural already has an
   entry for person`, `plural_rules.go:227`). After FIX-154 moved acronyms and casing to `strcase`,
   flect is the only remaining process-global input to naming, and `Singularize` / `Pluralize` are
   its only two remaining uses anywhere in the repo.

**Decided fix (2026-08-28).** Four decisions, each measured before being taken.

**D1 — Replace flect with an sqlgen-owned inflector.** New `cmd/sqlgen/gen/inflect.go`; drop
`github.com/gobuffalo/flect` from `cmd/sqlgen/go.mod` entirely. Port flect v1.0.3's
`plural_rules.go` / `singular_rules.go` tables in-tree as frozen data (MIT — attribute in the file
header) rather than hand-authoring English rules: porting keeps every existing answer identical by
construction and drops only the `init()` that reads the CWD. 601 lines across the five relevant
flect files; the ported subset is smaller. This is what closes defect 4.

**D2 — Acronyms are frozen in the singular direction, no exceptions.** If the final word case-folds
to a canonical acronym, `singularize` returns the input unchanged — an acronym is not an English
plural. Explicitly including `IDS` / `IPS`: `user_ips` → `UserIPS`, not `UserIP`. The `ID`/`IDS`,
`IP`/`IPS` and `HTTP`/`HTTPS` prefix pairs make any splitting rule a three-entry judgment call
rather than a mechanical one, and the uniform rule was chosen over it.

**D3 — The plural direction always appends; it is never frozen.** `pluralize` appends `s`, or `es`
when the name already ends in `s`/`S`. It must not be a no-op: `QueryName` and `QueryNamePlural`
land in the same `extend type Query` block (`templates/api/schema.graphqls.tmpl:116,120`), and
`StructName` / `StructNamePlural` declare two methods on one receiver
(`templates/api/resolvers.go.tmpl:49,69`; `seeds.go.tmpl:19,27`), so a frozen plural emits a
duplicate SDL field and a duplicate Go method for any acronym-final table — under the default
operations preset, which has both `Get` and `Connection` on (`config/config.go:1029-1035`).
Appending never inflects an acronym: no stem change, no `-ves`, no doubling. `user_ip` →
`user_ips` is preserved, which relationship field naming depends on (`gen/context_table.go:1117,1157`).

**D4 — The non-acronym `-s` tail is in scope.** A second frozen list beside `canonicalAcronyms`, of
common nouns ending in `s` that are not plurals (`lens`, `gas`, `bias`, `canvas`, `atlas`, …), takes
the same guard as an acronym in both directions. The list is a judgment call, not a closed set;
`tables.<t>.struct_name` stays the escape hatch and the PRD should say so.

The whole rule, both directions:

| Final word | `singularize` | `pluralize` |
|------------|---------------|-------------|
| canonical acronym, or non-plural `-s` noun | unchanged | `+s`, or `+es` if it ends in `s`/`S` |
| anything else | ported English rules | ported English rules |

```
user_ips  → UserIPS  / TableUserIPSes      user_ip   → UserIP / TableUserIPs
client_os → ClientOS / TableClientOSes      tls       → TLS    / TableTLSes
lens      → Lens     / TableLenses          user_xsrf → user_xsrfs  (was user_xsrves)
```

**Also in scope: the fourth `Table<Plural>` deriver.** Five sites build the constant in three
spellings — `gen/context_table.go:392`, `gen/context_view.go:99`, `gen/orchestrate.go:1976,:1984`,
and `cli/lint.go:165`, which calls `flect.Pluralize(gen.StructName(...))` directly and must stay
byte-identical to the generator or the lint type registry desyncs for every acronym-final table.
Same shape FIX-163 closed for file stems: export one `gen.TableConstantName(table, schema,
collisions)` and route all five through it. `StructName` / `SnakeName` must also stop calling
`flect.Singularize` directly (`gen/naming.go:141,160`) — wrapping `toSingular` alone does not reach
them, since neither calls it.

**Regression tests.** Table-driven over `singularize` / `pluralize` with one case per failure mode
(doubling, acronym truncation, non-acronym truncation, `-ves` on an acronym, plus `data`→`datum`
and `user_ip`→`user_ips` pinned as unchanged), `StructName` / `SnakeName` cases for `user_ips`,
`client_os` and `lens`, a `TableConstantName` test asserting all five call sites agree, and a
context-level assertion that an acronym-final table yields distinct `QueryName` /
`QueryNamePlural`. Verify failing-first. Expect **no golden churn**: none of the 34 table and view
names across the repo's `.sql` fixtures is acronym-final or hits any of the three defects
(measured across all of them).

**PRD.** §8.5 gains a statement about inflection, which today it does not cover at all — the
"neither depends on process-global state" sentence is scoped to the acronym set and the splitter
and is accurate as written, so this is an addition rather than a correction. State that
singularization and pluralization are sqlgen-owned and free of process-global state, that a final
canonical acronym is frozen in the singular direction and always takes an appended marker in the
plural direction, and that the non-plural `-s` noun list is a judgment call with
`tables.<t>.struct_name` as the escape hatch.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go:107,112` (`toSingular`, `toPlural`), `:141,160` (`StructName`,
  `SnakeName`), `gen/funcmap.go:41` (template funcmap entry).
- flect v1.0.3 `ident.go:110` (`xappend`, `ReplaceSuffix`), `custom_data.go:14` (the CWD load),
  `plural_rules.go:227` (the init panic), `LICENSE` (MIT).
- Consumers: `gen/context_table.go:392` (`TableNameConstant`), `:1117,:1157` (relationship plural),
  `gen/context_view.go:99`, `gen/orchestrate.go:1976,:1984`, `gen/context_api.go:1338,:1401`
  (`QueryNamePlural`, `StructNamePlural`), `gen/context_client.go:44` (`AccessorName`),
  `cli/lint.go:165`.
- Collision sites for D3: `gen/templates/api/schema.graphqls.tmpl:116,120`,
  `gen/templates/api/resolvers.go.tmpl:49,69`, `gen/templates/api/seeds.go.tmpl:19,27`,
  `config/config.go:1029-1035` (default preset).
- PRD §8.5 "Acronym Detection"; §5.5 struct naming.
- FIX-154 — removed the `flect.LoadAcronyms` init that produced half this behavior.
- FIX-163 — the same duplicate-deriver shape, closed for file stems.

**Resolution notes.** Implemented as decided (2026-08-28). The engine is sqlgen's own; the
dependency is gone.

- **`cmd/sqlgen/gen/inflect.go`** (new) — `singularize` / `pluralize` over frozen in-tree tables.
  flect's `dictionary` and `singularToPluralSuffixList` are ported verbatim (MIT, attributed in the
  file header) along with its map- and rule-construction order, so every name that inflected
  correctly still inflects to the same word by construction rather than by argument. What is *not*
  ported is `Ident`: `ReplaceSuffix` trims an uppercased acronym off a lowercase original, the trim
  fails, and the singular is appended to the whole input. `splitLastWord` returns `(prefix, word)`
  by index instead, so `prefix+word` is the input byte for byte and the append shape cannot occur.
  flect's two `init()` panics on a duplicate entry are replaced by first-entry-wins plus
  `TestInflectDictionary_NoDuplicates`.
- **The freeze** — `isInflectionFrozen` over `canonicalAcronyms` ∪ `nonPluralSNouns` (19 entries,
  each verified corrupted before it was added). Singular returns the input; plural appends `s`, or
  `es` when the name already ends in `s`. `corps` was deliberately left out: appending spells
  `corpses`, a different word's plural.
- **`gen/naming.go`** — `toSingular` / `toPlural` route to the inflector, and `StructName` /
  `SnakeName` now call `toSingular` instead of reaching past it to `flect.Singularize` directly
  (they were the two sites "wrap both helpers" would have missed).
- **Two exported derivers replace five private ones.** `StructNamePlural(structName)` and
  `TableConstantName(table, schema, collisions)`; `gen/context_table.go:392`,
  `gen/context_view.go:99`, `gen/orchestrate.go:1976,:1984`, `gen/context_api.go:1338,:1401`,
  `gen/context_client.go:44` and `cli/lint.go:165` all go through them. `TableNameEntry.ConstantName`
  now carries the whole constant and `templates/tablename.go.tmpl` emits it verbatim rather than
  prefixing `Table` itself — byte-identical output, and one less place the name is assembled.
- **`cmd/sqlgen/go.mod` / `go.sum`** — `github.com/gobuffalo/flect` removed. It has no remaining

- **`guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md`** — `inflect.go` added to the `gen/` map; the flect row dropped

depends on process-global state" sentence is scoped to the acronym set and the splitter and was
