- Sanity check while in the files: `toSnakeCase`'s comment (`naming.go:37-46`) is accurate and
  should stay; it is the direction gqlgen never observes.

Verify by grepping `go_initialisms` / `initialisms` across `--include='*.go' --include='*.tmpl'`
afterwards — the only surviving hits should be in this tracker's historical FIX-152/FIX-155 text.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go:15-19`, `:30-32`; `cmd/sqlgen/gen/acronyms.go:12-19`, `:25-27`,
  `:32-34`, `:44-45`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/merge.go:14-48` (`MergeInput` — no initialism field);
  `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_field_overrides.go` (the mechanism that actually ships).
- PRD §8.5:2337 (the correct rule), §8.5:2359 (the correct mixed-case rationale), §26.5.6:11039
  ("Go field naming").
- FIX-152 / FIX-155 — the change (`84d90ab`) that superseded the described mechanism.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-27. Comments only — no code, template, golden or test-body
change; the diff is 4 files, all comment prose (3 Go doc comments + 1 SQL fixture header).

- `gen/naming.go` — `toPascalCase`'s second paragraph now states the real invariant: the spelling
  is sqlgen's own and deliberately unshared, and generated code may name a gqlgen-emitted field
  because `APIGoFieldOverrides` *dictates* it as `models.<T>.fields.<f>.fieldName` (§26.5.6 "Go
  field naming"), with prediction named as the FIX-152 / FIX-155 defect. `toCamelCase`'s paragraph
  now says the camelCase result is the GraphQL field name — the join key — and that the Go name on
  gqlgen's side is stated rather than derived back out of it, because camelization is lossy at a
  digit boundary. `toSnakeCase`'s comment was checked and left as-is (accurate).
- `gen/acronyms.go` — head comment drops the `go_initialisms` push and the non-existent §26.5.6
  "Go initialism alignment" subsection, replacing both with the dictation pointer and the
  "sharing a list was tried and is insufficient" reason (PRD §8.5:2388). `UID` dropped from the
  CommonInitialisms example list (it is excluded 11 lines below); the source is now described as
  adopted for its own sake, matching the PRD's wording. Mixed-case exclusion rationale replaced
  with PRD §8.5:2410's — the caser matches a whole word case-folded to upper, so `Mbps`/`WiFi`
  could never fire — verified against both engines: `strcase`'s `convert.go:230-243` upper-cases
  the word before the map lookup, and flect's is `baseAcronyms[strings.ToUpper(word)]`
  (`ident.go:37,75`). The already-correct tail (`No entry is excluded on gqlgen's account`) was
  kept and de-duplicated against the rewritten head.
- `testdata/examples/graphql/schema.sql` — the FIX-152 fixture header carried the same stale
  push (found by auto-review, see F3 below).
- **Beyond the filed scope, same defect:** the sortedness rationale (`Sorted so CanonicalAcronyms
  emits deterministically into the merged gqlgen.yml`) named a symbol that no longer exists — the
  set is unexported and nothing writes a gqlgen.yml key — and `acronyms_test.go:80-84` repeated
  both that claim and the "gqlgen upper-cases every configured initialism" one. Both rewritten:
  sorting is now justified as hand-maintenance hygiene (it puts prefix pairs like UI/UID adjacent
  for review), uppercase by the caser's fold. Confirmed order-independent first — flect stores
  acronyms in a `map[string]bool` (`custom_data.go:56-59`) and `identCaser` takes a set, so no
  behavior rides on the order.

**Auto-review (applied).** The reviewer confirmed 7/8 PRD rows PASS, 0 non-comment lines changed
under `cmd/sqlgen/gen/`, and independently re-verified the mixed-case rationale against both
upstreams. It surfaced three accuracy findings, all fixed in the same change:

1. **F1 — `naming.go` `toCamelCase`, in-diff.** The rewrite claimed the camelCase result *is* the
   GraphQL field name. Only true under the default casing: `graphQLFieldName`
   (`gen/context_api.go:2283-2288`) returns `prefixIfDigitLeading(sqlName, "col_")` under
   `field_casing: snake_case` and never calls `toCamelCase`, which also spells Go-side client
   field and query names (`gen/context_client.go:24-54`) that gqlgen never sees. Now scoped to the
   default casing with both other roles named; the dictation point moved to its own paragraph so
   it holds either way.
2. **F2 — `acronyms.go` tail, in-diff.** The pre-existing sentence FIX-157 judged "already
   correct" is not: "a token that would read badly in gqlgen's output cannot reach it" contradicts
   the very next paragraph, because `APIGoFieldOverrides` emits `GoFieldName` ← `FieldName` ←
   `toPascalCase` ← this set, so an entry *does* reach gqlgen's output — dictated. PRD §8.5:2388
   keeps the qualifier the tail dropped ("a list **both engines consult**"). Rewritten to the true
   claim: gqlgen never consults the set, it receives whatever spelling the set produces, so
   membership is decided purely by sqlgen-side consequences.
3. **F3 — sibling staleness, out of diff.** `testdata/examples/graphql/schema.sql:186-188` — the
   FIX-152 fixture's own header — still said the set was "pushed into gqlgen as `go_initialisms`",
   while its `line2_id` note 20 lines down correctly describes dictation. The exact head/tail split
   FIX-157 diagnosed, in a third file. Fixed; the original verification grep missed it because it
   passed `--include='*.go' --include='*.tmpl' --include='*.yml'` and the fixture is `.sql`.

**Verification.** `make check` clean (33 modules, `-race`, exit 0) and `make check-examples` clean
(13 example modules against real DBs, exit 0), both re-run after the auto-review edits —
`check-examples` because `cmd/sqlgen/gen/**` and `testdata/examples/**` are on the path-based E2E
trigger list. `git status` after the sweep shows no golden drift, confirming the `schema.sql`
comment edit does not reach generated output (nothing hashes the schema text; the manifest carries
no checksum). Final grep for `go_initialisms` with **no** `--include` filter returns zero hits
outside this tracker's historical FIX-152 / FIX-155 / FIX-157 text.

**Also corrected (was initially deferred).** `identCaser`'s doc comment (`acronyms.go:83-91`) said
the split rules "must agree with gqlgen's `templates.ToGo`" and that matching the lower→digit rule
is "a requirement rather than a preference" — and PRD §8.5 "Word splitting" said the same, so it
was first held back as a spec question rather than a comment fix. Settled by checking gqlgen
instead: bind-target matching is `equalFieldName`
(`gqlgen@v0.17.90/codegen/util.go:51-57`, called from `codegen/field.go:354,418`), which is
`strings.EqualFold` after stripping underscores. A word-split difference only moves *case*, never
the letter/digit sequence, so it cannot break a bind — and on gqlgen-*generated* types nothing is
derived at all, since the names are dictated. The parity claim is therefore stale in the same way
the push was, and it contradicted §8.5:2388 ("deliberately not shared with gqlgen") two paragraphs
above it.

Both the comment and the PRD sentence now give the real reason the rules are frozen: the split
decides the **published GraphQL field name** (`userID` and `userId` are distinct fields on the
wire) and every generated Go identifier, so moving it re-spells a live API. The rule itself is
unchanged — behavior, goldens and tests are untouched; only the stated reason moves. Recorded here
rather than opened as a new FIX: a comment-accuracy fix that spawns its own tracker entries is a
waterfall, and this is the same defect, same session, same two files.

### FIX-156

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 8, cmd/sqlgen/config
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-153 scoping audit (2026-08-27)

**Issue.** **`tables.<table>.column_map.<column>.type` and `.import` are declared and documented
but never read — and `type_map`, the one wired per-column type override, cannot carry an import.
Together that means a per-column override to an *external* Go type is unexpressible today.**

The two halves compound. Silently ignoring `column_map.<col>.type` would be survivable if
`type_map` covered the same ground, and PRD:721 presents it as exactly that ("a shorthand for
overriding only the Go type of a column"). It does not: the `type_map` branch resolves the type
and drops the import. Measured against the resolver (`postgres`, non-nullable `numeric`):

```
type_map literal      resolved Name       Import
decimal.Decimal       decimal.Decimal     ""              ← no import emitted
uuid.UUID             uuid.UUID           ""
netip.Addr            netip.Addr          ""
json.RawMessage       json.RawMessage     "encoding/json" ← only because it is a known type
```

`decimal.Decimal` is **the PRD's own `type_map` example** (PRD:728). The generated file compiles
only when some *other* column independently pulls the package in — via `overrides.types`, which
does carry an `import`. In the tree today that accident always holds: the only `type_map` entries
in any fixture are `int32` (builtin) and `Address` (same-package composite), so nothing covers the
external case and nothing fails.

**Root cause.** `ColumnOverride.Type` / `.Import` are declared at `config/config.go:560-561`; the
only field of `tableCfg.ColumnMap` that reaches the type resolver is nothing at all — the call
sites pass `tableCfg.TypeMap` (`gen/context_table.go:484`, `gen/context_tenancy.go:197`). Inside
the resolver, step 1 short-circuits before the override chain that knows about imports:

- `Resolver.Resolve` (`gotype/gotype.go:381-388`) — `if goType, ok := tableTypeMap[columnName]; ok
  { return FromLiteral(goType, nullable) }`, returning before `resolveByType` and therefore before
  `overrides.types` is ever consulted.
- `FromLiteral` (`gotype/gotype.go:693-704`) sets `Import` only from `knownGoTypes`
  (`gotype/gotype.go:172-197`) — a fixed 24-entry registry of builtins plus `time`, `net`,
  `encoding/json` and `types.JSON`. Everything else falls to `deriveZeroValue` with an empty
  import.
- `ColumnContext.Import` is `gt.Import` (`gen/context_table.go:511`) and `collectColumnImports`
  (`gen/context_table.go:469`) is the only source of per-column imports, so an empty one is a
  missing import line.

`ResolveAggregate` (`gotype/gotype.go:403-409`) has the same step-1 short-circuit for view
columns.

**Suggested fix.** Wire `.type` / `.import` as the per-column escape hatch they are documented to
be, and make the `type_map` / `column_map` split honest rather than redundant.

1. **Resolve `column_map` type overrides in `buildColumnContext`** (`gen/context_table.go:484`),
   ahead of `Resolver.Resolve`: when `override.Type != ""`, build the `GoType` from
   `FromLiteral(override.Type, col.Nullable)` and set `Import` from `override.Import` when
   non-empty (falling back to the `knownGoTypes` value so `column_map.type: time.Time` still works
   without an explicit import). Precedence over `type_map` is already specified — PRD:731,
   PRD:1935.
   Prefer this over threading a per-column `map[string]config.TypeOverride` into `Resolver.Resolve`:
   `column_map`-beats-`type_map` is a config-precedence decision, not a type-resolution one, and
   the resolver's six-step chain and signature stay untouched. Apply the same shape at
   `gen/context_tenancy.go:197` so a tenant column's override is honoured.
2. **Decide the nullable story explicitly.** `column_map` has no `nullable:` sub-field, so a
   nullable column overridden this way gets `FromLiteral`'s treatment — `*T`, or bare `T` for
   natively-nilable types. It does **not** get the Null-wrapper machinery `overrides.types`
   offers via `TypeOverride.Nullable` (`config/config.go:419-424`). Either document that
   asymmetry in §8.5 or route `column_map` through a synthesised `TypeOverride`; documenting is
   the smaller change and matches how `type_map` already behaves.
3. **Close the `type_map` import gap** in the same pass, one of two ways — decide explicitly:
   (a) document `type_map` as builtin / same-package only and point at `column_map.type` +
   `.import` for anything external (makes the two features non-redundant and needs no code), or
   (b) let a `type_map` literal fall through to `overrides.types` for its import when the SQL type
   has an entry. **(a) is the recommendation** — (b) mixes a by-column and a by-SQL-type lookup and
   would resolve differently depending on an unrelated column's config.
4. **Validation** (`config/validate.go`, alongside FIX-153's shipped column-name checks):
   - `import` set without `type` is an error — an import with nothing to import for;
   - `type` must be a non-empty, syntactically plausible Go type literal;
   - `type` on a column removed by `exclude_columns` is an error (same shape as the existing
     `access` rule, `config/validate.go:73-77`);
   - the column must exist on the parsed table (post-parse phase).

**Tests (verified failing-first).**

- `gotype` — pin the measured table above so the `type_map` import behavior is asserted rather
  than incidental, whichever way step 3 is decided.
- `gen/context_test.go` — `column_map.<col>.type` + `.import` resolves the Go type, emits the
  import through `collectColumnImports`, and beats a conflicting `type_map` entry for the same
  column.
- `config/validate_test.go` — the four rules in step 4.
- End-to-end: a fixture column carrying an external type via `column_map` in one of the
  `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/*` trees, so the emitted import is compiled rather than asserted.
  Choosing a package the example already depends on keeps the fixture's `go.mod` untouched.

**Doc / PRD deltas.**
- PRD § "Column Overrides" (PRD:673-682) — `type` / `import` rows stay; add the nullable-asymmetry
  note from step 2.
- PRD § "Type Map" (PRD:719-731) — state the import limitation and the resulting division of
  labour; the `price: decimal.Decimal` example at PRD:728 is currently misleading and should
  either move to `column_map` or gain the caveat.
- PRD config-error table (~PRD:1100) — rows for the step-4 validations.

**Relationship to FIX-153.** Same class (a declared, documented, unread `ColumnOverride` field),
same file, adjacent validation. Deliberately split because the `.name` fix is a naming-surface
change touching relationships, tenancy, soft-delete, templates and the gqlgen handoff, while this
one is confined to type resolution — and because this one carries a real design question
(the `type_map` overlap) that should not ride on a rename. **FIX-153 landed 2026-08-27**, so the
validation scaffolding already exists: `validateColumnNameOverrides` (pre-parse) and
`validateColumnNameOverridesSchema` (post-parse) in `config/validate.go` are the shape to extend
— add the step-4 rules alongside them rather than starting a third walk over `ColumnMap`. The
resolution point for the Go type is likewise the sibling of `resolveColumnFieldName`
(`gen/context_table.go`), which FIX-153 introduced next to `buildColumnContext`'s resolver call.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:556-561` (`ColumnOverride`), `:419-424` (`TypeOverride` — the
  import-bearing shape `column_map` lacks).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go:172-197` (`knownGoTypes`), `:381-388` (`Resolve` step 1),
  `:403-409` (`ResolveAggregate` step 1), `:693-704` (`FromLiteral`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:469` (`collectColumnImports`), `:484`, `:511`;
  `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_tenancy.go:197`.
- PRD:656-682 (Column Overrides), PRD:719-731 (Type Map), PRD:1935 (`column_map` beats
  `type_map`).
- FIX-153 (resolved 2026-08-27) — the sibling `.name` gap; its validators and its
  `resolveColumnFieldName` are the shape this fix extends.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-27. `column_map.<col>.type` / `.import` are now read.
`resolveColumnGoType` (`gen/context_table.go`, sibling of FIX-153's `resolveColumnFieldName`)
applies the override ahead of `Resolver.Resolve` — `.import` wins when set, otherwise the
`knownGoTypes` value stands, so `type: time.Time` still needs no import. Called from
`buildColumnContext` and from `resolveTenantColumnType` (`gen/context_tenancy.go`), so a tenant
column's override reaches the tenancy context and the row struct identically; §29.2.4's
`tenancy.type` still outranks it, with `column_map` sitting inside step 3 ahead of `type_map`.
The resolver's six-step chain and signature are untouched.

**Decisions taken** (confirmed with the user before implementation, all three as recommended):
(3) **doc-only split** — `type_map` stays builtin / same-package only, no fallthrough to
`overrides.types`; (2) **hard error** for a package-qualified literal that could never be
imported, on both surfaces; (4→step 2) **document the nullable asymmetry** rather than add a
`nullable:` sub-field — a nullable `column_map` override resolves to `*T` (bare `T` when natively
nilable), never a Null wrapper.

**Deviation from step 4.** The registry-aware guardrail cannot live in `config/validate.go`:
`gotype` imports `config`, so the reverse edge is an import cycle. It lives in
`gen.validateColumnTypeLiterals`, called from `buildSingleTableContext` next to
`validateResolvedFieldNames` — the same precedent FIX-153 set for rules needing the type /
naming engine, and it reads the registry through a new exported `gotype.KnownLiteral`. The three
rules that need no registry stayed in `config/validate.go` as specified, folded into FIX-153's
existing walks rather than a third pass: `validateColumnNameOverrides` →
`validateColumnOverrides` (`.name` rules + `.type` must parse as a Go type expression via
`isGoTypeExpression`, `.import` without `.type` is an error, either field on an
`exclude_columns` column is an error) and `validateColumnNameOverridesSchema` →
`validateColumnOverridesSchema` (column must exist, now for `.type` as well as `.name`).

**Docs.** Beyond the three deltas the entry listed, **PRD §7.1 omitted `column_map.<col>.type`
from the canonical resolution chain entirely** — the doc-level root of the confusion. It is now
step 1 of six, with the per-column / per-SQL-type split, the import limitation and the
nullable-wrapper restriction stated there. §26.4.1-adjacent §29.2.4 step 3 now names the column's
own resolution rather than "type-override map". "Column Overrides" gained the nullable note and
precise `type` / `import` rows; "Type Map" gained the import limitation, the division of labour,
and the `price: decimal.Decimal` example moved out of `type_map` into `column_map`; the
config-error table gained five rows.

**Tests** (all verified failing-first by stashing the source change and keeping the tests):
`gotype/gotype_test.go::TestTypeMapLiteralImports` pins the measured table so `type_map`'s import
behavior is asserted rather than incidental; `gen/column_type_override_test.go` covers resolution,
import emission through `collectColumnImports`, `column_map` beating `type_map`, both nullable
shapes, and the guardrail with its negative control; `gen/context_tenancy_test.go` covers the
tenant-column override and the `tenancy.type` precedence it must not disturb;
`config/column_type_validate_test.go` covers the four config rules.

**Fixtures.** `postgres` — `audit.users.source_ip INET` retyped to `netip.Addr` + `net/netip`
(stdlib, no `go.mod` change; `net/netip` appears in `models_gen.go` only because of the
override), with a value round-tripped through pgx in `TestAuditUserCRUD`. `graphql` —
`order_items.external_ref TEXT` retyped to `uuid.UUID`, round-tripped through the live gqlgen
handler in `TestScalars/UUIDViaColumnMapOverride`, proving the override survives the gqlgen
handoff onto the existing `UUID` scalar. It also demonstrates the nullable asymmetry concretely:
the field is `*uuid.UUID` carrying the `UUID` scalar, where this example's `uuid` columns resolve
through `overrides.types.uuid.nullable` to `uuid.NullUUID` and the `NullUUID` scalar. Two placement constraints found the hard way and
recorded in the fixture comments: **not** `users` (it is FIX-066's "no numeric non-PK columns"
fixture — a decimal column there flips `UpdateUser`'s signature and strands the checked-in
resolver body) and **not** `orders` (`TestWrapperRewriter_PanicStubFlipToDelegation` injects its
own `tables.orders` entry, which collides as a duplicate YAML key). Both examples use a single
`models_gen.go`, so import emission is proven by the postgres tree; the graphql tree proves the
gqlgen handoff.

**Verification.** `make check` clean (33 modules, `-race`); `make check-examples` clean (13
example modules against real DBs); `TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean and idempotent across two
consecutive `-update-e2e` runs.

**Auto-review follow-ups (applied).** The reviewer confirmed bug closure 6/6 with 0 blocking
findings and surfaced five issues; four were addressed in the same change. (1) The graphql fixture
originally used `decimal.Decimal` on a TEXT column, which enrolled it in the Increment surface —
`OrderItemIncrementDiscount` plus `discount_inc` / `discount_dec`, generating `SET "col" = "col" +
$1` against text. Rerouted to `uuid.UUID` on `order_items.external_ref`: still a registry scalar,
so the gqlgen handoff is still proven, but not arithmetic. The underlying gap — increment
eligibility keys on the resolved Go type with no SQL-type sanity check, unlike tenancy's
`checkOverrideAgainstSQLType` — is pre-existing (reachable via `type_map` alone) and is logged as
**FIX-160**. (2) `isGoTypeExpression` rejected generic instantiations
(`omittable.Value[string]`); it now handles `*ast.IndexExpr` / `*ast.IndexListExpr`, recurses into
slice / map / chan element types, and drops a dead `*ast.Ellipsis` arm and the `go/types`
dependency. (3) `type_map` values got no syntax check at all — the same defect class this fix
addresses — so `validateTypeMapLiterals` now applies the same rule there. (4) The two
registry-aware rows were added to a §4.13 table introduced as "validated immediately after
loading, before parsing or generation begins", but they fire during generation; §4.13 now
documents a third **resolution-level** phase and marks the three rows that belong to it, which
also covers FIX-153's collision rule (same pre-existing property). The fifth finding — the
guardrail is skipped for excluded / PK-less tables, a narrow unreachable path via
`BuildTenancyContext` — is recorded here rather than fixed; nothing in the tree reaches it.

**Spun off.** Scoping the graphql fixture surfaced that `api.graphql.scalars` is validated in two
places and read nowhere — `graphQLTypeForGoType` falls through to `String` for any unknown Go
type — which is why that fixture uses a registry scalar rather than `netip.Addr`. Logged as
**FIX-159** (same declared-but-unread class), with the two design questions it carries.

### FIX-155

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-152 auto-review (2026-08-27)

**Issue.** **`sqlgen generate` still emits non-compiling filter and input translators for any
column where an acronym directly follows a digit-terminated word**, under the default
`field_casing: camel_case`. FIX-152 closed the acronym-*set* disagreement; this is a second,
independent mechanism in the same class that FIX-152's Issue text never covered, and it is
pre-existing rather than introduced by that fix.

Confirmed against real gqlgen v0.17.90 with FIX-152's `go_initialisms` alignment applied:

| Column | GraphQL field | sqlgen Go | gqlgen Go |
|---|---|---|---|
| `line2_id` | `line2ID` | `Line2ID` | `Line2id` |
| `address2_id` | `address2ID` | `Address2ID` | `Address2id` |
| `s3_url` | `s3URL` | `S3URL` | `S3url` |
| `md5_id` | `md5ID` | `Md5ID` | `Md5id` |
| `sha256_id` | `sha256ID` | `Sha256ID` | `Sha256id` |
| `x509_id` | `x509ID` | `X509ID` | `X509id` |

`line2_id` and `address2_id` are ordinary column names (postal address line 2). 162 of the 163
canonical acronyms are affected in the `<word><digit>_<acronym>` shape. Failure mode is identical
to FIX-152: `in.Line2ID undefined (type model.EventFilter has no field or method Line2ID, but
does have field Line2id)`.

**Root cause.** Camelization is lossy at this boundary and gqlgen cannot recover it. sqlgen emits
the GraphQL field name `line2ID`; gqlgen's `wordWalker` breaks only on lower→non-lower, so after
the `line`/`2` break it sees `2ID` as a single run with no seam before the acronym and lower-cases
it to `id`. sqlgen's splitter (`SplitBeforeNumber`, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/acronyms.go`) keeps `2` and
`ID` as separate words and uppercases the acronym.

This is **casing-mode-specific**: under `field_casing: snake_case` the GraphQL field name is the
raw column, gqlgen sees the underscore, and there are **zero** divergences. So the correct
gqlgen-side Go name genuinely differs per casing mode, which means the two names FIX-152 collapsed
into one — `APIFilterField.GoFieldName` (gqlgen's spelling) and `.ModelFieldName` (sqlgen's) —
cannot stay equal in camel mode.

**Suggested fix.** Three options, none free; pick deliberately:
- **Derive `GoFieldName` from the GraphQL field name** using gqlgen's word-walker semantics, which
  is what `context_api.go:540-543`'s doc comment has always claimed. Restores the two-name split
  and is exact, but requires vendoring the walker — the drift risk FIX-152 explicitly rejected
  (the walker's ID/IP carve-out changed between v0.17.44 and v0.17.94).
- **Decline to uppercase an acronym that directly follows a digit** in `identCaser`, so sqlgen
  emits `Line2Id` and matches gqlgen in camel mode. Cheap and local, but it desynchronizes
  `snake_case` mode, where gqlgen produces `Line2ID` — so it trades one broken mode for the other
  unless the rule is made casing-aware.
- **Reject the shape at codegen time** with a clear error naming the column and pointing at a
  rename, on the same "impossible to emit something the translator cannot handle" principle as
  §26.5.3's completeness lint. Honest and safe, but refuses ordinary schemas.
- Regression test: extend `cmd/sqlgen/gen/acronyms_test.go` with the six columns above, and add
  at least `line2_id` to the `graphql` example so a golden compiles it against real gqlgen.
  Verify failing-first — it fails today.

**References.**
- FIX-152 — same class, different mechanism; its alignment work is the precondition for this one.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/acronyms.go` (`identCaser`, `SplitBeforeNumber`), `cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:540-543` (`GoFieldName`'s stated contract), `:1886-1888`
  (`graphQLFieldName`), `buildAPIFilterFields`, `buildAPIInputFields`.
- gqlgen `codegen/templates/templates.go` (`wordWalker`) — the lower→non-lower break rule.
- PRD §8.5 "Word splitting", §26.5.6 "Go initialism alignment".

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-27 alongside FIX-152, by removing the mechanism rather
than choosing among the three suggested options — all three assumed sqlgen must reproduce gqlgen's
spelling. It does not have to: gqlgen honours `models.<Type>.fields.<field>.fieldName` in place of
its own `templates.ToGo` result, for generated model fields (`plugin/modelgen/models.go:436-439`)
and for resolver method names (`codegen/field.go:172`) alike. sqlgen now emits one such entry per
referenced identifier (`gen/api_field_overrides.go`), so the lossy-camelization boundary this entry
documents is never consulted — the name is stated, not derived.

`line2_id`, `address2_id` and `s3_url` were added to the `graphql` example's `events` table and
compile against real gqlgen v0.17.90 as `Line2ID` / `Address2ID` / `S3URL`; the same three are
pinned as unit cases in `gen/acronyms_test.go`. The casing-mode split this entry identified —
`snake_case` diverging where `camel_case` agrees and vice versa — is moot for the same reason.

### FIX-153

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 8, cmd/sqlgen/config
- **Surfaced by:** FIX-152 auto-review (2026-08-27)
- **Scoped:** 2026-08-27 — decision taken (wire it), full plan below

**Issue.** **`tables.<table>.column_map.<column>.name` is documented as the Go field-name override
but is never read by the generator.** A consumer who sets it gets silence, not an error and not an
override. PRD §8.5 and the config reference (§ "Table Configuration", `name: APIKey  # fix acronym
casing`) both advertise it.

**Root cause.** `ColumnOverride.Name` is declared at `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:558`, but the
only fields read out of `tableCfg.ColumnMap` are `.Access` (`gen/context_table.go:486`) and
`.Description` (`:558`). The field name is assigned unconditionally at `gen/context_table.go:509`
as `FieldName: FieldName(col.Name)`.

**Second-order sites (audited 2026-08-27).** Almost every downstream consumer already reads
`col.FieldName` off `ColumnContext` — the model/filter/input/FieldOptions builders
(`context_table.go:1106`, `:1262`, `:1275`, `:1357`, `:1675`, `:1706`), the API surface
(`context_api.go:1940`, `:1444`, `:1762`), the manifest (`manifest/builder.go:355`, `:470`,
`:857`, `:1453`) and the event hook contexts (`context_event.go:179`, `:201`, `:206`). Template
locals are `.FieldName | toCamelCase | safeGoIdent`, so they follow too. **Six sites bypass it and
recompute from the raw SQL name** — each is a Go identifier that would stop resolving the moment a
rename lands:

| Site | Expression | Resolves against |
|---|---|---|
| `gen/context_table.go:838` | `FKFieldName: FieldName(r.FKColumn)` | the **target** table's column |
| `gen/context_table.go:870` | `FKFieldName: FieldName(r.FK)` | the **target** table's column |
| `gen/context_api.go:1662` | `base := toPascalCase(col.Name)` (`SetGoField` / `IncGoField` / `DecGoField`) | own table |
| `gen/context_tenancy.go:384` | `ctx.FieldName = FieldName(entry.Column)` | own table |
| `templates/table/{count,client,delete,exists,get,pagination,stream}.go.tmpl` — 17 sites | `.SoftDelete.Column \| toPascalCase` | own table |
| `templates/table/update.go.tmpl:87,362,528,763` | `input.{{ . \| toPascalCase }}` over `.UpdateColumns` | own table |

`FKFieldName` is the sharp one: `get.go.tmpl:370,385,417` spells `filter.<FKFieldName>`,
`relFieldOptions.<FKFieldName>` and `r.<FKFieldName>` on the **target** struct, so it must resolve
through the *target* table's `column_map`, which `relationshipToContext` cannot see.
`conflictConstantSuffix` (`context_table.go:1001`) also PascalCases column names, but into
constant *names* (`UserConflictEmail`), not field references — deliberately left on the SQL name.

**Decision (2026-08-27) — wire it.** This is the documented escape hatch for the cases acronym
detection gets wrong (`api_key` → `APIKey`) and for the digit-leading `Col<N>…` names PRD §8.5
already points at it for. Deleting it would remove the only lever a consumer has over a generated
identifier, and §8.5's canonical acronym set is explicitly *not* consumer-configurable, so there
is no substitute. Wire it as a **Go-identifier-only** rename.

**Rename scope (normative).**

| Surface | Follows the override? |
|---|---|
| Entity struct field, composite-PK struct, `<T>Filter`, `Create/Update<T>Input` (+ `_inc`/`_dec`), `<T>FieldOptions`, sorter, cache, template locals | **Yes** |
| `FKFieldName` on relationships pointing *at* the renamed column | **Yes** (via the target table) |
| Tenancy `FieldName`, soft-delete field reference, auto-update-column field reference | **Yes** |
| Manifest `go_field` | **Yes** |
| `<T>IncrementXxx` constant names (the enum and the resolver constant must agree) | **Yes** |
| `db:` / `json:` struct tags, SQL column constants, `<T>ConflictXxx` constant names | **No** — SQL name |
| GraphQL field name, `<T>SortField` enum value | **No** — wire contract, stays SQL-derived |

The rule to write into the PRD: *the override renames the Go identifier and nothing a client can
observe.* A consumer who wants a different GraphQL field name has `api.graphql.field_casing`; a
per-column GraphQL rename is a separate feature and is not in the PRD.

**Why the FIX-152 hazard no longer applies.** The original entry warned that a Go-only rename on
an API-exposed column would reintroduce the FIX-152 mismatch. That was true against the *predict*
architecture. Commit `84d90ab` replaced prediction with **dictation**: `APIGoFieldOverrides`
(`gen/api_field_overrides.go`) emits `models.<Type>.fields.<field>.fieldName` into the temp
gqlgen.yml for every gqlgen-*generated* type sqlgen references, and gqlgen's modelgen discards its
own `templates.ToGo` result when that key is present. Those entries are sourced from
`GoFieldName`, which is `col.FieldName` (`context_api.go:1444`, `:1762`, `:1940`) — so a rename
propagates into gqlgen's generated `<T>Filter` / `Create<T>Input` / `Update<T>Input` structs
automatically and the translators keep matching. **No change is needed for the generated types.**

**The one new gqlgen obligation — bound row types.** `api_field_overrides.go` deliberately omits
bound types ("gqlgen matches fields against the consumer's own struct with a case-insensitive
comparison and no override applies"). That premise holds only while the Go field is derived from
the GraphQL name. `cli/graphql.go:270` binds the row type (`models[t.StructName] = <pkg>.<T>`),
and gqlgen resolves a bound field via `findBindTarget(obj.Type, ToGo(gqlName))` →
`equalFieldName` (case-insensitive, `_`-stripped — `codegen/field.go:195`, `codegen/util.go:51`).
A renamed field breaks that match: GraphQL `ipAddr` would look for `IpAddr`/`IPAddr` and never
find `ClientIP`. `codegen/field.go:172-173` honours `fields.<f>.fieldName` for bound types too, so
the fix is to emit the row-type entry **for renamed columns only** — gated on an explicit
`FieldNameOverridden` flag threaded `ColumnContext` → `APIFieldContext`, never on a comparison
against a predicted spelling. Emitting it unconditionally for every row field also works and
churns no golden (the merged config is a temp file), but it inflates every merged gqlgen.yml and
weakens the "dictate only what must be dictated" shape; prefer the gate.

**Implementation plan.**

1. **`gen/context_table.go:509` — the single resolution point.** Resolve
   `tableCfg.ColumnMap[col.Name].Name` when non-empty, else `FieldName(col.Name)`. Add
   `FieldNameOverridden bool` to `ColumnContext` alongside it.
2. **Relationship FKs.** Delete `FKFieldName: FieldName(...)` from `relationshipToContext`
   (`:838`) and `configRelationshipToContext` (`:870`); resolve it in the existing second pass
   `wireRelationshipFKMetadata` (`context_table.go:52`, def `:57`), which already looks the FK
   column up on the target table's built context for `FKGoType` / `FKNullable` /
   `FKColumnGoType`. Same lookup, one more field — no config threading, one call site.
3. **`gen/context_api.go:1662`.** `base := toPascalCase(col.Name)` → `base := col.FieldName`.
   Byte-identical without an override (`FieldName` *is* `toPascalCase`), and `:1671` already
   reads `col.FieldName` for `IncColumnConst`.
4. **`gen/context_tenancy.go:384`.** `attachTenancyToTables` runs after the columns are built —
   look `entry.Column` up in `tc.Columns` and take its `FieldName`; fall back to
   `FieldName(entry.Column)` if absent. `context_event.go:148` reads `t.Tenancy.FieldName`, so
   the event surface follows for free.
5. **Soft delete.** Add `FieldName string` to `SoftDeleteContext` (`context.go:214`), populate at
   `context_table.go:301` from the built column, and replace all 17
   `.SoftDelete.Column | toPascalCase` template sites with `.SoftDelete.FieldName`. Leave the
   ~20 `printf "%q" .SoftDelete.Column` sites alone — those are SQL names.
6. **Auto-update columns.** `TableContext.UpdateColumns []string` (`context.go:452`) carries only
   the SQL name while `update.go.tmpl` needs both. Promote it to a two-field struct
   (`{Name, FieldName}`) and update the four `range .UpdateColumns` blocks: `{{ . }}` → `{{ .Name }}`
   for the `setClauses` key, `{{ . | toPascalCase }}` → `{{ .FieldName }}` for the input field.
   `manifest/builder.go:1006` reads `cfg.Generation.UpdateColumns` (config, not context) and is
   unaffected.
7. **gqlgen row-type binding.** In `tableGoFieldOverrides` (`api_field_overrides.go:76`), emit
   `set(t.StructName, f.GraphQLName, f.GoFieldName)` for each field whose column carries an
   override. Update the function's doc comment — the "bound types never appear" claim becomes
   "bound types appear only for an explicitly renamed field".
8. **Validation** (below) in `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go`.

**Validation rules.** Two phases, mirroring the `access` split:

- Pre-parse, in `validateColumnAccess`'s neighbourhood (`validate.go:52`) — a new
  `validateColumnNameOverrides`:
  - reject a value that is not a **valid exported Go identifier** (first rune an uppercase
    letter, remainder letters/digits/`_`) — generated fields must be exported to scan and
    marshal;
  - reject a value that is a Go keyword-derived non-identifier; `Type`, `Range`, `Map` are legal
    and must stay accepted (PRD §8.5 "Reserved Word Handling" — the `Val` escape is locals-only);
  - reject `name` on a column removed by `exclude_columns` (same shape and wording as the
    existing `access` rule at `validate.go:73-77`).
- Post-parse, in `validateColumnAccessSchema`'s neighbourhood (`validate.go:670`) — column must
  exist on the parsed table, and the **resolved field name must be unique across the table's
  columns *and* its relationship field names** (both land on the same entity struct —
  `templates/table/model.go.tmpl:15-24`). Report the losing pair by SQL name.

Error strings follow the established shape:
`tables.%s.column_map.%s.name: %q is not a valid exported Go identifier`.

**Tests (each verified failing-first).**

- `config/validate_test.go` — table-driven: non-identifier, unexported, digit-leading, excluded
  column, non-existent column, collision with another column's default name, collision with
  another column's override, collision with a relationship field name, and the accepted cases
  (`APIKey`, `Type`, `FiscalYear2010Revenue`).
- `gen/context_test.go` — a `TableConfig` with `column_map.<col>.name` asserting the resolved
  `ColumnContext.FieldName`, the `FilterFieldContext` / input / FieldOptions field names, the
  soft-delete and tenancy field names, and `UpdateOps.SetGoField`.
- `gen/context_table_test.go` — a two-table fixture where the *child* table renames the FK
  column, asserting the parent's `RelationshipContext.FKFieldName` picked up the rename (the
  cross-table case step 2 exists for).
- `gen/api_field_overrides_test.go` — assert the row-type entry appears **only** for the renamed
  column and that the generated-type entries carry the new name.
- **End-to-end, the load-bearing one.** Add a renamed column to
  `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql` (`sqlgen.yml` already has a `column_map` block at `:74`)
  and let the example compile against real gqlgen — the same guard FIX-152/FIX-155 rely on. A
  column whose default spelling is *wrong* is the honest fixture: e.g. `osi_layer` → `OSILayer`
  (also the FIX-154 shape) or an `ip_addr` → `ClientIP` rename, on an API-exposed column so the
  bound-row-type path in step 7 actually fires.

**Golden churn.** Zero except where a fixture opts in — no config in the tree sets
`column_map.<col>.name` today (only `access`, in the `graphql` and `events` examples). Steps 3–6
are byte-identical without an override by construction. Adding the graphql-example fixture churns
that example's `expected/` tree plus its manifest `go_field` entries, intentionally.

**Doc / PRD deltas.**

- PRD §8.5 "Field Name Resolution" — replace the bare `Override:` line with the rename-scope
  table above and the validation rules.
- PRD §8.5 line 2389 — delete the "declared in the config schema … but is not currently read by
  the generator — see the tracked fix" parenthetical.
- PRD §8.5 "Digit-Leading Handling" (line 2454) — the escape-hatch sentence becomes true; leave
  it, cross-reference the new scope table.
- PRD §26.5.6 "Go field naming" — record that a bound row type receives
  `fields.<f>.fieldName` when, and only when, a column is renamed.
- PRD config-error table (~line 1100) — three new rows for the validation errors.
- PRD § "Column Overrides" table (line 673-682) — `name` row stays; see the out-of-scope note.

**Explicitly out of scope — now FIX-156.** `ColumnOverride.Type` and `.Import`
(`config.go:560-561`) are **also declared, documented and never read**, and `type_map` — the one
wired per-column type override — cannot carry an import, so a per-column external type is
unexpressible today. Same class, same file, adjacent validation; split out because this fix is a
naming-surface change and that one is confined to type resolution with a real design question of
its own. See FIX-156; the shared `column_map` validation scaffolding should be written once by
whichever lands first.

**Incidental — now FIX-157.** `gen/naming.go:15-19`, `:30-32` and `gen/acronyms.go:12-19` still
describe the canonical acronym set as "pushed into gqlgen as `go_initialisms`". That approach was
implemented and then removed in `84d90ab` (`MergeInput` has no such field); the comments are stale
and misdescribe the very mechanism this fix leans on — an implementer trusting them would think
predicting gqlgen's spelling is safe. Correct them while in the files, or take FIX-157 first.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:556-569` (`ColumnOverride`), `config/validate.go:51-79`, `:663-694`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:486`, `:509`, `:558`, `:838`, `:870`, `:52`/`:57`
  (`wireRelationshipFKMetadata`), `:229`/`:374` (`UpdateColumns`), `:301` (`SoftDeleteContext`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:1444`, `:1662`, `:1762`, `:1940`;
  `gen/api_field_overrides.go:38`, `:76`; `gen/context_tenancy.go:384`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/cli/graphql.go:262-330` (`buildMergeInput`), `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/merge.go:14-48`.
- gqlgen v0.17.90 `codegen/field.go:172-195`, `codegen/util.go:51` (`equalFieldName`) — why a
  bound row type needs the override.
- PRD §8.5 "Field Name Resolution" / "Acronym Detection" / "Digit-Leading Handling", §26.5.6.
- FIX-152 / FIX-155 — the dictate-don't-predict architecture this fix relies on.
- FIX-156 — the sibling `.type` / `.import` gap. FIX-157 — the stale comments describing it.
- FIX-154 — the `toSnakeCase` inverse bug; the override is also the workaround for it.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-27. Wired, with the GraphQL question answered the way the
scoping audit predicted: **Go-identifier-only**, and the FIX-152 hazard the original entry warned
about does not apply, because `84d90ab` had already replaced prediction with dictation.

**What shipped.**

1. **One resolution point.** `resolveColumnFieldName` (`gen/context_table.go`) returns the
   override when set, else `FieldName(col.Name)`, and reports which. `ColumnContext.FieldName`
   carries the result; `FieldNameOverridden` carries the provenance. Every model, filter, input,
   field-options, cache, manifest and event surface already read `FieldName`, so those needed no
   change.
2. **Six recompute sites closed.** `FKFieldName` moved out of `relationshipToContext` /
   `configRelationshipToContext` into the existing `wireRelationshipFKMetadata` second pass, which
   already resolved `FKGoType` / `FKNullable` / `FKColumnGoType` cross-table — the FK field is
   spelled on the *target* struct, so the target table's rename is the one that counts.
   `buildUpdateOps` reads `col.FieldName` instead of re-PascalCasing. `attachTenancyToTables`
   looks the tenant column up in the table's resolved columns. `SoftDeleteContext` gained
   `FieldName`, replacing 17 `.SoftDelete.Column | toPascalCase` template sites across seven
   templates. `TableContext.UpdateColumns` became `[]UpdateColumnContext{Name, FieldName}`,
   replacing four `input.{{ . | toPascalCase }}` sites in `update.go.tmpl`. **No column-derived
   `toPascalCase` remains in any template** — the two survivors operate on enum/set *values*.
3. **The FK wiring was consolidated while there.** Three parallel `map[table]map[column]X`
   lookups (nullability, Go type, and the new field name) collapsed into one
   `map[table]map[column]ColumnContext`, dropping a parameter from `wireRelFKMetadata` /
   `wireRelFKFromTable` rather than adding a fourth.
4. **gqlgen — one new obligation, gated.** The generated types (`<T>Filter`,
   `Create/Update<T>Input`) needed nothing: `APIGoFieldOverrides` already sources their
   `fieldName` entries from `GoFieldName` = `col.FieldName`, so the rename propagates. The
   **bound row type** did: gqlgen binds it by comparing against the name derived from the GraphQL
   field, which no longer matches. `tableGoFieldOverrides` now emits a row-type entry for a
   renamed column — and only for a renamed, API-readable one, so the merged config stays minimal
   and nothing is emitted for a field the schema does not carry. Verified end-to-end: the real
   gqlgen subprocess emits `return obj.ClientIP, nil` on `*models.User` for `User.ipAddr`, with
   no resolver stub.
5. **Validation, split by what each phase can see.** `config.ValidatePreParse` rejects a
   non-identifier, an unexported name, and a rename on an excluded column;
   `config.ValidatePostParse` rejects a rename on a column the table does not have. The
   resolved-name **collision** rule lives in `gen.validateResolvedFieldNames` instead, because
   `config` cannot import the acronym engine that produces the default names — and it reports
   only collisions an override *introduces*, so a schema that already produced duplicate field
   names does not start failing.

**Scope decision recorded in PRD §8.5.** The override renames the Go identifier and nothing a
client can observe: `db:` / `json:` tags, SQL column constants, `<T>Conflict…` constant names, the
GraphQL field name and the `<T>SortField` enum value all stay SQL-derived. `<T>Increment…`
constant names **do** follow the rename — `increment.go.tmpl` and `APIUpdateOp.IncColumnConst`
both build them from `col.FieldName`, and they must agree or the resolver references a constant
that does not exist. (The scope table first shipped with `<T>Increment…` grouped under the
SQL-derived row; auto-review caught the contradiction and the row was corrected in both the PRD
and this entry — the code was right.) Deviation from the entry's plan: none of substance.

**Tests (all verified failing-first).** `config/column_name_validate_test.go` — identifier,
exported, excluded-column, non-existent-column, batch reporting.
`gen/column_name_override_test.go` — resolution + provenance + untouched tags; the derived
surfaces (soft delete, update columns, filter/create/update inputs); tenancy; the cross-table FK
case; the collision rule. `gen/api_field_overrides_test.go` — the row-type entry appears only for
a renamed, readable column. `gen/get_test.go`'s soft-delete table gained a renamed-field case and
its guard assertion was tightened from a truncated prefix to the full `input.Filter.<Field> ==
nil` expression, which is what let the empty-`FieldName` fixtures pass silently at first.
Failing-first was checked **behaviourally**, not just by compilation: re-deriving each of the six
sites from the SQL name (with the new struct fields left in place) fails every assertion —
`FKFieldName = "UserID", want "OwnerID"`, `SoftDelete.FieldName = "DeletedAt", want "ArchivedAt"`,
`Tenancy.FieldName = "TenantID", want "OrgID"`, and so on.

**E2E fixture.** `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql` gained `users.ip_addr TEXT` with
`column_map.ip_addr.name: ClientIP` — public, so the rename crosses every surface including the
bound row type. Goldens show `ClientIP *string \`db:"ip_addr" json:"ip_addr"\`` on the entity,
`ClientIP *NullableStringComparator \`json:"ipAddr,omitempty"\`` on gqlgen's `UserFilter`,
`ipAddr` in the schema and `IP_ADDR` as the sort-enum value.

**Golden churn.** Confined to the `graphql` example (26 files) — the fixture that opts in. Every
other example is byte-stable, because items 2–3 are byte-identical without an override by
construction and no other config in the tree sets `column_map.<col>.name`.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all 33 modules (`cmd/sqlgen/cli` ~351s,
`cmd/sqlgen/gen` ~27s). `make check-examples` clean across all 13 example modules —
`graphql/tests` ~40.2s, which compiles and runs the regenerated GraphQL code against a real
database. `TestE2EGoldenFiles` clean with no drift after regeneration.

**Docs.** PRD §8.5 "Field Name Resolution" replaces the bare `Override:` line with the
rename-scope table and the validation rules; the "not currently read by the generator" caveat in
"Acronym Detection" is gone; §26.5.6 "Go field naming" records the bound-type exception; the
config-error table gains three rows; the `ColumnOverride.name` row states the Go-only scope.

**Auto-review follow-up.** Two findings were fixed inline (the `<T>Increment…` scope row above,
and two missing regression assertions — the relationship-collision case and `UpdateOps`'
`SetGoField` / `IncGoField` / `DecGoField` / `IncColumnConst` under a rename, both now
failing-first verified; the fixture gained an `integer` column so the operator pair is actually
produced). One was logged as **FIX-158**: the collision rule covers columns and relationships but
not the identifiers the shared templates emit on the same structs (`<T>Filter`'s `PKs` / `And` /
`Or`, `<T>FieldOptions`' `Columns` / `ColumnMap` / `HasSelectedColumns`), and it is unreachable
from `sqlgen validate`, which stops before `BuildTableContexts`. Both are the rule landing
narrower than its purpose rather than regressions, and widening the domain plus moving the phase
boundary is scope beyond this entry.

**Related.** FIX-156 (the sibling `.type` / `.import` gap) and FIX-157 (the stale
`go_initialisms` comments) stay open — both were split out of this entry's scoping audit and
neither is a prerequisite. FIX-158 (resolved 2026-08-28) widened this entry's collision rule with
an ungated reserved-name rule and made both halves reachable from `sqlgen validate`. FIX-154 is
unaffected; the override is now a real workaround for it.

### FIX-152

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** exhaustive audit of the FIX-147/FIX-148 bug class (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **`sqlgen generate` emits non-compiling filter *and* input translators for any column
whose name contains a token where sqlgen's acronym set and gqlgen's initialism set disagree.**
The translators reference gqlgen-emitted struct fields by Go name, but that name is taken from
sqlgen's own flect-derived spelling rather than gqlgen's. Where the two lists differ, the field
referenced does not exist. Confirmed end-to-end against the real `graphql` example with the real
gqlgen (v0.17.90) — plain `TEXT` columns, so this is purely a naming failure, not a type one:

```
filter_translate_gen.go:190:8: in.MAC undefined (type *model.EventFilter has no field or
                               method MAC, but does have field Mac)
input_translate_gen.go:240:8:  in.MAC undefined (type model.CreateEventInput has no field or
                               method MAC, but does have field Mac)
```

A sweep of ten acronym-bearing column names found **six** divergent tokens, in **both**
directions (left = what the generated code references, right = what gqlgen actually emitted):

| Column | sqlgen emits | gqlgen emits |
|---|---|---|
| `mac` | `MAC` | `Mac` |
| `pk_val` | `PKVal` | `PkVal` |
| `fk_val` | `FKVal` | `FkVal` |
| `io_count` | `IOCount` | `IoCount` |
| `os_name` | `OSName` | `OsName` |
| `ascii_art` | `AsciiArt` | **`ASCIIArt`** |

`SSL`, `TTL`, `RAM`, `EOF`, `UI`, `UTF8`, `URL`, `API`, `IP`, `HTTP`, `SQL`, `CPU`, `ID` agree and
are unaffected. Note `ascii_art` diverges the *other* way — gqlgen uppercases where sqlgen does
not — so this cannot be fixed by only adding to sqlgen's list.

`mac`, `os_name`, `io_count`, `pk_val` and `fk_val` are all ordinary column names; any consumer
with one and `api.graphql` enabled cannot generate at all.

**Root cause.** `APIFilterField.GoFieldName` is **documented** as "the gqlgen-generated Go field
name … derived by capitalizing the GraphQL field's first letter — gqlgen's default Go field
naming" (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:540-543`), but both producers assign it the *model's*
field name instead:

- `buildAPIFilterFields` — `GoFieldName: ff.FieldName` (same value as `ModelFieldName`)
- `buildAPIInputFields` — `GoFieldName: f.FieldName` (same value as `ModelFieldName`)

`f.FieldName` comes from `cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go`, which is flect plus a custom acronym list
(`SSL, TTL, PK, FK, UI, IO, EOF, OS, RAM` — `naming.go:13`). gqlgen derives its field names from
its own golint-descended initialism list. The two coincide for most names, which is why this has
never been hit. **The project already knows this hazard exists** — `APISortField`'s doc comment
(`context_api.go:555-559`) states that comparing on the raw enum string "sidesteps any drift
between flect's PascalCase and gqlgen's Go-const naming conventions when an SQL column contains
an acronym", and PRD §26.5.3 records the same reasoning. The sort surface was deliberately
protected; the filter and input surfaces reference gqlgen struct *fields* by Go name and were
never given the equivalent guard.

**Suggested fix (revised 2026-08-27 — supersedes the original bullets).** The original
suggestion was to make `GoFieldName` live up to its doc comment by deriving it from the GraphQL
field name with gqlgen's own rules, sourced from `templates.ToGo` or a vendored mirror of its
initialism list. Research into how gqlgen actually resolves names found a better mechanism and
disqualified both of those sources; see the evidence block below for the measurements.

**Why not `templates.ToGo` or a vendored list.** The consumer chooses the gqlgen version
(`gqlgen_bin: go run github.com/99designs/gqlgen` resolves from the consumer's module), and both
halves of gqlgen's naming have moved inside 0.17.x: `AWS` and `GCP` were added to
`CommonInitialisms` between v0.17.44 and v0.17.94, and `wordWalker`'s `ID`/`IP` special case was
rewritten over the same range. Importing `templates` would pin a version in sqlgen's go.mod with
no relationship to the one the subprocess runs — compile-time coupling without runtime parity —
and it breaks the §26.5.6 module invariant. A vendored mirror drifts by construction, exactly the
way `naming.go`'s did.

**The mechanism that works.** gqlgen's initialism list is *configuration*:
`codegen/config/initialisms.go` defines `go_initialisms: {replace_defaults, initialisms}`, and
`LoadConfig` applies it by replacing the package-level `templates.GetInitialisms` func that
`ToGo`'s word-walker reads. sqlgen already merges into a temp gqlgen.yml at invocation time
(`wrapper.MergeInput` → `schema:` / `models:` / `skip_validation:`), so pushing the list is a
third field on machinery that exists — and needs **no gqlgen import**, leaving
`TestNoGqlgenDependency` intact.

**Plan.**

1. **One canonical acronym list** in a new `cmd/sqlgen/gen/acronyms.go` — 165 entries, frozen as
   flect v1.0.3's 144 base ∪ gqlgen v0.17.90's 47 `CommonInitialisms` ∪ sqlgen's 9 custom, plus
   `GPU` and `SKU`, minus twelve exclusions: the five mixed-case flect entries (`Mbps`, `MoCA`,
   `WiFi`, `gbps`, `kbps`) that cannot round-trip because gqlgen upper-cases every configured
   initialism; `DEC`, which collides with the `_dec` operator suffix; and `CLI`, `DES`, `IPS`,
   `LAN`, `NIC`, `SYN`, each a proper prefix of a common identifier word. Now specified in
   PRD §8.5.
2. **Rewrite `naming.go`'s three helpers** on a `github.com/ettle/strcase` `Caser` built from
   that list — `NewCaser(false, canonical, NewSplitFn([]rune{'_','-',' ','.'}, SplitCase,
   SplitAcronym, SplitBeforeNumber))`. flect stays for `Singularize` / `Pluralize` only. All 34
   call sites funnel through `toPascalCase` / `toCamelCase` / `toSnakeCase`, so this is a
   one-file change. flect cannot be the authority: `LoadAcronyms` is additive-only, and its base
   entries can be neither removed nor enumerated, so a flect-derived set is both irreducible and
   impossible to communicate to gqlgen.
3. **Add `GoInitialisms` to `wrapper.MergeInput`**, emitting `go_initialisms: {replace_defaults:
   true, initialisms: [...]}` from the same list. **sqlgen-owned — it overwrites a
   consumer-declared value**, joining `skip_validation` as the second documented exception to
   step 3's consumer-wins rule (PRD §26.5.6, "sqlgen-owned keys"). Consumer-wins is wrong here
   because the key expresses an agreement between two generators rather than a preference: a
   consumer list that differs from §8.5's silently reinstates this bug, and it surfaces as an
   undefined-field compile error inside generated code rather than as an actionable config
   conflict. `replace_defaults: true` is load-bearing — under `false`, gqlgen's version-dependent
   defaults union in, reintroducing dependence on a version sqlgen does not control.
4. **Pin it.** A codegen fixture asserting emitted spellings for `mac`, `os_name`, `io_count`,
   `pk_val`, `fk_val`, `ascii_art`, `csv_data`, `tcp_port`, `utf8_body`, `http2_flag`, verified
   failing-first; plus the same columns in the `graphql` example so a golden compiles them
   end-to-end against real gqlgen. The example is the only check that catches drift in the half
   sqlgen does not control.

**Measured.** Against real flect v1.0.3 and real gqlgen v0.17.90 `templates.ToGo`, over 67
columns: today **25 divergences**; list-alignment alone (step 3, keeping flect) **2**; steps 2+3
together **0**. The 2 residual cases under list-alignment-only are `utf8_body` and `http2_flag` —
digit-boundary word-splitting, which no list can fix and which step 2 closes.

**Accepted trade.** Parity means `utf8_body` → `Utf8Body`, not `UTF8Body`. gqlgen's word-walker
splits unconditionally at a lower→digit boundary, so it can never emit `UTF8Body` from
`utf8Body`; the choice is parity or `UTF8`, and parity wins. Recorded in PRD §8.5.

**Decisions taken (user, 2026-08-27).** `go_initialisms` is sqlgen-owned rather than
consumer-wins. Golden churn from step 2 is accepted — the project is unpublished, and step 1's
list adds `ASCII`, `CSV`, `TCP`, `TLS`, `XML`, `GUID`, `UID`, `VM`, `GPU`, `SKU` and 16 others to
sqlgen's effective set, so model field names move. Two PRD examples that are wrong today become
true as a result: §8.5 claimed `GPU`/`CSV`/`TCP`/`TLS`/`XML`/`CSS` were built-in acronyms when
none of them were in flect's list, and "Upsert Conflict Keys" documents `sku` → `SKU` when the
generator produces `Sku`.

**Still open — check the third consumer.** The resolver / seed templates reference gqlgen-emitted
resolver method names, which `ToGo` derives from *table*-level GraphQL names. Step 3 aligns those
too, but the class is not closed until a table with an acronym-bearing name is exercised
end-to-end. Note this is the one surface binding cannot help with, unlike the filter/input
surface (see below).

**Alternative worth considering separately (does not replace the plan).** gqlgen matches fields
on the *bound* path with `codegen/util.go:51 equalFieldName` — underscores stripped,
`strings.EqualFold` — so acronym casing is irrelevant for any type bound via `models:`. That is
precisely why `Event` itself never broke and only gqlgen-*generated* types do. Binding
`<T>Filter` / `Create<T>Input` / `Update<T>Input` to sqlgen-emitted Go structs, the same pattern
tables already use, would kill this bug class outright and be immune to gqlgen version skew in
both list and algorithm — at the cost of sqlgen emitting those structs and choosing an
optionality representation (pointers vs `graphql.Omittable`). It does not remove the need for
step 3: resolver method names still come from `ToGo`.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:540-543` (the doc that states the intended contract),
  `:555-559` (the sort surface's guard against this exact drift), `buildAPIFilterFields`,
  `buildAPIInputFields`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go:10-16` (sqlgen's flect acronym registration).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/{filter_translate,input_translate}.go.tmpl`.
- PRD §26.5.3 (sort translator — "cases compare on the raw enum string so the generator does not
  need to mirror gqlgen's PascalCase Go-const naming for acronym-bearing column names").
- FIX-151 — found in the same audit; independent cause, same blind spot.
- gqlgen `codegen/config/initialisms.go` (`GoInitialismsConfig`, `setInitialisms`) and
  `codegen/config/config.go:331` (the `LoadConfig` call site) — the configurability this fix
  rides on.
- gqlgen `codegen/templates/templates.go` (`ToGo`, `wordWalker`, `CommonInitialisms`,
  `GetInitialisms`) — the algorithm and list sqlgen must agree with.
- gqlgen `codegen/util.go:51` (`equalFieldName`) — why bound types never break.
- flect v1.0.3 `acronyms.go` / `custom_data.go` (`LoadAcronyms` is the only exported acronym
  entry point; `baseAcronyms` is private, additive-only, un-enumerable).
- `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/merge.go` (`MergeInput`, consumer-wins precedence),
  `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/init.go` (`InitConfigContent` scaffold).
- PRD §8.5 "Acronym Detection" (canonical set, splitter, digit rule) and §26.5.6 "Go initialism
  alignment" / "sqlgen-owned keys" — both landed 2026-08-27 as the normative spec for this fix.

**Evidence — name derivation table (computed 2026-08-27).** Produced by running the real
`flect v1.0.3` (with sqlgen's `init()` acronym registration from `naming.go:13` applied) against
the real `gqlgen v0.17.90` `templates.ToGo`, over a 53-column sweep. It reproduces all six pairs
in the table above exactly.

The two derivations, for column `os_name`:

| Step | Producer | Function | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DB schema | — | `os_name` |
| 2 | sqlgen model field | `toPascalCase` → `flect.Pascalize` + 144 base acronyms + 9 custom (`SSL TTL PK FK UI IO EOF OS RAM`) | `OSName` |
| 3 | sqlgen GraphQL field (`camel_case`, default) | `toCamelCase` → `flect.Camelize` | `osName` |
| 3′ | sqlgen GraphQL field (`snake_case`) | raw column, verbatim | `os_name` |
| 4 | gqlgen model field | `templates.ToGo(step 3)` → golint wordWalker + 50 `CommonInitialisms` | `OsName` |

The bug is step 2 vs step 4: the translators emit step 2's spelling; the struct carries step 4's.

*Agreement (unaffected):*

| Column | GraphQL field | sqlgen Go | gqlgen Go |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user_id` | `userID` | `UserID` | `UserID` |
| `api_key` | `apiKey` | `APIKey` | `APIKey` |
| `http_status` | `httpStatus` | `HTTPStatus` | `HTTPStatus` |
| `ttl_seconds` | `ttlSeconds` | `TTLSeconds` | `TTLSeconds` |
| `json_body` | `jsonBody` | `JSONBody` | `JSONBody` |
| `ip_addr` | `ipAddr` | `IPAddr` | `IPAddr` |
| `acl_rules` | `aclRules` | `ACLRules` | `ACLRules` |
| `udp_port` | `udpPort` | `UDPPort` | `UDPPort` |
| `2010_revenue` | `col2010Revenue` | `Col2010Revenue` | `Col2010Revenue` |

*sqlgen uppercases, gqlgen does not:*

| Column | GraphQL field | sqlgen Go | gqlgen Go | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mac` | `mac` | `MAC` | `Mac` | flect base has `MAC`; gqlgen does not |
| `mac_addr` | `macAddr` | `MACAddr` | `MacAddr` | same |
| `pk_val` | `pkVal` | `PKVal` | `PkVal` | sqlgen custom `PK` |
| `fk_val` | `fkVal` | `FKVal` | `FkVal` | sqlgen custom `FK` |
| `io_count` | `ioCount` | `IOCount` | `IoCount` | sqlgen custom `IO` |
| `os_name` | `osName` | `OSName` | `OsName` | sqlgen custom `OS` |
| `ssl_mode` | `sslMode` | `SSLMode` | `SslMode` | sqlgen custom `SSL` |
| `utf8_body` | `utf8Body` | `UTF8Body` | `Utf8Body` | **not list membership** — see below |

*gqlgen uppercases, sqlgen does not:*

| Column | GraphQL field | sqlgen Go | gqlgen Go |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ascii_art` | `asciiArt` | `AsciiArt` | `ASCIIArt` |
| `csv_data` | `csvData` | `CsvData` | `CSVData` |
| `xml_body` | `xmlBody` | `XmlBody` | `XMLBody` |
| `tcp_port` | `tcpPort` | `TcpPort` | `TCPPort` |
| `tls_version` | `tlsVersion` | `TlsVersion` | `TLSVersion` |
| `css_class` | `cssClass` | `CssClass` | `CSSClass` |
| `guid` | `guid` | `Guid` | `GUID` |
| `uid` | `uid` | `Uid` | `UID` |
| `vm_size` | `vmSize` | `VmSize` | `VMSize` |
| `qr_code` / `pdf_blob` / `svg_icon` | … | `QrCode` / `PdfBlob` / `SvgIcon` | `QRCode` / `PDFBlob` / `SVGIcon` |
| `aws_region` / `gcp_project` | … | `AwsRegion` / `GcpProject` | `AWSRegion` / `GCPProject` |
| `rpc_name` / `sla_days` / `lhs_val` | … | `RpcName` / `SlaDays` / `LhsVal` | `RPCName` / `SLADays` / `LHSVal` |
| `xsrf_token` / `xss_filter` | … | `XsrfToken` / `XssFilter` | `XSRFToken` / `XSSFilter` |
| `kvk_number` / `qps_limit` | … | `KvkNumber` / `QpsLimit` | `KVKNumber` / `QPSLimit` |
| `http2_flag` | `http2Flag` | `Http2Flag` | `HTTP2Flag` |

**Three findings that bear on the fix.**

1. **The divergence rate is far higher than the ten-column sample suggested** — **25 of 53**
   columns swept diverge, not 6 of 10. `csv_data`, `xml_body`, `tcp_port`, `tls_version`,
   `css_class` and `aws_region` are as routine as `mac`.
2. **Two of the divergences are word-splitting, not list membership.** `UTF8` is in *both*
   lists, yet `utf8_body` still breaks: gqlgen's golint-descended wordWalker splits `utf8Body`
   at the lower→digit boundary, so it never sees the word `UTF8`. `http2_flag` breaks the same
   way in the other direction. **No amount of list-mirroring closes these** — only calling
   gqlgen's own `ToGo` does. This is the strongest argument for the `templates.ToGo` option in
   the suggested fix over a vendored list.
3. **`naming.go:11-12`'s comment is factually wrong** and is a trap for anyone fixing this by
   extending the custom acronym list. It claims "flect already handles: … TCP, UDP, DNS, TLS,
   HTML, CSS, JSON, XML, CSV, CPU, GPU", but **TCP, TLS, CSS, XML, CSV and GPU are not in
   flect's 144-entry base list**. Adding them to sqlgen's custom list would move those columns
   *away* from gqlgen's spelling, not toward it.

**`field_casing` changes the divergence set.** In `camel_case` mode gqlgen re-derives from
sqlgen's already-Camelized output, so some of sqlgen's uppercasing survives the round trip; in
`snake_case` mode gqlgen derives independently from the raw column. The two modes therefore break
on different columns, and any regression fixture must cover both:

| Column | sqlgen Go | gqlgen Go (`camel_case`) | gqlgen Go (`snake_case`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user_ids` | `UserIDS` | `UserIDS` (gqlgen receives `userIDS`, `IDS` preserved) | `UserIds` — diverges |

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-27. The shipped mechanism is **not** the one the entry
proposed, and not the acronym-list alignment first attempted — both of those predict what gqlgen
will name a field. sqlgen now **dictates** the name instead.

**What landed.** gqlgen's `plugin/modelgen` discards its own `templates.ToGo` result whenever
`models.<Type>.fields.<field>.fieldName` is set (`models.go:436-439`), and `codegen/field.go:172`
does the same for resolver method names. sqlgen emits one such entry for every Go identifier its
generated code references on a gqlgen-*generated* type:

- new `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_field_overrides.go` — `APIGoFieldOverrides` builds
  `map[GraphQLType]map[GraphQLField]GoName` covering `<T>Filter`, `Create<T>Input`,
  `Update<T>Input` (including the `_inc` / `_dec` pair), and the `Query` / `Mutation` root fields;
- `APIFilterField` / `APIInputField` gained `GraphQLName`, and `APIUpdateOp` gained
  `IncGraphQLName` / `DecGraphQLName`, so the GraphQL name — the join key between the two
  generators — is derived exactly once per column (`graphQLNamesByColumn`);
- `tableQueryFieldNames` / `tableMutationFieldNames` now return `APIRootField{GraphQLName, GoName}`
  pairs, so the schema template, the seed template, the panic-stub rewriter's managed-field set
  and the overrides all resolve to one gated source rather than re-deriving the operation set;
- `wrapper.MergeInput.ModelFields` + `mergeModelFields` write the entries into the temp
  gqlgen.yml, merging **per field** so a consumer's own `fieldName` is preserved;
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/acronyms.go` holds the canonical acronym set (170 entries) and an
  `ettle/strcase` caser driving `toPascalCase` / `toCamelCase`. `toSnakeCase` stays on
  `flect.Underscore` — its splitter is list-driven, so it recovers `APIURL` → `api_url` where a
  rune-driven one cannot — with the canonical set loaded into flect at init.

**Why not the acronym-list alignment.** It was implemented first (`go_initialisms` with
`replace_defaults: true`) and taken back out. It closed the reported symptom but not the class:
the auto-review found that an acronym following a digit-terminated word still diverged
(`line2_id` → sqlgen `Line2ID`, gqlgen `Line2id`), because the GraphQL field name is a lossy
encoding — `line2ID` gives gqlgen's word walker no seam before the acronym. No shared list can
express that. Sharing the list also had costs of its own: it re-spelled gqlgen's *own* enum
constants (`DESCRIPTION` → `DESCription` via flect's `DES`), forcing seven tokens out of the set
for gqlgen's benefit; all seven are restored now that the list is sqlgen's alone.

**Ownership.** `fieldName` entries are sqlgen-authored but **not** sqlgen-owned: they merge per
field and a consumer's explicit value wins. This is a deliberate reversal of the earlier decision
to make `go_initialisms` an override — a whole-list override was justified because one wrong list
desynchronized every name at once, whereas a single field the consumer renames is a local,
self-evident choice. `skip_validation` remains the only overwritten key.

**Two defects surfaced and fixed during implementation.** (a) `buildUpdateOps` builds the
`_inc` / `_dec` Go names by appending a literal suffix; while the list was shared, flect's `DEC`
made gqlgen emit `PriceDEC` against the template's `PriceDec` — a hard generation failure in the
`graphql_top_level` example, and the "third consumer" this entry flagged. Dictating those two
names removes the coupling entirely. (b) `normalizeForCasing` initially stripped all punctuation,
which would have re-spelled the `read/write` enum identifier from `READ_WRITE` to `READWRITE`;
it now filters only `.` (matching flect's non-splitting treatment, which is what keeps
`asset.primary` → `ASSETPRIMARY`) and treats every other non-alphanumeric as a word boundary.

**Tests.** `gen/api_field_overrides_test.go` — exact-shape assertion plus
`_CoversEveryReferencedName`, which walks the context rather than a fixed list so a newly
referenced field cannot be added without being covered, and `_RootFieldPairsStayInStep`, pinning
that the managed-field set and the overrides come from one source. `gen/acronyms_test.go` — 26
spellings including the three digit→acronym shapes, plus the snake-inverse round trip with
prefix-pair guards. `wrapper/merge_test.go` — YAML shape, per-field consumer-wins, coexistence
with a `model:` binding, absent-when-unset, and that a fields-only entry never emits a `model:`
path (which would make gqlgen bind rather than generate). **Failing-first verified** for the
original 23 spellings against the pre-fix code path: 16 of 23 failed.

**End-to-end.** Thirteen columns on the `graphql` example's `events` table — `mac`, `os_name`,
`io_count`, `pk_val`, `fk_val`, `ascii_art`, `csv_data`, `tcp_port`, `utf8_body`, `http2_flag`,
plus `line2_id`, `address2_id`, `s3_url` for the FIX-155 shape. gqlgen emits `Line2ID`,
`Address2ID`, `S3URL`, `MAC`, `ASCIIArt`, `CSVData`, `Utf8Body`, `HTTP2Flag` — sqlgen's spellings
verbatim — and the example compiles against real gqlgen v0.17.90.

**Churn.** One pre-existing example column changes spelling: `sku` → `SKU`, renaming
`ProductConflictSku` → `ProductConflictSKU` and `CreateProductInput.Sku` → `.SKU`. That makes two
PRD statements true that were previously false. 53 hand-written example test files updated.

**Verification.** `make check` clean across all modules under `-race`; `make check-examples` clean
across all 13 example modules; `make update-golden` and `make update-golden-e2e` regenerated.

**Specification.** PRD §8.5 rewritten (the set is sqlgen's own; canonical list enumerated; word
splitting and the digit rules) and §26.5.6 gained "Go field naming" with the coverage and
precedence rules; §26.5.3's sort-translator note now explains why that surface never developed
the defect. `guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md` records the new file and the `ettle/strcase` dependency.

**Closes FIX-155** (the digit→acronym divergence) as well — dictation removes the mechanism rather
than working around it. **FIX-154** (flect's snake-inverse prefix pairs) and **FIX-153**
(`column_map.<column>.name` declared but unwired) remain open; both are independent of the gqlgen
handoff.

### FIX-150

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** nit
- **Origin:** phase 25, cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **25.3's two new GraphQL E2E tests are not rerun-safe.**
`TestDecimalComparator_OverHTTP` and `TestNullableComparator_IsNullOverHTTP` seed their
fixtures under a hard-coded name prefix, and `categories.name` is `TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, so a
second execution against the same container fails during setup rather than during an assertion:

```
--- FAIL: TestDecimalComparator_OverHTTP
    comparator_surface_test.go:68: seeding category: create category: sqlgen: unique constraint
    violation on constraint categories_name_key: Key (name)=(gql-decimal-category) already exists.
--- FAIL: TestNullableComparator_IsNullOverHTTP
    comparator_surface_test.go:115: ... Key (name)=(gql-isnull-category) already exists.
```

Reproduced with `GOWORK=off go test ./tests/ -count=2`. CI is unaffected — `make test-examples`
pins `-count=1` — so this is a developer-loop and flake-diagnosis nit, not a pipeline break. It
matters because `-count=N` is the standard way to check a suspected flake, and here it reports a
failure that has nothing to do with the behaviour under test.

**Root cause.** `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/tests/comparator_surface_test.go:29`
(`seedDecimalProducts`, `const prefix = "gql-decimal"`) and `:110` (`const prefix = "gql-isnull"`)
use fixed prefixes. The sibling pins added in the same sub-item do not: the postgres / mysql /
sqlite `decimal_filter_test.go` each build `prefix := "decimal-order-" + ksuid.New().String()`,
so only the GraphQL leg is affected.

**Suggested fix.**
- Derive both prefixes per-run the way the sibling tests already do
  (`ksuid.New().String()`), or seed the category with a unique suffix and keep the assertion
  prefix stable.
- Verify with `go test ./tests/ -count=2` on the `graphql` example module.
- While in the file: replace the hand-rolled `equalStrings` helper (`:203`) with `cmp.Diff`,
  per `guidelines/TESTING.md` — `github.com/google/go-cmp` is already a dependency of this
  module and every sibling E2E test in the sub-item uses it.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/tests/comparator_surface_test.go:29,110,203`.
- Sibling precedent: `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/{postgres,mysql,sqlite}/tests/decimal_filter_test.go`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/schema.sql:16` (`name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`).
- `guidelines/TESTING.md` (no hand-rolled comparison helpers; `cmp.Diff` for slices).

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26. The suggested per-run `ksuid` prefix was **not** the
fix taken: `ksuid` is not a dependency of the `graphql` example module (unlike the postgres /
mysql / sqlite ones, which is why only those siblings could use it), and this package already has
the idiomatic answer — `truncateAll(t)`, used by ten-plus sibling tests for exactly this
clean-slate need. Both tests now call it first, so the fixed prefixes stay readable and no
dependency was added. The prefixes are still carried on every seeded row because the assertions
scope with a `startsWith` filter.

`equalStrings` deleted in favour of `cmp.Diff(tt.want, got)` at both call sites, per
`guidelines/TESTING.md` — `github.com/google/go-cmp v0.7.0` is already required by this module's
`go.mod`, and the diff output is strictly more useful on an ordering failure, which is the shape
these tests fail in. One stale doc line fixed in passing: `seedDecimalProducts` claimed to
"return the category the products hang off" and returns nothing; it now describes the prefix
contract the callers actually rely on.

**Verified with the entry's own repro:** `GOWORK=off go test ./tests/ -count=2` on the `graphql`
example module, which failed on `categories_name_key` before and passes now.

### FIX-149

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** nit

- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **Two doc comments on `APIComparatorTranslator` still describe the pre-25.3
delegating design, and the 25.3 completion record still marks two closed items as open.**
25.3 deliberately stopped nullable translators delegating to their base (PRD §26.4 Rule 2 makes

generator's own type documentation was not updated with it:

1. `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:219-220` — "Nullable variants delegate to the base translator
   and lift the result into the `Nullable<X>` wrapper." This is directly contradicted by the
   `InputTypeName` doc eight lines above it (":211-214", "a nullable translator cannot delegate
   to its base by forwarding the same value") **and** by the implementation, so the struct

Separately, `docs/tracker/phase-25.md:279-280` still labels the auto-review's **R3** (the
`TimeComparator` / undeclared `scalar Time` gap) and the **PRD text drift** item
`(open, tracked)`. FIX-141 and FIX-139 respectively closed both, and the fix-round paragraph

carried in `docs/tracker/STATUS.md`'s 25.3 paragraphs ("is logged, not fixed here"; "the
base-form change needs a delta", which FIX-140 landed).

Behaviour is correct in every case; this is documentation that will mislead the next reader of
this code, which is what FIX-146 was opened to clear and what these four lines escaped.

**Root cause.** FIX-146 swept `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL.md`, `orchestrate.go`'s
`comparatorTranslatorsUseTime` doc, and the `api_comparator_families_test.go` rationale comment,
but not the `APIComparatorTranslator` type docs; and the tracker/STATUS narrative sections were
appended to rather than reconciled once the fix round closed the items they describe.

**Suggested fix.**
- Rewrite `context_api.go:219-220` to state that nullable variants take their own
  `Nullable<X>Comparator` input, copy the operands directly (field promotion through the
  embedded `<X>`), and set `Null` from `isNull` — matching the `InputTypeName` doc above it.
- Correct the signature in `context_api.go:200` to `*NullableNumericComparator`.
- Mark R3 and the PRD-text-drift item **resolved** in `docs/tracker/phase-25.md:279-280`, citing

- No test change — this is comment/tracker text only.

**References.**

- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/expected/graph/comparator_translate_gen.go:274`.
- PRD §26.4 Rule 2, §26.5.3 (nullable-translator paragraph as rewritten by FIX-139).
- FIX-146 — the prior sweep of the same class; FIX-139 / FIX-141 — the entries that closed

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26; all four items closed. (1) `APIComparatorTranslator`'s
`Nullable` doc (`context_api.go`) rewritten to state that a nullable variant takes its own

`translateNullableNumericComparatorInt32(*NullableNumericComparator)`, matching
