### FIX-148

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **`sqlgen generate` emits a non-compiling input translator for any `float32`
column when `api.graphql` is enabled — the same defect FIX-147 fixed for sized ints, on the
float axis, and FIX-147's fix does not cover it.** gqlgen binds the GraphQL `Float` scalar to
Go `float64`, but sqlgen narrows a `real` / `float4` (PostgreSQL) or `float` (MySQL) column to
Go `float32`. No cast is applied on any of the three arms. Reproduced against a fixture table
with `reading REAL NOT NULL` and `offset_val REAL` — the rendered
`api/input-translate` body is:

```go
out.Reading = in.Reading                          // float64 -> float32   (create, NOT NULL)
out.OffsetVal = omittable.Set(in.OffsetVal)       // *float64 -> Value[*float32] (create, nullable)
out.Reading = omittable.Set(*in.Reading)          // float64 -> Value[float32]   (update, NOT NULL)
```

All three fail to compile. This is **broader than the nullable-only shape FIX-147 addressed**:
the sized-int case only reached the nullable arm because gqlgen emits bare `int` for a required
`Int` field and `funcInputCoerceBare` casts it, whereas here `CastTo` is empty on every arm, so
the required arms break too. Like FIX-147 this is **pre-existing** (dating from phase 16, not
introduced by 25.3) and unexercised — neither API-enabled example has a `real` / `float4` /
`float` column, so nothing catches it.

The comparator surface 25.3 built is **not** affected: `resolveComparatorType` routes the column
to `Number[float32]`, `makeNumericTranslator` emits `translateNumericComparatorFloat32`, and the
`NumericT` cast block renders `v := float32(*in.Eq)` correctly. The gap is confined to the
create / update (mutation) input translators.

**Root cause.** `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:1818` (`inputCoercionFor`) sets `CastTo` only via
`isSizedIntGoType(bareGoType)` (`context_api.go:1787-1794`), whose switch lists the integer
widths and **omits `float32`**. With `CastTo == ""`, `PointerCast` (`:1778`) is false, so the
nullable arm falls to `funcInputCoerceDeref`'s `ModelInnerIsPointer` branch
(`funcmap.go:159-163`) and threads `*float64` through unconverted; the required arms fall to
`funcInputCoerceBare` (`funcmap.go:117-126`) and `funcInputCoerceDeref`'s default
(`funcmap.go:166-171`), both of which apply a cast only when `CastTo` is non-empty. The Go type
itself is correct — `gotype.go:75,96,123` maps `float4` / `real` / `float` to `goFloat32` by
design.

**Suggested fix.**
- Widen the cast gate to cover the float width mismatch — either add `"float32"` to
  `isSizedIntGoType` and rename it to something accurate (`isNarrowedNumericGoType`), or add a
  sibling `case` in `inputCoercionFor`'s switch. The former keeps one predicate; the latter
  keeps the existing name honest.
- Confirm `PointerCast` then covers the nullable arm automatically (it will — it is keyed on
  `CastTo != ""`), so no template change should be required.
- Add a codegen test alongside `TestInputTranslate_NullableSizedIntGoesThroughALocal`
  (`api_comparator_families_test.go:750`) covering a `real NOT NULL` **and** a nullable `real`
  column, asserting all three arms convert and that `float64` columns are left alone. Verify
  failing-first.
- Consider an example fixture with a `real` column on an API-enabled module so a golden
  compiles the result — this is the same blind spot that let FIX-147 survive from phase 16.
  (Adding one to the `graphql` example is a schema change; weigh against the note that a
  non-PostgreSQL API-enabled example is the durable fix for this whole class — tracked as FIX-169,
  closed 2026-09-01 by the MySQL and SQLite API surfaces; the "FIX-135" this line originally cited
  is an unrelated PRD documentation entry.)

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:1778,1787-1794,1818` (`isSizedIntGoType`, `inputCoercionFor`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap.go:117-126,159-171` (`funcInputCoerceBare`, `funcInputCoerceDeref`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype.go:75,96,123` (`float4` / `real` / `float` -> `float32`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/input_translate.go.tmpl:29-42,58-66`.
- **FIX-147** — the integer-width instance of this identical defect, same root helper, fixed
  2026-08-26. This entry is its float sibling.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26 via the **single-predicate** option. `isSizedIntGoType`
gained `"float32"` and was renamed `isNarrowedNumericGoType` — the old name was accurate when only
integers were listed, and the narrow name is precisely what made the float axis easy to overlook,
so keeping it while widening the body would have preserved the trap. Its doc now states the rule
once for both axes: gqlgen binds each numeric GraphQL scalar to one Go type (`Int` → `int`,
`Float` → `float64`) while sqlgen resolves to the column's native width, so every type that
differs from gqlgen's binding needs a conversion.

**No template or funcmap logic changed**, which was the point of fixing it at the predicate: the
helper has exactly one caller (`inputCoercionFor`), and `CastTo` is consumed only by
`funcInputCoerceBare`, `funcInputCoerceDeref`'s two casting arms, and the template's `PointerCast`
block. `PointerCast` is keyed on `CastTo != ""`, so the nullable arm was covered automatically —
verified, not assumed. Doc comments on `CastTo`, `PointerCast`, `inputCoercionFor` and both
funcmap helpers were corrected to name both axes rather than "sized int".

**Pinned by `TestInputTranslate_Float32ColumnsAreCast`** (`api_comparator_families_test.go`),
sitting next to FIX-147's pin. It asserts all four arm/nullability combinations convert
(`out.Reading = float32(in.Reading)`, the deref-convert-readdress local for the nullable one on
both create and update, `omittable.Set(float32(*in.Reading))` on update), that the three
uncastable spellings appear nowhere, and that `float64` columns are left **untouched** on every
arm — a self-conversion there would trip `unconvert`. **Verified failing-first** by reverting the
one-word predicate change: all seven assertions fail, covering both the required arms (which
FIX-147's shape never reached) and the nullable one.

**Golden impact: none.** No example module has a `real` / `float4` / `float` column with
`api.graphql` enabled — that is why the bug survived from phase 16 — so `make check-examples` and
the E2E goldens are unmoved. The blind spot itself is *not* closed by this fix; the durable
closure is FIX-169's non-PostgreSQL API-enabled example module (landed 2026-09-01: MySQL under
FIX-166, SQLite under FIX-169), and this entry is the second consumer-facing bug (after FIX-147) to
have hidden in it.

### FIX-144

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **The F7 decimal-ordering E2E covers PostgreSQL and MySQL but not SQLite**, though
25.3's "Tests Required" names all three. The pin matters because a decimal column filters through
`comparator.String` on its canonical string form, and the ordering is only correct if the
*database* coerces the parameter against a numeric column; the fixture is built so the numeric
and lexicographic orderings disagree (`"1000.00" < "100.50"` as text, `>` as a number).
Whether SQLite gives the same answer is currently unverified.

**Root cause.** The SQLite example schema has no decimal column — SQLite has no `DECIMAL` type
and the example maps its numerics to REAL, so there is nothing for the `decimal.Decimal`
override to bind to. Adding one is a change to that example's schema, which was out of 25.3's
scope.

**Suggested fix.**
- Decide first whether decimal-on-SQLite is a supported configuration at all (SQLite's NUMERIC
  affinity does coerce a numeric-looking string, so the comparison is likely correct — but
  "likely" is what the pin exists to remove).
- If supported: add a `NUMERIC`-affinity column to the SQLite example schema with the
  `decimal.Decimal` override, regenerate, and mirror
  `TestDecimalFilter_OrderedOperatorsAreNumeric`.
- If not supported: say so in PRD §11.2 / §26.4 and strike SQLite from the requirement rather
  than leaving the checkbox overstating coverage.

**References.**
- `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` §25.3 "Tests Required".
- `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/{postgres,mysql}/tests/decimal_filter_test.go` — the two pins
  that exist.
- PRD §26.4 "Decimal columns", §11.2.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26 — **and the open question it posed is answered: decimal-on-SQLite works.** No schema change was needed. The SQLite example already carries the same `warehouses` fixture as postgres and mysql, with a table-scoped `real → decimal.Decimal` override (`sqlgen.yml`) over `price REAL NOT NULL`. `TestDecimalFilter_OrderedOperatorsAreNumeric` was mirrored into `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/tests/decimal_filter_test.go` against that fixture, using the same disagreeing-orderings seed (`"1000.00" < "100.50"` as text, `>` as a number). All four legs (`gt` / `gte` / `lt` / `lte`) pass: SQLite's REAL affinity coerces the text parameter for the comparison rather than collating it, so the ordered operators are numerically correct on all three dialects. The test header records the affinity caveat so the result is not mistaken for exact-numeric semantics.

### FIX-142

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, cmd/sqlgen/gen (tests)
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **Two load-bearing branches added by 25.3 have no failing-first pin — deleting either
leaves the suite green while the generated schema breaks.**
1. The paired-`Decimal` scalar registration (`registerColumnScalars`) exists precisely for a
   project whose decimal columns are **all nullable**. `TestDecimalComparator_routing`'s fixture
   carries a NOT NULL `price`, which registers `scalar Decimal` on its own, so removing the
   branch does not fail that test.
2. The range-carry-onto-twin branch in `collectComparatorFamilies` declares `NumericRange` /
   `TimeRange` alongside the twin when only the twin is referenced.
   `TestComparatorTranslateFile_importsTimeForNullableOnly` builds exactly that fixture
   (nullable-only timestamp) but asserts only translators and imports — drop the branch and
   `NullableTimeComparator.between: TimeRange` references an undeclared input.

**Root cause.** Both branches were written for the nullable-only shape, and the tests that use a
nullable-only fixture assert a different property than the one the branch protects. Neither
example module has a nullable-only decimal or timestamp column, so the goldens cannot catch
either.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add a nullable-only-decimal fixture asserting `scalar Decimal` is declared and
  `NullableDecimalComparator` names it; verify it fails with the pairing branch removed.
- Extend `TestComparatorTranslateFile_importsTimeForNullableOnly` (or add a sibling) with one
  assertion that the rendered shared schema declares `input TimeRange`; verify it fails with the
  carry branch removed.
- Both are the same class as the two blocking defects the 25.3 auto-review caught — branches
  that only the PostgreSQL-example blind spot hides.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `registerColumnScalars`, `collectComparatorFamilies`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_comparator_families_test.go` — `TestDecimalComparator_routing`,
  `TestComparatorTranslateFile_importsTimeForNullableOnly`.
- PRD §26.4 Rule 2 (nullable twin emission).

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26. Branch 1 (paired-`Decimal` registration for a nullable-only decimal column) is covered by FIX-141's `TestComparatorFamilies_operandScalarsAreDeclared` — its second case builds exactly the nullable-only fixture the entry asked for, and FIX-141's generalisation subsumed the branch itself. Branch 2 (range-carry-onto-twin) is pinned by three assertions added to `TestComparatorTranslateFile_importsTimeForNullableOnly`, which already built the nullable-only-timestamp fixture but asserted only translators and imports: the fixture emits `NullableTimeComparator` and **not** the base `TimeComparator` (so the twin-only path is genuinely exercised), `input TimeRange` is declared, and it is declared exactly once. **Failing-first verified:** disabling the carry branch fails with `NullableTimeComparator names TimeRange but the schema never declares it` and `TimeRange declared 0 times, want exactly 1`.

### FIX-141

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25 (pre-existing), cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **A generated schema can reference an undeclared `Time` scalar.** `TimeComparator` /
`NullableTimeComparator` / `TimeRange` type their operands with the `Time` scalar, but
`scalar Time` is declared only when some column's Go type is literally `time.Time` (the
`UsedScalars` registry keys on the Go type). A project that binds `timestamptz → types.DateTime`
**globally** has no `time.Time` column at all, yet `resolveSimpleComparator` still routes
`types.DateTime` / `types.NullDateTime` to the Time family — so the shared schema declares
`scalar DateTime` and emits `input TimeComparator { eq: Time … }` against a scalar nothing
declared. gqlgen rejects the schema; the failure is build-blocking when hit.

**Root cause.** Two independent mappings that never agreed: `graphQLTypeForGoType` picks the
*field* scalar from the Go type (`types.DateTime` → `DateTime`), while `resolveSimpleComparator`
picks the *comparator family* from the same column (`types.DateTime` → `Time`, `context_table.go`),
and the comparator family's operand type is fixed at `Time`. Nothing forces the operand's scalar
to be declared. 25.3 fixed exactly this shape for decimals — `registerColumnScalars` registers
the non-null `Decimal` alongside `NullDecimal` because both comparator forms take `Decimal`
operands — but did not add the symmetric `DateTime`/`NullDateTime → Time` pairing. Review
bounded the blast radius: `Time` and `Decimal` are the **only** two families whose operands use a
non-builtin scalar (ID→`ID`, Numeric→`Float`, Bool→`Boolean`, String→`String`), so this is the
sole remaining instance.

**Suggested fix.**
- `registerColumnScalars` — when a column's projection resolves to the Time family and its own
  scalar is `DateTime` / `NullDateTime`, also register the `time.Time` → `Time` registry entry,
  mirroring the `NullDecimal → Decimal` branch.
- Consider generalising both into one rule keyed on the family's operand scalar rather than two
  hand-written pairs, so a future family with a custom-scalar operand cannot reintroduce it.
- Failing-first test: a fixture whose only timestamp columns bind to `types.DateTime`, asserting
  the rendered shared schema declares every scalar its comparator inputs name. Neither
  PostgreSQL example reaches this today.

**References.**
- PRD §26.4 "Comparator input projection" (operand types), §26.4.1 Scalar Marshaling.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `registerColumnScalars`, `graphQLTypeForGoType`,
  `builtInScalarRegistry`; `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go` — `resolveSimpleComparator`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/shared.graphqls.tmpl` (scalar declarations come from
  `UsedScalars`).
- FIX-140 — the same undeclared-scalar failure mode, from the emission side.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26, and **generalised** rather than adding a second hand-written pair as the entry's first bullet suggested. `registerColumnScalars` now walks the resolved projection's operand list and registers the scalar named by each operand type, driven by a new `comparatorOperandScalars` table (`Time` → `time.Time` stdlib, `Decimal` → `decimal.Decimal` from the column's package). This replaces the bespoke `NullDecimal → Decimal` branch entirely and closes the rule rather than the two known instances — a future family whose operands name a custom scalar is covered without another edit. Operand types are matched after stripping list syntax, so `[Time!]` registers the same scalar as `Time`. **Failing-first verified:** removing the loop makes `TestComparatorFamilies_operandScalarsAreDeclared` fail with exactly the reported symptom — `TimeComparator names operand scalar "Time", which the schema never declares`. The test asserts the general property (every scalar any emitted comparator input names is declared) on two fixtures neither example reaches: timestamps bound globally to `types.DateTime`, and a decimal column that is nullable-only. Zero golden churn — both API examples already declared `Time` and `Decimal` via a column field type.

### FIX-140

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 25, docs/PRD.md (§26.4) / cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **25.3 made *base*-form comparator emission conditional on usage, which PRD §26.4
does not authorize — and the change is not byte-neutral.** `docs/PRD.md:10505` conditions only
the nullable twin: "The `Nullable` variant of a family is emitted **only when some nullable
column actually references it**." Nothing in §26.4 says the same of the `NOT NULL` form, and
before 25.3 the five base inputs were emitted unconditionally. `collectComparatorFamilies` now
emits a base family only when referenced, and `graphql_top_level` consequently lost
`input BooleanComparator` and `input IDComparator` from its shared schema — it has neither a
boolean nor a non-PK ID column.

**Root cause.** The conditionality was introduced for a real reason: `DecimalComparator`'s
operands are typed with the `Decimal` scalar, which is itself declared only when a column uses
it, so an unconditional `DecimalComparator` block would reference an undeclared scalar and
gqlgen would reject the schema. Extending that rule to all six families was the coherent
implementation choice, but it widened a spec-sanctioned rule for the nullable twin into an
unsanctioned one for the base form, and the 25.3 completion record then wrongly claimed the
result was byte-neutral (corrected in place 2026-08-26).

**Suggested fix.** Pick one and make spec and code agree:
- **Preferred** — amend §26.4 so the emission rule reads on the family, not on the nullable
  variant alone: a comparator input of either form is emitted only when some column references
  it. State the reason (operand types can name a usage-gated custom scalar, so an unreferenced
  input can reference an undeclared one), which also documents why the rule is not merely a
  size optimisation.
- Alternative — restore unconditional emission for the five base families and special-case
  `DecimalComparator`. Rejected on review as incoherent, and it leaves the `Time` gap in
  FIX-141 wide open.
- Either way, add a unit test that pins the chosen rule directly (today it is only implied by
  `TestComparatorFamilies_emittedOnlyWhenReferenced`).

**References.**
- PRD §26.4 "Comparator input projection" (`:10494-10530`), Rule 2 (`:10501-10505`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` `collectComparatorFamilies`.
- Goldens: `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql_top_level/graph/shared_gen.graphqls` (lost
  `BooleanComparator`, `IDComparator`), `.../expected/graph/shared_gen.graphqls`.
- FIX-141 — the `Time` instance of the same undeclared-scalar failure mode.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26 via the **preferred** option — the spec was amended to match the code, not the reverse. `docs/PRD.md` §26.4 gains **Rule 3**: a comparator input is emitted only when some column references it, for **both** forms. The rule is stated as a correctness requirement rather than a size optimisation, with the reason on the page — a family's operand type may name a scalar that is itself declared only on use (`Time`, `Decimal`), so an unreferenced input can name an undeclared scalar and gqlgen rejects the document. Rule 3 also pins the companion-range behaviour (`NumericRange` / `TimeRange` declared exactly once alongside whichever form is emitted). `TestComparatorFamilies_emittedOnlyWhenReferenced` was repointed to cite Rule 3, so the newly-normative rule has a direct pin rather than being implied. The alternative (reverting base-form conditionality and special-casing `DecimalComparator`) was rejected as incoherent and because it leaves FIX-141's `Time` gap open.

### FIX-139

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 25, docs/PRD.md (§26.5.3)
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **PRD §26.5.3 describes a nullable-translator shape that 25.3 makes inexpressible.**
`docs/PRD.md:10796` states that nullable variants "take the **`Nullable<X>Comparator`** input
([§26.4] Rule 2), **delegate the shared operands to the base translator**, lift the result into
`comparator.Nullable<X>`, and carry that input's `isNull` operand into the wrapper's `Null`
field". The first and last clauses are correct; the middle one cannot hold. Rule 2 makes
`<X>Comparator` and `Nullable<X>Comparator` two distinct GraphQL input types, so gqlgen emits
two distinct Go types and `translateNullableStringComparator(in *NullableStringComparator)`
has nothing it can pass to `translateStringComparator(in *StringComparator)`.

**Root cause.** B4 wrote the sentence during 25.0, when the nullable variant genuinely did
delegate (it took the *same* base input, and the base translator was force-registered
alongside it). 25.0's own F1 post-review round then introduced Rule 2's separate-input-type
model without revisiting §26.5.3's delegation clause, so the two halves of the same paragraph
became mutually exclusive. 25.3 implemented Rule 2 and dropped the delegation; the paragraph
did not follow.

**Suggested fix.**
- `docs/PRD.md:10796` — replace "delegate the shared operands to the base translator, lift the
  result into `comparator.Nullable<X>`" with a statement of what is actually generated: the
  nullable variant copies the shared operands directly onto the `comparator.Nullable<X>` value,
  which is possible without duplication because `Nullable<X>` embeds `<X>` and Go promotes the
  field assignments.
- Say explicitly that the base translator is emitted only when a NOT NULL column references it
  — it is no longer implied by the nullable one.
- No code change; the implementation is the correct reading of Rule 2.

**References.**
- PRD §26.5.3 (`:10796`), §26.4 "Comparator input projection" Rule 2 (`:10501-10505`).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/comparator_translate.go.tmpl` (the `api/comparator-operands`
  fragment, shared by both variants), `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` `buildAPIFilterFields`
  (base no longer force-registered).
- FIX-134 — the prior instance of 25.0 text pinning a shape the implementation then had to
  diverge from.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26. `docs/PRD.md` §26.5.3 — the delegation clause is replaced with what is actually generated: the nullable variant copies the shared operands **directly onto** a `comparator.Nullable<X>` value, because Rule 2 makes the two inputs distinct GraphQL types and therefore distinct Go types, leaving it nothing to hand to `translate<X>Comparator`. The paragraph now also records why this costs no duplication (`Nullable<X>` embeds `<X>`, so one operand block compiles against either receiver through field promotion) and adds the consequence the old text hid: the base translator is emitted **only when a `NOT NULL` column references it**, no longer pulled in by the nullable one. Documentation only — no code change; the implementation was the correct reading of Rule 2 all along.

### FIX-135

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, docs/PRD.md (§11.1 / §11.5 / Appendix A)
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.0 (2026-08-25)

**Issue.** **Ticket D has no normative PRD text: B8 was never in the delta list, and §11.1's
relationship-filter invariant 2 points at a section with no relevant content.** `grep -n
"PrefixConditions\|prefixCondition\|qualified at codegen" docs/PRD.md` returns **zero** hits, so

Invariant 2 (`:6921`) closes with "see [§11.5](#115-condition-composition)", but §11.5
(`:7012-7086`) documents raw condition types and `ConditionBuilder` and says nothing about
aliasing, prefixing, or qualifiers — the F5 post-review repoint moved a dangling reference from
Appendix A to §11.5 rather than resolving it. Two smaller gaps ride along: §11.1 says "one
field per **list** relationship" and then "the FK column for O2M / **O2O**" (`:6835`, `:6892`) —
an O2O is not a list relationship, so an implementer can defensibly emit no member for
`task.project`; and the `EXISTS` example is PostgreSQL-only (`$N`, `"…"`) with no statement of
cross-dialect shape, against the project's multi-dialect rule.

**Root cause.** The design doc's §5 delta table enumerated B1–B7 and omitted the `sql/`
affordance entirely, so 25.0 could not have landed it; the tracker records this as B8
outstanding. Invariant 2's wording is the residue of the post-review F4 correction, which
replaced a wrong rule with an accurate statement of the *problem* and left the citation
pointing at the nearest plausible section.

**Suggested fix.**
- Settle the rev-F4 correlation-qualifier decision recorded above §25.10 in
  `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` (recommendation on file: structured `sql.Exists(...)`), then land
  **B8** — Appendix A and/or §11.5 gain the affordance, the alias-prefixing behavior of the O2O
  read path, and the qualifier contract — before 25.10 starts.
- Repoint §11.1 invariant 2 at the new B8 text once it exists.
- §11.1 — say explicitly which relationship kinds contribute a filter member (list only: O2M /
  M2M) and keep the join-metadata sentence separate from the emission rule, so `FKColumn` reads
  as "where the metadata lives" rather than "O2O gets a member".
- §11.1 — add one sentence on the cross-dialect `EXISTS` shape (identical structure; quoting and
  placeholder style per dialect).
- No test — documentation only; 25.10/25.11 carry the tests.

**References.**
- PRD §11.1 "Relationship filters" (`:6889-6923`), §11.5 (`:7012`), Appendix A.
- `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` — the OPEN DECISION block above §25.10 (rev-F4 / rev-F6), which
  already gates Ticket D.
- `sql/condition.go:143-167` (`prefixCondition`), `sql/builder.go:90-124` (`BuildSelect`
  unaliased vs `BuildSelectJoin` aliased) — the behavior needing normative text.
- `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL_READ_SURFACE.md` §1.2 F8, §2-D10, §3.4.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-25. The blocking half — the rev-F4 correlation-qualifier decision — was settled as **D11: structured `sql.Exists(correlationColumn, subquery)`, qualifier resolved by the builder**. Two properties decided it: codegen never has to know which read path will run, and exemption from alias prefixing is **by construction** (a structured condition value is not a leaf clause — the same shape `And` / `Or` / `Subquery` / `Range` already take through `expandCondition`, `sql/builder.go:462`) rather than a `Qualified bool` opt-out a caller can forget. The substitute-token and always-alias alternatives were rejected — stringly-typed clauses failing at the DB, and rewriting the SQL text of every non-join `SELECT` in the project, respectively. **B8 then landed:** PRD §11.5 gains `Exists` in the raw-types list plus a **Correlated EXISTS and qualifier resolution** subsection (two-builder qualifier table; four rules — builder supplies the qualifier, `PrefixConditions` never rewrites it, placeholder numbering unchanged, dialect deltas are quoting/placeholders only); Appendix A gains an **Alias-qualified columns** note pointing at it; §11.1 invariant 2 was repointed from the contentless `#115-condition-composition` target to `#correlated-exists-and-qualifier-resolution` and now states the rule instead of the problem. The earlier ungated halves (list-only emission scope with the to-one carve-out, the cross-dialect sentence, and 25.11's realignment) landed 2026-08-25 as recorded above. `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL_READ_SURFACE.md` carries D11 and a settled-marker on §3.4's F8 paragraph; `docs/tracker/phase-25.md`'s OPEN DECISION block is now SETTLED and 25.10 / 25.11's tasks name the chosen mechanism. Ticket D is unblocked. No code change in this fix — 25.10 implements it.

  (`resolveGenericComparator`, `columnIsFilterable`, `isComparableSliceElement`).

### FIX-134

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 25, docs/PRD.md (§8.5 / §26.4 sort enum)
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.0 (2026-08-25)

**Issue.** **The PRD states the D1 single-derivation invariant for sort but never pins the
canonical enum-value spelling, so 25.1 can satisfy every written requirement and still emit an
invalid schema.** §8.5's GraphQL table (`docs/PRD.md:2420-2424`) covers *field* names only
(`2010_revenue` → `col2010Revenue` / `col_2010_revenue`); §26.4 says only "Enum values always
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" (`:10192`, `:10239`). F5 is exactly the disagreement between
`screamingSnakeCase` (`funcmap.go:300-302`, `col_` prefix on digit-leading names) and
`strings.ToUpper(toSnakeCase(...))` (`context_api.go:1154`, no prefix). D1 (`:10771`) requires
the two emitters to converge but not on **which** spelling — and converging on the translator's
current one yields `2010_REVENUE`, which is not a legal GraphQL `Name`
(`/[_A-Za-z][_0-9A-Za-z]*/`), so the generated schema would fail to parse.

**Root cause.** B4 landed the invariant as a *structural* requirement (one derivation, two
readers) without landing the *value* requirement it presupposes. The PRD's only digit-leading
guidance lives in §8.5's field-name table, which a reader implementing sort enums has no reason
to treat as normative for enum values.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add one row (or one sentence) to §8.5's GraphQL surface table covering **enum values**:
  `2010_revenue` → `COL_2010_REVENUE`, with the GraphQL `Name`-grammar reason — the same guard
  that already forces `col2010Revenue` for fields.
- Cross-reference it from §26.4's sort-enum text so the sort emitter's spec is reachable from
  the section that emits it.
- 25.1's acceptance criteria should then cite that row for its F5 case instead of asserting the
  spelling itself.
- No test in this fix — 25.1 carries the digit-leading golden case.

**References.**
- PRD §8.5 Naming Rules (GraphQL surface table), §26.4 (`:10192`, `:10239`), §26.5.3 D1
  invariant (`:10771`).
- `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL_READ_SURFACE.md` §1.2 F5 — the finding, with both spellings cited.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap.go:300-302`, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go:1154`.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved inline 2026-08-25 during `/verify 25.0` follow-up. §8.5 gained a **GraphQL enum values** paragraph directly under the existing field-name guard: enum values carry the same `Name` constraint, so a value derived from a digit-leading column takes the `col_` guard in both `field_casing` modes — `2010_revenue` → `COL_2010_REVENUE`, with the explicit note that a bare `2010_REVENUE` is not a legal GraphQL `Name` and the schema would fail to parse. It names `<T>SortField` and `<t>SortFieldToColumn` as the consumers that must agree. Three cross-references now point at it: §26.4's naming table row (which gained `COL_2010_REVENUE` as an example), the §26.4 field-casing paragraph, and §26.5.3's D1 invariant, which now closes by resolving the single sort derivation to the §8.5 spelling. 25.1's F5 case is therefore citable rather than derivable.

### FIX-132

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 25, docs/PRD.md (§26.4 comparator input projection)
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.0 (2026-08-25)

**Issue.** **Rule 1's monomorphization list wrongly includes `Number[T]`, contradicting the
family matrix, the worked example, §26.5.3, and the shipped template.** `docs/PRD.md:10467`
states that "`comparator.Enum[T]` / `Slice[T]` / `Number[T]` cannot be a single input type —
each is specialized per concrete type parameter", but the matrix at `:10482` maps
`Number[T]` / `NullableNumber[T]` to a **single** `NumericComparator` with `Float` operands,
the example at `:10334` writes `stock: NumericComparator`, and `:10765` explains that only the
*translators* are per-Go-`T` (`translateNumericComparatorInt32`) precisely **because** the
GraphQL scalar is one shared `Float`. `templates/api/shared.graphqls.tmpl:38-46` emits exactly
one `NumericComparator` today. 25.1's acceptance criterion requires byte-identical
regeneration for the existing five families, which Rule 1 as written forbids.

**Root cause.** Rule 1 was written from design decision D3, which enumerated the three generic
Go comparator families without distinguishing the one whose type parameter **collapses** on the
GraphQL side: every Go numeric binds to the single `Float` scalar, so `Number[T]` has nothing
to monomorphize *over*. Two dependent statements inherit the error: the Sharing rule at
`:10495` ("one input type per (family, type parameter, nullability) triple") implies
`Int32NumericComparator` / `Float64NumericComparator`, and the §26.4 mapping-table row at
`:10231` ("one per comparator family **per concrete type parameter**") was never updated for
Rule 2's nullability split, so the summary row a reader hits first describes neither the
pre-25.0 nor the post-25.0 model.

**Suggested fix.**
- `docs/PRD.md:10467` — drop `Number[T]` from Rule 1's list and state the carve-out explicitly:
  every Go numeric type binds to the one `Float` scalar, so the numeric family projects
  **unmonomorphized** and the per-`T` split lives in the translator (§26.5.3), not the schema.
- `docs/PRD.md:10495` — restate Sharing as "(family, **GraphQL operand type**, nullability)" so
  the numeric collapse falls out of the rule instead of contradicting it.
- `docs/PRD.md:10231` — rewrite the mapping row to name both axes actually in play:
  monomorphized generic families **and** the `Nullable<X>` split.
- No test — documentation only. The exit gate is that 25.1's byte-identity criterion and
  25.3/25.4/25.5's naming can each cite text that agrees with the others.

**References.**
- PRD §26.4 "Comparator input projection" (Rule 1, Sharing, family matrix), §26.5.3 (translator
  per-`T` rationale), §11.2 (Go-side selection).
- `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL_READ_SURFACE.md` §2-D3 — the decision Rule 1 was derived from.
- `templates/api/shared.graphqls.tmpl:38-46` — the single shipped `NumericComparator`.
- Same defect class as the 25.0 post-review F1 (Rule 2 self-contradiction), one rule over.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved inline 2026-08-25 during `/verify 25.0` follow-up. Rule 1 retitled "monomorphize the generic families **whose type parameter survives the binding**": `Enum[T]` and `Slice[T]` are specialized per concrete type, `Number[T]` is called out as the explicit exception (every Go numeric width binds to the one `Float` scalar, so the family projects unmonomorphized as a single `NumericComparator` and the per-`T` split lives in the translator, §26.5.3). Sharing is now keyed on (family, **GraphQL operand type**, nullability) so the numeric collapse falls out of the rule instead of contradicting it, with an explicit sentence saying so. The §26.4 mapping row was rewritten to name both live axes (monomorphized generic families **and** the `Nullable<X>` split) instead of the stale per-type-parameter phrasing. Design decision D3 needed no change — it never listed `Number[T]`; the error was introduced when D3 was transcribed into Rule 1. No code, template, or golden change.

### FIX-131

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 24, event/natsbus
- **Surfaced by:** /implement 24.8 auto-review (sqlgen-reviewer, 2026-07-31)

**Issue.** `(*Bus).Close` and `(*subscription).Unsubscribe` both read and nil
each subscription's `natsSub` / `jsConsume` handles, but `Close` did so
**outside** the bus lock while `Unsubscribe` does so **under** `b.mu`. A
concurrent `bus.Close()` + `sub.Unsubscribe()` is therefore an unsynchronized
read/write of the same fields — a data race, and a possible double
`Stop()`/`Unsubscribe()` on one handle. Latent (no test exercised the
concurrent path; `-race` passed only because nothing raced it), but real.

**Root cause.** `Close` snapshotted `b.subs` and released `b.mu`, then iterated
the snapshot mutating `s.jsConsume`/`s.natsSub` with no lock held
(`natsbus.go` Close loop). The pattern predates 24.8 — it is identical to the
prior `natsSub`-only `Close` (commit 169786b) — but 24.8 copied it to the new
`jsConsume` field, widening the exposed surface, so it is fixed here.

**Root fix.** `Close` now detaches each subscription's handles **under the
lock** (captures them into a local `pending` slice and nils the shared fields
in the same critical section), then performs the network `Stop()` /
`Unsubscribe()` calls on the captured copies **outside** the lock (and
`conn.Drain()` stays outside the lock as before). Both `Close` and
`Unsubscribe` now touch the handle fields only under `b.mu`; whichever runs
first nils them and the other sees nil and skips, so each handle is stopped
exactly once. No lock is held across a network call that wasn't already (the
long `Drain` remains off-lock).

**References.**
- `event/natsbus/natsbus.go` — `(*Bus).Close`, `(*subscription).Unsubscribe`.
- 24.8 completion record (`docs/tracker/phase-24.md`) — auto-review "Regression Risks".
- PRD §28.2 — natsbus concurrency-safety claim.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved inline 2026-07-31 during 24.8. Reworked `Close`
to the snapshot-and-nil-under-lock pattern above (network calls stay off the
lock; `Drain` unchanged). Added `TestCloseUnsubscribeConcurrentNoRace`
(`natsbus_test.go`) — 8 core subscriptions with `Close` raced against a
concurrent `Unsubscribe` on every one; passes `-race` (verified `-count=50`).
`make check` green all modules; `golangci-lint` 0 issues; `gofumpt` clean. No
`event`-pkg/generator/golden change; no E2E or security trigger
(`event/natsbus/**` matches no path glob).

### FIX-130

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** nit
- **Origin:** phase 19, cmd/sqlgen/mcp
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 19.3 (2026-07-10)

**Issue.** `sqlgen_find_referencing`'s result sort omits the `Kind` field
from its tiebreak, so two `Reference` values that differ *only* in `Kind`
would sort as equal under the unstable `sort.Slice` and could serialize in
either order — a latent violation of the §6.5 byte-equal-on-repeat
determinism rule. The trigger is practically unreachable (it needs two
references with identical `Entity` + `RelationshipName` + `FKColumn` but
different `Kind`), but §6.5 makes determinism a hard rule regardless of
reachability.

**Root cause.** `lessReference` (`cmd/sqlgen/mcp/tools_graph.go:98-107`)
orders on `Entity`, then `RelationshipName`, then `FKColumn`, and stops —
while `findReferencing` deduplicates on the full `Reference` struct
including `Kind` (`tools_graph.go:55-61`). The dedup key is wider than the
sort key, so a `Kind`-only difference survives dedup but has no defined
sort order. `findMethod`'s `sort.Slice` (`tools_entity.go:175-181`) has the
same theoretical shape for a name duplicated across `Methods.Query` and
`Methods.Mutation`, and is equally benign.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add `Kind` as the final tiebreak in `lessReference` (after `FKColumn`).
- Optionally harden `findMethod`'s comparator with a `Signature` (or
  `Kind`) final tiebreak for symmetry.
- Add a `TestDispatch_Deterministic`-style case (or extend
  `TestFindReferencing`) with two references differing only in `Kind` to
  pin the order — or note in the test that the case is unreachable and the
  tiebreak is defensive.

**References.**
- MCP.md §6.5 — determinism (byte-equal JSON-RPC on repeat; sorted
  collections, no map-iteration leaks).
- `cmd/sqlgen/mcp/tools_graph.go:98-107` (`lessReference`), `:55-61`
  (full-struct dedup).
- Surfaced by the `sqlgen-reviewer` independent pass during /verify 19.3.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-07-10 via /fix-implement. Widened both
affected comparators to match their dedup keys: `lessReference`
(`cmd/sqlgen/mcp/tools_graph.go`) gains `Kind` as the final tiebreak (after
`FKColumn`), so two references differing only in `Kind` now have a defined,
byte-stable order; `findMethod`'s `sort.Slice` (`cmd/sqlgen/mcp/tools_entity.go`)
gains a `Signature` final tiebreak for the same reason (a name duplicated
across `Methods.Query`/`Methods.Mutation`). Regression test
`TestFindReferencingKindTiebreak` (`tools_graph_test.go`) constructs the
otherwise-unreachable Entity+RelationshipName+FKColumn tie (Target owns two
same-named `link` relationships to A over `a.ref_id`, differing only in kind)
and pins the `m2o`-before-`o2m` order plus byte-equality across independent
runs. `make check` clean (0 lint, all unit tests `-race`); no goldens affected
(MCP is not in the generation path, so `make check-examples` not triggered).

### FIX-127

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/manifest
- **Surfaced by:** /implement 18.9 (2026-07-09)

**Issue.** CHECK constraints do not surface in the manifest end-to-end. A
table-level `CONSTRAINT ... CHECK (unit_price >= 0 AND quantity > 0)` on
postgres `order_items` (and column/table CHECKs on sqlite) generates without
error but produces empty `check` fields in the emitted `manifest_gen.json`.
The symptom is that no `Column.check` value ever appears for a real generated
package, so PRD §30.7's per-column CHECK surface is unrepresented despite the
builder having flatten logic for it.

**Root cause.** `checkExpressionForColumn`
(`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go:641`) flattens a CHECK onto a column only when
`slices.Contains(c.Columns, colName)` — i.e. only when `parser.Constraint.Columns`
lists the column. But none of the three dialect parsers populate
`Constraint.Columns` for CHECK-typed constraints; they set only
`CheckExpression` (postgres `parseConstraintNode` CONSTR_CHECK case sets
`CheckExpression` via `deparseExpr` but never a column list; sqlite
`parseTableConstraint` and mysql `parseConstraintDef` likewise). So the flatten
predicate is never true and every `check` field stays empty. The 18.2 builder
unit tests masked this by hand-setting `Constraint.Columns` on synthetic
`parser.Table` fixtures, proving the flatten given populated columns but never
that any parser populates them.

**Suggested fix.**
- Extend each dialect parser to extract the referenced column identifiers from
  the CHECK expression AST into `parser.Constraint.Columns` when parsing a
  CHECK constraint (postgres `parser/postgres/postgres.go` CONSTR_CHECK;
  sqlite `parser/sqlite/sqlite.go` `parseTableConstraint`; mysql
  `parser/mysql/mysql.go` `parseConstraintDef`).
- Alternatively/additionally, have the manifest builder emit table-wide CHECKs
  (empty `Columns`) at entity level rather than only per-column, per PRD §30.7.
- Add regression coverage: a real-pipeline test (or an example fixture golden)
  asserting a multi-column CHECK surfaces on each participating column's
  `check` field. Re-add the deferred 18.9 CHECK example fixtures (postgres +
  mysql `order_items`) once surfacing works, and regenerate goldens.

**References.**
- PRD §30.7 — `check` per-column extended metadata.
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go:481` (call site), `:639-657` (`checkExpressionForColumn`).
- 18.2 completion record (builder_test synthetic CHECK coverage) in `docs/tracker/phase-18.md`.
- Related: FIX-107 (parser Constraint extended with Method/Where for index metadata).

**Resolution notes.** Fixed builder-side (matching origin `cmd/sqlgen/manifest`)
rather than touching three parser ASTs: the parsers all populate
`CheckExpression` correctly — only `Constraint.Columns` is empty for CHECKs — so
the builder can derive the participating columns from the expression itself. New
`checkConstraintColumns` falls back, when `c.Columns` is empty, to
`columnsInExpression`, which matches identifier tokens from the CHECK expression
against the table's real column names. Tokenizing is done by a lightweight
`expressionIdentifiers` (+ `skipStringLiteral` / `readQuotedIdent` helpers): it
emits bare and double/backtick-quoted identifiers and skips single-quoted string
literals (honouring `''` escapes) so a column name inside a literal does not
falsely match. An explicit `Columns` list still takes priority, keeping the
existing hand-set test green. Regression tests added:
`TestBuild_CheckConstraintDerivesColumnsFromExpression` (real parser shape —
`CheckExpression` set, `Columns` empty — asserts the CHECK flattens onto exactly
the two named columns) and `TestBuild_CheckConstraintExpressionLiteralNotMatched`
(string-literal skip). Re-added the deferred E2E fixtures: a named table-level
`CHECK (unit_price >= 0 AND quantity > 0)` on postgres + mysql + sqlite
`order_items`; regenerated goldens — `check` now flattens onto `quantity` +
`unit_price` in `manifest_gen.json` and the per-entity markdown's "Check
constraints" section. Each dialect's deparser emits a different expression
shape, so the three fixtures together exercise all tokenizer paths: postgres
`unit_price >= 0 AND quantity > 0` (bare identifiers), mysql
`unit_price >= 0 and quantity > 0` (vitess lowercases `and`), and sqlite
`"unit_price" >= 0 AND "quantity" > 0` (rqlite double-quotes identifiers,
exercising `readQuotedIdent`). `make check` +
`make check-examples` (Docker) clean; regenerated example output compiles and
passes against real postgres/mysql. Parser-side extraction of `Constraint.Columns`
was deliberately not pursued — it would duplicate identifier extraction across
three different AST libraries and diverge the DDL-parse path from the introspect
path (which also sets only `CheckExpression`); the builder-side derivation keeps
all paths uniform.

### FIX-129

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/gen
- **Surfaced by:** /implement 18.9 (2026-07-09)

**Issue.** `output.layout: file_per_table` emitted per-table `*_gen.go` files
that did not compile: each file was missing the `context`, `comparator`, `sql`,
`database`, `omittable`, `iter`, `time`, `errgroup` (etc.) imports its body
referenced, e.g. `article_gen.go` used `context.` / `comparator.` 92 times with
only `hook` + `types` imported. No example had ever used `file_per_table`, so
the breakage was latent — surfaced when 18.9 flipped the sqlite example to that
layout to guard the manifest_embed stale-sweep ordering.

**Root cause.** A table/view context's declared `Imports`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:326-338`) are intentionally incomplete —
`context`/`comparator`/`sql`/… are back-filled by goimports import-resolution.
`generateTablesSingleFile` runs `Format` (goimports with resolution) so the
single combined file gets them. But `generateTablesPerFile` /
`generateViewsPerFile` used `FormatOnly` (gofmt, no resolution) on each file,
trusting the incomplete `Imports` — so the back-filled packages were never
added.

**Suggested fix.**
- Resolve the package's complete import set once over the concatenated bodies
  (`resolvePackageImports`, `cmd/sqlgen/gen/format.go`) — a single module-cache
  scan — then emit each per-file with that full set and `Format`, which prunes
  the imports the file does not use WITHOUT re-scanning (goimports skips the
  scan when nothing is missing; measured ~6ms/file). Keeps output correct and
  file_per_table generation fast (~one scan regardless of table count) rather
  than `Format`-per-file (a scan each, ~1.3s/file).
- Regression coverage: `gen.TestResolvePackageImports_BackfillsAndPrunes`
  (unit) + the sqlite `file_per_table` E2E example, whose `TestE2EGoldenFiles`
  + `check-examples` compile guards against future import drift.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go` `generateTablesPerFile` / `generateViewsPerFile`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/format.go` `Format` vs `FormatOnly` (`FormatOnly:` option).
- PRD §5 (deterministic, compiling generated output).

**Resolution notes.** Fixed in-scope during /implement 18.9 (blocking 18.9's
file_per_table stale-sweep guard). `generateTablesPerFile` /
`generateViewsPerFile` now resolve the complete import set once via
`resolvePackageImports` and emit each file with prune-only `Format`. sqlite
file_per_table output compiles; `make check` + `make check-examples` green.

### FIX-128

- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/manifest
- **Surfaced by:** /implement 18.9 (2026-07-09)

**Issue.** View entities emitted `"indexes": null` in `manifest_gen.json`, which

- Regression coverage: the real-output schema validation

**References.**

- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/schema/v1.json` (`indexes` typed as array).

### FIX-126

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/cli
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 18.8 (2026-07-09)

**Issue.** `sqlgen manifest diff` under-detects column and method **changes**.
`columnSig` (`cmd/sqlgen/cli/cmd_manifest_diff.go:238-244`) builds a column's
change-signature from `GoType`, `DBType`, and `Nullable` only. A column that
flips `PK`, `Unique`, `Default`, `DefaultKind`, `Check`, `Comparator`, or
`Comment` — with its Go/DB type unchanged — produces an identical signature, so
the diff reports **no change** for that column. `methodSig`
(`cmd_manifest_diff.go:257-263`) similarly omits `Errors[]` and `Notes`.
Added/removed detection is correct; only the "changed" dimension is blind. For a
tool whose PRD §30.8 purpose is gating "schema changes are intentional and
reviewed," a silently-missed PK or UNIQUE flip is a meaningful blind spot in a
PR-review workflow.

**Root cause.** `columnSig` intentionally hashes a narrow subset of
`manifest.Column` fields; `methodSig` a narrow subset of `manifest.Method`. The
enumerated 18.8 acceptance criteria only require detecting a column *type*
change (which is covered and tested), so the narrower attributes were never
folded into the signatures. PRD §30.8 does not enumerate the column-attribute
set, so this is a robustness gap rather than a stated-requirement failure.

**Suggested fix.**
- Widen `columnSig` to include, at minimum, `PK`, `Unique`, and `Default`
  (consider `DefaultKind` / `Check` / `Comparator` as well) so a constraint
  flip surfaces as a `~ <col>` change with a readable old→new rendering.
- Widen `methodSig` to include `Errors[]` (join sorted) so an error-set change
  surfaces; `Notes` is lower priority.
- Add `cmd/sqlgen/cli/cmd_manifest_diff_test.go` cases: a column flipping
  `Unique: false → true` (and `PK` membership) yields a `~ <col>` change entry;
  a method gaining an error sentinel yields a `~ <method>` change entry.

**References.**
- PRD §30.8 — "walk entities / columns / methods / sentinels / features, print
  structured diff (added / removed / changed)"; stated purpose "schema changes
  are intentional and reviewed."
- `cmd/sqlgen/cli/cmd_manifest_diff.go:238-263` (`columnSig` / `methodSig`).
- `manifest/types.go` — full `Column` / `Method` field sets available to diff.

**Resolution notes.** Widened `columnSig`
(`cmd/sqlgen/cli/cmd_manifest_diff.go`) to render `null` / `pk` / `unique` /
`default=…` / `default_kind=…` / `check=…` / `comparator=…` alongside the
Go/DB type, and `methodSig` to append a **sorted** `errors=[…]` clause — so a
constraint or error-set flip on a column/method with unchanged type surfaces as
a `~ <name>` change, while a mere reordering of `errors[]` is not a spurious
diff. Added `TestManifestDiff_ColumnConstraintFlipped` (unique / pk / default
subtests), `TestManifestDiff_MethodErrorSetChanged`, and
`TestManifestDiff_MethodErrorReorderNotChanged`. `make check` clean across all
8 modules; change is confined to `cmd/sqlgen/cli/**` (no generated-output or
golden impact, no `check-examples` trigger).

### FIX-125

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/config
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 18.6 (2026-07-09)

**Issue.** A validation-legal manifest config produced a **non-compiling**
generated package. With `manifest: { enabled: true, formats: [markdown] }` (JSON
excluded from `formats`; `embed_in_client` defaults to `true`), `RunStage` skips
`EmitJSON` (gated on `formatEnabled(m, json)`) but still rendered
`manifest_embed_gen.go`, whose `//go:embed manifest/manifest_gen.json` directive
then targeted a file that was never written. The consumer's `go build` failed on
the missing embed target. The default `formats` (`[json, markdown]`) is safe;
the break required an explicit `formats` override that drops `json`.

**Root cause.** The two gates were independent and inconsistent:
`formatEnabled` (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit.go`) gates JSON emission on
`m.Formats`, while `gen.BuildManifestEmbedContext`
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_manifest.go`) gates the embed file only on
`Enabled` + `EmbedInClient` — never checking whether JSON is actually emitted.
`validateManifestEnabledFields` (`cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go`) did not reject
`embed_in_client: true` with a `formats` list lacking `json`, so nothing
prevented the embed directive from referencing an unemitted JSON file.

**Chosen approach.** Validation rule — the smallest, most explicit fix: reject
the incoherent config up front rather than silently emitting a broken package or
force-emitting an artifact the user excluded.

**Fix applied.**
- Added a rule to `validateManifestEnabledFields` (`cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go`):
  when the *effective* `embed_in_client` is true (`ptrVal(m.EmbedInClient, true)`
  — nil resolves to the §30.2 default of true) and `formats` is non-empty but
  lacks `json`, it errors citing PRD §30.2 / §30.6 / §4.13 and names the two
  escape hatches (`embed_in_client: false` or add `json`). The `len(Formats) > 0`
  guard avoids double-reporting with the existing empty-formats rule.
- Treats nil as true (not explicit-true-only): the real bug fires with a
  *defaulted* embed (`applyManifestDefaults` sets it true when enabled), so an
  explicit-true-only check would miss the common case.
- Tests (`cmd/sqlgen/config/manifest_test.go`): new
  `TestValidatePreParse_Manifest_EmbedRequiresJSON` (5 cases: explicit-true /
  defaulted-nil / embed-off / json+markdown / json-only). Updated the existing
  `TestValidatePreParse_Manifest_UnknownFormat` cases to set
  `embed_in_client: false` so the "markdown-only valid" case stays focused on
  format-name validation without tripping the new rule.

**References.**
- PRD §30.2 (`formats`, `embed_in_client`); §30.6 (runtime-embedded manifest);
  §4.13 (manifest validation rules).
- `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go` (`validateManifestEnabledFields`);
  `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit.go` (`formatEnabled`);
  `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_manifest.go` (`BuildManifestEmbedContext` gating).

**Resolution notes.** `make check` clean across all 8 modules (lint 0 issues,
`-race`). Config-side fix only — no generated-output change; the emit/embed gates
were left as-is since validation now rejects the incoherent config before
generation runs. `make check-examples` re-run (validate.go path touched); no
example excludes json from a manifest `formats` list, so example output is
byte-unchanged.

**PRD-sync note (for /close-phase 18).** This rule *extends* rather than quotes
PRD §4.13's enumerated manifest-validation list — §4.13 currently ends at
"embed_in_client:true with enabled:false → error". The new rule is a
PRD-consistent inference from §30.6 ("`//go:embed manifest/manifest_gen.json`
(always)"): if the embed always references the JSON, json must be an emitted
format. Add the rule to §4.13's list during the 18.10 PRD sync so the spec and
validator stay in lockstep. Flagged by the /fix-implement auto-review.

### FIX-124

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/manifest
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 18.6 (2026-07-09)

**Issue.** PRD §30.3 (*GraphQL breadcrumbs*) states that when GraphQL is enabled
"the generated `graph/` package receives breadcrumb files (`graph/CLAUDE.md`,
`graph/AGENTS.md`)… via a relative path… so it adapts **whether graph is nested
under models or a top-level sibling**." 18.6's `RunStage` only emitted graph
breadcrumbs in **top-level-sibling (layered)** mode. In the default **nested**
layout (`resolver_dir: ./models/graph` under `output.dir: ./models`, as used by
the primary `graphql` example), no graph breadcrumb was emitted. This is a
PARTIAL against 18.6's "produces the full artifact set per PRD §30.3" acceptance
criterion. The gap is significant because the graph breadcrumb carries content a
parent `models/CLAUDE.md` does **not** — pointers to the sibling `*_gen.graphqls`
files and PRD §26 resolver/walker semantics — so upward agent traversal to
`models/CLAUDE.md` is not a substitute.

**Root cause.** `ResolveGraphBreadcrumbDir` (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit.go`)
gated on `graphTopLevel(cfg)`, returning `""` for any non-layered graph layout;
`RunStage` then passed `GraphDir: ""` to both `EmitBreadcrumbs` and `CleanStale`,
so the graph breadcrumb was never emitted or managed in nested mode. Yet
`EmitBreadcrumbs` was *built and tested* to handle a nested graph dir —
`TestEmitBreadcrumbs_LayeredRelativePath` (`emit_breadcrumbs_test.go:91`, "nested
graph under models") pins the inward `../manifest/_index.md` relative path — and
18.5's own task text specified 18.6 sets `GraphDir` "when GraphQL is enabled,"
not "when layered." The wiring narrowed that to `graphTopLevel`.

**Chosen approach.** Emit breadcrumbs for the nested graph package too — the PRD
reading. The graph breadcrumb carries graph-specific pointers the parent models
breadcrumb lacks, so it is emitted whenever the graph package is a distinct
directory, regardless of layered vs nested.

**Fix applied.**
- Broadened `ResolveGraphBreadcrumbDir` to gate on `graphQLEnabled(cfg)` (not
  `graphTopLevel`) and return `cfg.API.GraphQL.ResolverDir`, with a guard that
  returns `""` when the graph dir resolves to `output.dir` itself
  (`filepath.Rel == "."`) so the graph breadcrumb never collides with the models
  breadcrumb on `<output.dir>/CLAUDE.md`.
- No emitter change: `EmitBreadcrumbs` / `CleanStale` already consume `GraphDir`
  and compute the inward relative path, so broadening the resolver auto-covers
  both emission and stale-cleanup symmetrically.
- Added `TestRunStage_NestedGraphBreadcrumbs` (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit_test.go`):
  a nested-graphql config (`resolver_dir = <output.dir>/graph`) asserts
  `graph/CLAUDE.md` + `graph/AGENTS.md` are emitted with the inward
  `../manifest/_index.md` pointer (distinct from the models breadcrumbs), and are
  swept on disable.

**References.**
- PRD §30.3 (*GraphQL breadcrumbs*, line ~12731); PRD §26.5.8.
- docs/tracker/phase-18.md §18.6 (acceptance: "full artifact set per PRD §30.3");
  §18.5 Tasks (GraphDir "when GraphQL is enabled").
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit.go` (`ResolveGraphBreadcrumbDir`);
  `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit_breadcrumbs_test.go:91` (nested case tested at the
  emitter layer since 18.5).

**Resolution notes.** `make check` clean across all 8 modules (lint 0 issues,
`-race`). `graphTopLevel` is retained (still drives the `generation_config`
`graph_top_level` toggle in `builder.go`); only the breadcrumb-dir resolver was
decoupled from it. `make check-examples` re-run (manifest path touched); no
example enables manifest, so example output is byte-unchanged.

### FIX-123

- **Surfaced by:** /verify 18.4 (2026-07-09)

**Issue.** 18.4's per-entity markdown template renders gated Read/Write example

UNTESTED. Not a §18.4 *Tests Required* item nor a pinned acceptance criterion —
a coverage gap on an implemented surface, tracked for closure before
`/close-phase 18`.

**Root cause.** `Entity.Examples` is `*Examples` (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/types.go`);
the shared fixture (`usersEntity` / `activeUsersView` in
`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit_json_test.go`) never populates it, and no dedicated
markdown test sets it, so the `## Read examples` / `## Write examples` fenced-`go`
blocks in `entity.md.tmpl` are never rendered or golden-pinned. In real
generation the branch *is* exercised (the 18.2 builder populates
`Entity.Examples` when `include_examples` resolves true, default true), so this
is a test-coverage gap, not dead code.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add a fixture entity (or a variant of `usersEntity`) that sets
  `Entity.Examples` with at least one Read line and one Write line, and pin its
  rendered `.md` (golden or `strings.Contains` assertions on the `## Read
  examples` / `## Write examples` headings + the `` ```go `` fences).
- Assert the fenced-`go` blocks are emitted verbatim (guards against
  `normalizeMarkdown` mangling multi-line example bodies — the fence-aware
  branch it added specifically to protect this content).
- Keep it in `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit_markdown_test.go` alongside the existing
  `TestEmitMarkdown_*` tests.

**References.**
- PRD §30.3 (per-entity artifact layout); §30.4.2 (`examples.{read,write}` shape).
- docs/tracker/phase-18.md §18.4 (task: "Read examples + write examples (gated
  by `include_examples`)").
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/templates/entity.md.tmpl` (the `{{- if .Examples }}`
  blocks); `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit_markdown.go` (`normalizeMarkdown`
  fence-awareness the example bodies rely on).

**Resolution notes.** Test-only fix — no production change (the branch was
already correct; it was merely unexercised). Added `TestEmitMarkdown_Examples`
(`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/emit_markdown_test.go`) with two subtests: (1) *read and
write* sets `Entity.Examples` with a multi-line Read body containing **two
consecutive** blank lines + a single Write line, and asserts both `## Read
examples` / `## Write examples` headings, exactly two ` ```go ` fences, the Write
line, and — the load-bearing assertion — that both blank lines between the two
Read lines survive verbatim inside the fence (`FindByID(ctx, id)\n\n\nlist,
err`), pinning `normalizeMarkdown`'s fence-awareness; (2) *read only* sets only
`Read` and asserts the Write heading + second fence are omitted, covering the
two independently-gated `{{- if .Examples.Read }}` / `{{- if .Examples.Write }}`
branches. Used a one-off entity via the existing `entityWithMethod` /
`renderEntityMarkdown` helpers rather than mutating `newFixtureDocument`, so the
shared JSON + markdown goldens are untouched.

**Auto-review catch (addressed before resolve).** The reviewer flagged that the
first draft used a *single* blank line, which would survive even without the
`inFence` guard — `normalizeMarkdown` only collapses a *run* of blanks (the first
blank in any run is always kept), so the fence-awareness claim was unguarded.
Corrected to two consecutive blank lines: fence-aware output keeps both
(`\n\n\n`); a regression that dropped the guard collapses them to one (`\n\n`),
so the assertion now truly distinguishes the paths. Verified by mutation —
neutering the `if !inFence &&` guard makes `TestEmitMarkdown_Examples` fail;
restoring it passes. `make check` + `make check-examples` clean (0 lint issues);
`TestEmitMarkdown_*` green. (`/fix-implement FIX-123`, 2026-07-09.)

### FIX-122

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/manifest
- **Surfaced by:** /implement 18.3 (2026-07-08) — flaked the `manifest` package test sweep (~1 in 4 runs)

**Issue.** `TestBuild_SQLBodies_InsertColumnSet` (`cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder_test.go`)
is **non-deterministically flaky** — it fails on roughly 1 in 4 runs with:

```
Upsert DO UPDATE SET wrong
  want substring: DO UPDATE SET "name" = excluded."name"
  --- body ---
  INSERT INTO "accounts" ("email", "name") VALUES ($1, $2) ON CONFLICT ("id")
    DO UPDATE SET "email" = excluded."email", "name" = excluded."name" ...
```

**Root cause.** Test-only defect; the generator output is deterministic and
correct. The `accounts` fixture has a serial PK `id` **and** a unique
constraint on `email`, so `buildMutationMethods` (`builder.go:1141`, iterating
the ordered `tc.ConflictTargets` slice) deterministically emits **two** upsert
methods: `Upsert` (conflict target `id`) and `UpsertByEmail` (conflict target
`email`). The test then selects "the first `Upsert*`" by ranging a **Go map**:

```go
byName := map[string]manifest.Method{}   // builder_test.go:842
...
for name, m := range byName {            // builder_test.go:869 — nondeterministic order
    if strings.HasPrefix(name, "Upsert") { upsert = m; break }
}
```

Map-iteration order is randomized, so the test grabs `Upsert` or `UpsertByEmail`
at random. Its assertions (`DO UPDATE SET "name"` only; `"email" = excluded`
banned) hold **only** for the `email`-conflict variant; when the range yields
the PK-conflict `Upsert`, its `DO UPDATE SET` legitimately updates the
non-conflict columns `email` + `name`, so the `"email" = excluded` ban trips.

**Suggested fix.** Test-only — no production change. Select the intended method
deterministically instead of by map order, e.g. `upsert := byName["UpsertByEmail"]`
(guard `ok`), or iterate a sorted key list and assert each `Upsert*` variant
against its own conflict target. Confirm green under `go test -run
TestBuild_SQLBodies_InsertColumnSet -count=50 ./cmd/sqlgen/manifest/`.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder_test.go` (`TestBuild_SQLBodies_InsertColumnSet`,
  the map-range selection at ~L869).
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder.go:1141` (`buildMutationMethods` — one upsert
  method per ordered conflict target).
- FIX-120 (the `sql_bodies` INSERT/UPSERT column-set work this test guards).
- PRD §5.7 (deterministic output — the property the test itself must honor).

**Resolution notes.** Fixed in `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/builder_test.go`.
`TestBuild_SQLBodies_InsertColumnSet` now selects the email-conflict `Upsert*`
variant **deterministically by its SQL body** (the one whose postgres body
contains `ON CONFLICT ("email")`) instead of taking the first `Upsert*` from a
Go-map range. Selecting on SQL content rather than a hardcoded method name keeps
it robust to upsert-naming changes and directly matches the test's stated intent
(the email-conflict variant strips `email` + the PK `id`, leaving only `name`
updatable). Green 50/50 under `go test -run TestBuild_SQLBodies_InsertColumnSet
-count=50 ./cmd/sqlgen/manifest/`; full `make check` clean under `-race`.
**Test-only — no production / codegen change** (generator output was already
deterministic; `buildMutationMethods` iterates the ordered `ConflictTargets`
slice). (`/fix-implement FIX-122`, 2026-07-09.)

### FIX-120

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/manifest
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 18.2 (2026-07-08); suggested-fix corrected during /verify review (2026-07-08)

**Issue.** `sql_bodies` for `Create` / `Upsert*` insert **all** columns
(`columnNames(tc)`), diverging from the generated `_gen.go` INSERT. Established
during /verify review by tracing the codegen INSERT path:
- The generated `Create` (`gen/templates/table/create.go.tmpl`) builds its
  column list **dynamically at runtime** — its membership depends on which
  omittable input fields the caller sets. It always **excludes** computed
  columns (`IsComputed`) and, for `PKStrategy == db`, auto-increment/serial PKs
  (`context_table.go:1262-1272`); nullable / `HasDefault` columns appear only
  when the caller supplies a value.
- The manifest's `sqlCreate` (`sql.go:163`) passes `columnNames(tc)` — every
  column unconditionally — so it includes serial PKs and computed columns the
  generated INSERT never emits.

Two consequences: (1) PRD §30.7's "agree by construction" is **unattainable in
the literal sense** for INSERT/UPSERT — there is no single static column list,
the runtime set is caller-dependent; the manifest can only publish a
*representative* body. (2) Even the representative body is wrong today because
it includes never-inserted columns (serial PK, computed).

**Root cause.** `sqlCreate` (`sql.go:163`) and `sqlUpsert` (`sql.go:178`) use
raw `columnNames(tc)` (sql.go:38) instead of the generation-time insert-column
classification. `TestBuild_SQLBodies_CoverEveryMethodType` (builder_test.go:695)
only asserts the `INSERT INTO "users"` prefix, so the column-set divergence is
unpinned. Upsert diverges a **second** way: its update-set uses
`nonConflictColumns` (sql.go:268), which strips only the conflict-target
columns, whereas the generated upsert (`upsert.go.tmpl:131`) also strips **all
PK columns and the tenant column** from the `DO UPDATE SET` clause.

**Suggested fix.**
- Derive the manifest INSERT columns from the already-exported, already-computed
  `tc.CreateInputFields` (`gen/context.go:456`, populated by `buildCreateInputFields`)
  rather than raw `columnNames(tc)`. Each field exposes `ColumnName` / `Required`
  / `Omittable`, so the manifest reproduces the computed + auto-inc-PK exclusion
  without reaching into unexported `gen` helpers. Emit the **maximal insertable
  set** (all required + all omittable columns) as the representative body.
- For `sqlUpsert`, also exclude PK columns and the tenant column from the
  update-set, mirroring `excludeColumns(columns, conflict + PK + tenant)` at
  `upsert.go.tmpl:131`.
- Update the `sql.go:11-16` header comment: "agree by construction" holds for
  the builder/dialect *shape*, not the column set for INSERT/UPSERT — state that
  those bodies are representative (maximal-insertable), since the runtime set is
  caller-dependent.
- Strengthen the test to pin the exact representative column list (assert serial
  PK / computed columns are absent), and cross-check against a real example
  golden during 18.9 E2E bring-up.

**References.**
- PRD §30.7 — `methods[].sql_bodies` "agree by construction" (needs the
  representative-body caveat).
- `cmd/sqlgen/manifest/sql.go:163` (sqlCreate), `sql.go:178` (sqlUpsert),
  `sql.go:268` (nonConflictColumns).
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go:1249-1290` (buildCreateInputFields exclusion
  rules), `gen/context.go:456` (`TableContext.CreateInputFields`),
  `gen/templates/table/create.go.tmpl`, `upsert.go.tmpl:131`.

**Resolution notes.** _Resolved 2026-07-08._ `sqlCreate` / `sqlUpsert`
(`manifest/sql.go`) now derive their INSERT column list from
`tc.CreateInputFields` via a new `insertableColumns(tc)` helper — the
maximal-insertable representative set — instead of raw `columnNames(tc)`. This
inherits `buildCreateInputFields`'s exclusions (computed columns, and
auto-increment/serial PKs under `PKStrategy == db`) with no reach into
unexported `gen` helpers, so the manifest INSERT column set now matches what the
generated `_gen.go` INSERT can emit. RETURNING is intentionally left as the full
`columnNames(tc)` set (the manifest documents the full row shape returned to the
caller; the generated Create RETURNs only the PK then re-reads via `Get`, a
different divergence out of FIX-120's scope). `sqlUpsert`'s `DO UPDATE SET` now
strips conflict + all PK + tenant columns via a new `upsertUpdateExclusions(tc,
conflict)` helper, mirroring `excludeColumns(columns, conflict + PK + tenant)` at
`upsert.go.tmpl:131` (previously it stripped only the conflict target). The
`sql.go:11-16` header comment now documents the representative-body caveat —
"agree by construction" holds for the builder/dialect shape, not a literal
column-for-column INSERT/UPSERT match. New regression test
`TestBuild_SQLBodies_InsertColumnSet` (`builder_test.go`) uses a serial-PK table
with a UNIQUE(email) conflict target to pin the exact representative INSERT
column list (serial PK absent from the VALUES half) and the upsert `DO UPDATE
SET` (conflict `email` + PK `id` stripped, only `name` remains). `make check`
clean across all modules; `make check-examples` clean (Docker) — the manifest
change is a read-only pass and does not perturb example generated output. No
manifest golden harness exists yet (Phase 18 emission lands in a later sub-item),
so no goldens regenerated; the suggested "cross-check against a real example
golden during 18.9 E2E bring-up" remains a forward note for that sub-item.

### FIX-119

- **Origin:** phase 18, cmd/sqlgen/manifest
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 18.2 (2026-07-08)

**Issue.** The conventions comparator block omits the `examples` key shown in

§30.4.1 exactly.

**Resolution notes.** Added `Examples map[string]string \`json:"examples,omitempty"\``
to `ComparatorConvention` (`types.go`) and populated it in `buildConventions`

none matched the real runtime comparator surface. Conventions the snippets now
follow: scalar operators are pointer fields (Go 1.26 `new(v)`), `In`/`Nin` are

are illustrative). **Auto-review caught an initial `is_null` snippet that named

before close.** Also synced the drifted **MANIFEST.md §5.2** comparator block
(families, `shape_notes`, `[]*Filter` composition, examples) and its §7 prose
family list to the real surface, since that design doc was the source of the
stale snippets. PRD §30.4.1 is intentionally abstract (`examples: {...}`) — left
