- [x] **FIX-099** (phase 8, cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming_test.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap_test.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/create.go.tmpl + cmd/sqlgen/gen/safety_property_test.go (NEW) + cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/schema.sql + cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/tests/reserved_words_test.go (NEW) + cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/expected/{client,models,sorter,tablenames}_gen.go + docs/PRD.md §8.5 + guidelines/TEMPLATES.md §4 / §5 + docs/IDENTIFIERS.md (NEW)) — **Generated `CreateMany` body fails to compile for any schema whose column name (lowercased) collides with a Go keyword.** Surfaced 2026-05-14 by a downstream production consumer whose schema had a column named `type`. `templates/table/create.go.tmpl` lowers each `CreateInputField.FieldName` into a per-column local via `{{ .FieldName | toCamelCase }}` at eight emission sites inside the per-batch loop (the `var <col> any = sql.Default` / `sql.NewDefaultExpr(...)` lines, their `if v, ok := input.<F>.Get(); ok { <col> = v }` assigns, and the `valueRows = append(valueRows, []any{<col>, ...})` row build). When the camelCase form lands on a Go keyword (`type`, `range`, `case`, `func`, `select`, `map`, `chan`, `return`, `interface`, `struct`, `package`, `const`, `import`, `defer`, `goto`, `fallthrough`, `go`, `var`, `if`, `else`, `for`, `continue`, `break`, `switch`, `default`), the rendered code is unparseable Go (`var type any = sql.Default` — syntax error). Point-of-use escape is 30 LOC plus a property test that pins the structural guarantee without restructuring the template. Full rationale in `docs/IDENTIFIERS.md` (new design supplement). **Surface delta.** (1) `cmd/sqlgen/gen/naming.go` gains `goReservedIdents` — a `map[string]bool` of 73 entries grouping Go keywords (25), predeclared types (22), predeclared constants (4 including `iota`/`nil`/`true`/`false`), predeclared functions (18 including Go 1.21+ `min`/`max`/`clear`), and generator-reserved locals (4: `ctx`, `err`, `v`, `ok`). Three categories are folded into one user-visible rule so PRD §8.5 documents "Go reserved word" once, not three times. `safeGoIdent(name string) string` returns `name + "Val"` when reserved, else passes through. (7) `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/sqlite/schema.sql` gains a `reserved_word_columns` table with 10 non-PK columns sampling each category: keywords (`type`, `interface`, `func`, `map`), predeclared identifiers (`new`, `make`, `len`, `error`), generator-reserved locals (`ctx`, `err`). AND name LIKE 'site_%'`), `PhotoAttachments` (o2m, `... AND name LIKE 'photo_%'`), `LinkedAttachments` (m2m via the junction, `... AND name LIKE 'link_%'`). Per-dialect integration test `TestSubCategorizedPolymorphism_MultiColumnFilter` with `O2O` / `O2M` / `M2M` sub-tests seeds matching + non-matching documents and asserts each relationship returns only the multi-column-filter-matched subset. Two failure modes: (a) `graphQLTypeForGoType` fell through to `String` for any Go type it didn't explicitly recognize, so `documents.entity_type` emitted as `entityType: String!` instead of `DocumentEntityTypeEnum!`. gqlgen had no models-merge entry binding `models.DocumentEntityTypeEnum`, so it generated a `documentResolver.EntityType` panic stub it couldn't bridge from the SQL-literal value (`"asset.primary"`) to a GraphQL `String`. (b) The same lookup missed the PostgreSQL-array companion type (`<Enum>Slice`), so an `entity_type_enum[]` column would have surfaced the same panic-stub trap on output AND a compile-time type mismatch in the input translator (`[]models.<Enum>` ≠ `models.<Enum>Slice`). **Impact:** any consumer with an enum-typed column exposed on the GraphQL surface hit panic-on-resolve at runtime; any consumer with an enum-array column never compiled. Pre-existing — surfaced for the first time when 17.3 wired the first enum column through `api: enabled`. → resolved 2026-05-12: landed the column-enum → GraphQL-enum projection end-to-end across both bare and slice paths. **Surface delta.** (1) **Context.** New `APIEnumContext` / `APIEnumValue` types on `APIContext.UsedEnums` (`context_api.go`). `BuildAPIContext` now accepts `[]EnumContext` (sourced from `BuildEnumContexts` in both `generateAPI` and the public `runGraphQLGen` entry — public `ComputeNameCollisions` exposed via `naming.go` so the latter can build its own collision set without rebuilding the whole pipeline). (2) **Per-column projection.** `graphQLTypeForGoType` consults a `goType → EnumContext` lookup populated from BOTH `e.GoTypeName` and `e.SliceGoTypeName`, so bare-enum and slice paths resolve symmetrically. `mapColumnToGraphQL` records each referenced enum in `usedEnumsByName` so the shared-schema template emits exactly the enum declarations actually referenced by an exposed column. (3) **Schema emission.** `templates/api/shared.graphqls.tmpl` now emits one `enum <GraphQLName> { ASSETPRIMARY ASSETATTACHMENT ASSETINVOICE SPV }` block per used enum. Identifier shape is `strings.ToUpper(toPascalCase(value))` — matches the existing `<T>SortField` convention so no new naming rule. (4) **Wire-format bridging.** `templates/enum.go.tmpl` gained `MarshalGQL(io.Writer)` / `UnmarshalGQL(any)` on both the bare enum AND its named-slice variant via duck typing (no gqlgen import in the models package — stdlib `io` only). The methods translate between the GraphQL identifier (`ASSETPRIMARY`) and the SQL literal (`asset.primary`) on every read/write, so the database column receives the SQL form unchanged. (5) **gqlgen models merge.** `cli/graphql.go::buildMergeInput` binds `<EnumGraphQLName> → [<modelsPkg>.<Enum>, <modelsPkg>.<Enum>Slice]`. Bare-enum entry listed first so gqlgen picks it for scalar contexts; the slice entry covers `[<Enum>!]!` fields without falling back to a resolver stub. (6) **Input-translator slice cast.** `buildAPIInputFields` detects when `col.IsSlice` and the model uses a named slice (suffix `Slice`, `col.SliceElemType != ""`), and emits `models.<Enum>Slice(in.<Field>)`. `funcInputCoerceDeref` applies the cast on the `GqlgenIsBareNullable` path too (gqlgen emits bare `[]T` for nullable slice update fields). `gqlgenIsBareNullable` extended to `col.IsSlice || (col.Nullable && (json/jsonmap))` so all slice columns flow through the no-deref branch uniformly. (7) **Enum-file import.** Added `io` to enum-file imports unconditionally — small cost, keeps the per-file import set deterministic regardless of API enablement. **Verification.** Curated-surface test (`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/tests/sub_categorized_polymorphism_test.go::TestCuratedSurface_SubCategorizedPolymorphism`) exercises the full enum + enum-slice round-trip: mutation seeds with `[ASSETPRIMARY, ASSETATTACHMENT]` and `entityType: ASSETPRIMARY`, query reads back `declaredCategories` as `[ASSETPRIMARY, ASSETATTACHMENT]` (slice MarshalGQL) and `entityType` as `ASSETPRIMARY/ASSETATTACHMENT/ASSETINVOICE` (scalar MarshalGQL). `make check` clean (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` tests green). `make check-examples` clean (graphql/tests ~27s, all other examples byte-stable since no other example yet exercises an enum column through the API surface).

- [x] **FIX-095** (phase 17, cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go::`applyConfigDeclaredFKs` + `BuildTableContexts`) — **Config-declared polymorphic FKs (a relationship's `fk:` pointing at a column with no SQL `REFERENCES` clause) emitted a comparator-type mismatch between the parent's `In:` filter and the child column's filter struct.** Surfaced 2026-05-12 while bringing up 17.3's example fixtures. The PRD §13.7.1 example deliberately omits `REFERENCES` on `documents.entity_id` because polymorphism allows multiple parent tables. The relationship loader emits `&comparator.ID{In: assetIDs}` for the FK predicate, but the column-side `DocumentFilter.EntityID` was typed `*comparator.String` because `resolveSimpleComparator` only upgrades to `ID` when `col.PrimaryKey || col.FKReference != nil`. With no SQL FK declared, neither condition holds, so the column-comparator and the loader-injected filter disagreed at compile time. **Impact:** any config-declared polymorphic FK against a column with no SQL `REFERENCES` clause broke generation with a Go compile error in the parent client's `loadRelationships` body. Pre-existing — surfaced only when 17.3 wired the first such FK. → resolved 2026-05-12: added `applyConfigDeclaredFKs(schema, cfg)` as a pre-pass at the top of `BuildTableContexts`. The helper walks every `cfg.Tables[*].Relationships[*]`, looks up the target column on the schema, and stamps a synthetic `parser.FKReference` when none exists. Synthetic ref's destination points back to the declaring parent for traceability; only its existence influences codegen (`resolveSimpleComparator`'s comparator-type decision). The guard short-circuits when `col.FKReference != nil` already so a config-declared FK against a column with a real SQL `REFERENCES` is a no-op. **Why not change `resolveSimpleComparator` instead.** The comparator-type decision is column-keyed throughout the codegen pipeline — pagination cursors, filter input wiring, GraphQL filter input types, and the loader call site all consult `col.FKReference` independently. Stamping the FK at context-build time means every downstream consumer agrees on a single answer without needing to thread "but this column is FK-by-config" through six call sites. **Verification.** No pre-existing example regenerated differently — every prior `fk:` in YAML targets a column already carrying a SQL `REFERENCES` clause, so the guard short-circuits. New `documents.entity_id` correctly types `DocumentFilter.EntityID` as `*comparator.ID` and the loader's `&comparator.ID{In: assetIDs}` compiles + executes against all three dialects (postgres / mysql / sqlite integration tests at `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/{postgres,mysql,sqlite}/tests/sub_categorized_polymorphism_test.go` all green). `make check` clean (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` tests green). `make check-examples` clean.

PRD §13.7.3 groups o2o and o2m under a *single* key shape `(target_table, fk_column, filter)`, so a config declaring both `o2o(documents, entity_id, "x")` and `o2m(documents, entity_id, "x")` should be flagged as a duplicate. The key now uses only a structural distinction between m2m (longer key shape — junction fields) and non-m2m, prefixed with sentinels `"m"` / `"x"` so an o2o/o2m entry with empty fk cannot alias into an m2m bucket. (2) `isM2M`: new private helper, three-line `switch` accepting `m2m` and `many_to_many` synonyms — kept in `validate.go` rather than a shared util since the synonym handling is dedup-key-internal. (3) `TestValidatePreParse_Relationships_DedupRules`: added two new cases pinning the strict-PRD reading — `duplicate (target, fk, filter) with mixed o2o/o2m → error` and `duplicate full key across type-synonym variants → error` (mixes `o2o` and `one_to_one`). - [x] **FIX-087** (phase 4/6, cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/client.go.tmpl + cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go + cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_cache.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_event.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap.go + cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/*.go.tmpl + cmd/sqlgen/cli/pipeline.go + docs/PRD.md §4.4 / §4.8 / §4.13 / §6.4 / §8.6 / §9.1 / §9.4b / §27.7 / §28.6 + docs/design/CACHE.md §12 / §19.1) — **`sqlgen generate` panics with `reflect: slice index out of range` when any input table has no PRIMARY KEY clause.** Reproducible on real-world schemas where uniqueness is added via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE` after the `CREATE TABLE` (no inline PK) — e.g. counter / junction / ACL tables. PK-keyed methods in the client template index `.PKColumns 0` unconditionally and the reflect engine panics on the empty slice. `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go::ResolveTableConnection` already handles "no PK → Connection omitted" with a warning, but nothing downstream skips the PK-keyed CRUD surface; the auto-detection logic also has no way to opt-in a UNIQUE-but-not-PK column as the row identity.

  **Failure surface.**

  - `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/client.go.tmpl` — unguarded `(index .PKColumns 0).GoType` at line 12 (`Get`), 26 (`Exists`), 60 (`Update`), 84 (`Increment`), 92 (`SoftDelete`), 95 (`SoftDeleteMany`), 107 (`Restore`), 110 (`RestoreMany`), 122 (`HardDelete`), 125 (`HardDeleteMany`).

  - `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/event_hooks.go.tmpl:44-46, 109-120` — early-returns on empty `mc.AffectedPKs` and constructs `event.Event{PK: pk, …}` per affected PK; with no PK, the hook is structurally dead code.

Neither extends to the broader PK-keyed surface.

  **Resolution plan — three sub-items, in implementation order:**

  ---

  **87.1 — Per-table `primary_key.columns` override** (`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go` + `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go` + `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go`). Smallest patch; eliminates the largest share of affected tables (counter tables with `UNIQUE (organization_id)` and similar where the developer treats the unique column as row identity).

  *Config shape.* Extend the existing `TablePrimaryKeyConfig` struct (`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:425-428`) with a new `Columns []string` field — it sits alongside the existing `Strategy` and `UUIDVersion` fields under the same `tables.<name>.primary_key:` key. Backward-compatible: existing configs that set only `strategy:` / `uuid_version:` keep working.

  ```yaml
  tables:
    baseline_counter:
      primary_key:
        columns: [organization_id]      # NEW — declare PK when auto-detect misses
        strategy: caller                # existing
    join_asset_ppa:
      primary_key:
        columns: [asset_id, ppa_id]     # composite override
  ```

  *Implementation.* In `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go::buildTableColumns` (around line 212-217 where `pkColumns` is populated from the auto-detected `columns[i].PrimaryKey` flag), after the loop:

  1. If `tableCfg.PrimaryKey != nil && len(tableCfg.PrimaryKey.Columns) > 0`, ignore the auto-detected set entirely.
  2. Build an ordered slice from the override list — preserve declaration order (load-bearing for composite-PK cache key ordering, CACHE.md §16).
  3. Flip `PrimaryKey: true` on the matching `ColumnContext` items, clear it on others (so the auto-detected flag doesn't double-count).
  4. Return the new ordered `pkColumns`.

  Downstream code paths (`compositePK := len(pkColumns) > 1`, cache key construction, event PK extraction, Get/Update/Exists signatures, `keyFor{{ .Struct }}` emission) all read only `PKColumns` so they pick up the override transparently. No template changes needed for 87.1 alone.

  *Validation* — new rules in `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go::ValidatePostParse` (runs after parsing, has the schema in scope):

  | Rule | Severity | Message |
  |------|----------|---------|
  | Override column doesn't exist on table | Error | `tables.<name>.primary_key.columns: column %q does not exist on table %s` |
  | Override column is nullable | Error | `tables.<name>.primary_key.columns: column %q is nullable; primary key columns must be NOT NULL` |
  | None of the override columns are covered by a UNIQUE constraint | Warning | `tables.<name>.primary_key.columns: no UNIQUE constraint covers the declared PK on table %s; sqlgen assumes uniqueness — enforce it at the application level if not at the DB level` |
  | Both auto-detected PK AND override set | (no warning — silent override) | — |

  Rationale for warn-not-error on the UNIQUE check: the user is the only one who knows whether uniqueness is enforced in application code. Erroring would block legitimate cases. Rationale for silent override on the conflict case: the user has final word — override is the explicit declaration, auto-detection is the guess.

  - `cmd/sqlgen/config/config_test.go` — add a YAML round-trip case for `tables.<name>.primary_key.columns: [a, b]` (asserts the field round-trips through Marshal/Unmarshal without dropping the slice).

  - `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate_test.go` — three new cases for each validation rule (column doesn't exist, nullable column, no UNIQUE — asserts warning not error).

  ---

  **87.2 — Top-level `exclude_tables`** (`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go` + `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go` + `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go`). Promotes the existing `introspect.exclude_tables` to a top-level field that filters regardless of input source (file or introspection).

  *Config shape.* Add `ExcludeTables []string \`yaml:"exclude_tables"\`` to `RootConfig` (`cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go` — same level as `Tables`, `Generation`, `Views`). The existing `IntrospectConfig.ExcludeTables` stays for backward compatibility with no behavior change; if both are set, the union of patterns applies (introspect's runs at introspection time, root-level runs post-parse — the union is equivalent regardless of input source).

  ```yaml
  exclude_tables:                     # NEW — top-level, file + introspect
    - temp_*                          # glob: any temp_-prefixed table
    - _internal_*
    - report_acl                      # exact name
  ```

  *Glob syntax.* Reuse the exact pattern semantics already documented in §6.4 (`*` = any sequence, `?` = any single character, case-sensitive). The existing `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go::matchTablePattern` helper (the one `IntrospectConfig.ExcludeTables` uses) gets lifted to a package-level helper if it isn't already.

  *Implementation.* In `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go` where the parsed `*parser.Schema` is consumed for table-context build, filter `schema.Tables` against `cfg.ExcludeTables` patterns before `assembleTableContext` is called. Drop matching tables silently — they never enter the generation pipeline. Emit one info-level log line per excluded table: `"table %s excluded by exclude_tables pattern %q"` (so consumers can verify the filter is firing without scrolling through warnings).

  *Validation.* No new rules — pattern syntax errors are caught at glob-match time. Unknown table names in `exclude_tables` are NOT an error (configs are forward-looking; a pattern that matches nothing today may match a future table).

  - `cmd/sqlgen/config/config_test.go` — YAML round-trip for top-level `exclude_tables: [temp_*, foo]`.
  - `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate_test.go` — file-input case: schema with tables `[users, temp_a, temp_b]` + config `exclude_tables: [temp_*]` → resulting `TableContext` slice contains only `users`; two info log lines fired.

  **87.3 — Filter-only client + cache/event suppression for residual no-PK tables** (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/client.go.tmpl` + `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go::resolvedOps` + `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_cache.go` + `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/event_hooks.go.tmpl` + `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go`). After 87.1 + 87.2, the residual set is tables the user neither excluded nor declared a PK on. This sub-item makes those tables generate successfully with a reduced surface instead of panicking.

  *Method matrix.* For a no-PK table, the generated client interface contains:

  | Method | Emitted (no PK)? | Reason |
  |--------|:----------------:|--------|
  | `GetMany` | Yes | Filter-keyed, no PK needed |
  | `Count` | Yes | Filter-keyed |
  | `Stream` | Yes | Filter-keyed, cache already bypassed |
  | `Paginate` | Yes | Offset-based, no PK needed |
  | `CreateMany` | Yes | INSERT path doesn't read PK; sequences/identity still work as before |
  | `UpdateWhere` | Yes | Filter-keyed |
  | `HardDeleteWhere` | Yes | Filter-keyed |
  | `SoftDeleteWhere` | Yes (when soft-delete column present) | Filter-keyed |
  | `RestoreWhere` | Yes (when soft-delete column present) | Filter-keyed |
  | `ExistsWhere` | Yes | Filter-keyed |
  | `Get` | **No** | Requires PK arg |
  | `Exists` | **No** | Requires PK arg |
  | `Update` | **No** | Requires PK arg |
  | `UpdateMany` | **No** | Requires `(pk, input)` items |
  | `Upsert` | **No** | Requires conflict target; no PK → no canonical conflict target |
  | `Increment` | **No** | Requires PK arg |
  | `SoftDelete` / `SoftDeleteMany` | **No** | Requires PK arg / PK slice |
  | `Restore` / `RestoreMany` | **No** | Requires PK arg / PK slice |
  | `HardDelete` / `HardDeleteMany` | **No** | Requires PK arg / PK slice |
  | `Create` | Discussion: see below | — |
  | `Connection` | **No** | Already omitted via cursor-keys decision |

  *`Create` design question (flag during 87.3 implementation):* `Create` returns the inserted entity via `Get(pk)` for full re-read. Without a PK, the re-read isn't expressible. Options: (a) skip `Create` entirely — only `CreateMany` available, which still works because `CreateMany` returns from a single `RETURNING` (Postgres) or per-row `LastInsertId` (MySQL) without a Get round-trip; (b) emit `Create` but return a partial entity built from the input plus the inserted PK if obtainable. Option (a) is the safer default and matches the "filter-only" framing. Lock in at implementation time.

  *Template implementation.* Guard each PK-keyed method in `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/client.go.tmpl`:

  ```
  {{- if .PKColumns }}
  Get(ctx context.Context, id {{ (index .PKColumns 0).GoType }}, ...) (*{{ .StructName }}, error)
  {{- end }}
  ```

  Same guard wraps the corresponding method-body templates: `get.go.tmpl`, `exists.go.tmpl`, `update.go.tmpl`, `upsert.go.tmpl`, `increment.go.tmpl`, `delete.go.tmpl` (the soft-delete / hard-delete / restore single + Many variants). Resolver-side: in `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_table.go::assembleTableContext` next to the existing `cursorDecision.Emit` branch at `:280-282`, add `if len(pkColumns) == 0 { resolvedOps.Get = false; resolvedOps.Exists = false; resolvedOps.Update = false; resolvedOps.UpdateMany = false; resolvedOps.Upsert = false; resolvedOps.Increment = false; resolvedOps.SoftDelete = false; resolvedOps.Restore = false; resolvedOps.HardDelete = false; resolvedOps.Connection = false }`. The resolver-side flip means the existing `{{- if .Operations.Get }}` guards in the templates do most of the work; the new `{{- if .PKColumns }}` guards only protect the unconditional `.PKColumns 0` index expressions that aren't already op-gated (e.g. `Get` is always-on today per §9.1 — that constraint must be relaxed to "always-on when the table has a PK").

  *Cache implementation* (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_cache.go`). When `len(table.PKColumns) == 0`, exclude the table from `CachedTables` entirely — no `keyFor{{ .Struct }}` function, no fingerprint, no `readThrough{{ .Struct }}`, no entry in the cache config's tenancy machinery. Reads on no-PK tables bypass cache like `Stream` already does (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/stream.go.tmpl:100` sets `options.SkipCache = true`). Writes (`CreateMany`, `UpdateWhere`, `HardDeleteWhere`, `SoftDeleteWhere`, `RestoreWhere`) still need to invalidate any *related* tables that hold this table's FK — the existing `handleInvalidation` path at `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/cache.go.tmpl:138-143` already supports `InvalidateTable(table)` with an empty `pks` slice. Wire the write hooks for no-PK tables to call `InvalidateTable` instead of `InvalidateMany`. Coarse but correct; subscribers handle whole-table invalidation already (CACHE.md §9).

  *Event implementation* (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/event_hooks.go.tmpl`). Suppress `new{{ .StructName }}EventHook` emission entirely for no-PK tables — `event.Event.PK` has no meaningful value, and lines 44-46 (`if len(mc.AffectedPKs) == 0 { return result, nil }`) would make the hook a structural no-op. Don't emit it. Subscribers needing "something changed in this table" listen on the cache invalidation source (the `InvalidateTable` signal from the write hooks) instead.

  *Validation surface.* New `ValidatePostParse` rule:

  |------|----------|---------|
  | Table has no PK after override resolution | Warning | `table %s has no primary key; filter-only client generated (no Get/Update/Delete/cache/events). Use tables.<name>.primary_key.columns to declare a PK or exclude_tables to skip.` |

  **Order rationale.** 87.1 first — shrinks the residual set most cheaply, reuses every existing PK code path, no template changes. 87.2 second — useful independently of 87.3 (e.g. excluding `temp_*` tables that the user just doesn't want generated); smaller than 87.3. 87.3 last — by then the residual set is small and easier to audit end-to-end; this is also the biggest blast radius (template guards across many files + cache + event suppression + validation rule + new example fixture + golden regen). Each sub-item is independently shippable. Documentation updates land alongside the implementation sub-items, not as a separate phase.

  → **resolved 2026-05-12** — all three sub-items shipped together. **87.1 (primary_key.columns override)**: extended `TablePrimaryKeyConfig` with `Columns []string` (`config.go:425`); `buildTableColumns` now honors the override silently when non-empty, rebuilding `pkColumns` in user-declared order and clearing the auto-detected `PrimaryKey` flag on non-override columns to prevent double-counting. Three new `ValidatePostParse` rules in `validate.go::validatePrimaryKeyOverride`: hard-error on missing or nullable override columns, warning on no UNIQUE coverage (uniqueCovers helper checks inline `Unique` + table-level `UniqueGroups` + column-level `PrimaryKey`, with set-equality matching so a composite override needs a composite-matching UNIQUE). `SchemaColumn` gained `Nullable`/`Unique` fields and `SchemaTable` gained `UniqueGroups [][]string`; `cli/pipeline.go::toSchemaTables` populates them from `parser.Table.Constraints` (both `Unique` and `PrimaryKey` constraint types contribute groups so composite-PK schemas also satisfy uniqueness coverage on their own PK columns). **87.2 (top-level exclude_tables)**: added `ExcludeTables []string` to `RootConfig` (sibling of `Tables`/`Views`); new `MatchExcludeTablePattern` helper in `config.go` reuses `filepath.Match` for `*`/`?` glob syntax and tests both bare and schema-qualified forms (`audit.*` patterns work). `BuildTableContexts` filters `input.Schema.Tables` against patterns silently before per-table context build. The existing `IntrospectConfig.ExcludeTables` is unchanged for back-compat — the two fields compose. **87.3 (filter-only client + cache/event suppression)**: new `disableNoPKOperations` helper in `context_table.go` forces every PK-keyed flag (Get / Exists / Create / Update / UpdateMany / Upsert / Increment / SoftDelete / Restore / HardDelete / Connection) to false when `len(pkColumns) == 0`, wired into `assembleTableContext` alongside the existing `cursorDecision.Emit` branch. New `firstPK` funcmap helper (`funcmap.go::funcFirstPK`) replaces every panicking `index .PKColumns 0` call at the top of `get/exists/update/upsert/increment/delete/create.go.tmpl` and at the O2M-relationships loadRelationships path in `get.go.tmpl:347` — the helper returns `ColumnContext{}` when PKColumns is empty so the variable assignment doesn't panic, and the rest of each template is gated by `Operations.X` (now false) so the zero value is never read. `client.go.tmpl:5-15` gained an explicit `{{- if .Operations.Get }}` wrap around the `Get` method declaration (the only PK-keyed method without an existing op-gate). `get.go.tmpl:62-143` gained a matching `{{- if .Operations.Get }}` wrap around the `Get` function body so it disappears from no-PK tables while `GetMany` / `loadRelationships` / `scan<Struct>s` stay. **Cache suppression**: `context_cache.go::BuildCacheContext:97-114` skips tables with `len(t.PKColumns) == 0` before the `ResolveTableCacheEnabled` check — no `keyFor<Struct>`, no fingerprint, no `readThrough<Struct>` is emitted for those tables; mutations route through `InvalidatePattern(BuildTablePattern(...))` like the existing `*Where` ops do (CACHE.md §12). **Event suppression**: `context_event.go::BuildEventHooksContext:57-69` skips no-PK tables symmetrically — no `new<Struct>EventHook` is emitted; subscribers needing change signals listen on the cache `InvalidationSource` instead (PRD §28.6 / §27.9). **Validation surface**: new `validateMissingPrimaryKey` warning fires once per table that has no auto-detected PK AND no override AND isn't already being skipped via `exclude_columns`-exhaustion; text directs the user toward `primary_key.columns` or top-level `exclude_tables`. **Reconciliations vs original spec**: (1) **Filter-only method matrix differs slightly from spec text** — `ExistsWhere` is gated by `Operations.Exists` (family-level flag, not separate), which `disableNoPKOperations` turns off, so `ExistsWhere` is omitted for no-PK tables too. Same for `SoftDeleteWhere`/`HardDeleteWhere`/`RestoreWhere` — each is family-gated. The spec text listed them as kept; the actual filter-only surface is `GetMany` / `Count` / `Stream` / `Paginate` / `CreateMany` (gated by separate flag) / `UpdateWhere` (gated by separate flag). Users wanting an existence check can use `Count > 0`; users wanting bulk deletes can drop the table or fix the schema. PRD §9.4b documents the actual surface. (2) **Create design decision** — option (a) from the spec: `Create` is also disabled for no-PK tables. The current template re-reads via `Get(pk)` for the full-entity return, which isn't expressible without a PK; option (b) (return partial entity) would require a separate template path. Out of scope; revisit if a user needs it. (3) **Cache table-wide invalidation for related tables not implemented** — the spec text said writes on no-PK tables should invalidate related cached tables holding FKs. The existing cache architecture invalidates per-table, not cross-table, so this is a forward-looking enhancement rather than something to backfill. Existing behavior preserved: writes on no-PK tables silently skip cache invalidation because no per-row cache exists for them. (4) **E2E example fixture deferred** — adding a no-PK table to one of the existing examples would require regenerating ~all goldens for that example and writing live tests; coverage is provided through 8 unit/template tests instead. Reviewer may file a follow-on FIX if E2E coverage is desired. (5) **`SchemaColumn` extension** — needed `Nullable`+`Unique` fields and `SchemaTable.UniqueGroups` (not in original spec) so `validatePrimaryKeyOverride` can run pre-codegen; the spec implicitly assumed this would be possible. Added to the cli/pipeline `toSchemaTables` converter. (6) **`uniqueCovers` semantics** — uses set-equality, not subset coverage, so a single-column UNIQUE on `(a)` does NOT cover a composite override `(a, b)` (a per-column UNIQUE doesn't make the pair unique). A composite UNIQUE `(a, b)` does cover the override `(a, b)` order-independently. (7) **Get method body wrap** — `get.go.tmpl` already had structure-without-guard for `Get`; added `{{- if .Operations.Get }}` ... `{{- end }}` around lines 62-143 (the `Get` function only, NOT `scan<Struct>s` or `GetMany` which stay accessible for filter-only tables). The `loadRelationships` helper at line 347 uses `firstPK .PKColumns` defensively even though it's already gated by `HasO2MRelationships` (parser-side relationship detection requires a PK or UNIQUE on the parent, so no-PK tables get no O2M relationships in practice). **Regression coverage**: 13 new tests across config + gen packages — `TestValidatePostParse_PrimaryKeyOverride_MissingColumn` / `_NullableColumn` / `_NoUniqueCoverage` / `_UniqueCovered` / `_CompositeUniqueCovered` / `_SilentWhenAutoPKExists`, `TestValidatePostParse_MissingPrimaryKey` / `_SilentWithOverride`, `TestLoadConfig_PrimaryKeyColumns`, `TestLoadConfig_TopLevelExcludeTables`, `TestMatchExcludeTablePattern` (9 sub-cases), `TestBuildTableContexts_PKOverride_FillsEmpty` / `_WinsOverAutoDetect` / `_CompositePreservesOrder` / `_Fallthrough`, `TestBuildTableContexts_ExcludeTables` / `_SchemaQualified`, `TestBuildTableContexts_NoPK_DisablesPKKeyedOps` / `_WithOverride_KeepsPKKeyedOps`, `TestBuildCacheContext_noPKTableSkipped`, `TestEventHooks_noPKTableSkipped`, `TestClientTemplate_filterOnlyNoPK` (filter-only interface emission + Go-format validity). Existing event hooks test fixtures (`event_hooks_template_test.go`) had `PKColumns` added so they don't get accidentally skipped by the new no-PK guard; `funcmap_test.go::TestFuncMap_returnsPopulatedMap` updated for the new `firstPK` entry. Client template goldens regenerated (single-line shift from the new `{{- if .Operations.Get }}` wrap eating a blank line in the output). **PRD updates** landed simultaneously: §4.4 IntrospectConfig table + new "Top-level `exclude_tables`" subsection; §4.8 `primary_key` row extended to mention the `columns:` sub-field; §4.13 four new validation rule rows (filter-only warning + three primary_key.columns rules); §5 testing list (line 1748) extended with the four new test scenarios; §6.4 top-level exclude_tables paragraph with YAML example; §8.6 new "PK Column Override" subsection + Resolution Order step added for the column declaration; §9.1 `Get`/`Exists` rows narrowed to "always generated when the table has a PK"; new §9.4b "Filter-only client (no-PK tables)" subsection with method matrix + cache/event behavior + migration path; §27.7 new row in cache behavior table; §28.6 new "No-PK tables emit no events" paragraph. CACHE.md §12 extended with a "No-PK tables" paragraph documenting `BuildCacheContext` exclusion + `InvalidatePattern` routing; §19.1 `CachedTable` struct comment clarifies the always-non-empty PKColumns invariant + explanatory note referencing PRD §8.6 / §9.4b. **Verification**: `make check` clean (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` tests green — cmd/sqlgen/cli ~52s, cmd/sqlgen/wrapper ~39s, cmd/sqlgen/gen ~6s, cmd/sqlgen/config ~1.8s, full suite ~95s). `make check-examples` clean across all 8 example modules (lint + tests against Postgres / MySQL / SQLite + graphql harness). No existing example was modified; the FIX-087 path is exercised entirely through new unit/template tests since no example currently ships with a no-PK table. **Follow-on FIXes filed**: the no-PK surface is not complete after FIX-087 alone. Five separate entries track the remaining work, each independently shippable: **FIX-088** (E2E no-PK fixture in the `postgres` example — regression coverage for the filter-only path against a live DB), **FIX-089** (single-row `Create` on no-PK tables via CreateMany-wrapper — closes the `client.X().Create(input)` UX gap), **FIX-090** (cross-table cache invalidation from no-PK writes to cached parent tables — correctness bug when cache is enabled AND the schema has FKs into no-PK tables), **FIX-091** (alias `introspect.exclude_tables` into top-level `exclude_tables` at load-time — cleanup pass, low priority), **FIX-092** (split `Operations.Exists/.SoftDelete/.HardDelete/.Restore` family flags into per-variant flags so `ExistsWhere`/`*DeleteWhere`/`RestoreWhere` survive `disableNoPKOperations` — restores filter-keyed surface for no-PK tables). All five are filed under `## Open` with full implementation reference. **Reviewer findings addressed in same PR**: F1 — PRD §9.4b method matrix updated to mark `Exists/ExistsWhere`, `SoftDelete*` / `Restore*` / `HardDelete*` `*Where` variants as **No** with a closing paragraph explaining the family-gate behavior; `TestClientTemplate_filterOnlyNoPK` tightened to assert `ExistsWhere`/`*DeleteWhere`/`RestoreWhere` are absent from the emitted interface (pins the documented surface). FIX-092 will flip those PRD entries back to **Yes** once landed. F3 — CACHE.md §12 "Every mutation on a no-PK table routes through `InvalidatePattern`" softened to the accurate "only `UpdateWhere` reaches `InvalidatePattern` (via the existing `*Where` family arm); `CreateMany` on a no-PK table falls into a switch arm where the table is absent, so no cache call fires." FIX-090 will close the cross-table cascade gap separately.

PRD §9.4b retitled "No-PK tables are skipped" — method matrix removed (there is no surface to document); §27.7 / §28.6 / CACHE.md §12 / §19.1 updated to match. The gate fires iff `cfg.API != nil && cfg.API.Enabled && cfg.API.GraphQL != nil && cfg.API.GraphQL.Enabled` AND neither `--no-graphql` nor `SQLGEN_NO_GRAPHQL` is set. **Pre-flight:** `runGraphQLGen` stat-checks `graphQLConfigPath(cfg)` before doing any wrapper work; absent gqlgen.yml returns an `*exitError{code: ExitConfig}` with the message `api.graphql.enabled is true but <path> is missing — run 'sqlgen graphql init' to scaffold a starter gqlgen.yml`. The matching `SQLGEN_NO_GRAPHQL` env var (any non-empty value) provides the same opt-out for CI environments that don't thread flags through every `go generate` invocation. **Failure mode:** when the gqlgen subprocess fails, `runGraphQLGen` reports `Error: gqlgen subprocess failed: <details>; sqlgen-side artifacts emitted at <output.dir>` and returns `*exitError{code: ExitGeneration}` — the sqlgen-side files emitted earlier in the run stay on disk; consumers fix the gqlgen issue and re-run. **Reporting:** `wrapper.Gen` now returns `(*GenResult, error)` carrying `SeedFiles []string` (the resolver seed files newly written this run, including the optional `resolver.go` scaffold under follow-schema layout — files that already existed on disk are excluded so re-runs don't double-count). The new `printGenerateReport` helper folds these into the verbose listing (`graphql seed: <path>` lines after the existing file list and before `deleted:` lines) and the headline file count (`sqlgen: generated %d files (%d tables, %d views) in %s`). gqlgen-emitted artefacts (`model/models_gen.go`, `generated_gen.go`) are NOT enumerated — those paths are subject to consumer-controlled gqlgen.yml plumbing and the wrapper has no authoritative list; the headline count therefore reflects sqlgen-side files plus the seed files we know we wrote, with gqlgen's own emit being summarised through gqlgen's stdout/stderr passthrough. **Refactor scope:** the wrapper signature flip cascaded through `writeSeedFiles` → `writeFollowSchemaSeeds` → `writeSingleFileSeed` → `writeResolverScaffold` → `mergeResolverScaffold`; `writeResolverScaffold` returns the path it touched (empty string when an existing `resolver.go` didn't need a merge), `mergeResolverScaffold` returns a `(rewritten bool, error)` tuple so the caller can attribute scaffolds it actually rewrote. The chained block in `makeGenerateRunE` was extracted into two helpers (`chainGraphQLGenIfEnabled` + `printGenerateReport`) to keep the function under the project's cyclomatic-complexity ceiling (cyclop max=15). **Tests:** new `cli/generate_test.go::TestShouldChainGraphQLGen` table-tests the gate in isolation across nine cases: `api+graphql enabled`, `api disabled`, `graphql disabled`, both block-nil shapes, `--no-graphql` flag honoured, `SQLGEN_NO_GRAPHQL=1` honoured, `SQLGEN_NO_GRAPHQL=true` honoured (any non-empty value short-circuits), `SQLGEN_NO_GRAPHQL=""` does not opt out. New `TestGenerate_ChainedGraphQL_MissingGqlgenYml` runs the full CLI with `api.graphql.enabled: true` and no gqlgen.yml on disk — asserts `ExitConfig` and that stderr suggests `sqlgen graphql init` and references `gqlgen.yml`. New `TestGenerate_ChainedGraphQL_NoGraphQLFlag` + `TestGenerate_ChainedGraphQL_EnvVar` both assert that with `--no-graphql` (or `SQLGEN_NO_GRAPHQL=1`) set, the FIX-078 pre-flight error does NOT fire even when gqlgen.yml is absent — proving the escape hatch short-circuits before the chain runs. - [x] **FIX-070** (phase 11, gen/templates/cache.go.tmpl) — `TestReadThrough_SingleflightDedup` flaked ~25% on a clean tree because the outer cache probe sat outside the singleflight in `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/cache.go.tmpl` (lines 240–317): when a flight completed faster than late stragglers traversed the gap between Get-miss and `sf.DoChan`, stragglers registered a new flight and ran a second DB query. `singleflight` releases each in-flight slot the moment `fn` returns, so the slot-relinquish window was what late stragglers (outer-miss-observed-but-not-yet-`DoChan`-registered callers) slipped through to start fresh duplicate flights. → resolved: added an in-flight `cache.GetAs` re-check at the top of the `DoChan` callback in `cache.go.tmpl` (breaker-gated; the inner re-check emits no metrics — the outer probe already accounted for `Miss` / `breaker.RecordSuccess` / `GetLatency`, and an inner-Get error is silently dropped since the outer probe already routed any backend error through `RouteError`). Test coverage: `TestCacheTemplate_readThroughInFlightRecheck` + `_CompositePK` template tests (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/cache_template_test.go`) pin the emitted shape — the in-flight `cache.GetAs` lives inside the `DoChan` callback before `next(ctx, q)`, gated by `if c.breaker == nil || c.breaker.Allow()`, with no `metrics.Hit` / `metrics.Miss` / `metrics.GetLatency` / `breaker.RecordSuccess` / `cache.RouteError` calls in the re-check branch. `TestReadThrough_SingleflightLateStraggler` (`cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/cache/tests/read_through_test.go`) deterministically pins the late-straggler path via a `firstMissBackend` wrapper that returns miss on the first backend Get for any given key and delegates after — outer probe sees miss, the in-flight re-check sees the populated entity, zero DB queries, exactly two backend Gets. Existing `TestReadThrough_MissThenHit` cold-miss expectation updated from `1 get + 1 set` to `2 get + 1 set` (outer + inner re-check + Set) since the dual-probe contract is now load-bearing on the cold path; the warm-cache hit path stays at 1 backend Get because the outer probe hits and the flight is never entered. Documentation propagated: PRD.md §27.7 table + Stampede-protected feature bullet (line 10575) updated to mention the dual-check; CACHE.md §9.3 sketch rewritten to show outer probe + flight-callback re-check separately, scope-and-semantics gained a 7th bullet covering the FIX-070 invariants; §22 decision #20 expanded with the re-check sentence; §G2 design note's Resolution bullet 1 + 3 updated and a new bullet 6 added (`Re-check is silent`); §20.1 `singleflight_test.go` follow-up added the late-straggler regression-guard requirement with a pointer to the deterministic test. `make check` (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` unit tests green) + `make check-examples` (8 example modules, 0 lint, all `-race` E2E tests green) clean. `make update-golden` + `make update-golden-e2e` byte-identical on a second consecutive run.

- [x] **FIX-069** (phase 6, gen/templates/table/get.go.tmpl + gen/funcmap.go + gotype/gotype.go + config/config.go) — O2M relationship loader emitted `r.<FK>.String()` on the FK column when the FK was nullable and its Go type was a Null-wrapped struct (e.g. `uuid.NullUUID` from a `uuid UUID REFERENCES users(id)` column under the `uuid → uuid.UUID` override). `uuid.NullUUID` exposes `UUID` + `Valid` fields and has no `String()` method, so the generated source failed to compile. Affected every O2M whose child FK was nullable and bound to a struct override (uuid.UUID, decimal.Decimal, time.Time-style types). Surfaced in 16.8a on `events.user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id)`; the temporary 16.8a workaround was making the FK NOT NULL. → resolved: built a resolver-aware "scalar extraction" descriptor (`gotype.ScalarExtraction`) and plumbed the FK column's resolved Go type onto `RelationshipContext.FKColumnGoType`, then taught the O2M loader template to emit a guard + unwrap before stringifying. The implementation comprises five layers:

  1. `config.NullableVariant` gained four optional YAML fields (`underlying_field`, `valid_field`, `valid_method`, `valid_invert`) describing how to read the wrapper's underlying scalar without assuming the `Valid bool` convention. Built-in integrations (`uuidgoogle`, `uuidgofrs`, `decimal`, `dateTimeOverride`) populate `UnderlyingField` so user configs that already use them get the new behavior for free; `enrichOverride` was extended to backfill these fields from integrations onto user overrides whose `Nullable.Type` matches.

  2. `gotype.ScalarExtraction` (`GuardExpr` / `UnwrapExpr` / `StringMethod`) plus `(*Resolver).DeriveScalarExtraction(goType)` (nil-safe receiver). Lookup order: user-declared wrappers from `sqlgen.yml` overrides (registered into `r.userWrappers` at Resolver init via `registerWrappersFromOverrides` + `maybeRegisterWrapper`) → static `knownWrapperExtractions` map (covers `sql.NullString` / `NullInt16` / `NullInt32` / `NullInt64` / `NullFloat64` / `NullBool` / `NullTime` / `NullByte` + `uuid.NullUUID` + `decimal.NullDecimal` + `types.NullDateTime`) → pointer fallthrough (`(*$v)` paren-wrapped to bind `.String()` correctly) → bare-type fallthrough. `buildGuardExpr` renders the guard from a `NullableVariant`, applying the `ValidField: "Valid"` default and the `ValidInvert` negation. Built-in known wrappers always win over user-declared entries with the same Go type name (precedence pin in `TestDeriveScalarExtraction_BuiltinWinsOverUser`).

  3. `RelationshipContext.FKColumnGoType` parallels existing `FKGoType` / `FKNullable`. Wired in `wireRelListFKMetadata` (refactored into `wireRelFKMetadata` + `resolveFKGoType` to satisfy cyclop ≤ 15) by looking up the FK column on the target table (O2M / O2O) or the junction's local FK (M2M). Final fallback assigns `FKGoType` so unit fixtures and bare tables still produce sensible expressions.

  4. Funcmap helpers `funcFKLoadGuard(resolver)` / `funcFKLoadKey(resolver)` close over a `*gotype.Resolver` and substitute the `$v` placeholder. Registered via a new `gen.FuncMapWithResolver(dialect, resolver)` constructor; `gen.FuncMap(dialect)` keeps the legacy nil-resolver behavior for tests. `loadTemplatesWithResolver` is the new internal entry point used by `Generate()`.

  5. `get.go.tmpl:401-409` switched to: `{{- with fkLoadGuard .FKColumnGoType $fkVar }} if !({{ . }}) { continue } {{- end }}` followed by `key := {{ fkLoadKey .FKColumnGoType $fkVar }}`. For `events.user_id uuid.NullUUID` (the originally-broken case), the generated loader now emits `if !(r.UserID.Valid) { continue }; key := r.UserID.UUID.String()`. For non-null FK columns the output stays byte-identical to before — guard expr is empty so the `with` block elides.

  Validation in `config/validate.go::validateNullableVariants` rejects `valid_field` + `valid_method` declared together, `valid_invert` without `valid_method`, and `underlying_field` without `nullable.type`. The 16.8a workaround was reverted: `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/schema.sql` now declares `events.user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id)` (nullable), so the graphql E2E example exercises the fix path. `phase-16.md` reconciliation note (3) updated to reflect the revert.

  Regression coverage: `TestDeriveScalarExtraction` (13 cases — bare / pointer / sql.NullX / built-in integration wrappers), `TestDeriveScalarExtraction_CustomValidField` / `_CustomValidMethod` / `_InvertedValidMethod` / `_BuiltinWinsOverUser` in `cmd/sqlgen/gotype/gotype_test.go`; `TestFuncFKLoadGuard` (8 cases) + `TestFuncFKLoadKey` (12 cases) + `TestFuncFKLoadKey_UserDeclaredWrapper` in `cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap_test.go` (helpers exposed via `FKLoadGuardForTest` / `FKLoadKeyForTest` in `gen/export_test.go`); `TestValidatePreParse_NullableValidConflict` / `_NullableInvertWithoutMethod` / `_NullableUnderlyingFieldWithoutType` / `_NullableValidConfigsPass` in `cmd/sqlgen/config/validate_test.go`. Existing `TestGetTemplate_o2mRelationshipLoading_nullableNumericFK` / `_nullableStringFK` fixtures updated to set `FKColumnGoType` (`*int64` / `uuid.NullUUID`) — production codegen populates this via `wireRelListFKMetadata`; unit fixtures must set it manually, mirroring the FIX-059 / FIX-068 pattern. `make check` (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` tests green) passes cleanly. `TestE2EGoldenFiles` regenerated +168 / -42 across mysql + postgres + postgres_stdlib + sqlite + tenancy + graphql expected/ + models/ — pure additions of the new doc comment in O2M loaders, plus the graphql `events.user_id` revert that adds the guard-+-unwrap shape on the events relationship loader. The pre-existing `mysql_version_test.go` "exists in expected/ but was not generated" failure is unrelated to FIX-069 (reproduces on main without these changes).
