Conditional wrapping at the producer (vs. unconditional parens at the template) avoids 72 lines of cosmetic E2E golden churn (`!= 0` → `!= (0)`) — only struct-typed PKs get the parens. The other 6 `zeroValue` interpolation sites (in `return` position: `create.go.tmpl:433/443/447`, `upsert.go.tmpl:224/236/240`) don't go through `O2OJoinDetail.PKZeroValue` and are unaffected. Regression coverage: `gen/context_test.go::TestParenIfComposite` (8 sub-tests covering composite literals — `uuid.UUID{}`, `decimal.Decimal{}`, `decimal.NullDecimal{}` — and sentinels — `uuid.Nil`, `0`, `""`, `false`, `nil`); `parenIfComposite` exposed via `gen/export_test.go::ParenIfCompositeForTest` (mirrors the existing `AttachTenancyToTablesForTest` / `APIImportDirForTest` test-export pattern). `make check` (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` tests green; cmd/sqlgen/gen ~5s, cmd/sqlgen/cli ~38s) passes cleanly. Zero golden-file regeneration was needed — the existing E2E examples' `overrides.types` is empty (postgres binds uuid columns to Go `string` under pgx), so no existing golden contains a struct-typed PK comparison.

- [x] **FIX-064** (phase 16, gen/orchestrate.go + gen/templates/api/resolvers.go.tmpl + gen/templates/api/seeds.go.tmpl + gen/templates/api/input_translate.go.tmpl + wrapper/gen.go + wrapper/seeds.go + wrapper/init.go + cli/graphql.go) — sqlgen's per-table resolver methods are emitted to `resolvers_gen.go` on `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver` directly inside `resolver.dir`. gqlgen's `resolvergen` plugin scans every `.go` file under `resolver.dir`, finds those methods, and **copies the bodies into its own destination file** (`<schema>.resolvers.go` under `follow-schema`, `resolver.go` under `single-file`) without removing them from `resolvers_gen.go`. Result: duplicate `func (r *queryResolver) X(...)` declarations on the very first `sqlgen graphql gen` run, which fails to compile with `... redeclared in this block`.

  → resolved: **shipped Shape A as specified** — Q/M helper sub-package + layout-aware seed file emission + post-gqlgen panic-stub rewriter, plus an extra ergonomic improvement (auto-emitted `resolver.go` scaffold).

  **1. sqlgenresolver/ helper sub-package.** The resolvers template (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/resolvers.go.tmpl`) was rewritten to emit `type Q struct{Client *<modelspkg>.<Client>}` + `type M struct{Client *<modelspkg>.<Client>}` plus per-table query/mutation methods on `*Q` / `*M` receivers. Output goes to `<resolver_dir>/sqlgenresolver/resolvers_gen.go` (package "sqlgenresolver"). The exported `IncrementOp[T]` and `InvalidInputError` helpers also live there — seeds in the parent graph package import them directly. Q/M methods take **model-side input types** only (`*<pkg>.<Table>Filter`, `*<pkg>.Create<Table>Input`, etc.); the gqlgen→model translation happens in seed delegations, breaking the import cycle that would otherwise form between sqlgenresolver/ and graph/. The other modules-package-dependent helpers — `field_options_gen.go`, `connection_walker_gen.go`, `middleware_gen.go`, `errors_gen.go` — also moved into `sqlgenresolver/` so the per-table methods can call them without crossing package boundaries.

  **2. Layout-aware seed file emission.** A new `api/seeds.go.tmpl` template emits per-table delegation bodies with conflict checks (`_set` + `_inc` / `_inc` + `_dec`), gqlgen→model input translation calls, and `r.Q.<Field>(...)` / `r.M.<Field>(...)` delegations. A new `api/input_translate.go.tmpl` template emits the `translateCreate<Table>Input` / `translateUpdate<Table>Input` / `hasUpdate<Table>SetFields` helpers in the graph package (they reference gqlgen-emitted input types and stay co-located). The orchestrator emits `input_translate_gen.go` directly; the wrapper layer writes seeds at runtime via `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/seeds.go::writeSeedFiles`. Seeds are written **only when absent** — gqlgen owns each file after the first run and preserves bodies verbatim. Both `follow-schema` (per-`<table>_gen.resolvers.go`) and `single-file` (combined `<resolver_dir>/<resolver.filename>`) layouts are supported; `parseResolverLayout` extracts the consumer's gqlgen.yml `resolver:` block at wrapper invocation time without modifying the on-disk file.

  **3. Post-gqlgen panic-stub rewriter.** `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/seeds.go::rewritePanicStubs` runs after the gqlgen subprocess returns. It AST-parses every gqlgen-owned file in `resolver.dir`, finds top-level method declarations on `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver` whose body is a single `panic(...)` call, checks the method name against the sqlgen-managed field set (computed by `gen.CollectSqlgenManagedFields`), and rewrites the body to `return r.Q.<Field>(<args>)` / `return r.M.<Field>(<args>)`. Bounded input set + bounded body shape + GraphQL field-name uniqueness make the rewriter unambiguously safe per the spec's safety properties; consumer-authored fields are never touched.

  **Bonus: auto-emitted `resolver.go` scaffold + migration AST-merge.** Beyond the spec, `writeResolverScaffold` handles two cases:
  - **No `resolver.go` yet** (greenfield, follow-schema): emit a starter `resolver.go` with `Resolver struct { Client; Q; M }` already wired, plus the Query() / Mutation() interface methods and queryResolver / mutationResolver type defs gqlgen would have scaffolded. Single-file layout prepends the equivalent type defs to the seed body.
  - **Existing `resolver.go`** (migration from pre-FIX-064 sqlgen, or from a previous `gqlgen generate` run): `mergeResolverScaffold` AST-parses the file, finds `type Resolver struct { ... }`, and adds `Q *sqlgenresolver.Q` / `M *sqlgenresolver.M` (and `Client *<modelspkg>.Client` if missing) without disturbing consumer-added fields, methods, or imports. Adds the `sqlgenresolver` import too. Without this merge, an existing resolver.go would compile-fail because the seed delegations reference `r.Q.X(...)` / `r.M.X(...)` against a Resolver struct that doesn't have those fields.
  
  Mutation()/mutationResolver/M are gated on the presence of mutation operations so schemas with read-only-only ops still compile (gqlgen's MutationResolver interface won't exist in that case). Eliminates the manual-edit step the spec called for in its "Consumer wiring contract" — consumers initialize Client/Q/M at app boot but don't have to add the field declarations themselves, even when migrating from an older sqlgen version.

  **CLI integration.** `cmd/sqlgen/cli/graphql.go::buildSeedsAndManagedFields` ties the gen and wrapper layers together: it calls `gen.RenderAPISeeds` + `gen.CollectSqlgenManagedFields` and threads the results through `wrapper.GenOptions.Seeds` + `wrapper.GenOptions.SqlgenManagedFields` + `wrapper.GenOptions.SeedImports` (consumer's models alias/import path + the sqlgenresolver helper sub-package import path). The `sqlgen graphql init` post-stdout was updated to reflect the auto-scaffold (no manual `Q *sqlgenresolver.Q` / `M *sqlgenresolver.M` field-add step required, just initialize at app boot).

  **APIContext fields added.** `gen.APIContext` gains `SqlgenResolverPkgName` (always "sqlgenresolver") + `SqlgenResolverImportPath` (computed from `go.mod` + `cfg.API.GraphQL.ResolverDir + "/sqlgenresolver"`) so the seeds template can emit fully-qualified references and the wrapper preamble builder can wire the right import line.

  **FIX-058 fallout.** The Resolver / queryResolver type-decl collision FIX-058 originally worked around went away: sqlgen no longer emits methods on `*queryResolver` in `resolver.dir`. The `TestResolvers_NoTypeDefsAvoidsGqlgenScaffoldCollision` assertions were rewritten as `TestResolvers_QMShape_NoQueryResolverMethods` (sqlgenresolver/ output must NOT have `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver` receivers — only `*Q` / `*M`) plus `TestSeeds_DelegateToQM` (seeds output MUST have `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver` delegations into `r.Q.<X>` / `r.M.<X>` and must NOT contain field-options walker calls or error mapping — those live in Q/M). The auto-scaffolded `resolver.go` now declares the Resolver / queryResolver / mutationResolver types intentionally; the FIX-058 collision is avoided by the write-only-if-absent guard plus gqlgen's own preserve-existing-file behavior.

  **Test plan reconciliation.** The spec's test plan called for `TestInit_WritesSeedFiles_FollowSchema` and `…_SingleFile`. Shipped equivalent coverage as `TestWriteSeedFiles_FollowSchemaOnlyWhenAbsent` (asserts seed file written first time + preserved on second pass when consumer has edited it), `TestWriteSeedFiles_SingleFile` (combined output), `TestWriteSeedFiles_AutoResolverScaffold` (Resolver struct emission with Client/Q/M fields), `TestWriteSeedFiles_AutoResolverScaffold_NoMutations` (read-only mode gating), `TestWriteSeedFiles_MergeExistingResolver` (migration path: existing resolver.go gains Q/M fields + sqlgenresolver import without disturbing consumer-added Logger field, Client field, or methods), `TestPostStubRewriter` (panic-stub → delegation, with negative cases for consumer-authored stubs and pre-existing delegation bodies), and `TestParseResolverLayout` (gqlgen.yml resolver-block extraction across follow-schema/single-file/all-defaults). Existing unit tests (`api_resolvers_test.go`, `api_pagination_test.go`) were updated to test both the Q/M output (`q.Client.<Tables>().<op>(ctx, ...)`) and the seeds output (`(r *queryResolver) X(...)` delegations) where the assertion crossed the boundary.

  **Tests passing.** `make check` (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` tests green; cmd/sqlgen/wrapper ~3.6s, cmd/sqlgen/cli ~37s, cmd/sqlgen/gen ~4.5s) passes cleanly. **The 16.8 graphql E2E example (in flight) will exercise the real `go run github.com/99designs/gqlgen` subprocess path under both layouts and lock the cross-layout invariant** — the spec's load-bearing test. No existing example currently enables `api.graphql.enabled`, so no E2E golden regeneration was needed.

  **Known reconciliations vs the spec.**
  - **Q/M method signatures take model-side types, not gqlgen input types.** The spec example (`return r.M.CreateProduct(ctx, input)`) implied Q/M methods take gqlgen-emitted input types directly. That would form a cycle (sqlgenresolver imports graph for `CreateProductInput`; graph imports sqlgenresolver for `Q`/`M` field types). The shipped design moves the `translate*Input` helpers into the graph package alongside seeds; seeds call the translator before delegating (`r.M.CreateProduct(ctx, translateCreateProductInput(input))`). Q/M methods take the consumer's omittable-wrapped `*<pkg>.Create<Table>Input`, breaking the cycle.
  - **Update method incremental dispatch shape.** `M.UpdateProduct(ctx, id, setIn, hasSet, []IncrementOp[T])` accepts a pre-built slice of `IncrementOp[T]` rather than walking the gqlgen-input fields. The seed builds the slice (it has access to gqlgen-input field names like `input.StockInc`). This split keeps Q/M cycle-free while preserving the §26.5.4 dispatch order.
  - **Auto-emitted `resolver.go`.** Beyond the spec; the spec instructed consumers to add `Q`/`M` fields manually after the first gqlgen run. The shipped scaffold writes them automatically on the first `sqlgen graphql gen` run (gated on `resolver.go` being absent — gqlgen's preserve-existing-file behavior keeps the second-and-later runs as no-ops).

  **Layout coverage.** The duplication reproduces under **both** gqlgen layouts. The original entry suggested switching the scaffold default to `single-file` would suppress this; an empirical spike against gqlgen v0.17.90 disproved that — gqlgen single-file copies the same way. There is no layout the consumer can pick that lets sqlgen emit methods directly on `*queryResolver` without conflict.

  **Repro.** Run `sqlgen graphql gen` once in the 16.8 example dir under either `resolver.layout: follow-schema` or `single-file`; observe `func (r *queryResolver) Category(...)` redeclared across `resolvers_gen.go` and gqlgen's destination file. (Earlier description claiming the first run succeeds was incorrect — that scenario assumed a "move" semantic that gqlgen v0.17.90 does not implement.)

  **Why it wasn't caught.** No example currently exercises the real `go run github.com/99designs/gqlgen` subprocess. The 16.2 wrapper tests use a stub binary that mimics gqlgen's CLI surface without performing the resolvergen scan/copy pass.

  **Spike findings (gqlgen v0.17.90).** Five variants tested in `/tmp/sqlgen-spike-064`; results pinned to v0.17.90 — a follow-up spike against the oldest gqlgen version we want to support is needed before locking the design.

  | Variant | sqlgen emission shape | Layout | Outcome |
  |---------|----------------------|--------|---------|
  | 1 | `resolvers_gen.go` with method on `*queryResolver` | follow-schema | Run 1 fails: duplicate `Hello` in `resolvers_gen.go` + `schema.resolvers.go`. Body copied (not moved). |
  | 2 | embedded receiver (`queryResolver` embeds `*sqlgenresolver.Q`) | follow-schema | Run 1 fails: gqlgen ignores promoted methods, emits panic stub for `Hello` directly on `*queryResolver`. |
  | 3 | renamed receiver (`*sqlgenQueryResolver` returned by `Resolver.Query()`) | follow-schema | Run 1 fails: gqlgen hardcodes `queryResolver` as the type name and re-declares it, colliding with our `Resolver.Query()` decl. |
  | 4 | `resolvers_gen.go` with method on `*queryResolver` | single-file | Run 1 fails: duplicate `Hello` in `resolvers_gen.go` + `resolver.go`. Same copy-not-move behavior. |
  | **7 (Shape A)** | **sqlgen pre-writes `<schema>.resolvers.go` with delegating bodies into a `sqlgenresolver/` helper sub-package; lets gqlgen scaffold `resolver.go`** | follow-schema | **Run 1 + run 2: EXIT=0, build passes, body preserved verbatim, panic stubs emitted only for non-sqlgen fields.** |
  | **8 (Shape A)** | **sqlgen pre-writes `resolver.go` with delegating bodies into a `sqlgenresolver/` helper sub-package** | single-file | **Run 1 + run 2: EXIT=0, build passes, body preserved verbatim, panic stubs emitted only for non-sqlgen fields.** |

  **Key behavior Shape A relies on.** When sqlgen-seeded methods land in a file matching `resolver.filename_template` (or the `single-file` destination), gqlgen treats the file as its own and **preserves the method bodies verbatim** across regenerations via its documented "any resolver implementations will be copied through when generating" feature. It only emits panic stubs for fields whose method bodies don't yet exist — i.e., consumer-authored, non-sqlgen schema fields. Putting sqlgen's methods in a non-`*.resolvers.go` filename (today's `resolvers_gen.go`) opts *out* of this preservation flow and into the broken copy-not-move path.

  **Suggested fix — Shape A.** Three coordinated changes:

  1. **Helper sub-package (`<resolver_dir>/sqlgenresolver/`).** Move the per-table generation logic out of `resolvers_gen.go` and into a sqlgen-owned sub-package outside gqlgen's filename glob. The sub-package exports two structs — `*Q` (queries) and `*M` (mutations) — each holding `Client *<modelspkg>.Client`. Per-table methods attach to those receivers: `func (q *Q) GetProduct(ctx, id, opts...) (*models.Product, error)`, `func (m *M) CreateProduct(ctx, input, opts...) (*models.Product, error)`, etc. Same logic that's in `resolvers.go.tmpl` today, just with the receiver moved from `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver` onto `*Q` / `*M`, and `r.Client` references rewritten to `q.Client` / `m.Client`. This package is fully overwritten on every `sqlgen graphql gen`. Equivalent migration for `field_options_gen.go` and `connection_walker_gen.go` — both move into `sqlgenresolver/` since they are sqlgen-internal helpers, not gqlgen-shaped artifacts.

     **Consumer wiring contract.** The seed files (step 2) emit delegations of the form `return r.Q.GetProduct(ctx, id)` / `return r.M.CreateProduct(ctx, input)`. For these to compile, the consumer's gqlgen-scaffolded `Resolver` struct must hold `Q *sqlgenresolver.Q` and `M *sqlgenresolver.M` fields, both initialized at app boot with the same `*models.Client` the rest of the resolver uses. The init subcommand's stdout block should explicitly document this one-time setup; consumers add the two fields to the gqlgen-emitted `resolver.go` after the first `gqlgen generate` (gqlgen's one-shot scaffold doesn't know about them). This matches the existing FIX-058 pattern where consumers also add `Client *models.Client` to the same struct.

  2. **Layout-aware seed files.** On `sqlgen graphql gen`, read `resolver.layout` from the consumer's `gqlgen.yml` (the wrapper already parses it in `wrapper/merge.go`). Then:
     - `follow-schema`: for each generated `<table>_gen.graphqls`, write a seed `<resolver_dir>/<table>_gen.resolvers.go` *if absent*, containing delegating bodies for every managed field of that schema (one body per operation: `Get`, `Connection`, `Paginate`, `Create…`, `Update…`, `Delete…`, etc., each calling into `sqlgenresolver`).
     - `single-file`: write the seed at `<resolver_dir>/<resolver.filename>` (default `resolver.go`) *if absent*, containing delegating bodies for every managed field across all tables.
     - In both cases: never overwrite an existing seed file — gqlgen owns it after the first run and will preserve the bodies.

  3. **Post-`gqlgen-generate` panic-stub rewriter.** Closes the gap that opens when a sqlgen-managed table gains a new operation *after* its seed file already exists.

     *Trigger sequence.* (1) First `sqlgen graphql gen` runs against `products` with `api.operations: read_only`; sqlgen seeds `products_gen.resolvers.go` with delegations for `Get` / `Connection` / `Paginate` only. (2) Consumer later flips `api.operations: append_only`, which adds `createProduct` / `softDeleteProduct` / `restoreProduct` to the schema. (3) Next `sqlgen graphql gen`: seed step skips the file (it exists, sqlgen never overwrites). gqlgen runs, sees three schema fields with no method body, and emits panic stubs:
     ```go
     func (r *mutationResolver) CreateProduct(ctx context.Context, input CreateProductInput) (*models.Product, error) {
         panic(fmt.Errorf("not implemented: CreateProduct - createProduct"))
     }
     ```
     Package compiles; runtime panics on `createProduct`. The rewriter closes that gap.

     *What it does.* Runs in `wrapper/gen.go::Gen` after the gqlgen subprocess returns successfully, before `Gen` returns to its caller. Steps:
     1. Read each gqlgen-owned file in `resolver.dir` (files matching `filename_template` under follow-schema, or the single-file destination).
     2. AST-parse each file (`go/parser` + `go/ast`).
     3. For each top-level method declaration on `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver` whose body matches a panic-stub pattern (`panic("not implemented")` or `panic(fmt.Errorf("not implemented: %s - %s", …))`), check whether the method name is in the sqlgen-managed field set for this run. The set is concrete and authoritative: sqlgen owns the `*_gen.graphqls` files, so we hand the rewriter the exact list of `Query.*` and `Mutation.*` field names we wrote this run (computed once at the orchestrator layer from `apiCtx.Tables[i]` + the schema templates' field-name rules — same source of truth as the seed step).
     4. If the name matches: rewrite the body to the standard delegation call — same shape sqlgen would have produced in the seed: `return r.Q.<Field>(ctx, …)` for query resolvers, `return r.M.<Field>(ctx, …)` for mutation resolvers (matching the helper sub-package shape pinned in step 1).
     5. If the name does not match: it's a consumer-authored field — leave the panic stub untouched. The consumer fills it in.
     6. Write the file back; format with `gofumpt` to match the existing convention.

     *Lifecycle relationship to the seed step.* Seed (step 2) runs only when the per-schema file does not exist; rewriter runs after gqlgen has materialized any new stubs. They never operate on the same content in the same invocation. Insertion point in `Gen`:
     ```
     1. Read consumer gqlgen.yml
     2. Merge sqlgen-owned entries into temp config
     3. Seed per-schema files (Shape A step 2 — only if absent)
     4. Run gqlgen subprocess against temp config
     5. NEW: Post-process gqlgen-owned files — panic-stub rewriter
     6. Remove temp file
     ```

     *Safety properties.* Two structural facts make the rewriter unambiguously safe — no heuristic edge cases:
     - **GraphQL field-name uniqueness.** The GraphQL spec requires field names within an object type to be unique; gqlparser enforces this at schema-load time. So a method name on `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver` corresponds to exactly one `Query.*` / `Mutation.*` field. There is no namespace overlap between sqlgen-managed and consumer-authored fields.
     - **sqlgen owns the `*_gen.graphqls` files.** A consumer cannot author a field with a name in the sqlgen-managed set: declaring it in their own `.graphqls` would collide with our `_gen.graphqls` and fail schema validation before resolvers ever generate. So every panic stub for a name in the managed set was unambiguously emitted by gqlgen because we hadn't seeded it yet.
     Together: if `(method name ∈ sqlgen-managed set) ∧ (body matches a panic-stub pattern)`, the rewrite is correct by construction. The remaining properties:
     - **Bounded input set.** The managed set is the concrete list of field names from this run's `*_gen.graphqls` — handed to the rewriter, not derived heuristically. Consumer-named fields (e.g. `me`, `searchProducts`) are not in the set and are never touched.
     - **Bounded body shape.** Only matches the panic-stub patterns gqlgen emits. Consumer-edited bodies are non-panic and skip on shape alone, before the name check ever runs.
     - **Idempotent.** Running the rewriter twice produces the same output: the second pass finds no panic stubs left to match.
     - **Non-expanding.** Does not add or remove method declarations, does not reorder, does not touch type decls or `Query()` / `Mutation()`. Only swaps method bodies.

     *What it intentionally does not handle.*
     - **Field deletions.** When a managed operation is disabled, gqlgen detects the schema field is gone and moves the orphaned method into the WARNING comment block at the bottom of the file. The rewriter ignores that block — cosmetic noise, not a correctness issue.
     - **Signature changes.** When a managed input struct gains a column, the resolver signature is unchanged (the column lives on the struct, fully regenerated in the models package). gqlgen preserves the body; the body's delegation into the regenerated `sqlgenresolver` picks up the new column automatically. No rewriter action needed.
     - **First-time seeding.** That's step 3's job. The rewriter is the second-and-later-run mechanism.

  The wrapper's `Merge` step stays untouched — still only injects `schema:` + `models:`, no `resolver.layout` poking. The PRD §26.5.6 "consumer owns gqlgen.yml end-to-end" contract holds, and **both layouts are supported** without enforcement, override, or warn-on-incompatible logic.

  **Test plan.**
  - `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_resolvers_test.go` — replace the FIX-058-era "must NOT declare Resolver/queryResolver" assertions with the new shape: methods live on `*sqlgenresolver.Q` / `*sqlgenresolver.M` in the helper sub-package, seed `<schema>.resolvers.go` files contain delegations.
  - `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/wrapper_test.go::TestInit_WritesSeedFiles_FollowSchema` and `…_SingleFile` — temp dir with stub `gqlgen.yml` for each layout, run `Gen` against a fixture schema, assert correct seed file path + body shape + that the `sqlgenresolver/` helper package was emitted.
  - `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/wrapper_test.go::TestPostStubRewriter` — table-driven: input panic stub bodies (both panic-string and `fmt.Errorf` variants) for known sqlgen field names → expected delegation rewrites; non-sqlgen field stubs left untouched.
  - **16.8 E2E** (load-bearing) — runs the real `go run github.com/99designs/gqlgen` subprocess twice in a temp consumer dir, once with `layout: follow-schema` and once with `layout: single-file`, and asserts the consumer package compiles after each run. Locks the cross-layout invariant.

  **Notes.**
  - **Version sensitivity.** All findings above are pinned to gqlgen v0.17.90. The default `gqlgen_bin = "go run github.com/99designs/gqlgen"` (config.go:832) defers version selection to the consumer's module graph (`tools.go` pin or transitive requirement), so consumers on older gqlgen could see different preserve-bodies semantics. Re-run the spike against the oldest version we want to support before declaring the design final; document the supported gqlgen version range in the 16.8 example README.
  - **FIX-058 fallout.** The Resolver / queryResolver type-decl collision FIX-058 worked around goes away under Shape A — sqlgen no longer co-emits methods on `*queryResolver` in `resolver.dir`. The doc-block at `templates/api/resolvers.go.tmpl:5-12` and the `tests api_resolvers_test.go` "must NOT declare Resolver" assertions get replaced rather than retained.
  - **Init scaffold.** `wrapper.InitConfigContent` no longer needs to set a specific `resolver.layout` — both work. Keep gqlgen's default (`follow-schema`) in the scaffold so existing consumers' files stay untouched. Update the FIX-063 doc-block to remove any single-file-specific guidance that may have been added in flight. The post-`init` stdout block extends with the consumer-wiring callout from step 1: instruct the consumer to add `Q *sqlgenresolver.Q` and `M *sqlgenresolver.M` to their gqlgen-scaffolded `Resolver` struct and initialize both with the same `*models.Client` they use elsewhere.
  - **Migration for in-flight 16.x consumers.** Anyone who ran the old 16.3-era `sqlgen graphql init` has a `resolver.go` written by gqlgen plus a sqlgen-emitted `resolvers_gen.go`. Migration: delete `resolvers_gen.go` (and `field_options_gen.go`, `connection_walker_gen.go`), re-run `sqlgen graphql gen` to seed the per-schema files. No goldens shipped yet (16.8 in flight) so no public migration doc required, but worth a callout in the 16.8 example README.

### FIX-143

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** tracked
- **Origin:** phase 25, cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **`NullableNumericComparator` and `NullableBooleanComparator` are compiled by no
example.** Four of the six nullable twins 25.3 can emit appear in a golden and therefore get a
real Go compile (`NullableString`, `NullableTime`, `NullableID`, `NullableDecimal`); the numeric
and boolean twins appear in none, because neither API-enabled example has a nullable numeric or
nullable boolean column. The numeric one is the least trivial body in the family — it is the only
operand block that casts (`v := int32(*in.Eq)`) and it does so under the `NullableNumber[T]`
wrapper, where every assignment relies on Go promoting through the embedded `Number[T]`.

**Root cause.** Coverage follows the two example schemas, and both happen to declare their
numeric and boolean columns NOT NULL. The unit tests assert rendered *text*, not compilation, so
they cannot substitute.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add a nullable integer and a nullable boolean column to the `graphql` example schema (or a new
  fixture table), regenerate, and let the example build compile both twins.
- Extend `TestComparatorFamilies_translatorCopiesEveryOperator`'s fixture to cover all six twins
  so the derived check spans every family, not two of six.
- Review assessed the runtime risk as **low** (promotion through an embedded struct is sound Go
  and nothing type-specific is unexercised), which is why this is `tracked` rather than
  `blocking`.

**BLOCKED (2026-08-26) — attempting this fix surfaced a separate, pre-existing codegen bug.**
Adding `retry_count INTEGER` (nullable) and `succeeded BOOLEAN` (nullable) to the `graphql`
example's `events` table — the fixture table whose stated purpose is exactly to exercise
nullable scalar paths — makes `sqlgen generate` emit a **non-compiling input translator**:

```
models/graph/input_translate_gen.go:210:20: cannot use omittable.Set(in.RetryCount)
  (value of struct type omittable.Value[*int]) as omittable.Value[*int32] value in assignment
```

The nullable **boolean** is fine (`omittable.Set(in.Succeeded)`, `*bool` → `Value[*bool]`). The
defect is specific to a **nullable sized-int column on the GraphQL create/update input**:
gqlgen binds `Int` to Go `int`, the model column is `int32` / `int64`, and
`buildAPIInputFields`' `CastTo` machinery emits the `int32(*in.X)` cast only on the **non-null**
path — the nullable path emits neither a cast nor a deref-and-repoint
(`cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go`, `isSizedIntGoType` / `CastTo`;
`templates/api/input_translate.go.tmpl`). No example has a nullable INTEGER/BIGINT column
exposed to the API, which is why it has never been hit. Every SQL integer type on postgres maps
to a sized Go int (`integer`→`int32`, `bigint`→`int64`), so there is no column shape that
sidesteps it — the boolean half of this fix cannot land without the integer half also landing,
and dropping the integer column to get green would hide the bug rather than fix it.

The working tree was returned to the pre-attempt state (schema reverted, goldens regenerated,
`make check` + `make check-examples` clean, golden count unchanged) so nothing is left
half-applied. **This entry stays Open pending a decision on the input-translator defect, which
wants its own FIX — it is a different surface (mutation inputs) from this entry's comparator
twins, and it is a real consumer-facing bug independent of Phase 25.**

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/comparator_translate.go.tmpl` — the `Number` arm of
  `api/comparator-operands`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `buildAPIInputFields`, `isSizedIntGoType`, `APIInputField.CastTo`
  (the nullable-path gap that blocks this entry). *`isSizedIntGoType` was renamed
  `isNarrowedNumericGoType` by FIX-148, which widened it to the float axis.*
- `comparator/number.go` (`NullableNumber[T]` embeds `Number[T]`), `comparator/bool.go`.
- Goldens: neither `cmd/sqlgen/testdata/examples/graphql/**/shared_gen.graphqls` nor
  `graphql_top_level` declares `input NullableNumericComparator` / `NullableBooleanComparator`.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26 — unblocked by FIX-147, which fixed the codegen defect that made the fixture impossible to land. The `graphql` example's `events` table now carries `retry_count INTEGER` and `succeeded BOOLEAN`, both nullable, so all **six** nullable comparator twins are emitted and compiled by a golden: `translateNullableStringComparator`, `NullableTimeComparator`, `NullableIDComparator`, `NullableDecimalComparator`, and now `NullableNumericComparatorInt32` and `NullableBooleanComparator`. The `NumericT` cast block under a `NullableNumber[T]` wrapper — the entry's specific concern, and the least trivial body in the family — is therefore compiled by `make check-examples` rather than only string-matched. The second bullet also landed: `TestComparatorFamilies_translatorCopiesEveryOperator`'s fixture gained a nullable column per family (text, timestamp, integer, boolean, numeric, uuid FK), so the derived operator check spans all six twins instead of two of six.

### FIX-147

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** blocking
- **Origin:** phase 16, cmd/sqlgen/gen (API input translation)
- **Surfaced by:** /fix-implement FIX-143 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** **A nullable sized-integer column exposed to the GraphQL API generates a
non-compiling input translator.** Adding `retry_count INTEGER` (nullable) to a table in the
`graphql` example makes `sqlgen generate` fail at the gqlgen validation step:

```
models/graph/input_translate_gen.go:210:20: cannot use omittable.Set(in.RetryCount)
  (value of struct type omittable.Value[*int]) as omittable.Value[*int32] value in assignment
```

Every consumer with a nullable `INTEGER` / `BIGINT` / `SMALLINT` column and `api.graphql`
enabled hits this — the generated package does not build, so it is a hard stop, not a
degradation. A nullable **boolean** is unaffected (`*bool` into `Value[*bool]` needs no
conversion); the defect is specific to types where gqlgen's binding and the model's width
differ.

**Root cause.** `funcInputCoerceDeref` returns early on the `ModelInnerIsPointer` branch:

```go
if f.ModelInnerIsPointer {
    return "in." + f.GoFieldName
}
```

with the rationale "pointers thread identically". That holds only when the **pointee** types
match. For a nullable sized int they do not: gqlgen binds the GraphQL `Int` scalar to Go `int`
and emits `*int`, while the model size-narrows to the column's native width and stores
`omittable.Value[*int32]`. `buildAPIInputFields` computes `CastTo = "int32"` correctly (via
`isSizedIntGoType`), but the pointer branch returns before any cast is applied — the cast is
computed and then discarded on exactly the path that needs it. The non-null path
(`funcInputCoerceBare`) and the value-inner deref path both apply `CastTo` and are correct.

A cast cannot be inserted in expression position: Go has no way to convert a pointer's pointee
inline — `int32(p)` is illegal and `&int32(*p)` is not addressable. The fix therefore has to
move into the template, which already emits a statement block for this case.

No example has ever had a nullable integer column exposed to the API, which is why this
survived from phase 16. PostgreSQL maps every integer width to a sized Go int
(`integer` to `int32`, `bigint` to `int64`), so no column shape sidesteps it.

**Suggested fix.**
- Add a computed `PointerCast bool` to `APIInputField`, true when
  `ModelInnerIsPointer && CastTo != "" && !GqlgenIsBareNullable` (the bare-nullable and
  address-of branches already apply their own cast).
- In `templates/api/input_translate.go.tmpl`, emit the deref-convert-readdress form for that
  case in **both** the create and the update translator, matching the idiom the comparator
  translators already use:
  ```go
  if in.RetryCount != nil {
      v := int32(*in.RetryCount)
      out.RetryCount = omittable.Set(&v)
  }
  ```
- Leave `funcInputCoerceDeref` handling the other branches; correct its now-misleading
  "pointers thread identically" comment to say the pass-through is valid only when the pointee
  types agree.
- Regression fixture: a nullable integer column on an API-enabled example table, so the
  generated package is compiled by `make check-examples`. This is the same fixture FIX-143
  needs, so landing this unblocks that entry.
- **Adjacent risk, not fixed here (no evidence it is reachable):** `funcInputCoerceBare` has the
  mirror-image hole — with `AddressOf && CastTo != ""` it emits `&<Cast>(in.X)`, which is also
  not addressable. That combination needs a non-null slice column whose model inner is a
  pointer; no example produces it and the examples compile. Worth a guard or an explicit
  assertion that it cannot occur.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/funcmap.go` — `funcInputCoerceDeref`, `funcInputCoerceBare`.
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` — `buildAPIInputFields` (`CastTo` / `ModelInnerIsPointer` /
  `GqlgenIsBareNullable` / `AddressOf` computation), `isSizedIntGoType`, `APIInputField`.
  *`isSizedIntGoType` is now `isNarrowedNumericGoType` (FIX-148).*
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/api/input_translate.go.tmpl` — both translator bodies.
- PRD §26.5.4 Mutation Translation; §26.4.1 Scalar Marshaling (the gqlgen `Int` to Go `int`
  binding that creates the width mismatch).
- FIX-143 — blocked on this; its fixture is the regression pin.

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26. `APIInputField` gains a computed `PointerCast` flag (`ModelInnerIsPointer && CastTo != "" && !GqlgenIsBareNullable`), and `templates/api/input_translate.go.tmpl` emits the deref-convert-readdress form for it in **both** the create and the update translator:

```go
if in.RetryCount != nil {
	v := int32(*in.RetryCount)
	out.RetryCount = omittable.Set(&v)
}
```

The branch was written as an inner-only swap so the surrounding `if` / brace structure stays byte-identical — the only golden churn outside the new columns is the doc comment. `funcInputCoerceDeref` keeps the other branches, with its "pointers thread identically" rationale corrected to say the pass-through is valid only when the pointee types agree. **Fixture:** the `graphql` example's `events` table gains `retry_count INTEGER` and `succeeded BOOLEAN`, both nullable — `events` is already the example's nullable-scalar fixture table, so this is where it belongs. `sqlgen generate` now completes where it previously failed at the gqlgen validation step, and `make check-examples` compiles the result. **Unit pin:** `TestInputTranslate_NullableSizedIntGoesThroughALocal` covers `integer` and `bigint` in both translators, asserts the uncastable `omittable.Set(in.RetryCount)` form appears nowhere, and asserts a nullable **bool** is left threading unconverted so the fix stays narrow. `buildAPIInputFields` tripped the `cyclop` ceiling once the flag landed, so the whole coercion derivation was extracted into `inputCoercionFor` returning an `inputCoercion` struct — one readable unit instead of four loose locals. The adjacent `funcInputCoerceBare` `AddressOf && CastTo` hole noted in the entry was **not** fixed: it remains unreachable (it needs a non-null slice column with a pointer model inner, which no example produces).

### FIX-146

- **Status:** Resolved
- **Severity:** nit
- **Origin:** phase 25, cmd/sqlgen/gen + docs
- **Surfaced by:** /verify 25.3 (2026-08-26)

**Issue.** Four small text/deadwood items left by 25.3, none affecting generated output:
1. `APIFilterProjection.Nullable` is written and never read — its doc comment claims a
   schema-emitter consumer that does not exist. (25.3's dead-code sweep cleared the translator
   struct but not the projection struct.)
2. `api_comparator_families_test.go`'s rationale for reading `comparator/*.go` via `go/ast`
   says a test-only require "would put a module edge in the graph that the architecture
   forbids"; `guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md` explicitly permits CLI → Runtime. The choice is still
   right — `cmd/sqlgen/go.mod` has no runtime require and adding one for a test is not worth it
   — but the stated reason is wrong.
3. `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL.md` "One per comparator family — reused across all tables" is now false
   (variants are per family **and** nullability, and numerics per Go T);
   `comparatorTranslatorsUseTime`'s doc comment still says `time` is used "only … via the
   `Range` generic argument", which stopped being true when `in` / `nin` began inlining
   `[]time.Time`.
4. `nlike`, `nbetween` and `isNull` have single-dialect SQL-shape tests rather than the
   cross-dialect sweeps 25.3's "Tests Required" names. Down-severitied from `tracked` because
   all three are provably dialect-invariant — `NLike` / `IsNull` / `IsNotNull` in
   `sql/condition.go` and `parseNull` / `parseNBetween` in `comparator/comparator.go` take no
   `sql.Dialect`, and `sql.Range` is expanded generically on `$` tokens — so extra sweeps would
   exercise identical code. `nin` was the one operator with a real dialect split (ALL vs
   NOT IN) and did get a sweep.

**Root cause.** Items 1–3 are stale text following 25.3's structural changes; item 4 is a
requirement written before the invariance was established.

**Suggested fix.**
- Delete `APIFilterProjection.Nullable`, or give it a reader in 25.4/25.5 if the twin-selection
  logic wants it.
- Correct the test's rationale comment to "the CLI module does not depend on the runtime module
  and a test-only require is not worth adding".
- Update `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL.md` and the `comparatorTranslatorsUseTime` doc comment.
- Either add the three sweeps for symmetry, or record the invariance argument next to the
  requirement so the gap is a decision rather than an oversight.

**References.**
- `cmd/sqlgen/gen/context_api.go` (`APIFilterProjection.Nullable`),
  `cmd/sqlgen/gen/orchestrate.go` (`comparatorTranslatorsUseTime` doc),
  `cmd/sqlgen/gen/api_comparator_families_test.go` (rationale comment).
- `guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md` (CLI → Runtime permitted), `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL.md`.
- `sql/condition.go`, `comparator/comparator.go`, `sql/builder.go` (invariance evidence).

**Resolution notes.** Resolved 2026-08-26; all four items closed. (1) `APIFilterProjection.Nullable` deleted — it was written at construction and read nowhere, and its doc comment described a schema-emitter consumer that does not exist; the projection is now built with `var proj APIFilterProjection`. (2) `api_comparator_families_test.go`'s rationale for the `go/ast` approach rewritten — ARCHITECTURE.md permits a CLI → Runtime edge, so the comment now states the real reason (a cost judgement: `cmd/sqlgen/go.mod` has no runtime require, and adding one plus its version pin and `go mod tidy` surface to satisfy one test is not worth it). (3) `docs/design/archive/GRAPHQL.md:154` corrected — the comparator row now reads "One per (family, operand type, nullability)" with the Rule 2 twin and the Rule 3 emission gate; `comparatorTranslatorsUseTime`'s doc comment corrected to say the Time family references `time.Time` from four operands in **both** variants, which is what made the import gate load-bearing. (4) The cross-dialect sweep gap is recorded as a decision rather than closed: the invariance argument now sits next to the requirement in `docs/tracker/phase-25.md` §25.3 — only `nin` has a dialect split and it got a four-dialect sweep; `nlike` / `nbetween` / `isNull` take no `sql.Dialect` anywhere on their path, so a sweep would exercise identical code three times.

- [x] **FIX-063** (phase 16, wrapper/gen.go + wrapper/init.go + cmd/sqlgen/cli/graphql.go) — `sqlgen graphql gen` invokes `go run github.com/99designs/gqlgen` as a subprocess in the consumer's working directory. Without `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod` (or a pre-run `go mod download` against gqlgen's transitive build deps), the subprocess fails with a cascade of `missing go.sum entry for module providing package …` errors covering `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages`, `golang.org/x/text/cases`, `github.com/urfave/cli/v2`, `github.com/agnivade/levenshtein`, etc. — gqlgen's *build*-time deps that the consumer's runtime go.sum has no reason to pin.

  → resolved: **shipped both complementary changes from the suggested fix.** `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/gen.go` extracts a new unexported helper `subprocessEnv(name, args []string) []string` that returns `os.Environ()` plus `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod` when the invocation shape is `name == "go" && len(args) > 0 && args[0] == "run"`; `Gen` assigns the result to `cmd.Env` so the subprocess inherits the parent env unchanged for non-`go run` invocations (consumer `GOFLAGS` continues to work) and gains the `-mod=mod` override only for the default `go run github.com/99designs/gqlgen` path. `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/init.go::InitConfigContent` gains a `# go.sum requirement (FIX-063):` comment block documenting the auto-injected `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod`, the rationale (gqlgen's transitive build deps live outside the consumer's runtime go.sum), and the `tools.go` opt-in pattern (`//go:build tools` + `import _ "github.com/99designs/gqlgen"` + `go mod tidy`) for consumers who want hermetic CI builds. `cmd/sqlgen/cli/graphql.go::newGraphQLInitCmd` extends the post-scaffold stdout with a 5-line note pointing at the same go.sum/`tools.go` rationale so consumers see it on the first `sqlgen graphql init` without having to read the scaffolded yaml comments.

Shipped two tests instead, since the fix's behaviour is "inject the env var on the right shape" (a unit-level invariant) plus "the subprocess actually sees it" (an integration-level invariant) — and a real gqlgen-dependent test would be slow + network-coupled. `cmd/sqlgen/wrapper/wrapper_test.go::TestSubprocessEnv` is table-driven across 6 invocation shapes (`go run package`, `go run multi-arg`, `go build` ≠ `go run`, `go` no-args, non-`go` binaries with and without run-shaped args) and asserts `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod` presence + `PATH=` parent-env inheritance. `TestGen_GoRunInheritsModMode` stages a tiny self-contained `main.go` (prints `GOFLAGS=$GOFLAGS` to stdout, no external deps) plus a minimal `go.mod` in a temp dir, invokes `wrapper.Gen` with `GqlgenBin = "go run ."`, and asserts the captured stdout contains `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod` — proving the env reaches the actual subprocess. The exemption is narrowly scoped: the marker only suppresses the lint for `init.go`, the actual `cmd/sqlgen` import graph is unchanged.

  `make check` (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` tests green; cmd/sqlgen/wrapper ~3.9s, cmd/sqlgen/cli ~37.7s, cmd/sqlgen/gen ~4.5s) passes cleanly. - [x] **FIX-059** (phase 6, gen/funcmap.go + gen/context.go) — `pkFilterInExpr` / `pkFilterInExprStr` template helpers ignored the FK column's nullability when emitting the comparator constructor for O2M relationship loaders. - [x] **FIX-058** (phase 16, gen/templates/api/resolvers.go.tmpl + orchestrate.go) — generated `resolvers_gen.go` defined `Resolver`, `queryResolver`, `mutationResolver` types plus the `Query() QueryResolver` / `Mutation() MutationResolver` interface methods inline. gqlgen's `resolvergen` plugin also writes a one-shot `resolver.go` file containing those exact same declarations (file-existence-gated, not symbol-gated — gqlgen scans for the *file* path, not the type names). On the first `sqlgen graphql gen` run against a fresh consumer project, both files would declare `type Resolver struct{...}` / `type queryResolver struct{ *Resolver }` / `type mutationResolver struct{ *Resolver }` in the same `graph` package and the consumer's build would fail with `Resolver redeclared in this block`. Blocked the consumer-customization story for 16.x — users adding their own `.graphqls` files (custom queries / mutations / scalars) could not integrate sqlgen's curated surface into their gqlgen server because the generated package would not compile end-to-end against a real gqlgen run. gqlgen owning `resolver.go` is the correct division of responsibility per gqlgen's documented extension model: consumers add dependency fields (`Logger *slog.Logger`, `AuthService AuthClient`) to the gqlgen-scaffolded `Resolver` struct, and our per-table methods access those via the embedded `*Resolver` receiver on `queryResolver` / `mutationResolver`. Why this wasn't caught in 16.3: no example module enables API generation yet, so the partial 16.3 → 16.4 → 16.5 → 16.6 codegen output never goes through a full gqlgen subprocess invocation.

Per-table methods continue to attach to `*queryResolver` / `*mutationResolver`; gqlgen's `resolvergen` plugin AST-scans `resolver.dir` (via `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages` — the `_gen.go` suffix is meaningless to it), matches each schema field's PascalCase form against existing methods on the configured receiver types, and skips stub generation on a name+receiver match. `invalidInputError` (top-level helper) and all `translateCreate*Input` / `translateUpdate*Input` / `hasUpdate*SetFields` package-level helpers preserved.

Without the gate, a schema with API enabled but every operation disabled would produce a file containing only `invalidInputError` plus an unused models-package import, which would fail to compile. With the gate, that edge case emits only the `gqlerror` import and `invalidInputError` — both compile cleanly. The `context` / `errors` / `omittable` imports remain scoped per their existing feature flags; `gqlerror` remains unconditional because `invalidInputError` is always emitted.

  **Honest scope reconciliations against the original FIX-058 spec.** Two pieces of the originally-proposed scope were descoped during implementation review:

  1. **Edit 5 originally proposed expanding `models:` to alias generated inputs (`Create<Table>Input`, `<Table>FilterInput`, etc.) and generic envelopes (`Connection[T]` / `PaginateResult[T]`).** Both aliases are wrong as scoped:
     - **Generated inputs are gqlgen-autogen-owned.** Aliasing `CreateProductInput → <consumer-pkg>.CreateProductInput` would force gqlgen's JSON unmarshaler to round-trip through the consumer's `omittable.Value[T]` fields — the consumer's input shape is sqlgen-style (per-field omittable wrapper) while the gqlgen-side input is plain pointers. Resolution sequenced into 16.5/16.6 when non-generic `<Table>Connection` / `<Table>ListResult` typedefs are introduced in the consumer's models package alongside the filter/sort/pagination translation layer.
     - Both deferred concerns documented inline at `buildMergeInput`'s godoc.

The unit test in `cmd/sqlgen/cli/graphql_test.go` verifies the same invariant at test time and surfaces the same regression signal — a CI failure when `buildMergeInput` accidentally drops the row-struct or scalar loop.

The 16.8 E2E example is the canonical regression guard for the full-compile path — at that point the consumer's `graph/` directory will contain gqlgen's `resolver.go` (one-shot, never regenerated), gqlgen's `*.resolvers.go` per schema file (auto-stubbed only for consumer-added custom fields), and our `resolvers_gen.go` (regenerated each run, methods-only, no type collisions). `make check` (8 modules, 0 lint, all `-short -race` unit tests green) and `make check-examples` (7 example modules, 0 lint, all E2E `-race` tests green) pass cleanly post-fix. No goldens regenerated — no example module enables `api.graphql.enabled`, so the resolver template's render path is exercised only by unit tests.

- [x] **FIX-055** (phase 6, gen/templates/table + tenancy) — generated tenanted clients re-invoked the user-supplied tenant resolver 3× per chained operation. A single `Create` ran `c.resolveTenant(ctx)` three times: once in `Create` (auto-set `workspace_id` + verify-match + populate `MutationContext.Tenant`), once in the terminal `Get` (re-read for `QueryContext.Tenant`), and once in `GetMany` (filter WHERE predicate). Observable counts on the tenancy example: 3 for `Create`, 3 for `Upsert`, 2 per batch for `CreateMany`, N+1 for `UpdateMany`, 2 per `*Where` op. Violated PRD §29.6 "resolver is called once per mutation hook entry"; the over-resolve compounds with expensive resolvers (JWT parse, Redis session read, auth RPC).

  → resolved: **ctx-cached single-resolve plumbing.** Added two generic helpers to `tenancy/tenancy.go` — `WithResolvedTenant[T comparable](ctx, value, apply) context.Context` and `CachedTenant[T comparable](ctx) (value, apply, ok bool)`. The cache key is a private `resolvedKey[T] struct{}` parameterised by T so multi-client apps with different tenant types don't collide on the same ctx slot. Both helpers carry godoc marking them as generator-emitted plumbing (consumers don't call them directly).

  **Templates touched (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/`):**
  - `client.go.tmpl` — generated per-client `resolveTenant` now begins with `if v, apply, ok := tenancy.CachedTenant[T](ctx); ok { return v, apply, nil }` before the existing required:true / required:false body.
  - `create.go.tmpl` — Create + CreateMany stash `ctx = tenancy.WithResolvedTenant(ctx, resolvedTenant, apply)` after their own resolve and error check, in both the composite-PK + InPrimaryKey branch and the general non-composite branch. Both `apply=true` and `apply=false` cache the decision so the chained terminal Get/GetMany inherits the same "skip filter" outcome under required:false + zero resolver.
  - `upsert.go.tmpl` — same pattern at both Upsert resolve sites.
  - `update.go.tmpl` — Update, UpdateMany (per-batch resolve), and UpdateWhere all stash on ctx; UpdateMany's per-input verify-match loop now hits the cache after the first item, dropping the 200-row batch from N+1 resolves to 1.
  - `delete.go.tmpl` — six chaining ops (`SoftDelete`, `SoftDeleteMany`, `SoftDeleteWhere`, `Restore`, `RestoreMany`, `RestoreWhere`) stash on ctx; HardDelete* skipped (no chained Get/GetMany). SkipTenancy path on every op short-circuits before resolveTenant — the chained terminal inherits SkipTenancy via the internal opts copy and never re-resolves.

  **Result.** Single `Create` chain resolves 1× (was 3×); `UpdateMany` batch resolves 1× (was N+1×); SkipTenancy continues to skip the resolve entirely. Cache scope is per-op: two sequential `Create` calls on the same caller-supplied ctx resolve twice (the helper returns a derived ctx and never mutates the input ctx), so consumers who set ctx state between ops still observe their changes.

  - Added `TestTx_Resolver_SequentialOpsResolveIndependently` — two sequential `Create` calls assert `count == 2`, guarding against cache leakage past op boundaries.

Each error case asserts no `SAVEPOINT` SQL was issued — validation rejects before `conn.Exec`.

- [x] **FIX-053** (phase 6, gen/templates + context_tenancy) — `tenancy.required: false` did not skip the tenant filter on a zero-value resolver return. PRD §29.2 line 10933: "When false, missing tenant skips the filter — effectively becomes a cross-tenant query." The generator populated `TenancyContext.Required` via `config.ResolveTableTenancyRequired` (context_tenancy.go:142) and threaded it into the per-field Required shape (context_tenancy.go:381), but no template consumed it to gate the tenant-filter-append or the verify-match branch. Every tenanted op unconditionally called `resolveTenant(ctx)` and appended `WHERE {tenantCol} = $N` regardless — so a resolver returning `(zeroValue, nil)` under `required: false` produced `WHERE workspace_id = '00000000-...-0'` rather than omitting the predicate. Under `required: true` the generator also relied entirely on the caller's resolver to return `tenancy.ErrMissing` explicitly on missing tenant; a resolver returning `(zero, nil)` silently proceeded and filtered against the zero value.

  → resolved: **runtime gate in `resolveTenant`.** Changed the signature from `(T, error)` to `(T, bool, error)` in `cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/table/client.go.tmpl`. New semantics encode both required branches:
  - `required:true`: `resolver==nil` OR `(zero, nil)` → `(zero, false, tenancy.ErrMissing)`. Non-zero → `(v, true, nil)`. Non-nil resolver error → `(zero, false, err)`.
  - `required:false`: `resolver==nil` OR `(zero, nil)` → `(zero, false, nil)` (the PRD §29.2 "skip filter" path). Non-zero → `(v, true, nil)`. Non-nil resolver error → `(zero, false, err)` (required:false does NOT swallow resolver errors).

  The `required:true` branch is template-expanded per-table from `.Tenancy.Required` so the zero-check is emitted only where it applies; behaviour is stable at codegen time.

Every `if !options.SkipTenancy { ... }` block now wraps its tenancy logic in an inner `if apply { ... }` guard.

- [x] **FIX-051** (phase 5, config + gen/context_table + gen/context_view + view templates) — `cursor_keys` validation was strict in all cases: `validateCursorKeys` (cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:300) returned a hard error whenever any resolved key (global or per-table) was missing on a table. The built-in default `["id"]` therefore failed validation on every table without an `id` column, forcing consumers to set `generation.cursor_keys` or per-table `cursor_keys` everywhere even when a PK-based cursor was the natural fallback. `ViewConfig` (cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go:450) also had no `cursor_keys` field, so views could only inherit the global — when the global didn't match the view's projection the generator produced a `Connection` method whose emitted SQL referenced columns the view didn't have (latent runtime failure). → resolved in conjunction with PRD §4.6/§4.7/§4.9/§4.13/§14 amendments (2026-04-23):

  **Config surface.** Added `CursorKeys []string` to `ViewConfig` for explicit per-view override. Introduced `CursorKeysDecision{Keys, Emit, Warning, Err}` and two new resolvers in `cmd/sqlgen/config/config.go`: `ResolveTableConnection(tableCfg, global, qualifiedName, columns, pk)` and `ResolveViewConnection(viewCfg, global, qualifiedName, columns)`. Both implement the §4.13 ruleset: (1) explicit override + missing column → `Err`; (2) inherited default + any column missing + table has PK → silent fallback to PK (single or composite); (3) inherited default + any column missing + no PK (or view) → `Emit=false` with `Warning` naming the entity. Partial matches trigger full fallback — never subset — so sort semantics cannot silently shift. Removed the old `ResolveTableCursorKeys` (the only non-test caller, `context_table.go`, now uses `ResolveTableConnection`).

  **Validator surface.** Rewrote `validateCursorKeys` (now at cmd/sqlgen/config/validate.go:301) to delegate to the per-entity resolvers and forward `Warning` entries into the existing `[]Warning` slice. Added `PrimaryKey bool` to `SchemaColumn` (populated from `parser.Column.PrimaryKey` via `toSchemaTables`), a new `SchemaView` type, and `toSchemaViews` in cmd/sqlgen/cli/pipeline.go. `ValidatePostParse` now takes `(cfg, tables, views)` — all three call sites (cli/pipeline.go, cli/validate.go, cli/generate.go) updated.

  **Codegen surface.** `context_table.go` builds the decision up-front, threads `Keys` into `TableContext.CursorKeys`, and flips `Operations.Connection = false` when `Emit` is false — the existing `{{- if .Operations.Connection }}` gates in `table/client.go.tmpl` and `table/pagination.go.tmpl` then omit the method cleanly (no template change needed). `context_view.go` mirrors this via a new `ViewContext.HasConnection bool`; `view/client.go.tmpl` and `view/pagination.go.tmpl` gate the Connection method + `cursorKeys` field/init + `encodeXCursor` helper on `{{- if .HasConnection }}`. Views have no PK, so the decision for views reduces to rules 2/5.

  **Tests.** Rewrote the cursor_keys block in `config/validate_test.go` with 8 table-driven tests covering all 5 PRD §4.13 rules (plus partial-match full-fallback and the explicit-present happy paths for both tables and views). Updated the `schemaTables()` fixture to mark `id` as `PrimaryKey: true` so PK-fallback paths are exercisable; added `pklessSchemaTable()` for the no-PK warning path. Updated `TestValidatePostParse_MultipleErrors` to use an explicit table-level override (the inherited path no longer errors). Updated gen `TestViewClientTemplate` fixture (`view_test.go:testViewContext_withPK`) with `HasConnection: true` since the test's columns include `id`. Updated two E2E comment lines in postgres/postgres_stdlib view tests noting CategoryStat loses Connection under the new rules.

  **E2E goldens.** The `category_stats` view across all 4 non-cache examples (postgres, postgres_stdlib, mysql, sqlite) exercises rule 4 naturally — columns are `category_name/product_count/total_price/avg_price/min_price/max_price/product_names`, no `id`. Regenerated goldens show the Connection method + `cursorKeys` field + `encodeCategoryStatCursor` helper omitted (1156 lines deleted across 8 files). `product_summary` retains Connection (has `id` via `@pk`). Verified end-to-end: running `sqlgen validate` on `testdata/examples/postgres` now emits `Warning: cursor_keys: inherited default does not match view category_stats; Connection method omitted (views have no primary key fallback)` to stderr.

- [x] **FIX-050** (phase 13, gen/templates/table/upsert) — `Upsert` on a tenanted table emitted `updateColumns := excludeColumns(columns, append(conflictColumns, "id"))`, excluding only the PK and conflict columns. Because the tenancy auto-set block appends `"workspace_id"` (or the per-table tenant column) to `columns`, the tenant column leaked into the UPDATE-set portion of the conflict clause across every dialect — `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET workspace_id = EXCLUDED.workspace_id, ...` on postgres/sqlite and `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE workspace_id = VALUES(workspace_id), ...` on mysql — violating PRD §29.4.2 ("the SET clause excludes the tenant column"). Happy-path no-op in value (auto-set = resolver), but masks a subtle bug class on the SkipTenancy-with-explicit-tenant path where the upsert would silently move a row between tenants on conflict. Surfaced by cross-dialect upsert tenancy template coverage following the 13.9 cross-dialect E2E deferral decision. → resolved: `gen/templates/table/upsert.go.tmpl` line 95 exclusion literal now appends the tenant column when `.Tenancy.Tenanted` (`append(conflictColumns, "id", "workspace_id")` etc., dialect-agnostic since the `updateColumns` slice is the single source feeding both ON CONFLICT and ON DUPLICATE KEY branches). Added four new cross-dialect template tests in `gen/tenancy_template_test.go`: `TestTenancyTemplate_upsert_autoSetAcrossDialects` (postgres/mysql/sqlite resolve + mismatch + auto-set emission), `TestTenancyTemplate_upsert_tenantExcludedFromUpdateSet` (exclusion-list invariant per dialect — the regression guard), `TestTenancyTemplate_upsert_sharedTableOmitsTenancy` (shared tables never widen the literal), and `TestTenancyTemplate_upsert_skipTenancyUsesExplicitTenant` (SkipTenancy branch uses caller's value). Also renamed the dialect-aware helper to `renderUpsertTenancy` to satisfy `unparam`. Regenerated gen goldens (`upsert_products_gen.go`, `upsert_order_items_gen.go`) and E2E goldens for all 6 example projects (+ tenancy) — non-tenanted examples get only the comment-line diff; tenanted tables carry the widened exclusion literal (`workspace_id` or `org_id` per table). `make check` and `make check-examples` pass with 0 lint issues.

Bidirectional auto-detected o2o (e.g. `users` ↔ `user_profiles` via `UNIQUE` FK) produced SQL like `... AND pr.workspace_id = ? AND pro.workspace_id = ? ...` for aliases that were never JOINed, so `FieldOptions{Profile: ...}` failed with "no such column: pr.workspace_id". → resolved: replaced the static per-child append loop in `get.go.tmpl` with a generated `tenantedAliases := map[string]string{...}` literal + a runtime `for _, j := range o2oJoins { if col, ok := tenantedAliases[j.Alias]; ok { ... } }` loop. `collectTenantedO2OChildren` remains the source of truth for which aliases are tenant-scoped; the runtime intersection against the actually-emitted joins is self-correcting whenever FieldOptions selects a strict prefix of an o2o chain. Updated `TestTenancyTemplate_o2o_bothTenanted_emitsBothFilters` and `TestTenancyTemplate_o2o_childOnlyTenanted_emitsChildFilter` to assert the new pattern, added `TestTenancyTemplate_o2o_multipleTenantedChildren_rendersMap` covering a direct + chained pair. Restored `TestRelationship_O2O_TenantPropagatesToChild` (was rewritten as `DirectChildGetIsTenantScoped` under 13.9 as a workaround) and added `TestRelationship_O2O_PartialChainSelection` against the bidirectional users↔user_profiles tree — both pass. - [x] **FIX-048** (phase 12, gen/templates/cache) — `hydrate{Table}` emitted only the `sync.Map` dedup + fresh-timeout-context scaffolding; it never re-queried the DB, never populated the cache, and was never invoked from anywhere. PRD §27.8 / CACHE.md §13 require the background goroutine to refill the cache with the full entity for partial-fetch hits. → resolved: (1) `hydrate{Struct}` signature now takes `next hook.QueryHandler`; the goroutine builds a fresh `&hook.QueryContext{Op: OpGet, Table: {{TableConstant}}, Schema, PK, CallOptions: CallOptions[{FO}]{FieldOptions: fullParentFieldOptions{Struct}(), SkipHooks: true}}`, calls `next(ctx, q)`, breaker-gates + `cache.SetAs[*{Struct}]` on success, and reports `metrics.HydrationComplete(..., err)` with the real `next` / `SetAs` error (or `nil` on clean success / nil-entity / breaker-open). (2) `readThrough{Struct}` gained a partial-fetch branch that fires **before** the singleflight block: when `extractFieldOptions(q.CallOptions) != nil`, it runs `next(ctx, q)`, kicks off `c.hydrate{Struct}(pk, next)` (fire-and-forget), and returns the partial result without ever writing to cache — preserving the §27.6 full-entity invariant. (3) `QueryHook` gained a pre-dispatch bypass `if !c.hydrationEnabled && extractFieldOptions(q.CallOptions) != nil { return next(ctx, q) }` so the partial + hydration-off row of §27.7 is pure pass-through with no cache read. Updated `TestCacheTemplate_emitsHydrateHelper` for the new signature and added 5 template-rendering tests (signature takes next for single + composite PK, full FieldOptions + SkipHooks re-run, SetAs/metrics in body, HydrationComplete with real error in three branches, partial branch ordering before singleflight, QueryHook partial+hydration-off guard ordering). `make check` passes with 0 lint issues; no E2E goldens change (no example wires cache yet — 12.9 handles that).

- [x] **FIX-047** (phase 12, gen/templates/cache) — `MutationHook()` handled `OpCreate` / `OpCreateMany` as a no-op, so Create+Get sequences always paid an extra DB round-trip on the read path even though the full entity was already in hand. PRD §27.7 / CACHE.md §9.3 required Set-after-insert. → resolved: added per-table `set{Struct}(ctx, entity)` helper in `cache.go.tmpl` that reads the PK from the entity itself (for both single-PK and composite-PK via the generated `XxxPK` struct literal), gates on `c.breaker.Allow()`, calls `cache.SetAs[*Struct]` under the fingerprint-keyed path, times via `SetLatency`, and routes failures through `cache.RouteError` (cache outage never breaks the caller). Rewired `MutationHook` to forward `result` into `dispatchMutation`, added `fieldOptsSet := extractFieldOptions(m.CallOptions) != nil` capture, and replaced the `OpCreate` / `OpCreateMany` no-op with per-table type-assertion switches (`*Struct` for Create, `[]*Struct` for CreateMany) that short-circuit when `fieldOptsSet` is true — partial fetches and relationship-loaded entities must not land in cache (PRD §27.6). Added 6 template-rendering tests (set helper single-PK, set helper composite-PK with field-order guarantee, MutationHook result forwarding + dispatchMutation signature, OpCreate dispatch switch, OpCreateMany iterate+dispatch, fieldOptsSet guard ordering). `make check` passes with 0 lint issues; no E2E goldens change because no example wires cache yet (12.9 handles that).

- [x] **FIX-046** (phase 12, gen/templates/cache) — `QueryHook()` generated in `cache.go.tmpl` did not perform read-through. Current body only handled skip-cache / non-cached-table / circuit-breaker / relationship-bypass gates and then called `next(ctx, q)` — no `backend.Get`, no `c.sf.Do(key, fn)` singleflight wrapping, no `backend.Set` on DB-success, no `metrics.Hit`/`Miss`/`GetLatency`/`SetLatency`. The `sf singleflight.Group` field was declared on `Cache` but unused. `ttlFor{Table}` helpers were emitted but never called. PRD §27.7 and CACHE.md §9.3 (stampede dedup) not satisfied. → resolved: added per-table `readThrough{Table}(ctx, pk, q, next) (any, error)` helper in `cache.go.tmpl`, typed on the concrete entity (`cache.GetAs[*{Struct}]` / `cache.SetAs[*{Struct}]`) and the concrete PK (scalar for single-PK, `XxxPK` struct value for composite); dispatches from `QueryHook` via `switch q.Table` with a wrong-type fall-through to `next`. Every backend call is breaker-gated (independent gates around Get and Set) and errors route through `cache.RouteError`. Miss path wraps `next(ctx, q)` + `cache.SetAs` in `c.sf.DoChan(key, fn)` and the caller selects on `<-ch` / `<-ctx.Done()` so followers can cancel locally while the leader's Set still populates the cache for subsequent arrivals (CACHE.md §9.3 semantic). Removed the now-unused `cacheTableEnabled` helper — the switch + default handles that. Added 5 template-rendering tests (read-through helper emission, composite-PK signature, QueryHook dispatch, bypass-gate ordering, breaker gating) and verified zero-churn on all 5 non-cache E2E golden files (`TestE2EGoldenFiles`). `make check` passes with 0 lint issues.

- [x] **FIX-045** (phase 2, database + gen/templates) — `WithCallbackMode` is non-functional. The generated client template declares `callbackMode database.CallbackMode` on `clientOptions` and exposes `WithCallbackMode(mode)`, but the generated `Begin`/`WithTx`/`Commit`/`Rollback` methods never thread that value through to `database.NewTransaction`. Root cause is a missing piece of plumbing in the database layer: `database.TxOptions` has no `CallbackMode` field, and every driver adapter's `Begin` (`database/stdlib/stdlib.go`, `database/pgx/pgx.go`) declares `var mode database.CallbackMode` (empty string → defaults to `CallbackAsync` inside `database.NewTx`). So regardless of what the user passes to `WithCallbackMode`, transactions always fire `OnCommit` callbacks in a detached goroutine. This blocks deterministic synchronous event-commit tests in Phase 11.6, which currently work around the gap with a `collector.waitFor` polling helper. **Fix:** (1) add `CallbackMode database.CallbackMode` to `database.TxOptions` in `database/transaction.go`; (2) update driver adapters (`database/stdlib/stdlib.go`, `database/pgx/pgx.go`) to read the mode from `opts[0].CallbackMode` and pass it to `database.NewTx`; (3) update the generated client template (`cmd/sqlgen/gen/templates/client.go.tmpl`) so `Begin` and `WithTx` inject the client's `opts.callbackMode` into the forwarded `TxOptions` (merging with any user-supplied opts, with user-supplied taking precedence if non-empty); (4) regenerate E2E golden files. After the fix, `WithCallbackMode(database.CallbackSync)` should cause `OnCommit` callbacks — including event-hook publishing — to fire synchronously inside `Commit`, enabling the Phase 11.6 sync-commit test. → resolved: added CallbackMode field to database.TxOptions; stdlib + pgx adapters forward opts[0].CallbackMode to database.NewTx; generated client template adds applyTxDefaults helper that injects clientOptions.callbackMode into TxOptions when the caller does not specify one (caller wins); regenerated gen + E2E golden files; added TestEventTx_SyncCallbackModePublishesOnCommit to events example proving sync publish works without polling
